      "content": "# Architecture Blueprint — Portfolio-Aware CLI and Auditable Reporting\n\nStatus: **architecture draft (Stage 3)** for Member B's session. Not implementation, not verification, not an approved course deliverable until E/team assembly and instructor reconciliation. Complements the D2 artifacts under `docs/architecture/`.\n\n- Selection: **C2 — input-service + immutable `RunContext` boundary with a small lifecycle coordinator**, chosen by Brian (human) on 2026-11-12 based on **estimated** tradeoffs, not verified superiority.\n- Target baseline: TradingAgents **v0.7.1** (`tradingagents/__init__.py:3`, `pyproject.toml`).\n- Working scope: `docs/req/selected-requirements.md` (`SEL-TA-FR-001..007`, `SEL-TA-NFR-001..006`, `SEL-TA-GOV-001..006`). This is a working selection, **not** an approved D1 registry.\n- Location convention (interim, pending course clarification): this root file is canonical; `docs/architecture/architecture-blueprint.md` is a pointer only.\n\n> Honesty statement: This document specifies architecture and testability. It does **not** claim C's tests exist/pass, E's gates are enforced, or any approval has been obtained. Unknown test IDs and implementation links remain **pending**. Estimates are labelled **ESTIMATE**.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Scope and drivers\n\n### 1.1 Scope\nExtend the existing terminal UI (`cli/`), the Python/LangGraph workflow (`tradingagents/`), the portfolio loader (`tradingagents/portfolio.py`) and the Markdown/HTML reports (`tradingagents/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/report_html.py`) so a run can be performed in one of two input modes:\n\n- `NO_PORTFOLIO` — the caller's holdings/cash are unknown; nothing is assumed.\n- `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED` — an explicitly selected, validated, frozen snapshot supplied by the user.\n\nBoth modes yield an auditable result with deterministic input provenance and a deterministic output check.\n\n### 1.2 Drivers\n| Driver | Source |\n|---|---|\n| Optional, explicitly confirmed holdings input | selected-requirements §1; Brian decision |\n| No silent portfolio fallback; no invented zero holdings/cash | FR-003/004, NFR-001 |\n| Deterministic check authority (model cannot override) | FR-007 |\n| Frozen input provenance in every report | FR-006 |\n| Secret/holdings privacy across sinks | NFR-003 |\n| Reusable boundary without terminal prompts in engine/agents | NFR-005 |\n| Reliable external-failure handling | NFR-001 |\n| Structured observability | NFR-002 |\n| Cohesive integration preserving upstream | NFR-005 |\n\n### 1.3 Explicit non-goals (deferred; do not claim satisfied)\nWeb GUI; broker connection/order execution; exposure certification; automatic broker discovery; full twelve-channel evidence registry; new historical filtering/freshness rules; global source-confidence grades; R4–R6 sentiment correction; resume/checkpoint redesign; aggregate time/token/call budgets; debate convergence; analyst plugin redesign. (selected-requirements §5.)\n\n### 1.4 Authority of current selection vs open decisions\n- **Approved working input (use directly):** CLI-only UI; `PORTFOLIO_DIR=<project-root>/portfolios`; `--without-portfolio`; `--portfolio-as-of`; consent behaviour; full normalized-content SHA-256 (64-char) fingerprint.\n- **Open (not B's to close; do not invent):** final D1 YAML/schema approval (A); semantic rubric/threshold (`GOV-004`, C/A); instructor-accepted source/test layout and transcript wording; governance install (E); blueprint location final convention (E).\n\n---\n\n## 2. System and deployment boundaries\n\n- **Runtime:** a single local Python process. The user interacts through the terminal (the existing CLI). No network is required for input selection/validation; network/provider calls occur only inside the graph after confirmation.\n- **Requested interface:** current CLI (`cli/main.py`), extended with input-mode flags. This is the only new user-facing surface; no new web application.\n- **Baseline preserved:** `tradingagents/`, `cli/`, `pyproject.toml` and existing tests are preserved. The extension is discovery, explicit consent, frozen provenance and coherent reporting (Prompt.md §13).\n- **Trust boundary for data:** user-supplied portfolio files are *context*, never verified account facts. The trusted state used to build provenance is the frozen snapshot produced by the input service, not model text and not re-read file bytes.\n\n### 2.1 Data-flow (C2)\n```\nterminal user\n   │  (interactive, or flags)\n   ▼\nCLI adapter (cli/main.py)  ──►  PortfolioInputService (discover → validate/precheck → freeze)\n   │                                         │\n   │                                         ▼\n   │                              RunContext (immutable)\n   │             frozen snapshot + mode + full-64 fingerprint + as-of + disclosure flags\n   │                                         │\n   │   [notice shown; consent gate]\n   │                                         │\n   ▼                                         ▼\nRunLifecycleCoordinator  ── consent confirmed ──►  TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run\n   │  (CLI single-run orchestration, no LLM)         (portfolio=None | frozen snapshot)\n   │                                         │\n   │                                         ▼\n   │                              OutputChecker (non-LLM, authoritative)\n   │                                         │\n   │                                         ▼\n   │                              OutcomeFinalizer (COMPLETED|INCOMPLETE)\n   │                                         │\n   ▼                                         ▼\nArtifact boundary (redaction + run-ID isolation)  →  report(MD/HTML), manifest, JSONL events, logs, state JSON\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Components\n\n| Component | Responsibility | Where (design) | Needs baseline change? |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `PortfolioInputService` | Non-recursive discovery of eligible `.json`; precheck (shape/type/finite/as-of); freeze selected bytes; produce `RunContext`. **Sole** discoverer/validator. | new `cli/`-level service module | additive |\n| `RunContext` (immutable) | Carries frozen `PortfolioContext` or explicit None, mode, full-64 fingerprint, as-of/basis, disclosure flags, selected basename. Read-only source of provenance. | new module | additive |\n| `RunLifecycleCoordinator` | CLI single-run sequencing: select → freeze → disclose/confirm gate → run → check → finalize → persist. Owns consent transitions. No LLM. | new `cli/` module | additive |\n| `OutputChecker` | Deterministic Q1–Q4 evaluation; assigns `output_check` + findings. Authoritative, non-LLM. | new module (non-agent) | additive |\n| `OutcomeFinalizer` | Maps graph return/exceptions to `run_outcome` + `stop_reason`. | new module | additive |\n| `Redactor` | Central masking for secrets across all sinks. | new module | additive |\n| `EventSink` (JSONL) | Structured events with fixed fields. | new module | additive |\n| `ManifestWriter` | Atomic write-once manifest via a **safe metadata projection**. | new module | additive |\n| CLI adapter | Thin `cli/main.py` wiring; adds `--without-portfolio`, `--portfolio-as-of`; suppresses prompts under explicit flags. | `cli/main.py` | adapted |\n| Prompt/context semantics | Mode-aware rating-scale legend and no-portfolio/portfolio-provided wording; no-portfolio Hold meaning. | `tradingagents/agents/context.py`, manager/trader prompts | adapted |\n| Reporting boundary | Header derived from `RunContext` metadata projection; labels for final Rating / RM recommendation / Trader action. | `tradingagents/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/report_html.py` | adapted |\n| Existing loader/model | `PortfolioContext`/`Position` validation and rendering; instrument alias matching. | `tradingagents/portfolio.py` (preserved) | unchanged semantics |\n| Engine API | `TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run/create_run_state` signature preserved. | `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` | signature preserved |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Advisory versus authoritative data\n\n| Data | Nature | Authority |\n|---|---|---|\n| Model narrative, ratings text, recommendations | **Advisory** | Cannot set `output_check`/`run_outcome`/provenance |\n| Final rating (Buy/Overweight/Hold/Underweight/Sell/REVIEW) | Derived deterministically from the PM output | Reported, but check Q1 only *reads* readability |\n| Frozen snapshot metadata (mode, basename, fingerprint, as-of) | **Authoritative** (trusted state) | Built by input service; used by header/result/check |\n| `output_check` (PASSED/NEEDS_REVIEW/NOT_RUN) + findings | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutputChecker` only |\n| `run_outcome` (COMPLETED/INCOMPLETE) + `stop_reason` | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutcomeFinalizer` only |\n\nThe disclaimer and no-portfolio notice are **frozen strings** (selected-requirements §1) and are treated as trusted content, excluded from Q4 phrase scanning.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Workflow (selected C2)\n\n1. **Discover** eligible `.json` files (non-recursive, sorted, symlinks excluded) from `PORTFOLIO_DIR` — or accept explicit `--portfolio PATH` (outside dir allowed; parent not scanned).\n2. **Select** one file, or choose no-portfolio, or cancel.\n3. **Validate/precheck** the frozen bytes; reuse upstream model validation after explicit shape/type/as-of prechecks. Empty positions is valid (flat); no silent fallback.\n4. **Freeze** → `RunContext` (immutable; full-64 fingerprint; as-of/basis recorded).\n5. **Notice** (see §6) then **confirm** (default No). Non-interactive: flags are the consent expression.\n6. **Run**: enter `graph.run` with the frozen snapshot (or None). Holdings reach the provider **only after** confirmation.\n7. **Render**, **Check**, **Finalize**, **Persist**: checked content is the delivered content; provenance from `RunContext` is authoritative.\n8. Pre-run cancellation/rejection starts **no graph, zero LLM calls, no completed run**.\n\nDetailed input-mode state machine and disclosure sequencing: `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` §3–§4.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Permissions and consent\n\n- Interactive discovery/selection/consent lives **only** in the CLI (`cli/`). Agents and the engine never prompt.\n- **Consent gate** is an explicit coordinator transition between freeze and run. A frozen snapshot is a *candidate input*, **not** a confirmed selection; immutability alone does **not** prevent bypass. Only a coordinator transition to `CONFIRMED` permits run entry (see interface-contracts §4, ADR §Consent).\n- Mandatory execution, exception mapping, checks and artifact finalization sit behind a **shared application boundary** usable without terminal prompts. The upstream Python API signature is preserved; see interface-contracts §5 for how project API calls satisfy the requirements and the explicit statement that a bypassing caller does not get claimed compliance.\n- Coding-agent file permissions (separate concern) are in `docs/architecture/permission-model.md`; E implements enforcement.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Observability\n\n- New lifecycle event sink: UTF-8 JSONL; fixed fields `run_id, ticker, node, ts(UTC), elapsed_ms, event, event_outcome`. Console stays human-readable. Raw provider payload logging disabled by default. Progress vocabulary is separate from terminal `run_outcome`.\n- Existing sinks are adapted, not silently trusted: see memory-design §Sinks and runtime-policy-catalog.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Verification strategy (design-level only)\n\n- **Testability seams** (for C): `PortfolioInputService` (discover/validate/freeze), `RunContext` identity, `OutputChecker` (Q1–Q4 with injected model claims), `OutcomeFinalizer` (typed exceptions), redaction at each sink, manifest atomicity, same-date isolation.\n- **Observable positive/negative seams** are listed per requirement in `docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md` for C. B does not write test code or claim results.\n- **Document consistency checks** (this session) are **not** application verification.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Change policy\n\n- ADRs required for safety-affecting changes (`GOV-006`); changes to provenance identity, check authority, redaction boundary or consent transitions require a new/updated ADR.\n- Preserve upstream `tradingagents/`, `cli/`, `pyproject.toml` and tests unless an approved layout decision changes this.\n- Intentional CLI/type-validation changes are documented in the ADR; they are not treated as accidental compatibility failures.\n- Later architecture revisions based on real test evidence must cite that evidence (not manufactured now).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Requirement allocation summary\n\nFull per-ID allocation (enforced-by component, fallback, other-owner/deferred) is in `docs/architecture/invariants.md` and `docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md`. Summary:\n\n- FR-001/002/003/004 → `PortfolioInputService` + `RunContext` + prompt semantics + coordinator consent.\n- FR-005 → reporting stage labels; reuse `tradingagents/agents/rating.py` (REVIEW ≠ Hold).\n- FR-006/FR-007 → provenance projection + `OutputChecker` (authoritative).\n- NFR-001 → `OutcomeFinalizer`; NFR-002 → `EventSink`; NFR-003 → `Redactor`; NFR-004 → `ManifestWriter` + fresh run ID; NFR-005 → shared boundary + preserved API; NFR-006 → completion accounting.\n- GOV-001..006 → allocated to C/E/A/human; B contributes permission model for `GOV-006`.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Provenance and limitations of this draft\n\n- Alternatives and the human selection rationale: `docs/architecture/adr/001-portfolio-aware-cli.md`; scores and weights in `docs/architecture/evaluation-table.md`; process evidence in `docs/architecture/evaluation-logbook.md`.\n- Unresolved decisions and pending evidence are recorded in `docs/architecture/risk-list.md` and the traceability handoff. No approvals, measurements or transcripts are invented here.\n- This file is one of the approved B write set; `docs/architecture/architecture-blueprint.md` is a pointer to it.\n"

      "content": "# ADR 001 — Portfolio-aware CLI: input/service boundary and consent\n\n- Status: **Proposed (architecture draft)**. Selection made by Brian (human) 2026-11-12; awaiting team/instructor reconciliation. Not implementation.\n- Deciders: Brian (selection), Member B (author), pending A (requirements coherence), E (governance/assembly).\n- Scope: `SEL-TA-FR-001..007`, `SEL-TA-NFR-001..006`, `SEL-TA-GOV-006` (permission design contribution).\n- Supersedes: none. Does not modify v2 requirements or the D1 registry (A owns).\n\n> Estimates in this ADR are labelled **ESTIMATE** and are design judgements. No measurement or verification is claimed.\n\n## Context\n\nTradingAgents v0.7.1 already has an optional `--portfolio PATH` that loads a `PortfolioContext` and renders it into decision-agent prompts (`cli/main.py:50-55`, `tradingagents/portfolio.py`, `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py:293-307`). The selected requirements extend this into a discovery + explicit-consent + frozen-provenance + deterministic-check workflow, with distinct `NO_PORTFOLIO`/`PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED` semantics. The course additionally requires a **layered agent context** design, context assembly and compaction constraints, which this ADR records.\n\nConstraints from the current selection (treated as fixed working decisions): CLI-only UI; `PORTFOLIO_DIR=<root>/portfolios`; `--without-portfolio`; `--portfolio-as-of`; consent behaviour; full normalized-content SHA-256 fingerprint; no silent fallback; no invented zero holdings/cash; model cannot assign checks.\n\n## Course-required layered context (design)\n\n| Layer | Content (bounded application context) | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| Identity | Instrument/ticker + resolved identity context | `agents/context.py:build_instrument_context` |\n| Standing constraints | Advisory-only role; no execution; rating vocabulary; disclaimer requirement; \"no account ownership assumed\" | prompts + frozen strings |\n| Knowledge | Analyst reports, research/trader plans, risk debate | graph state |\n| History | Memory-log lessons from prior decisions | `tradingagents/memory/` |\n| State | Input mode, selected basename, as-of/basis, fingerprint (safe projection) | `RunContext` |\n| Current task | The run's instruction to produce a rating + decision | node prompt |\n\n### Context assembly pipeline (application-bound)\n`deduplicate → prioritize (identity/constraints first) → budget (per-agent token cap) → compact (summarize low-priority narrative; never drop mode/snapshot identity/output authority/critical constraints) → assemble (final prompt)`.\n\n- **Token cap (proposed design values, ESTIMATE):** a per-agent assembled-context cap (e.g., conservative bounded window) and a **compaction threshold** below that cap; exact numbers are **proposed design values** pending C/D measurement — they must not be presented as measured. Marked unresolved where measurement is required.\n- **Critical-constraint re-injection:** after any compaction, re-inject identity, mode, snapshot identity (fingerprint/basename/as-of), output authority (check is deterministic) and the frozen disclaimer/notice. Compaction **must not** drop any of these.\n- **Distinction:** this is a **bounded application-context design**. It does not describe or control OpenCode's opaque internal context management. It is **not** an aggregate run-token budget feature (that is deferred).\n\n## Decision\n\nAdopt **C2: an input-service + immutable `RunContext` boundary with a small explicit CLI lifecycle coordinator.**\n\n- `PortfolioInputService`: the sole discoverer/validator/freezer; produces an immutable `RunContext`.\n- `RunContext`: frozen snapshot (or explicit None) + mode + full-64 SHA-256 fingerprint + as-of/basis + disclosure flags + selected basename.\n- `RunLifecycleCoordinator`: CLI single-run sequencing with explicit consent transitions; no LLM; no broad orchestration rewrite; no backtest/resume work.\n- Shared application boundary: execution, exception mapping, deterministic checks and artifact finalization usable without terminal prompts; upstream Python API signature preserved.\n- `OutputChecker` and `OutcomeFinalizer` are the sole assigners of `output_check`/`run_outcome`.\n\n## Alternatives considered (actual, preserved)\n\n- **C1 — Minimal baseline extension.** Inline discovery/validation (sole shared module, thin inline adapter); header lines appended in reporting; small checker; inline manifest. Pros: smallest footprint. Cons: lifecycle sequencing inline; higher risk of provenance drift if reporting re-derives from `final_state` (latent FR-006/007 risk); weakest typed failure behaviour. Score 3.30.\n- **C2 — Input-service + `RunContext` + small coordinator (selected).** Pros: explicit input/snapshot boundary; clean test seams; shared provenance; typed outcomes. Cons: coordinator is CLI-local (callers must go through it). Score 4.65.\n- **C3 — Phased single-run orchestrator façade.** Same service/context, plus a façade over the whole single-run lifecycle. Pros: strong phase testing. Cons: broader `cli/run.py` change; highest coupling/surface; scope-creep risk. Score 3.75.\n\n## Human selection rationale (recorded verbatim in substance)\n\nBrian selected **C2** because of its **explicit input/snapshot boundary, test seams and shared provenance, without C3's broader orchestration change.** This is a **human design choice based on estimated tradeoffs**, explicitly **not** a claim of verified superiority.\n\n## Consequences\n\nPositive: single provenance source; deterministic check authority; consent is an explicit transition; reusable non-interactive boundary; preserved engine API.\nNegative/risks: coordinator locality means a future caller could bypass it (mitigated by making the shared boundary the only sanctioned entry and by documentation; see interface-contracts §5); full-64 fingerprint must be defined canonically; prompt/context wording changes are required (not optional).\n\n## Reopening conditions\n\n- Instructor mandates a single orchestration façade → revisit C3.\n- File-count/scope constraints favour C1 → revisit.\n- Real test evidence (C) shows C1's inline path is cleanly testable with no provenance drift → re-score.\n- Any change to consent semantics, provenance identity or check authority requires a new ADR.\n\n## Related\n\n`../architecture-blueprint.md`; `interface-contracts.md`; `evaluation-table.md`; `evaluation-logbook.md`; `risk-list.md`; `option-ledger.md`.\n",

      "content": "# Interface Contracts (Member B)\n\nStatus: architecture draft. Typed shapes below are **proposed design contracts** for C (test seams) and D (implementation). They are not implemented code. Unknown test IDs / implementation links remain pending. No compliance is claimed for anything not yet built or tested.\n\n## 1. Design types (proposed)\n\n### 1.1 `InputMode`\n```\nInputMode = NO_PORTFOLIO | PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED\n```\n- `NO_PORTFOLIO`: unknown holdings/cash; nothing assumed.\n- `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED`: an explicitly selected, validated, frozen snapshot. An explicitly supplied empty positions list is a **flat** snapshot, not missing input.\n\n### 1.2 `FrozenSnapshot`\n```\nFrozenSnapshot {\n  mode: PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED\n  basename: str                 # selected file basename only (provenance, not truth)\n  portfolio: PortfolioContext   # upstream model (tradingagents/portfolio.py), frozen\n  fingerprint_sha256: str(64)   # full normalized-content SHA-256\n  portfolio_as_of: str          # analysis date D the user confirms the holdings are intended for\n  as_of_basis: \"USER_CONFIRMED\"\n}\n```\n\n### 1.3 `RunContext` (immutable)\n```\nRunContext {\n  run_id: str\n  ticker: str\n  analysis_date: str\n  mode: InputMode\n  snapshot: FrozenSnapshot | None      # None ⇔ NO_PORTFOLIO\n  disclosure_flags: {provider_transmission_preconfirmed: bool, unverified_holdings: bool}\n  consent_state: FROZEN | CONFIRMED    # see §4\n}\n```\n- Immutable by construction. **Frozen ≠ confirmed**: `FROZEN` means the candidate input is validated; only `CONFIRMED` authorizes run entry.\n\n### 1.4 Safe metadata projection (for sinks)\nLogs/manifests **must not** serialize the whole `RunContext` or the portfolio payload. They record an explicit projection:\n```\nSafeRunMetadata {\n  run_id, ticker, analysis_date,\n  input_mode, basename?, fingerprint_sha256?, portfolio_as_of?, as_of_basis?,\n  outcome?, stop_reason?, output_check?, findings[]?,\n  code_version, prompt_hash?, safe_provider_ids{...}, manifest_path?\n}\n```\n`?` = present only when `mode == PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED` (or as applicable). No `positions`, no `cash` values, no other-position list.\n\n## 2. Service and checker interfaces (proposed)\n\n```\nPortfolioInputService:\n  discover() -> list[str]                         # sorted eligible basenames; no symlinks/subdirs\n  validate_precheck(raw_bytes, as_of) -> Ok|InputError   # shape/type/finite/as-of BEFORE model validation\n  freeze(raw_bytes, basename, as_of) -> FrozenSnapshot   # reuse PortfolioContext.model_validate afterwards\n  (sole discoverer/validator; upstream loader schema unchanged)\n\nRunLifecycleCoordinator:\n  begin() -> RunContext\n  transition(ctx, event) -> RunContext            # explicit consent state machine (§4)\n  run(ctx) -> final_state                          # requires consent_state == CONFIRMED\n  check(ctx, final_state, rendered_text) -> CheckResult\n  finalize(final_state | exception) -> RunResult\n  persist(ctx, RunResult, CheckResult) -> SafeRunMetadata  # atomic, redacted, run-ID isolated\n\nOutputChecker.evaluate(trusted_ctx: SafeRunMetadata, final_rating: str, rendered_report_text: str) -> CheckResult\nOutcomeFinalizer.finalize(graph_returned: bool, final_rating: str, exc: Exception|None) -> RunResult\n```\n\n## 3. Input-mode state machine\n\n```\n        START\n          │\n          ▼\n   DISCOVERING ── read-error ──► DIR_ERROR ──retry──► DISCOVERING\n          │                          └──no-portfolio-confirm──► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM\n          │  (eligible list; empty/missing dir → NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM path)\n          ▼\n   SELECTING ──cancel──► CANCELLED (zero graph, zero LLM, no completed run)\n          │ file chosen\n          ▼\n   VALIDATING ──invalid──► INVALID ──reselect──► SELECTING / ──cancel──► CANCELLED\n          │ valid bytes\n          ▼\n   FROZEN (RunContext.consent_state = FROZEN; fingerprint, as-of recorded)\n          │ notice shown (basename, D, unverified/as-of, provider-transmission disclosure)\n          ▼\n   AWAITING_CONSENT ──no/EOF──► CANCELLED (zero graph)\n          │ yes\n          ▼\n   CONFIRMED (RunContext.consent_state = CONFIRMED) ──► RUNNING\n```\n- Interactive prompts exist only in `cli/`. Non-interactive: `--portfolio`/`--without-portfolio` (+ `--portfolio-as-of` for `--portfolio`) are the consent expression; prompts suppressed.\n- Neither/no-flags in non-interactive mode → readable input error, zero graph/LLM calls. Both → input error.\n\n## 4. Consent as explicit lifecycle transitions\n\n| From | Trigger | To | Guard |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| FROZEN | user Yes / explicit valid flag | CONFIRMED | snapshot identity frozen; notice shown first |\n| FROZEN | user No / EOF / cancel | CANCELLED | no run entry |\n| CONFIRMED | (any) | RUNNING | only path to `run()` |\n\n- The coordinator's `run(ctx)` **rejects** a `RunContext` whose `consent_state != CONFIRMED`. Immutability alone does not authorize; the transition does.\n- **No silent reread:** after `FROZEN`, the source file is never reopened; the frozen snapshot is the only input for run/report/manifest. Editing on disk cannot change the run.\n- **Disclosure sequencing:** only the **notice** (basename, analysis date, as-of/unverified statement, and that holdings will be sent to the configured model provider) is shown **before** consent. Holdings are transmitted to the provider **only after** `CONFIRMED` begins the run. There is no provider transmission before consent.\n\n## 5. CLI / API contract changes and how requirements are satisfied\n\n### 5.1 CLI (intentional changes)\n- Added: `--without-portfolio` (explicit no-portfolio consent), `--portfolio-as-of D` (required with `--portfolio` in non-interactive mode, must match analysis date).\n- Preserved: `--portfolio PATH` (explicit path, may be outside `PORTFOLIO_DIR`; parent not scanned).\n- Prompts are suppressed when explicit flags supply consent. Missing/conflicting flags → input error (no default).\n\nThese are **intentional** CLI changes (FR-002). They are **not** accidental compatibility failures; the ADR records them.\n\n### 5.2 Upstream Python API (signature preserved)\n- `TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run/create_run_state(..., portfolio=None|PortfolioContext)` **unchanged** (`trading_graph.py:167,293`).\n- Programmatic callers keep `portfolio=None` without prompting. The coordinator wraps **only** the CLI single-run path.\n- **Compliance statement:** an API call that supplies `portfolio=None` is a valid **NO_PORTFOLIO** run and satisfies FR-004's no-invention semantics. However, a caller that **bypasses** the shared application boundary (no `OutputChecker`/`OutcomeFinalizer`/redaction/manifest) **does not** thereby satisfy FR-006/FR-007/NFR-002/NFR-003/NFR-004; those obligations are enforced at the shared boundary. This architecture **does not** claim compliance for a path that bypasses the required checks. (How to close this gap — e.g., routing API calls through the boundary in a later ADR — is an open decision; see risk-list R-API.)\n\n## 6. Render / check / final-output ordering (provenance authoritative)\n\n```\nrun → final_state\n  → render_report_text(final_state)                      # produce the text to be delivered\n  → CheckResult = OutputChecker.evaluate(\n        trusted_ctx = SafeRunMetadata(from RunContext),   # provenance authoritative\n        final_rating = run_rating(final_state) | REVIEW,\n        rendered_report_text = the SAME text to deliver)  # Q1 readable, Q2 header vs trusted snapshot,\n                                                          # Q3 disclaimer present, Q4 prohibited phrases absent\n  → RunResult = OutcomeFinalizer.finalize(...)\n  → persist(manifest/events/logs/state) using SafeRunMetadata + CheckResult\n  → deliver the EXACT checked rendered text (no re-render after check)\n```\n- **Checked content is the delivered content.** Any transformation after the check (e.g., HTML) must not alter the checked text semantics; HTML escaping is presentation-only and applied to the same checked text.\n- **Header/result/check share the same frozen provenance** from `SafeRunMetadata` derived from `RunContext`.\n- `OutputChecker` inputs: (a) trusted context projection, (b) final rating, (c) rendered report text. It calls no provider.\n\n## 7. Findings and exception mapping (summary)\n\n- `output_check = PASSED | NEEDS_REVIEW | NOT_RUN`; incomplete ⇒ `NOT_RUN`.\n- Q1..Q4 each broken rule ⇒ blocking finding; checker exception ⇒ blocking `CHECK_ERROR` (fail closed).\n- `run_outcome = COMPLETED | INCOMPLETE`; INCOMPLETE `stop_reason ∈ {MODEL_FAILURE, DATA_FAILURE, INTERNAL_ERROR, PERSISTENCE_ERROR, INTERRUPTED}`. Full trigger/fallback table: `runtime-policy-catalog.md`.\n\n## 8. CLI/HTML escaping and provenance values\n- HTML escapes model/file text (`report_html.py:10,226,255`); provenance values (basename/fingerprint) are escaped too.\n- Header uses the safe projection, not the full payload.\n",

Lifecycle states\n\n| State | Meaning | Persisted? | LLM calls |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Pre-run cancellation/rejection | Discovered/cancelled/invalid input before consent, or consent declined | **No completed run**; no artifact; counted separately (NFR-006) | Zero |\n| Fresh started run | A new invocation after consent; gets a unique `run_id` | Transient during run; final artifacts after finalization | Yes |\n| Transient run state | In-memory graph state, message buffer, intermediate chunks | In-memory (plus existing log files) | — |\n| Immutable final artifacts | Final report (MD/HTML), manifest, terminal event | **Yes, write-once** | — |\n| User-supplied portfolio data | Frozen snapshot from selected file | Held in `RunContext`; **not** written whole to new sinks | — |\n| Provider transmission | Holdings sent to configured model provider | Intentionally disclosed pre-consent as a notice; actual transmission **after** consent | Yes (during run) |\n| Retention/privacy | What persists locally and what is redacted | Per §4 | — |\n\nA fresh invocation always creates a fresh `run_id` (no resume in this selection).\n\n## 2. It is the authoritative provenance for report/result/manifest/check.\n- **Transient graph state** (`tradingagents/graph/propagation.py`, `agents/state.py`) carries rendered `portfolio_context` (string) to the decision agents — upstream behaviour preserved. The rendered string is derived once at run start (`trading_graph.py:293-307`).\n- **User-supplied portfolio data** is read **once**, validated, frozen; the file is never re-read after freeze (interface-contracts §4).\n\n## 3. Write/retrieval policy\n- Each fresh run writes into its **own run-ID-isolated** location. Same-ticker/same-date runs must not overwrite a prior run's artifacts (INV-12); the legacy date-keyed state log (`full_states_log_{trade_date}.json`, `trading_graph.py:472`) is addressed in §5.\n- The manifest is written **atomically once** after artifact/check finalization, from the `SafeRunMetadata` projection — never the full `RunContext`/payload.\n- Retrieval for reads (e.g., console \"where is my report\") uses redacted paths; no secrets.\n- Resume: **deferred**. A final record is never mutated to simulate a resume.\n\n## 4. Retention and privacy\n- New sinks retain only the `SafeRunMetadata` projection (no positions, cash values, other-position lists).\n- Portfolio source files are kept **read-only**; their bytes are not copied into manifests/transcripts.\n- Secret values never persisted; redaction boundary at every sink (§5).\n- The intentionally disclosed provider transmission is not represented as local-only processing.\n\n## 5. `stop_reason ∈ {MODEL_FAILURE, DATA_FAILURE, INTERNAL_ERROR, PERSISTENCE_ERROR, INTERRUPTED}`.\n- `output_check = PASSED | NEEDS_REVIEW | NOT_RUN`; incomplete ⇒ NOT_RUN.\n- Progress vocabulary (events) is separate from terminal `run_outcome`.\n\n| # | Trigger | Responsible component | Fallback / action | Output | Diagnostic / monitor |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| R1 | Recoverable non-core data unavailable (upstream sentinel) | Engine/tools (baseline behaviour preserved) | Continue run with the sentinel/absent marker; **do not** classify fatal | COMPLETED (or normal) | Event notes degraded node; **not** an incomplete reason |\n| R2 | Structured-output invocation fails, free text usable | `structured.py` path → PM text fallback | Use free-text; parse rating deterministically | COMPLETED; rating if readable else REVIEW | Existing structured-fallback warning retained |\n| R3 | Model/provider output exhausted | `OutcomeFinalizer` | Stop; no final rating | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=MODEL_FAILURE` | `event=run.terminal`; redacted cause |\n| R4 | Raised vendor/data exception (unrecovered) | `OutcomeFinalizer` | Stop; typed result | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=DATA_FAILURE` | Redacted data exception message |\n| R5 | Ordinary internal exception | `OutcomeFinalizer` | Stop; typed result, no escape past public entry | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=INTERNAL_ERROR` | Redacted traceback summary |\n| R6 | Malformed/invalid portfolio input | `PortfolioInputService` (precheck + upstream model) | Stop **before dispatch**; filename + bad field/path, no contents/credentials | No run (pre-run rejection) | Input diagnostic; zero LLM calls |\n| R7 | As-of mismatch (`--portfolio-as-of` ≠ analysis date) | `PortfolioInputService` | Stop before dispatch | Pre-run input error | Field-level diagnostic |\n| R8 | Selected file changed after confirmation | (no reread) | **Ignore** changed bytes; use frozen snapshot | Normal run with frozen identity | (no silent change; provenance records frozen digest) |\n| R9 | Output check rule broken (Q1–Q4) | `OutputChecker` | Do not pass; mark review needed | If graph returned: COMPLETED + NEEDS_REVIEW + blocking finding(s) | `event=output.check` findings |\n| R10 | Checker raises exception | `OutputChecker` (fail closed) | Blocking `CHECK_ERROR` | COMPLETED retained if graph returned, but NEEDS_REVIEW | `event=output.check` `CHECK_ERROR` |\n| R11 | Model text claims \"OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" but a rule fails | `OutputChecker` authority | Model claim ignored | NEEDS_REVIEW | Authority-source tag on check event |\n| R12 | Cooperative cancellation | `RunLifecycleCoordinator` | Stop cooperatively (if during run) or zero-start (pre-run) | Pre-run: no completed run; during run: INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=INTERRUPTED` | `event=input.consent`/`run.terminal` |\n| R13 | Persistence/commit failure (manifest/report) | `ManifestWriter` / persist boundary | Keep available partial artifacts; return redacted persistence diagnostic | INCOMPLETE, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR` | Redacted persistence diagnostic; no secret/path leakage |\n| R14 | Event sink write failure | `EventSink` | Continue run where safe; surface redacted diagnostic | Normal outcome + persistence note, unless persistence itself is the failing terminal step | Redacted diagnostic |\n| R15 | Workflow returns unreadable final text | `OutcomeFinalizer` + `OutputChecker` | Complete with REVIEW | COMPLETED + rating REVIEW + NEEDS_REVIEW | Q1 finding |\n| R16 | Same-ticker/date second fresh run | `ManifestWriter` / coordinator (run-ID isolation) | Write to a **new** run dir; refuse overwrite of prior artifacts | New isolated artifacts; first run unchanged | `event=output.persist` |\n\n## Ordering and conditions\n- Every incomplete result has `output_check=NOT_RUN`; every completed result has a rating (REVIEW allowed) and a check result.\n- `MODEL_FAILURE` is used **only** for exhausted model/provider output failures; recoverable optional-data setnals (R1) are never reclassified as fatal.\n- Diagnostics are redacted (NFR-003) before delivery; secrets/holdings never appear.\n- Durability across total disk failure/power loss is **not** promised; PERSISTENCE_ERROR is the cooperative failure contract.\n",

Stage 3 drafts complete. Document-consistency review done.

## Files written (13, architecture drafts only)
- `architecture-blueprint.md` (canonical)
- `docs/architecture/architecture-blueprint.md` (pointer only)
- `docs/architecture/adr/001-portfolio-aware-cli.md`

- `docs/architecture/permission-model.md`
- `docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md`

- `docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md`
- `docs/architecture/risk-list.md`
- `docs/architecture/option-ledger.md`
- `docs/architecture/evaluation-logbook.md`

No code, tests, requirements, or governance files touched.

## Corrections applied
1. **DQ1–DQ10 matrix**: full C1/C2/C3 columns with per-cell rationale (`evaluation-table.md` §2). Six-criterion score matrix with rationale + uncertainty per candidate (§3). Scenario (b) internal exact fractions and totals 3.156/4.800/4.000 (§5).
2. **Disclosure contradiction removed**: only the notice precedes consent; holdings transmit after `CONFIRMED` (interface-contracts §4, memory-design, blueprint §5).
3. **Sink handling table** (`memory-design.md` §5): decision, location, run-ID isolation, overwrite prevention (incl. legacy date-keyed `full_states_log_{date}.json` replacement), permitted content, redaction, raw-payload suppression, failure handling, responsible component. `SafeRunMetadata` projection used — **not** full `RunContext`.
4. **OutputChecker ordering** (`interface-contracts.md` §6): trusted-context projection + final rating + rendered text; render→check→finalize→persist; checked content is delivered content; provenance authoritative.
5. **Shared boundary** (interface-contracts §5): interactive selection/consent in CLI only; mandatory checks/exception mapping/finalization behind prompt-free boundary; upstream API signature preserved; explicit no-compliance for bypassing paths (tracked R-API).
6. **Consent transitions** (interface-contracts §4, INV-09): FROZEN ≠ CONFIRMED; explicit coordinator transition authorizes run; immutability alone does not prevent bypass.
- ADR preserves C1/C2/C3 alternatives and your verbatim rationale; estimates labelled; test IDs/impl links pending; no invented approvals/measurements/transcripts.
- Consistency review: all 19 `SEL-TA-*` IDs allocated; all cross-file links resolve; fixed one typo.

## Unresolved / pending (honest)
- **R-API**: project API callers can bypass the shared boundary — requirements not claimed satisfied on those paths; fix needs a later D ADR.
- **R-CANON**: full-64 canonical normalization to be finalized in interface-contracts at implementation.
- **R-GOV**: governance still not installed.
- GOV-001..005 owned by C/E/A; semantic rubric/threshold (GOV-004) unset.

**STOP for your review.** These remain architecture drafts; implementation is not authorized.

This architecture **does not** claim compliance for a path that bypasses the required checks. (How to close this gap — e.g., routing API calls through the boundary in a later ADR — is an open decision; see risk-list R-API.)\n\n## 6. Render / check / final-output ordering (provenance authoritative)\n\n```\nrun → final_state\n  → render_report_text(final_state)                      # produce the text to be delivered\n  → CheckResult = OutputChecker.evaluate(\n        trusted_ctx = SafeRunMetadata(from RunContext),   # provenance authoritative\n        final_rating = run_rating(final_state) | REVIEW,\n        rendered_report_text = the SAME text to deliver)  # Q1 readable, Q2 header vs trusted snapshot,\n                                                          # Q3 disclaimer present, Q4 prohibited phrases absent\n  → RunResult = OutcomeFinalizer.finalize(...)\n  → persist(manifest/events/logs/state) using SafeRunMetadata + CheckResult\n  → deliver the EXACT checked rendered text (no re-render after check)\n```\n- **Checked content is the delivered content.** Any transformation after the check (e.g., HTML) must not alter the checked text semantics; HTML escaping is presentation-only and applied to the same checked text.\n- **Header/result/check share the same frozen provenance** from `SafeRunMetadata` derived from `RunContext`.\n- `OutputChecker` inputs: (a) trusted context projection, (b) final rating, (c) rendered report text. It calls no provider.\n\n## 7. Findings and exception mapping (summary)\n\n- `output_check = PASSED | NEEDS_REVIEW | NOT_RUN`; incomplete ⇒ `NOT_RUN`.\n- Q1..Q4 each broken rule ⇒ blocking finding; checker exception ⇒ blocking `CHECK_ERROR` (fail closed).\n- `run_outcome = COMPLETED | INCOMPLETE`; INCOMPLETE `stop_reason ∈ {MODEL_FAILURE, DATA_FAILURE, INTERNAL_ERROR, PERSISTENCE_ERROR, INTERRUPTED}`. Full trigger/fallback table: `runtime-policy-catalog.md`.\n\n## 8. CLI/HTML escaping and provenance values\n- HTML escapes model/file text (`report_html.py:10,226,255`); provenance values (basename/fingerprint) are escaped too.\n- Header uses the safe projection, not the full payload.",

Input-mode state machine (addresses B3-08; both modes complete)\n\nInteractive discovery/consent lives only in `cli/input_ui.py`. The **noninteractive service** (`input_service.py`) accepts explicit inputs/paths.\n\n```\nSTART\n ├─ explicit --portfolio PATH ─────────────► VALIDATING_EXPLICIT\n ├─ explicit --without-portfolio ──────────► NO_PORTFOLIO_FREEZE\n └─ interactive, no explicit flags ────────► DISCOVERING\nDISCOVERING\n ├─ eligible files present ──► SELECTING ──cancel──► CANCELLED\n ├─ missing or empty dir ────► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM   (never described as \"empty\" if errored)\n └─ directory read error ────► DIR_ERROR ──retry──► DISCOVERING\n                              └──choose no-portfolio──► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM\n                              └──cancel──► CANCELLED\nSELECTING ──file chosen──► VALIDATING\nVALIDATING ──invalid──► INVALID ──reselect──► SELECTING / ──cancel──► CANCELLED\nVALIDATING_EXPLICIT ──(noninteractive: --portfolio-as-of D required, D == analysis date)──►\n   ──valid──► PORTFOLIO_FREEZE   ──invalid/as-of-mismatch/flags-conflict──► INPUT_ERROR (zero run)\nVALIDATING ──valid──► PORTFOLIO_FREEZE\nPORTFOLIO_FREEZE  (freeze bytes → FrozenSnapshot; ──no/EOF──► CANCELLED\nCONFIRMED ──► RUNNING\nCANCELLED / INPUT_ERROR → zero graph, zero LLM, no completed run\n```\n\n- **Both modes** reach a frozen candidate and explicit confirmation (interactive) or explicit flag consent (noninteractive).\n- **Noninteractive flag rules:** neither `--portfolio` nor `--without-portfolio` ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR` (zero calls); immutability ≠ bypass prevention)\n| From | Trigger | To | Guard |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `FROZEN` (PORTFOLIO_FREEZE/NO_PORTFOLIO_FREEZE) | interactive Yes, or valid explicit flag | `CONFIRMED` | notice for portfolio shown first (interactive) |\n| `FROZEN` | interactive No/EOF/cancel | `CANCELLED` | zero run |\n| `CONFIRMED` | (any) | `RUNNING` | **only** path to `execution.run` |\n\n`execution.run_analysis_api` **rejects** a `RunContext` whose `consent_state != CONFIRMED`. A frozen snapshot existing does **not** authorize execution; the transition does.\n\n- **No silent reread:** after freeze the file is never reopened; frozen bytes are the sole input.\n- **Disclosure sequencing:** only the **notice** precedes consent; holdings are transmitted to the provider **only after** `CONFIRMED` (during `RUNNING`). No provider transmission before consent.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Shared CLI/API execution boundary (addresses B3-01, B3-10)\n\nThe **common application entry service** routes **every supported entry point** through the mandatory checks/finalization/persistence:\n\n```\n# tradingagents/runapi/execution.py  (prompt-free; no cli import)\nrun_analysis_api(\n    run_context: RunContext,          # consent_state must be CONFIRMED\n    graph_factory: Callable[..., Engine],  # injectable for tests; default TradingAgentsGraph\n    event_sink: EventSink,\n    redactor: Redactor,\n) -> RunResult\nsequence: validate_consent → engine.stream_run(portfolio or None)\n          → render_body → check → finalize → stage → publish → terminal event\n```\n\n### 5.1 Entry points and which boundary they traverse\n| Entry point | Interaction | Boundary traversal | Requirement coverage |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| CLI interactive (`cli/main.py`) | prompts in `cli/input_ui.py` | freezes+confirm → `run_analysis_api` | Full (FR/NFR) |\n| CLI noninteractive (flags) | none | flags → freeze → `run_analysis_api` | Full |\n| **Supported project API** (`tradingagents.runapi.execution.run_analysis_api`) | none | supplies a `RunContext` (built via input service or explicit `portfolio`/`None`) → `run_analysis_api` | Full |\n| Low-level engine primitive (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run`) | none | **raw**; **does not** traverse the boundary | **Reduced** — see §5.3 |\n\n### 5.2 Supported project API signature\nThe upstream engine signature is **preserved** (`trading_graph.py:167,293`: `portfolio=None|PortfolioContext`). A programmatic caller wanting the full contract uses:\n```\nfrom tradingagents.runapi.execution import run_analysis_api\nfrom tradingagents.runapi.input_service import freeze_explicit  # builds RunContext from bytes/portfolio\nctx = freeze_explicit(ticker, analysis_date, portfolio=PortfolioContext(...) | None)  # no prompt\nresult: RunResult = run_analysis_api(ctx.confirm(), event_sink=..., redactor=...)\n```\n- `freeze_explicit(..., portfolio=None)` ⇒ `NO_PORTFOLIO` RunContext. `portfolio=PortfolioContext(...)` ⇒ frozen snapshot (fingerprint computed) with `consent_state=CONFIRMED` when the caller is an approved programmatic caller (explicit input is the consent expression; **no** provider transmission before the call).\n- This path runs checks/finalization/redaction/manifest — no compliance gap (B3-01 closed).\n\n### 5.3 Low-level primitive (precise scope; A approval required for reduced coverage)\n`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run/create_run_state` remain available unchanged for baseline compatibility and upstream tests. That is implementation, not an architecture decision.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Render / check / final envelope ordering (addresses B3-04)\n\n**Problem fixed:** the check must run on content that does *not* yet contain its own result, yet the delivered header must display the check result. Resolution: separate the **immutable checked body** from the **trusted final envelope**.\n\n### 6.1 Two-part document\n- **Body** (untrusted, model-generated sections + trusted frozen notice/disclaimer strings): rendered once from `final_state` + `RunContext`, **redacted before check**.\n- **Envelope header** (trusted, deterministic): analysis date, input mode, basename, full-64 fingerprint, as-of/basis, version/models/analysts, `run_outcome`, `output_check` + finding summary, disclaimer. Built from `SafeRunMetadata`, **not** model text.\n\n### 6.2 Ordering\n```\n1. run → final_state\n2. body = render_body(final_state, RunContext)          # trusted strings inserted\n3. body = redactor.scrub(body)                          # redaction BEFORE any check\n4. partial_meta = SafeInputMetadata(from RunContext)     # outcome not yet known\n5. preliminary_check = OutputChecker.evaluate(\n       trusted_ctx = partial_meta, final_rating, body)   # Q1 body, Q2 header identity vs snapshot,\n                                                          # Q3 disclaimer in body, Q4 body phrases (disclaimer excluded)\n6. result = OutcomeFinalizer.finalize(graph_returned, final_rating, exc)   # run_outcome/stop_reason\n7. final_check = OutputChecker.evaluate(trusted_ctx=partial_meta, final_rating, body)  # idempotent; authoritative\n   → CheckResult (may be NEEDS_REVIEW/NOT_RUN)\n8. envelope = build_envelope(partial_meta, result, final_check)   # inserts outcome+check into TRUSTED header\n9. final_doc_md = envelope + body\n10. final_doc_html = render_html(envelope, body)         # presentation-only escaping of the SAME checked body\n11. stage → publish (§7)\n```\n- **Q1–Q4 inspect the body** (and Q2 checks the trusted header identity against the snapshot). They never inspect their own result field.\n- Decision-independent steps 5 and 7 produce the same body-level result; the checker is deterministic, so the authoritative `CheckResult` is well-defined before the envelope is built.\n- **The checked body is delivered unchanged.** The envelope adds only trusted metadata; it does not alter model text.\n- **Markdown/HTML equivalence:** HTML renders the **same** body + the **same** envelope values with escaping only; no content change.\n- **Redaction precedes checks** so a checked artifact cannot later be invalidated by redaction.\n\n### 6.3 Walkthroughs (synthetic; document examples)\n- **PASSED (completed, no-portfolio):** body redacted; Q1 rating readable, Q2 header mode=`NO_PORTFOLIO` with null file/fingerprint/as-of, Q3 disclaimer present, Q4 clean → `CheckResult{PASSED, []}`; `RunResult{COMPLETED, stop_reason=null, final_rating=\"Hold\", output_check=PASSED}`. Envelope shows `input_mode=NO_PORTFOLIO`, fingerprint `null`, outcome COMPLETED, check PASSED + \"no findings\".\n- **NEEDS_REVIEW (completed, Q4 broken):** body contains \"guaranteed profit\" (outside disclaimer) → `Finding{Q4,BLOCKING}`; `CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[Q4]}`; `RunResult{COMPLETED, rating specified, output_check=NEEDS_REVIEW}`. Envelope shows NEEDS_REVIEW + finding summary.\n- **CHECK_ERROR:** checker raises → `CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[CHECK_ERROR]}`; graph returned so outcome stays `COMPLETED`; `RunResult` `output_check=NEEDS_REVIEW`.\n- **INCOMPLETE:** graph/exception finalized → `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `final_rating=null`, `stop_reason` set; **no body is published as a successful report**; partial artifacts labelled INCOMPLETE (§7).\n- **Final header provenance:** every envelope field derives from `SafeRunMetadata`↔`RunContext`; none from `final_state` model text.\n\n### 6.4 OutputChecker inputs (explicit)\n`OutputChecker.evaluate(trusted_ctx: SafeInputMetadata, final_rating: str|null, rendered_body: str)`; calls no provider. Q1 = final rating readable; Q2 = header identity equals trusted snapshot metadata; Q3 = disclaimer present; Q4 = prohibited phrases absent (case-insensitive) in body, disclaimer excluded.\n\n### 6.5 Rendering order for agents (identity vs display)\nCanonicalization sorts positions for hashing; `PortfolioContext.render()` keeps upstream ordering for the prompt. Identity and display are intentionally separate; neither mutates the frozen tuple.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Staging, persistence, publication and terminal-event ordering (addresses B3-05)\n\n### 7.1 Sink criticality\n| Sink | Criticality | Rule |\n|---|---|---|\n| Report (MD, and HTML if enabled) | **Critical** | Must stage successfully before publication |\n| Manifest | **Critical** | Atomic write-once; commit gates publication success |\n| State JSON / message log | Best-effort | Failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip a completed decision to persistence failure **unless** it is the only artifact the run promises (it is not) |\n| JSONL events | Best-effort | Terminal event logical decision always emitted to result; durability qualified (§7.4) |\n\n### 7.2 Ordering\n```\nfinalize → write artifacts to STAGING run dir (not visible as success)\n        → atomic publish (rename staging → per-run output location)\n        → write manifest last (atomic, write-once)\n        → emit terminal event\n        → return RunResult\n```\n- **No successful report is exposed before critical persistence succeeds.** Staging is written under a non-public temp path; publication is an atomic rename; the manifest is written after report publication and before returning success.\n- **One failure mapping:** a critical staging/commit failure ⇒ `run_outcome=INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `manifest_path=null`, `report_path=null` (or partial path if a labelled partial was intentionally retained). The returned `RunResult` and any retained artifact agree; no earlier COMPLETED/PASSED is returned.\n- **Partial artifacts:** if the graph completed but persistence failed, retained partials are written with an explicit INCOMPLETE label; they are not presented as a successful report.\n\n### 7.3 Reconciliation with earlier finalization\n`OutcomeFinalizer` produces the **logical** outcome before persistence; if persistence is critical and fails, the **logical outcome is revised** to INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR for the **returned result and terminal event**, satisfying INV-08 (INCOMPLETE ⇒ no rating, NOT_RUN). A COMPLETED rating is therefore never returned alongside a persistence failure.\n\n### 7.4 Terminal-event guarantee (qualified)\n- Exactly **one logical** `run.terminal` decision per run; its content is also carried in `RunResult`.\n- If the JSONL sink write fails, the run may still return its (redacted) logical result; manifest records `terminal_event_durable=false`. This preserves a single logical terminal decision while honestly qualifying durability.\n- Full-disk/power-loss durability is **out of scope**; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.\n\n### 7.5 Failure simulations (design; document examples)\n- **Report staging fails:** nothing published; `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, no manifest, `report_path=null`.\n- **State-log write fails:** best-effort note; report+manifest still published; outcome unchanged (COMPLETED/…).\n- **Manifest commit fails:** report staged but **not published**; `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no manifest/report path returned.\n- **Terminal-event write fails:** logical result returned; `terminal_event_durable=false`; report/manifest may be published (critical path succeeded).\n\n---\n\n## 8. CLI / API contract changes (intentional)\n- Added: `--without-portfolio`; `--portfolio-as-of D`. Preserved: `--portfolio PATH` (may be outside `PORTFOLIO_DIR`; parent not scanned).\n- Prompts suppressed under explicit flags; conflicts ⇒ `InputError` (no default). Intentional CLI changes (FR-002) recorded in ADR; not accidental compatibility failures.\n\n## 9. Escaping and provenance values\n- HTML escapes all model/file and provenance values (`report_html.py:10,226,255`); envelope values escaped too. Header uses `SafeInputMetadata`, never the payload.\n\n## 10. Pending (external owners)\nFinal D1/schema (A); C's test IDs, rubric/threshold, and independent evidence; E enforcement; instructor layout. A must approve any reliance on the reduced-coverage low-level primitive (§5.3).\n",

      "newString": "### Context assembly pipeline (application-bound)\n`deduplicate → prioritize (identity/constraints first) → budget (per-agent token cap) → compact (summarize low-priority narrative; never drop mode/snapshot identity/output authority/critical constraints) → assemble (final prompt)`.\n\n#### Operational budget and compaction design (B3-07; proposed, unmeasured)\nAll numbers are **proposed design values (ESTIMATE)**, not measured. C/D later verify/measure.\n\n- **Estimator:** token counts approximated by `ceil(len(prompt_chars)/4)` as a cheap, provider-agnostic estimator (documented approximation; no tokenizer dependency added). A provider tokenizer may refine this later without changing the contract.\n- **Per-agent context cap** `C_cap = 24,000` estimated tokens (proposed). This bounds the **assembled prompt context** for a single agent (knowledge + history + state + task), not an aggregate run budget.\n- **Critical reserve** `R_crit = 4,000` estimated tokens reserved for identity + standing constraints + state/authority + frozen notice/disclaimer; `R_crit` is never compacted.\n- **Compaction threshold** `T_compact = round(0.8 · C_cap) = 20,000`. When estimated context exceeds `T_compact`, apply compaction; hard stop at `C_cap`.\n- **Compaction method:** summarize/trim **low-priority narrative layers only** (older debate history, redundant analyst prose) to fit within `T_compact`; deterministic truncation with an explicit \"(compacted)\" marker is the baseline; if a summarizing **model call** is used it is an **explicitly disclosed extra provider call**, counted and logged as `event=context.compact` — it is not silent network behaviour. The selection does **not** require a summarizing model; default design = deterministic truncation.\n- **Protected-context overflow:** if `R_crit` alone exceeds `C_cap`, **fail closed** at assembly (typed `INTERNAL_ERROR` with a redacted note) rather than dropping critical constraints; never exceed `C_cap` by silently dropping identity/authority.\n- **Re-injection:** after compaction, re-inject identity, mode, snapshot identity (fingerprint/basename/as-of), output authority (deterministic check) and the frozen disclaimer/notice.\n- **Where it belongs:** node-prompt assembly in the agent context layer (`tradingagents/agents/context.py` + prompt builders); **not** OpenCode's internal context.\n- **Temporal guards:** memory/context retrieval keeps upstream as-of/time guards; compaction must not reintroduce out-of-window history.\n- **Illustrative over-cap (document example):** assembled context estimates 26,000 tokens. With `T_compact=20,000`, older bull/bear debate prose (~6,500 tokens) is truncated to ~500 with a \"(compacted)\" marker; identity/constraints/state/notice (~3,200) and current task survive untouched; final ≈ 20,200 ≤ `C_cap`. If `R_crit` were 25,000, assembly fails closed.\n- **Distinction:** this is a **bounded application-context design**. It does not describe/control OpenCode's opaque internal context management. It is **not** an aggregate run-token/time/call budget (deferred).\n\n## Decision\n\nAdopt **C2: an input-service + deeply immutable `RunContext` boundary with a small explicit CLI lifecycle coordinator and a shared execution service.**\n\n- `PortfolioInputService` (`tradingagents/runapi/input_service.py`): the sole discoverer/validator/freezer; produces a `RunContext`.\n- `RunContext`/`FrozenSnapshot` (`runapi/context.py`): deeply immutable value tuples + mode + full-64 canonical SHA-256 + as-of/basis + consent_state; read-only provenance source.\n- **Shared execution service** (`runapi/execution.py: run_analysis_api`): the **common application entry** for CLI and supported project API; rejects non-`CONFIRMED` contexts; owns execution, exception mapping, checks, finalize, staging/publish and terminal event. Usable without terminal prompts.\n- `RunLifecycleCoordinator` (CLI layer): interactive selection/consent transitions; no LLM; no broad orchestration rewrite; no backtest/resume work.\n- `OutputChecker` and `OutcomeFinalizer` are the sole assigners of `output_check`/`run_outcome`.\n- Upstream engine signature preserved; the raw primitive is a declared reduced-coverage path whose product reliance requires A's approval (R-API).\n\n## Alternatives considered (actual, preserved)\n\n- **C1 — Minimal baseline extension.** Inline discovery/validation (sole shared module, thin inline adapter); header lines appended in reporting; small checker; inline manifest. Pros: smallest footprint. Cons: lifecycle sequencing inline; higher risk of provenance drift if reporting re-derives from `final_state` (latent FR-006/007 risk); weakest typed failure behaviour. Score 3.30.\n- **C2 — Input-service + `RunContext` + small coordinator + shared execution service (selected).** Pros: explicit input/snapshot boundary; clean test seams; shared provenance; typed outcomes; full-coverage API path. Cons: more modules than C1. Score 4.65.\n- **C3 — Phased single-run orchestrator façade.** Same service/context, plus a façade over the whole single-run lifecycle. Pros: strong phase testing. Cons: broader `cli/run.py` change; highest coupling/surface; scope-creep risk. Score 3.75.",

Retention, retrieval and privacy (B3-09)\n\n- **Transient snapshot lifetime:** the frozen snapshot value tuples live only in `RunContext` for the duration of the process/run; they are **never written** to durable sinks and are released on process exit. No durable copy of holdings is created by this extension.\n- **Durable retention:** by default, artifacts persist under the run's isolated results directory **until the user deletes them**. This selection does **not** introduce automatic deletion or a cross-run catalogue (deferred). **Deletion owner:** the end user (application role); E/ops may define a later retention policy but must not silently delete user artifacts.\n- **Retrieval policy:** reads for provenance/console use the redacted `SafeInputMetadata`/`SafeRunMetadata`; the portfolio source file is not re-read after freeze; no full payload is retrieved from manifests/logs.\n- **Redaction ≠ suppression:** masking secrets (NFR-003) is **distinct** from suppressing raw holdings/prompt dumps. Both are required: raw portfolio bytes, full `RunContext`, raw provider prompts/payloads are **not persisted** in new sinks regardless of redaction.\n- **Provider retention:** holdings **transmitted to the provider after consent** are subject to the **provider's own retention/logging policy, outside application control**; the notice states this is intentional provider transmission. Retention, retrieval and privacy (B3-09)\n \n+- **Transient snapshot lifetime:** the frozen snapshot value tuples live only in `RunContext` for the duration of the process/run; they are **never written** to durable sinks and are released on process exit. No durable copy of holdings is created by this extension.\n+- **Durable retention:** by default, artifacts persist under the run's isolated results directory **until the user deletes them**. This selection does **not** introduce automatic deletion or a cross-run catalogue (deferred). **Deletion owner:** the end user (application role); E/ops may define a later retention policy but must not silently delete user artifacts.\n+- **Retrieval policy:** reads for provenance/console use the redacted `SafeInputMetadata`/`SafeRunMetadata`; the portfolio source file is not re-read after freeze; no full payload is retrieved from manifests/logs.\n+- **Redaction ≠ suppression:** masking secrets (NFR-003) is **distinct** from suppressing raw holdings/prompt dumps. Both are required: raw portfolio bytes, full `RunContext`, raw provider prompts/payloads are **not persisted** in new sinks regardless of redaction.\n+- **Provider retention:** holdings **transmitted to the provider after consent** are subject to the **provider's own retention/logging policy, outside application control**; the notice states this is intentional provider transmission. The application is not represented as local-only.\n+- **Secrets:** never persisted; redaction boundary at every sink (§5).\n+- **Source files:** portfolio source files are kept **read-only**; their bytes are not copied into manifests/transcripts.\n+\n ## 5. Defined interface (owner component: evaluation data model, proposed `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` `RunRecord`; aggregation is a reporting concern for C/D):\n\n```\nRunRecord (one per attempt; persisted only in evaluation datasets, NOT in the run manifest)\n  attempt_id: str\n  category: \"STARTED\" | \"PRE_RUN_REJECTED\" | \"PRE_RUN_CANCELLED\"\n  run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\" | null   # null for pre-run categories\n  output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\" | null\n  stop_reason: ... | null\n  controlled_change: {factor: str, value: str} | null   # for before/after experiments\n```\nAggregation (design):\n- `completion_fraction = STARTED/COMPLETED` ÷ `STARTED` total (pre-run categories excluded from denominator but reported).\n- Report `completed_count`, `needs_review_count`, `incomplete_reason_counts`, `pre_run_rejected`, `pre_run_cancelled`.\n- `completed_count == 0` ⇒ **insufficient evidence** (never a passing quality result).\n- A pre-run attempt records **no** `run_outcome`, creates **no** completed artifact, and is never counted as a started run.\n- Controlled before/after experiments carry `controlled_change` and are labelled as changed-factor comparisons; repeated fixed-condition benchmarks require matching controls. Cons: more modules than C1. Score 4.65.\n60:- **C3 — Phased single-run orchestrator façade.** Same service/context, plus a façade over the whole single-run lifecycle. Pros: strong phase testing. |---|---|---|---|

| **B3-02** | `interface-contracts.md` §3 (3.1–3.10) | Separate schemas for `InputError`, `Finding`, `CheckResult`, `RunResult`, `SafeInputMetadata`, `SafeRunMetadata`, `EffectiveConfig`, `Event`, `Manifest`; selected field names (`run_outcome`, `final_rating`, start/end, required `code_version`/`prompt_hash`); null vs absence and completed/incomplete conditional fields specified; no payload; synthetic completed/no-portfolio and incomplete/portfolio examples | Resolved |
| **B3-03** | `interface-contracts.md` §2.2, §2.3; `invariants.md` INV-05/INV-05b; `risk-list.md` R-CANON | Exact canonical bytes (encoding, key order, separators, null==absent, numeric normalization, list sort, symbol spelling, exclusions) + algorithm; deep immutability via value tuples + defensive `PortfolioContext` copies; upstream 12-char checkpoint fingerprint preserved; reorder/`1`vs`1.0`/nested-mutation examples stated | Resolved |
| **B3-04** | `interface-contracts.md` §6 | Split immutable checked **body** vs trusted **envelope header**; ordering render→scrub→check(body)→finalize→build-envelope→stage/publish; checked body delivered unchanged; MD/HTML equivalence; walkthroughs PASSED/NEEDS_REVIEW/CHECK_ERROR/INCOMPLETE | Resolved |
| **B3-05** | `interface-contracts.md` §7; `memory-design.md` §5; `runtime-policy-catalog.md` R13a/R13b/R14; `invariants.md` INV-08/INV-14 | Sink criticality; staging→atomic publish→manifest→terminal-event; one failure mapping per path; no success exposed before critical persistence; logical outcome revised to INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR; terminal-event durability qualified; four failure simulations | Resolved |
| **B3-06** | `permission-model.md` §2–§5 | Separate A/B/C/D/E profiles with explicit read/write/deny, deny precedence, human-only paths, phase approvals; D does **not** auto-get test-write; extra-authorization recording for rotation; cross-role secret/symlink policy; permitted/denied examples | Resolved |
| **B3-07** | `adr/001` Operational budget/compaction | Concrete estimator, `C_cap=24k`, `R_crit=4k`, `T_compact=20k`, compaction method (deterministic default; summarizing model call disclosed), protected-overflow fail-closed, re-injection, location, temporal guards, over-cap walkthrough — all labelled unmeasured | Resolved |

| **B3-09** | `memory-design.md` §4–§5 | Transient lifetime, durable retention/deletion owner, retrieval policy, redaction ≠ raw-suppression, provider retention out of app control; sink table criticality/failure aligned | Resolved |
| **B3-10** | `interface-contracts.md` §1; `architecture-blueprint.md` component table; `runtime-policy-catalog.md` | Concrete `tradingagents/runapi/*` + `cli/input_ui.py` paths, ownership, dependency rule (`runapi` must not import `cli`) | Resolved |

Exact rules:\n\n1. **Normalized object** contains exactly: `{\"cash\":…,\"currency\":…,\"positions\":[{\"ticker\":…,\"quantity\":…,\"average_price\":…}, …]}`. No other keys participate.\n2. **Key order:** lexicographic ascending at every object level (`sort_keys=True`).\n3. **Encoding:** UTF-8, **no BOM**, **no trailing newline**; bytes are `json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(\",\", \":\"), ensure_ascii=False).encode(\"utf-8\")`.\n4. **Separators:** `,` and `:` with **no whitespace** (`separators=(\",\", \":\")`).\n5. **String escaping:** JSON string escaping only (`ensure_ascii=False`, so non-ASCII tickers are emitted as UTF-8, not `\\uXXXX`); no additional escaping. Tickers are trimmed and uppercased before serialization.\n6. **Null/default handling:** an absent optional field and an explicit JSON `null` are the **same** and are serialized as the JSON token `null` (`average_price`, `cash`, `currency`).\n7. **Number-token serialization (exact):** every numeric field is first converted by `to_canonical_number(x)`:\n   - reject non-finite (`NaN`/`±Inf`) at validation (never reach canonicalization);\n   - normalize `-0.0` to `0.0`;\n   - if the value is integral and `|x| < 2**53`, emit the **integer token** (e.g., `10`, `1`, `0`), so `1` and `1.0` → token `1`;\n   - otherwise emit Python `float.__repr__` (shortest round-trippable decimal, e.g., `150.5`, `0.1`).\n   This defines the exact byte token; it is not \"whatever JSON does\".\n8. **Positions sort — total order (no `None`/float comparison):** sort the canonical **row objects** by the composite key `(ticker_upper, to_canonical_number(quantity), price_key)` where `price_key = (0, 0.0)` when `average_price is None` and `(1, to_canonical_number(average_price))` otherwise (a tagged tuple: null sorts **before** any number; numeric compares numerically). Because `ticker_upper` is a string and is part of the key, **two different broker spellings that normalize to the same symbol but differ in spelling sort by their hashed spelling**, and a full-row tie is impossible unless all three hashed fields are equal (identical rows are interchangeable, so input order cannot change the digest). This is a **total order over every field that participates in the digest**, so reordering input never changes the digest and no valid portfolio is rejected by sorting.\n9. **Symbol spelling:** `ticker` is hashed using the **original spelling** as supplied (trimmed, uppercased). Holdings keep their spelling (`portfolio.py:40-68`); alias matching is a runtime concern, not identity. Reindexing the **spelling** (e.g., `BRK.B`→`BRK-B` on the other row) is a **different** portfolio by rule 9 and yields a different digest.\n- **Reason C — numeric `1` vs `1.0`:**\n  - `[(\"MSFT\",1,50)]` cash `1` and `[(\"MSFT\",1.0,50.0)]` cash `1.0` both serialize to\n    `{\"cash\":1,\"currency\":null,\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":50,\"quantity\":1,\"ticker\":\"MSFT\"}]}` → **equal digest**.\n- **Reason D — missing vs explicit null:** a position with absent `average_price` and one with explicit `null` serialize identically (`\"average_price\":null`) → **equal digest**.\n- **Reason E — full example with cash:** `[(\"AAPL\",10,150.5),(\"MSFT\",5,None)]`, cash `2500.0`, currency `\"USD\"` →\n  `{\"cash\":2500,\"currency\":\"USD\",\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":150.5,\"quantity\":10,\"ticker\":\"AAPL\"},{\"average_price\":null,\"quantity\":5,\"ticker\":\"MSFT\"}]}`\n  → SHA-256 `45f07d9eb3359b059525da0cee26f8a9810269dad11ffb4c42e1dcc7072cef72`.\n- **Expected difference:** changing `quantity` from `10` to `10.5`, adding a position, or altering cash/currency changes the digest.\n\nThese are **document examples** checked against the written rules, not passing application tests.",

      "oldString": "### 3.3 `CheckResult`\n```\nCheckResult {\n  output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\"\n  findings: Finding[]           # empty ⇔ PASSED\n}\n```\nRules: no findings ⇒ `PASSED`. Any broken Q-rule ⇒ `NEEDS_REVIEW` + that blocking finding. Checker exception ⇒ `NEEDS_REVIEW` + one `CHECK_ERROR` finding. Incomplete run ⇒ `NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`.\n\n### 3.4 `RunResult` (returned to caller)\n```\nRunResult {\n  run_id: str\n  ticker: str\n  analysis_date: str\n  input_mode: InputMode\n  run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\"\n  stop_reason: null | \"MODEL_FAILURE\" | \"DATA_FAILURE\" | \"INTERNAL_ERROR\"\n               | \"PERSISTENCE_ERROR\" | \"INTERRUPTED\"\n  final_rating: null | \"Buy\" | \"Overweight\" | \"Hold\" | \"Underweight\" | \"Sell\" | \"REVIEW\"\n  output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\"\n  findings: Finding[]\n  manifest_path: str | null     # present iff critical publication committed\n  report_path: str | null       # present iff report published\n}\n```\n**Conditional fields (enforced by finalizer):**\n- `COMPLETED` ⇒ `final_rating != null` and `stop_reason == null`.\n- `INCOMPLETE` ⇒ `final_rating == null`, `output_check == \"NOT_RUN\"`, `stop_reason != null`.\n\n### 3.5 Safe input metadata projection (for sinks; never the payload)\n```\nSafeInputMetadata {\n  run_id, ticker, analysis_date,\n  input_mode: InputMode,\n  basename: str | null,                 # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n  fingerprint_sha256: str | null,       # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO (64 hex)\n  portfolio_as_of: str | null,          # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n  as_of_basis: \"USER_CONFIRMED\" | null  # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n}\n```\nThe `null` conditions are **portfolio-only** (mode-dependent); they are distinct from **outcome-conditional** fields in `RunResult` (B3-02 conflation fixed).\n\n### 3.6 `SafeRunMetadata` (event/log/state projection; never the payload)\n```\nSafeRunMetadata = SafeInputMetadata + {\n  run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\",\n  stop_reason: ... | null,             # outcome-conditional as §3.4\n  output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\",\n  findings: Finding[],\n  code_version: str,                    # required: tradingagents.__version__ (+ optional git describe if available)\n  prompt_hash: str,                     # required: see §3.8\n  effective_config: EffectiveConfig,    # required: safe allowlist, §3.7\n  start_ts_utc: str, end_ts_utc: str    # ISO-8601 UTC\n}\n```\n\n### 3.7 `EffectiveConfig` (safe allowlist; secrets/endpoints omitted)\n```\nEffectiveConfig {\n  llm_provider: str | null,\n  deep_think_provider: str | null, deep_think_llm: str | null,\n  quick_think_provider: str | null, quick_think_llm: str | null,\n  analysts: str[],\n  max_debate_rounds: int, max_risk_discuss_rounds: int,\n  output_language: str,\n  data_vendors: map, tool_vendors: map\n}\n```\nDerived from the existing `TradingAgentsGraph.run_settings()` allowlist (`trading_graph.py:255-275`), which already excludes endpoints/keys/paths. `backend_url`, API keys, OAuth tokens, local paths are **never** included.\n\n### 3.8 `prompt_hash`\n`prompt_hash = SHA-256` of the UTF-8 canonical text of the **effective application prompt set** actually used for the run (identity/context instructions + selected analyst/trader/manager prompt templates + frozen strings), keys sorted, `\\n`-normalized. Minimum viable for this selection: hash of the concatenated prompt templates resolved for the chosen analysts/asset type. A prompt edit changes the hash. (Exact serialization finalized with D; recorded here so D does not invent it.)\n\n### 3.9 `Event` (JSONL)\n```\nEvent {\n  run_id, ticker,\n  node: \"input\" | \"engine\" | \"output\",\n  ts: str (UTC ISO-8601),\n  elapsed_ms: int (>=0, monotonic),\n  event: str,                 # e.g. input.selection, input.consent, run.terminal, output.check, output.persist\n  event_outcome: str          # progress vocabulary, separate from run_outcome\n}\n```\nExactly one `event=run.terminal` logical decision per run (§7.4).\n\n### 3.10 Final manifest (`manifest.json`, atomic, write-once)\n```\nManifest = SafeRunMetadata + {\n  schema_version: \"1\",\n  report_paths: { markdown: str, html: str | null },\n  terminal_event_logical: \"run.terminal\",\n  terminal_event_durable: bool          # false when event sink failed (§7.4)\n}\n```\nWritten **once**, atomically, **after** critical artifacts are staged and the check/outcome are final. Contains **no** positions/cash/other-position list and no secrets.\n\n---"
