Envelope shows `input_mode=NO_PORTFOLIO`, fingerprint `null`, outcome COMPLETED, check PASSED + \"no findings\".\n- **NEEDS_REVIEW (completed, Q4 broken):** body contains \"guaranteed profit\" (outside disclaimer) → `Finding{Q4,BLOCKING}`; `CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[Q4]}`; `RunResult{COMPLETED, rating specified, output_check=NEEDS_REVIEW}`. Envelope shows NEEDS_REVIEW + finding summary.\n- **CHECK_ERROR:** checker raises → `CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[CHECK_ERROR]}`; graph returned so outcome stays `COMPLETED`; `RunResult` `output_check=NEEDS_REVIEW`.\n- **INCOMPLETE:** graph/exception finalized → `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `final_rating=null`, `stop_reason` set; **no body is published as a successful report**; partial artifacts labelled INCOMPLETE (§7).\n- **Final header provenance:** every envelope field derives from `SafeRunMetadata`↔`RunContext`; none from `final_state` model text.\n\n### 6.4 OutputChecker inputs (explicit)\n`OutputChecker.evaluate(trusted_ctx: SafeInputMetadata, final_rating: str|null, rendered_body: str)`; calls no provider. Q1 = final rating readable; Q2 = header identity equals trusted snapshot metadata; Q3 = disclaimer present; Q4 = prohibited phrases absent (case-insensitive) in body, disclaimer excluded.\n\n### 6.5 Rendering order for agents (identity vs display)\nCanonicalization sorts positions for hashing; `PortfolioContext.render()` keeps upstream ordering for the prompt. Identity and display are intentionally separate; neither mutates the frozen tuple.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Staging, persistence, publication and terminal-event ordering (addresses B3-05)\n\n### 7.1 Sink criticality\n| Sink | Criticality | Rule |\n|---|---|---|\n| Report (MD, and HTML if enabled) | **Critical** | Must stage successfully before publication |\n| Manifest | **Critical** | Atomic write-once; commit gates publication success |\n| State JSON / message log | Best-effort | Failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip a completed decision to persistence failure **unless** it is the only artifact the run promises (it is not) |\n| JSONL events | Best-effort | Terminal event logical decision always emitted to result; durability qualified (§7.4) |\n\n### 7.2 Ordering\n```\nfinalize → write artifacts to STAGING run dir (not visible as success)\n        → atomic publish (rename staging → per-run output location)\n        → write manifest last (atomic, write-once)\n        → emit terminal event\n        → return RunResult\n```\n- **No successful report is exposed before critical persistence succeeds.** Staging is written under a non-public temp path; publication is an atomic rename; the manifest is written after report publication and before returning success.\n- **One failure mapping:** a critical staging/commit failure ⇒ `run_outcome=INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `manifest_path=null`, `report_path=null` (or partial path if a labelled partial was intentionally retained). The returned `RunResult` and any retained artifact agree; no earlier COMPLETED/PASSED is returned.\n- **Partial artifacts:** if the graph completed but persistence failed, retained partials are written with an explicit INCOMPLETE label; they are not presented as a successful report.\n\n### 7.3 Reconciliation with earlier finalization\n`OutcomeFinalizer` produces the **logical** outcome before persistence; if persistence is critical and fails, the **logical outcome is revised** to INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR for the **returned result and terminal event**, satisfying INV-08 (INCOMPLETE ⇒ no rating, NOT_RUN). A COMPLETED rating is therefore never returned alongside a persistence failure.\n\n### 7.4 Terminal-event guarantee (qualified)\n- Exactly **one logical** `run.terminal` decision per run; its content is also carried in `RunResult`.\n- If the JSONL sink write fails, the run may still return its (redacted) logical result; manifest records `terminal_event_durable=false`. This preserves a single logical terminal decision while honestly qualifying durability.\n- Full-disk/power-loss durability is **out of scope**; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.\n\n### 7.5 Failure simulations (design; document examples)\n- **Report staging fails:** nothing published; `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, no manifest, `report_path=null`.\n- **State-log write fails:** best-effort note; report+manifest still published; outcome unchanged (COMPLETED/…).\n- **Manifest commit fails:** report staged but **not published**; `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no manifest/report path returned.\n- **Terminal-event write fails:** logical result returned; `terminal_event_durable=false`; report/manifest may be published (critical path succeeded).\n\n---\n\n## 8. CLI / API contract changes (intentional)\n- Added: `--without-portfolio`; `--portfolio-as-of D`. Preserved: `--portfolio PATH` (may be outside `PORTFOLIO_DIR`; parent not scanned).\n- Prompts suppressed under explicit flags; conflicts ⇒ `InputError` (no default). Intentional CLI changes (FR-002) recorded in ADR; not accidental compatibility failures.\n\n## 9. Escaping and provenance values\n- HTML escapes all model/file/provenance values (`report_html.py:10,226,255`); envelope values escaped too. Header uses `SafeInputMetadata`, never the payload.\n\n## 10. Evaluation population interface (addresses B3-11)\n\nNFR-006 requires completion accounting over **started fresh runs**, with pre-run cancellations counted separately and **zero-completed ⇒ insufficient evidence**. Defined interface (owner component: evaluation data model, proposed `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` `RunRecord`; aggregation is a reporting concern for C/D):\n\n```\nRunRecord (one per attempt; persisted only in evaluation datasets, NOT in the run manifest)\n  attempt_id: str\n  category: \"STARTED\" | \"PRE_RUN_REJECTED\" | \"PRE_RUN_CANCELLED\"\n  run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\" | null   # null for pre-run categories\n  output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\" | null\n  stop_reason: ... | null",

Staging, single publication commit, and terminal-event ordering (addresses F1)\n\n### 7.1 Single publication commit point\nThe run directory is the unit of atomic publication on the same filesystem:\n```\nSTAGING dir: <results>/_staging/<run_id>/         # not visible as a successful run\n  reports/complete_report.md  (and .html if enabled)   # final envelope + checked body\n  manifest.json                                        # fully populated incl. terminal_event.durable\nCOMMIT:  os.replace/rename  <results>/_staging/<run_id>  ->  <results>/<ticker>/<run_id>/\n```\n- **One commit point.** Everything the manifest describes (report MD/HTML, manifest itself) is written into the **staging** directory **first**; the **only** publication action is a single atomic directory rename. Before the rename, nothing exists at the published path; after it, a complete, self-consistent run directory exists.\n- **No success is visible before the commit.** There is no earlier `rename` of the report into the published location; the \"report staged but unpublished\" state is real because the report lives only under `_staging`.\n- **Terminal event ordering (truthful durability):** the **logical** terminal decision is computed before commit. The **JSONL terminal event is appended to the staging `events.jsonl` before the commit**, so its success/failure is **known before** the manifest is finalized. `terminal_event.durable = (jsonl terminal append succeeded)`. A later event append is **not** part of the immutable manifest's claim; best-effort events written after commit are separate and cannot change `manifest.json`.\n- **Reader behaviour:** a run directory is a valid published run iff it exists at `<results>/<ticker>/<run_id>/` (the rename completed). `_staging/**` is never treated as a published run. Readers may ignore `_staging`.\n\n### 7.2 Sink criticality\n| Sink | Criticality | Rule (with single-commit) |\n|---|---|---|\n| Report MD (and HTML if enabled) | **Critical** | Written to staging; part of the commit unit |\n| Manifest | **Critical** | Written to staging with final `terminal_event.durable`; part of the commit unit |\n| JSONL terminal event | **Critical for the `durable` flag** | Appended to staging **before** commit; its outcome sets `terminal_event.durable` |\n| Other JSONL progress events | Best-effort | May be appended pre- or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; never changes the immutable manifest |\n| State JSON / message log | Best-effort | Written to staging or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip a completed decision |\n\n### 7.3 Failure mapping (one per path)\n- **Critical staging write fails** (report or manifest or terminal-event-to-staging) **before commit:** no rename performed; nothing appears at the published path; result `INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`. Staging dir is cleaned or left under `_staging` (not published).\n- **Commit rename fails:** same as above — nothing published; typed `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.\n- **Best-effort sink fails (progress event / state log / message log):** the commit still proceeds; outcome is unchanged (`COMPLETED`/…); a redacted note is recorded; `terminal_event.durable` reflects the **terminal** append only.\n- **Logical outcome revision:** `OutcomeFinalizer` produces the logical outcome; only a **critical staging/commit** failure (before any publication) revises the returned result to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`. Since nothing is published before commit, no published PASSED/COMPLETED can contradict the returned result.\n- **Full-disk/power-loss durability:** out of scope; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.\n\n### 7.4 Reconciliation with earlier finalization\n`OutcomeFinalizer` sends the logical outcome and `terminal_event.durable` into the staging manifest **before** commit. If critical persistence fails, the **returned** result is revised to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` (satisfying INV-08); nothing was published, so there is no stale success artifact.\n\n### 7.5 Chronological failure walkthroughs (document examples; states verified against §7.1–§7.4)\nLegend: `VISIBLE` = present at published path; `STAGED` = under `_staging` only.\n\n- **(a) Report staging write fails:** after staging the manifest is attempted? **No** — report write fails first → abort; no manifest, no commit. `STAGED`: partial report maybe; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, rating null, NOT_RUN, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`.\n- **(b) Manifest staging write fails:** report written to staging; manifest write fails → abort before commit; `STAGED`: report; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. No published COMPLETED exists.\n- **(c) Final publication (rename) fails:** staging complete (report+manifest+terminal event); rename fails → `STAGED`: full run; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. Reader sees no published run.\n- **(d) Best-effort JSONL progress write fails (after terminal already staged):** commit proceeds; `VISIBLE`: full run with `manifest.terminal_event.durable=true` (terminal append succeeded); returned `COMPLETED/…`; a redacted note about the dropped progress event. Immutable manifest unchanged by the dropped progress event.\n- **(e) Terminal-event append to staging fails:** `terminal_event.durable=false` recorded in the staging manifest; commit still publishes the run directory (report+manifest valid); returned outcome is the logical outcome (COMPLETED if graph returned); a redacted note. The manifest truthfully states the terminal event is **not durable**; no later append alters it.\n\nNo walkthrough publishes a report that contradicts the returned terminal result.",
      "oldString": "## 7. Staging, persistence, publication and terminal-event ordering (addresses B3-05)\n\n### 7.1 Sink criticality\n| Sink | Criticality | Rule |\n|---|---|---|\n| Report (MD, and HTML if enabled) | **Critical** | Must stage successfully before publication |\n| Manifest | **Critical** | Atomic write-once; commit gates publication success |\n| State JSON / message log | Best-effort | Failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip a completed decision to persistence failure **unless** it is the only artifact the run promises (it is not) |\n| JSONL events | Best-effort | Terminal event logical decision always emitted to result; durability qualified (§7.4) |\n\n### 7.2 Ordering\n```\nfinalize → write artifacts to STAGING run dir (not visible as success)\n        → atomic publish (rename staging → per-run output location)\n        → write manifest last (atomic, write-once)\n        → emit terminal event\n        → return RunResult\n```\n- **No successful report is exposed before critical persistence succeeds.** Staging is written under a non-public temp path; publication is an atomic rename; the manifest is written after report publication and before returning success.\n- **One failure mapping:** a critical staging/commit failure ⇒ `run_outcome=INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `manifest_path=null`, `report_path=null` (or partial path if a labelled partial was intentionally retained). The returned `RunResult` and any retained artifact agree; no earlier COMPLETED/PASSED is returned.\n- **Partial artifacts:** if the graph completed but persistence failed, retained partials are written with an explicit INCOMPLETE label; they are not presented as a successful report.\n\n### 7.3 Reconciliation with earlier finalization\n`OutcomeFinalizer` produces the **logical** outcome before persistence; if persistence is critical and fails, the **logical outcome is revised** to INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR for the **returned result and terminal event**, satisfying INV-08 (INCOMPLETE ⇒ no rating, NOT_RUN). A COMPLETED rating is therefore never returned alongside a persistence failure.\n\n### 7.4 Terminal-event guarantee (qualified)\n- Exactly **one logical** `run.terminal` decision per run; its content is also carried in `RunResult`.\n- If the JSONL sink write fails, the run may still return its (redacted) logical result; manifest records `terminal_event_durable=false`. This preserves a single logical terminal decision while honestly qualifying durability.\n- Full-disk/power-loss durability is **out of scope**; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.\n\n### 7.5 Failure simulations (design; document examples)\n- **Report staging fails:** nothing published; `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, no manifest, `report_path=null`.\n- **State-log write fails:** best-effort note; report+manifest still published; outcome unchanged (COMPLETED/…).\n- **Manifest commit fails:** report staged but **not published**; `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no manifest/report path returned.\n- **Terminal-event write fails:** logical result returned; `terminal_event_durable=false`; report/manifest may be published (critical path succeeded)."

The **JSONL terminal event is appended to the staging `events.jsonl` before the commit**, so its success/failure is **known before** the manifest is finalized. `terminal_event.durable = (jsonl terminal append succeeded)`. A later event append is **not** part of the immutable manifest's claim; best-effort events written after commit are separate and cannot change `manifest.json`.\n+- **Reader behaviour:** a run directory is a valid published run iff it exists at `<results>/<ticker>/<run_id>/` (the rename completed). `_staging/**` is never treated as a published run. A COMPLETED rating is therefore never returned alongside a persistence failure.\n+### 7.2 Sink criticality\n+| Sink | Criticality | Rule (with single-commit) |\n+|---|---|---|\n+| Report MD (and HTML if enabled) | **Critical** | Written to staging; part of the commit unit |\n+| Manifest | **Critical** | Written to staging with final `terminal_event.durable`; part of the commit unit |\n+| JSONL terminal event | **Critical for the `durable` flag** | Appended to staging **before** commit; its outcome sets `terminal_event.durable` |\n+| Other JSONL progress events | Best-effort | May be appended pre- or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; never changes the immutable manifest |\n+| State JSON / message log | Best-effort | Written to staging or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip a completed decision |\n \n-### 7.4 Terminal-event guarantee (qualified)\n-- Exactly **one logical** `run.terminal` decision per run; its content is also carried in `RunResult`.\n-- If the JSONL sink write fails, the run may still return its (redacted) logical result; manifest records `terminal_event_durable=false`. This preserves a single logical terminal decision while honestly qualifying durability.\n-- Full-disk/power-loss durability is **out of scope**; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.\n+### 7.3 Failure mapping (one per path)\n+- **Critical staging write fails** (report or manifest or terminal-event-to-staging) **before commit:** no rename performed; nothing appears at the published path; result `INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`. Staging dir is cleaned or left under `_staging` (not published).\n+- **Commit rename fails:** same as above — nothing published; typed `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.\n+- **Best-effort sink fails (progress event / state log / message log):** the commit still proceeds; outcome is unchanged (`COMPLETED`/…); a redacted note is recorded; `terminal_event.durable` reflects the **terminal** append only.\n+- **Logical outcome revision:** `OutcomeFinalizer` produces the logical outcome; only a **critical staging/commit** failure (before any publication) revises the returned result to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`. Since nothing is published before commit, no published PASSED/COMPLETED can contradict the returned result.\n+- **Full-disk/power-loss durability:** out of scope; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.\n \n-### 7.5 Failure simulations (design; document examples)\n-- **Report staging fails:** nothing published; `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, no manifest, `report_path=null`.\n-- **State-log write fails:** best-effort note; report+manifest still published; outcome unchanged (COMPLETED/…).\n-- **Manifest commit fails:** report staged but **not published**; `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no manifest/report path returned.\n-- **Terminal-event write fails:** logical result returned; `terminal_event_durable=false`; report/manifest may be published (critical path succeeded).\n+### 7.4 Reconciliation with earlier finalization\n+`OutcomeFinalizer` sends the logical outcome and `terminal_event.durable` into the staging manifest **before** commit. If critical persistence fails, the **returned** result is revised to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` (satisfying INV-08); nothing was published, so there is no stale success artifact.\n \n+### 7.5 Chronological failure walkthroughs (document examples; states verified against §7.1–§7.4)\n+Legend: `VISIBLE` = present at published path; `STAGED` = under `_staging` only.\n+\n+- **(a) Report staging write fails:** after staging the manifest is attempted? **No** — report write fails first → abort; no manifest, no commit. `STAGED`: partial report maybe; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, rating null, NOT_RUN, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`.\n+- **(b) Manifest staging write fails:** report written to staging; manifest write fails → abort before commit; `STAGED`: report; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. No published COMPLETED exists.\n+- **(c) Final publication (rename) fails:** staging complete (report+manifest+terminal event); rename fails → `STAGED`: full run; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. Reader sees no published run.\n+- **(d) Best-effort JSONL progress write fails (after terminal already staged):** commit proceeds; `VISIBLE`: full run with `manifest.terminal_event.durable=true` (terminal append succeeded); returned `COMPLETED/…`; a redacted note about the dropped progress event. Immutable manifest unchanged by the dropped progress event.\n+- **(e) Terminal-event append to staging fails:** `terminal_event.durable=false` recorded in the staging manifest; commit still publishes the run directory (report+manifest valid); returned outcome is the logical outcome (COMPLETED if graph returned); a redacted note. The manifest truthfully states the terminal event is **not durable**; no later append alters it.\n+\n+No walkthrough publishes a report that contradicts the returned terminal result.\n+\n ---\n \n ## 8.         "text": "|---|---|---|---|\n| CLI interactive (`cli/main.py`) | prompts in `cli/input_ui.py` | freezes+confirm → `run_analysis_api` | Full (FR/NFR) |\n| CLI noninteractive (flags) | none | flags → freeze → `run_analysis_api` | Full |\n| **Supported project API** (`tradingagents.runapi.execution.run_analysis_api`) | none | supplies a `RunContext` (built via input service or explicit `portfolio`/`None`) → `run_analysis_api` | Full |\n| Low-level engine primitive (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run`) | none | **raw**; **does not** traverse the boundary | **Reduced** — see §5.3 |\n\n### 5.2 Supported project API signature\nThe upstream engine signature is **preserved** (`trading_graph.py:167,293`: `portfolio=None|PortfolioContext`). A programmatic caller wanting the full contract uses:\n```\nfrom tradingagents.runapi.execution import run_analysis_api\nfrom tradingagents.runapi.input_service import freeze_explicit  # builds RunContext from bytes/portfolio\nctx = freeze_explicit(ticker, analysis_date, portfolio=PortfolioContext(...) | None)  # no prompt\nresult: RunResult = run_analysis_api(ctx.confirm(), event_sink=..., redactor=...)\n```\n- `freeze_explicit(..., portfolio=None)` ⇒ `NO_PORTFOLIO` RunContext. `portfolio=PortfolioContext(...)` ⇒ frozen snapshot (fingerprint computed) with `consent_state=CONFIRMED` when the caller is an approved programmatic caller (explicit input is the consent expression; **no** provider transmission before the call).\n- This path runs checks/finalization/redaction/manifest — no compliance gap (B3-01 closed).\n\n### 5.3 Low-level primitive (precise scope; A approval required for reduced coverage)\n`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run/create_run_state` remain available unchanged for baseline compatibility and upstream tests. They **do not** provide `OutputChecker`, `OutcomeFinalizer`, redaction, manifest or events. Scope and honesty:\n- Use is legitimate for baseline/existing upstream behaviour and for engine-level tests.\n- A caller using **only** the raw primitive **does not** satisfy FR-006/FR-007/NFR-002/003/004. This is not a *silent* demotion: it is a **declared, scoped low-level compatibility path**, and **A must approve** any excluded requirement coverage if a product-facing path relies on it. Residual risk tracked as **R-API** (open pending A approval); it is no longer \"deferred to D to design\" — the design exists here; only A's acceptance of the reduced-coverage primitive is pending.\n- Recommended (not required for this selection): D may later add a thin `run_analysis_api` wrapper used by `cli/run.py` to make the primitive internal. That is implementation, not an architecture decision.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Render / check / final envelope ordering (addresses B3-04)\n\n**Problem fixed:** the check must run on content that does *not* yet contain its own result, yet the delivered header must display the check result. Resolution: separate the **immutable checked body** from the **trusted final envelope**.\n\n### 6.1 Two-part document",

these paths are **readable by all A/B/C/D/E** (still subject to the secret denies above):\n```\nAGENTS.md, Prompt.md, architecture-blueprint.md, docs/architecture/**, docs/project-deliverables-and-ownership.md\n```\nThis makes the startup reading order runnable under default-deny without opening secret paths.\n\n### 2.2 Role write/extra-read profiles\n| Role (owner) | Writable (in-role) | Extra reads (beyond common) | Explicitly denied writable | Phase approval |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **A — Requirements** | `docs/req/**` | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `tests/**` | everything else writable (arch/code/tests/governance) | A publishes final D1 |\n| **B — Architecture** | approved B set: root `architecture-blueprint.md`, `docs/architecture/adr/**`, the 13 approved architecture files | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `tests/**`, `docs/req/**` | `docs/req/**`, `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `tests/**`, `pyproject.toml`, `AGENTS.md`, `Prompt.md`, `Report.md`, `.github/**`, `.agent/**`, `.opencode/**`, **`docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md` (E-owned)**, review docs, transcripts | approved write plan |\n| **C — Verification** | `tests/**`, `docs/verification/**`, `docs/review-memo.md`, `docs/bug-diary.md`, `docs/debt-register.md` | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `docs/req/**` | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `docs/req/**`, architecture (read only), governance/CI, transcripts | test-plan approval (GOV-001) before impl |\n| **D — Implementation** | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `prompts/**`, `docs/experiments/**` | `tests/**` (read), `docs/req/**` | **`tests/**` writes (does NOT auto-receive test-write)**, `docs/req/**`, architecture (read only), governance/CI, `.opencode/rules.md`, transcripts | C's approved tests; E's gates |\n| **E — Governance** | `AGENTS.md`, `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` (not `rules.md`), `.github/**`, `docs/code-governance/**`, **`docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md` (E-owned)**, `docs/ai-use-log.yaml`, `transcripts/index.md`, `README.md`, `Report.md` (final edit), `docs/submission/**`, `submission/**` | everything (read), subject to secret denies | `tradingagents/**`, `cli/**`, `tests/**`, `docs/req/**`, the 13 B-owned architecture files (**B-owned; E collects, does not edit**), `prompts/**` | human-authorized |\n\n**Trace-matrix authority (F5):** E is the **sole writer** of `docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md`; it is **removed from B's writable deny set only in E's column** and is **not** in B's writable set. To reconcile deny precedence, the file has exactly one owning role (E) with an explicit write allow; no other role (including B) has a writable allow for it, and any broad deny applied to `docs/architecture/**` for other roles simply keeps it unwritable for them. E's broad read is enumerated by the common startup set (§2.1) plus the role's own/governance paths — not a vague \"everything\".\n\n**Covenant/verification ownership:** `docs/code-governance/verification-constraints.md` → owner **C** (write); `.agent/rules.md` → owner **E**; `docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md` → owner **E**. Every required governance/covenant file has one authorized writer; none defaults to nobody.\n\n**Critical rule (B3-06):** D running the coding agent does **not** automatically receive write authority over `tests/**`. Test writes by D require an **explicit, recorded extra authorization** (E-recorded, human-approved exception with rationale), preserving C's independent-verification separation. The same recording applies if roles rotate.\n\n## 3. Application-run data policy (separate from coding agents)\n\n- `PORTFOLIO_DIR` defaults to `<project-root>/portfolios`; discovery **non-recursive**, regular `.json`, deterministic filename order, **symlinks excluded**. Do not search home/credentials/arbitrary folders.\n- Explicit `--portfolio PATH` may point outside `PORTFOLIO_DIR`; parent not scanned.\n- Selected file read **once**, frozen; not re-read after freeze; source read-only.\n- Secrets never emitted; central `Redactor` masks keys/OAuth access+refresh tokens/bearer [REDACTED]\n\n## 4. Enforcement (E) and denied-write behaviour (GOV-006)\n\n- E wires per-role whitelists into `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` and CI. A denied access attempt must be **blocked and logged without changing the file**. B specifies; E implements and demonstrates. This draft does **not** claim a demonstrated denial.\n- Branch protection requires passing checks + human review + ADR for safety changes. B's ADRs are the architecture contribution.\n\n## 5. Permitted/denied examples (document examples) — F5\n- **Startup reads:** A/B/C/D/E can all read `AGENTS.md`, `Prompt.md`, `architecture-blueprint.md`, `docs/architecture/**` → permitted.\n- **E writes `docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md`** → permitted (E sole owner); **B writes it** → denied.\n- **D writes `tests/test_output_check.py`** → **denied** (D lacks test-write) unless an E-recorded extra authorization exists.\n- **C writes `tests/...`** → permitted (C owns tests).\n- **Any agent edits `.opencode/rules.md`** → **denied** (human-only).\n- **Any agent reads `.env` or a real portfolio file** → denied.",

Do not search home/credentials/arbitrary folders.\n- Explicit `--portfolio PATH` may point outside `PORTFOLIO_DIR`; parent not scanned.\n- Selected file read **once**, frozen; not re-read after freeze; source read-only.\n- Secrets never emitted; central `Redactor` masks keys/OAuth access+refresh tokens/bearer [REDACTED]\n\n## 4. Enforcement (E) and denied-write behaviour (GOV-006)\n\n- E wires per-role whitelists into `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` and CI. A denied access attempt must be **blocked and logged without changing the file**. B specifies; E implements and demonstrates. This draft does **not** claim a demonstrated denial.\n- Branch protection requires passing checks + human review + ADR for safety changes. B's ADRs are the architecture contribution.\n\n## 5. Permitted/denied examples (document examples)\n- **D writes `tests/test_output_check.py`** → **denied** (D lacks test-write) unless an E-recorded extra authorization exists.\n- **C writes `tests/...`** → permitted (C owns tests).\n- **Any agent edits `.opencode/rules.md`** → **denied** (human-only).\n- **B edits `docs/architecture/invariants.md`** → permitted; **B edits `docs/req/...`** → denied.\n- **Any agent reads `.env` or a real portfolio file** → denied."

Holdings reach the provider **only after** confirmation.\n-7. **Render body → scrub → check (Q1–Q4 on body) → finalize → build trusted envelope → stage → atomic publish → write-once manifest → terminal event.** The checked body is delivered unchanged; the envelope adds only trusted metadata (§ see interface-contracts §6–§7).\n+7. **Render body → scrub → single check (Q1–Q4; Q2 inspects the pre-check provenance fragment) → finalize → build trusted envelope → stage report+manifest+terminal-event → one atomic directory commit.** Incomplete runs bypass the checker and get `NOT_RUN`. The checked body is delivered unchanged; the envelope adds only trusted metadata. Terminal-event durability is decided before the manifest is staged. (§ interface-contracts §6–§7).\n 8. Pre-run cancellation/rejection starts **no graph, zero LLM calls, no completed run**; a critical persistence failure yields a typed INCOMPLETE result that never contradicts a returned success.\n \n Detailed state machine, schemas, canonicalization, ordering and failure simulations: `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md`.\n \n",

One subtle inconsistency: §6.1 says envelope "must byte-match the pre-check provenance fragment for its Q2 fields," and §6.5 Q2-defect says the renderer bug emits `basename="c.json"` in `provenance_fragment`. If the defect is in the fragment rendering, the fragment equals trusted check would *fail* at Q2 (correct). But then the envelope is built from `SafeRunMetadata` (trusted b.json) and the guard compares envelope vs fragment → mismatch. This is coherent: Q2 catches the fragment defect, guard catches divergence. Good.

But §6.5 says "publication guard also catches envelope/trusted mismatch" — actually Q2 already caught it and aborted via NEEDS_REVIEW. Slight redundancy but not contradictory. Let me refine that one line to be precise.
````

We are continuing the CS5351 TradingAgents project in a NEW session.

Project root:
/home/brian/projects/CS5351

I am Member B, responsible for architecture. I am preparing a requirements-baseline proposal for Member A and the team to review. A owns final requirements approval; C owns independent verification; implementation and governance changes remain with their accountable owners.

## Background and objective

Member A previously produced a broader v2 requirements draft. Because it contained conflicts and underspecified requirements, the team selected a manageable subset first. That subset supported the C2 architecture and current implementation.

The selected requirements did NOT automatically replace or settle the broader draft.

Your task is to reconcile:
- A’s broader draft.
- The selected requirements.
- The current architecture and implementation.
- Verification evidence and review findings.
- The original course obligations.

Propose a coherent, achievable final requirements baseline. Do not simply add more requirements, automatically implement every historical proposal, or treat the selected subset as already final.

## Stage 1 — read-only assessment

Perform ONLY Stage 1 now.

First report:
- Working directory, branch, HEAD, and working-tree status.
- Applicable project instructions and governance files.
- Missing or inaccessible sources.
- Whether your assessment covers only the local checkout; do not claim knowledge of E’s latest remote fixes without evidence.

Do not pull, switch branches, merge, commit, push, install dependencies, or run live model evaluations.

Read these private handoff files:
/home/brian/.local/state/cs5351-handoffs/2026-11-20-architecture-session/HANDOFF.md
/home/brian/.local/state/cs5351-handoffs/2026-11-20-architecture-session/EXPORT_MANIFEST.json

Read this source index, verify its listed hashes, and read all five referenced source files:
/home/brian/.local/state/cs5351-handoffs/2026-11-20-architecture-session/sources/SOURCE_INDEX.json

The source pack contains:
- A’s requirements-draft-v2.md.
- The historical requirements-v2 review.
- The original course specification.
- The course introduction extract.
- The original team ownership allocation.

A’s draft hash is:
5742540b7b614487082ba399b7a5b33e17f0d24c7e87a88fa69827a6aa62519f

The historical review contains suggestions, not approved requirements. The handoff is historical context, not proof of current implementation or completed deliverables. Do not read the raw/sanitized session exports unless I request a specific history lookup.

Read the current repository sources, starting with:
/home/brian/projects/CS5351/docs/req/selected-requirements.md
/home/brian/projects/CS5351/architecture-blueprint.md
/home/brian/projects/CS5351/docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md
/home/brian/projects/CS5351/docs/reviews/project-review-2026-11-18.md
/home/brian/projects/CS5351/docs/reviews/evidence/live-diagnostic-2026-11-18.json

Follow relevant architecture references and inspect actual code/tests to substantiate coverage claims. Do not read credentials, .env files, SSH keys, or authentication stores.

## Required analysis

1. Inventory every original active requirement and account separately for withdrawn entries. Preserve IDs. Map original REQ-TA-* requirements to SEL-TA-* requirements by meaning, not matching numbers.

2. Classify each original requirement:
   - Covered.
   - Partially covered.
   - Needs clarification/conflict resolution.
   - Proposed for additional implementation.
   - Proposed for deferral/rejection.
   - Requires a human/team decision.

Explain the uncovered portion and rationale. Do not silently discard a previously accepted requirement.

3. Distinguish requirement contradictions, underspecification, implementation defects, missing verification, and missing governance/delivery artifacts.

4. Check course coverage: D1–D9, mandatory blocking gates, authentic transcripts, report/contributions/reflections, and the separate demonstration. Distinguish absent repository artifacts from work that may exist elsewhere.

5. Identify the meaningful improvement beyond upstream for each claimed enhancement. Existing functionality may belong in the baseline but must not be counted automatically as a new contribution.

6. Review invariants, quality, performance, cost, security, and governance. Propose measurable fit criteria and justified thresholds; identify measurements or decisions needed instead of inventing numbers.

7. Identify architecture, interface, test, implementation, and ownership impacts. Preserve C2 unless changed drivers justify reconsideration; flag proposed ADR changes rather than redesigning automatically.

## Portfolio decisions to preserve

- Users may confirm and proceed without a portfolio.
- Missing portfolio means unknown holdings.
- Explicit empty positions mean a supplied flat snapshot.
- A nonempty portfolio may still have no position in the analyzed instrument.
- Missing cash is unknown, not zero.
- Empty holdings do not require rejecting a run or forcing Hold.
- Research ratings remain distinct from account-specific instructions.
- F9 concerns unconditional advice about nonexistent holdings.
- Current PASSED certifies Q1–Q4 only; do not silently redefine it or add a new authoritative check.

A’s broader draft used research-only scope, while the later working selection deliberately introduced optional holdings. Record this scope change for A/team confirmation; do not automatically remove the existing feature.

## Stage 1 outputs — in chat only

Return:
A. Source inventory and verified baseline.
B. Complete original-to-selected requirement disposition matrix.
C. Course-obligation coverage matrix.
D. Prioritized gaps/conflicts and proposed resolutions.
E. Recommended final scope, with implementation and verification effort clearly labelled as estimates.
F. Draft acceptance scenarios, including the portfolio cases.
G. Decisions required from A/B/C/D/E or the instructor.
H. A proposed Stage 2 file/write plan.

Stage 2 may prepare candidate requirements/schema and change records after human review. It must preserve one authoritative final baseline under A’s ownership.

Do not modify files during Stage 1. Do not implement code or tests, invent approvals/results, or present recommendations as team decisions.

Stop after the assessment and wait for human review.

Price is the one core input (FR-005); a run without it has no basis for a rating. | Appendix C |\n33: | 14 | Six-plus `INCOMPLETE` reasons may be too complex; each may need a new component. | Reduced to 3: `DATA`, `MODEL`, `BUDGET`. Which budget was hit goes to the log, not the status. | RUN-001 |\n34: | 15 | `COMPLETE` and `VALIDATED_RESEARCH` are in one status set, though a run can be both. | Split into separate fields. | RUN-001 |\n35: | 16 | Relationship between `REVIEW` and `REVIEW_REQUIRED`. | `REVIEW` is a value of `rating` only. A `REVIEW` rating always gives `output_check = NEEDS_REVIEW` (rule R1). `REVIEW_REQUIRED` no longer exists. | RUN-001, ARCH-002 |\n36: | 17 | Define Hold without assuming an existing position. | Same as row 12. | FR-007 |\n37: | 18 | `VALIDATED_RESEARCH` had no reason code although non-`COMPLETE` statuses need one. | No longer applies: only `INCOMPLETE` carries a reason. | RUN-001 |\n38: | 19 | Define data-freshness rules. | Thresholds per data type and the behaviour when one is exceeded. | FR-006 |\n39: | 20 | RUN-001 allowed `COMPLETE` with `REVIEW` while unreadable output went to `REVIEW_REQUIRED` elsewhere. | One rule now: `COMPLETED` + `REVIEW` + `NEEDS_REVIEW`. | RUN-001 |\n40: | 21 | FR-003: resume already exists; focus tests on zero re-execution, signature and status in the list, and distinct records for repeated same-day runs. | FR-003 rewritten to those three tests. The distinct-records test is owned by NFR-REPRO-001 and referenced from FR-003. | FR-003 |\n41: \n42: ---\n43: \n44: ## Definitions (normative)\n45: \n46: Each term below is used only in this sense throughout the document.\n47: \n48: | Term | Meaning |\n49: |---|---|\n50: | Run | One analysis of one ticker for one analysis date, started through `TradingAgentsGraph.propagate` or the CLI. A resumed run is the same run; a rerun is a new run. |\n51: | *D* | The run's analysis date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, not later than today). |\n52: | Channel | One of the 12 evidence sources listed in FR-004. |\n53: | Evidence item | One retrieved unit from a channel: a price series, one news item, one social post, one financial statement, one macro series, one memory lesson. |\n54: | Core data | Price history (`core_stock_apis`) only. Technical indicators are computed from it and follow it. |\n55: | Gap | A channel whose `data_coverage` code is anything other than `OK`. |\n56: | Final rating | The Portfolio Manager's output: Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell, or `REVIEW` when none can be read. |\n57: | Intermediate judgment | The Research Manager's recommendation (5-tier) and the Trader's action (Buy / Hold / Sell). Never called a \"rating\" in reports. |\n58: | Completed | Only `run_outcome = COMPLETED`. It says the pipeline finished, never that the result is good. |\n59: | Output check | The deterministic, non-LLM component of ARCH-002. |\n60: | Finding | A rule the output check found broken. A **blocking** finding sets `NEEDS_REVIEW`. A **corrected** finding is fixed automatically and recorded. |\n61: | Offline / live profile | The two test set-ups in Appendix A. |\n62: | Parameter | A named number in Appendix D. Fit criteria refer to parameters by name. |\n63: \n64: ## Drafting principles (normative)\n65: \n66: - **P1 One owner per rule.** Each rule is stated in exactly one requirement. Other requirements cite it by ID and do not restate it.\n67: - **P2 Priority order.** A requirement depends only on requirements of equal or higher priority.\n68: - **P3 Defined terms.** Terms from Definitions are used only in their defined sense.\n69: - **P4 No loose numbers.** Every threshold is a parameter in Appendix D, marked fixed or provisional, with an owner.\n70: - **P5 Testable form.** Each fit criterion reads: **Given** (profile and fixtures, Appendix A) **when** (action) **then** (counts or booleans).\n71: \n72: ---\n73: \n74: ## Overview\n75: \n76: | ID | Type | Summary | Priority | Status |\n77: |---|---|---|---|---|\n78: | REQ-TA-RUN-001 | Functional | Every run records separate outcome, stop reason, rating, check and coverage fields | Must | proposed |\n79: | REQ-TA-FR-001 | Functional | Evidence IDs, traceable records, and visible source and date in the report | Must | proposed |\n80: | REQ-TA-FR-003 | Functional | Checkpoint list, resume without re-running persisted tasks, explicit rerun | Should | partial |\n81: | REQ-TA-FR-004 | Functional | No evidence dated after *D* reaches any agent | Must | partial |\n82: | REQ-TA-FR-005 | Functional | Gaps are disclosed with a code; missing price data stops the run | Must | partial |\n83: | REQ-TA-FR-006 | Functional | Freshness thresholds per data type | Should | partial |\n84: | REQ-TA-FR-007 | Functional | Ratings describe the stock, not the user's account; no ownership wording | Must | proposed |\n85: | REQ-TA-FR-008 | Functional | Sentiment score and confidence consistent with the data actually available | Should | proposed |\n86: | REQ-TA-NFR-001 | Quality (reliability) | No crash on vendor or model failure; each failure has one defined result | Must | partial |\n87: | REQ-TA-NFR-002 | Quality (maintainability) | Add or remove an analyst without editing orchestration | Could | partial |\n88: | REQ-TA-NFR-OBS-001 | Quality (observability) | Structured log records with fixed fields | Should | partial |\n89: | REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001 | Quality (reproducibility) | One immutable run record and report per run | Should | partial |\n90: | REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-001 | Performance | Single analysis within `RUN_TIME_CAP` | Should | proposed |\n91: | REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002 | Performance | Crossing the time budget ends the run `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` | Should | proposed |\n92: | REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001 | Cost | Run-level token budget, measured from provider usage | Should | proposed |\n93: | REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002 | Cost | Run-wide LLM call cap enforced before dispatch | Must | proposed |\n94: | REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003 | Cost | Debates end early on convergence | Could | proposed |\n95: | REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001 | Quality (evaluation) | Fixed counting rules for completion rate and quality scores | Should | proposed |\n96: | REQ-TA-SEC-001 | Security | Retrieved content cannot change config, coverage or check results | Must | proposed |\n97: | REQ-TA-SEC-002 | Security | No credentials or tokens in logs, reports, run records or errors | Must | partial |\n98: | REQ-TA-SEC-003 | Security | No guarantee of returns or capital protection | Should | proposed |\n99: | REQ-TA-ARCH-001 | Architectural constraint | Vendors behind one routing point | Should | partial |\n100: | REQ-TA-ARCH-002 | Architectural constraint | One deterministic output check; LLMs cannot set its result | Must | proposed |\n101: | REQ-TA-GOV-001 | Governance | Semantic evaluation gate on prompt and model changes | Must | proposed |\n102: | REQ-TA-GOV-002 | Governance | Test plan approved before implementation | Must | to be confirmed |\n103: \n104: Withdrawn: REQ-TA-FR-002, REQ-TA-NFR-SAFETY-001, REQ-TA-NFR-SAFETY-002 (Appendix C).\n105: \n106: **Scope.** Research-only. The system produces research and a rating about an instrument. It does not size positions or check exposure against an account. A portfolio file, which v0.7.1 accepts, is outside project scope: no requirement makes claims about runs that use one, and every fixture runs without one.\n107: \n108: ---\n109: \n110: ## Run result\n111: \n112: ### REQ-TA-RUN-001 Run result fields\n113: \n114: - **Type**: functional\n115: - **Statement**: Every run shall end with a run record holding the fields below. Each field describes one thing only, and only the combinations in the validity table are allowed.\n116: - **Fields**:\n117: \n118:   | Field | Values | Set by | Present when |\n119:   |---|---|---|---|\n120:   | `run_outcome` | `COMPLETED`, `INCOMPLETE` | Run engine | Always |\n121:   | `stop_reason` | `DATA`, `MODEL`, `BUDGET` | Run engine | Only when `INCOMPLETE` |\n122:   | `rating` | Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell, `REVIEW` | Portfolio Manager, read by the rating parser | Only when `COMPLETED` |\n123:   | `output_check` | `PASSED`, `NEEDS_REVIEW`, `NOT_RUN` | Output check (ARCH-002) | Always |\n124:   | `check_findings` | List of rule IDs, each marked blocking or corrected | Output check (ARCH-002) | Always (may be empty) |\n125:   | `data_coverage` | One code per channel (FR-005) | FR-005 | Always |\n126: \n127: - **Stop reasons**:\n128: \n129:   | Reason | Kind | Raised when | Owner of the rule |\n130:   |---|---|---|---|\n131:   | `DATA` | Failure | Core data is unavailable, absent or stale | FR-005, FR-006 |\n132:   | `MODEL` | Failure | A model step produced no usable output after retries and the free-text fallback | NFR-001 |\n133:   | `BUDGET` | Planned stop | A configured time, token or call limit was reached. Which limit is written to the log (OBS-001), not to the status. | PERF-002, COST-001, COST-002 |\n134: \n135: - **Validity table** (every other combination is invalid):\n136: \n137:   | `run_outcome` | `stop_reason` | `rating` | `output_check` |\n138:   |---|---|---|---|\n139:   | `INCOMPLETE` | `DATA` / `MODEL` / `BUDGET` | — | `NOT_RUN` |\n140:   | `COMPLETED` | — | Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell | `PASSED` or `NEEDS_REVIEW` |\n141:   | `COMPLETED` | — | `REVIEW` | `NEEDS_REVIEW` (rule R1) |\n142: \n143: - **Fit criterion**: Given every offline fixture in Appendix A, when each runs, then 100% of runs produce a run record; 100% of records match exactly one row of the validity table; 0 records have `COMPLETED` while some agent step produced no output.\n144: - **Dependencies**: none (all fields are owned here; their rules live in the owners named above)\n145: - **Baseline**: `propagate` returns `(final_state, signal)`, where `signal` is a 5-tier rating or `REVIEW` when no rating can be parsed (`graph/trading_graph.py`, `agents/rating.py`). There is no outcome, stop reason, check result or coverage field.\n146: - **Open**: Add the fields to the run record (NFR-REPRO-001) and set them on every exit path.\n147: - **Priority**: Must\n148: - **Status**: proposed\n149: - **Tradeoff**: The report header shows three short lines (outcome, rating, check) instead of one.\n150: \n151: ---\n152: \n153: ## Functional requirements\n154: \n155: ### REQ-TA-FR-001 Evidence IDs, records and visible source dates\n156: \n157: - **Type**: functional\n158: - **Statement**: The system shall give each evidence item admitted into a run one stable evidence ID, and shall keep a record for it with at least: source, ticker, and either observation time or publication time. Wherever the report cites an item, it shall show the item's source and date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) beside the citation. Records are kept for every run whatever its outcome: a run's outcome never changes or deletes its evidence records.\n159: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and `fixtures/fr001/evidence.jsonl`, when one run completes and every cited ID is collected, then (a) 100% of cited IDs resolve to exactly 1 record with non-empty `source`, `ticker` and one of `observed_at` / `published_at`; (b) 100% of citations in the rendered report show a source and a date; (c) all 12 channels of FR-004 write records, including the 2 that bypass the router. Given fixture `fixtures/fr001/timeout_after_price/`, which ends `INCOMPLETE(MODEL)` after price data was retrieved, then (d) the registry still holds the price records, unchanged (≥ 1 record, byte-identical to before the stop). An ID that is cited but not registered is the blocking finding R2 (ARCH-002).\n160: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-RUN-001\n161: - **Related**: ARCH-001 (when it is met, the registry write can sit in the router alone)\n162: - **Baseline**: Items carry their own dates and source labels in vendor text (news rows and price rows both carry a date), but nothing assigns an ID or keeps a record keyed by one.\n163: - **Open**: Add the registry write at the data boundary, including the two bypass channels, and render source and date at each citation.\n164: - **Priority**: Must\n165: - **Tradeoff**: One write per admitted item and one lookup per citation, plus storage under `results_dir`.\n166: - **Status**: proposed\n167: \n168: ### REQ-TA-FR-003 Checkpoint list, resume and rerun\n169: \n170: - **Type**: functional\n171: - **Statement**: The system shall list saved checkpoints, resume an interrupted run without re-running tasks that were already saved, and rerun from scratch on request.\n172: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and a run interrupted after all 4 analyst branches were saved, when (a) it is resumed with the same ticker, *D* and settings, then agent invocations for those 4 branches = 0 (4/4); (b) the checkpoint list is shown, then it lists ticker, *D*, the run signature, the number of saved tasks, and a status of `RESUMABLE` (signature matches current settings) or `CONFIG_CHANGED` (it does not) — checked on 1 fixture of each status; (c) it is rerun, then all 4 branches execute again (≥ 1 invocation each), the old checkpoint is cleared, and the rerun gets its own run record and report per NFR-REPRO-001.\n173: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-NFR-001, REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n174: - **Baseline**: Resume already works: per-node SQLite checkpoints keyed by a run signature, resume detection (`checkpoint_step`), fresh start when the signature changes, and clean-up after success (`graph/checkpointer.py`, `_run_signature` in `trading_graph.py`; tests `test_checkpoint_resume.py`, `test_checkpoint_lifecycle.py`, `test_graph_end_to_end.py::test_an_interrupted_run_resumes_from_its_checkpoint`). There is no list command and no explicit rerun command.\n175: - **Open**: Add the list and rerun commands. Turn the three checks above into acceptance tests.\n176: - **Priority**: Should\n177: - **Tradeoff**: Checkpoints are stored per ticker, so the list is per ticker unless an index file is added.\n178: - **Status**: partial\n179: \n180: ### REQ-TA-FR-004 Point-in-time evidence (no look-ahead)\n181: \n182: - **Type**: functional\n183: - **Statement**: For a run with analysis date *D*, no item published, observed, filed or resolved after the end of *D* shall reach any agent's prompt, through any channel. A date the model gives a tool shall never widen the window past *D*. Data with no historical version (live-only data) shall be withheld from a run dated before today. The one exception is the instrument's current name, which may be given only when it is labelled as the current name.\n184: - **Why Must**: An analysis or backtest that sees later news or prices looks better than it really is. Every evaluation result (EVAL-001) would be invalid.\n185: - **Channels** (normative; this list defines \"channel\" for the whole document):\n186: \n187:   | # | Channel | Entry point in v0.7.1 | Current guard |\n188:   |---|---|---|---|\n189:   | 1 | Price history | `get_stock_data` | Window end clamped to *D* (`as_of_window`) |\n190:   | 2 | Technical indicators | `get_indicators` | Date clamped to *D* (`as_of`) |\n191:   | 3 | Verified market snapshot | `get_verified_market_snapshot` (calls Yahoo directly, not through the router) | Date clamped to *D* |\n192:   | 4 | Company overview | `get_fundamentals` | Withheld on historical runs (`withhold_live_profile`) — live-only |\n193:   | 5 | Financial statements | `get_balance_sheet`, `get_cashflow`, `get_income_statement` | Date clamped; filtered by filing date |\n194:   | 6 | Ticker news | `get_news` | Window clamped; items trimmed by `in_window` |\n195:   | 7 | Global news | `get_global_news` | Date clamped; items trimmed by `in_window` |\n196:   | 8 | Insider transactions | `get_insider_transactions` | Run date passed from graph state |\n197:   | 9 | Macro indicators | `get_macro_indicators` (FRED) | Data vintage pinned to *D* |\n198:   | 10 | Prediction markets | `get_prediction_markets` (Polymarket) | Withheld on historical runs — live-only |\n199:   | 11 | Social posts | Reddit and StockTwits inside `sentiment_analyst.py` (not through the router) | Items trimmed by `in_window` |\n200:   | 12 | Memory lessons | `TradingMemoryLog.get_past_context(as_of=D)` | Only lessons resolved on or before *D* |\n201: \n202: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, *D* = 2026-01-09, and `fixtures/fr004/channels/` holding, for each of the 10 dated channels, one control item dated *D* and one planted item dated *D*+1 that carries the marker `LOOKAHEAD-<#>`, when one run executes and every prompt to the scripted model is captured, then: (a) 0/10 markers appear in any prompt; (b) 10/10 control items appear in at least one prompt; (c) the 2 live-only channels return their \"withheld\" notice (2/2) and 0 live values; (d) for each of the 12 dated tools in `agents/tools.py`, a model-supplied date of *D*+30 is served as *D* (12/12); (e) the instrument context holds 0 sector, industry or exchange values, and any name carries the \"current name\" label.\n203: - **Dependencies**: none\n204: - **Baseline**: Each channel already has its own guard and unit tests (`test_tool_date_enforcement.py`, `test_news_lookahead.py`, `test_social_lookahead.py`, `test_fundamentals_lookahead.py`, `test_memory_pointintime.py`, `test_undated_tools_as_of.py`, `test_statement_knowledge_time.py`); a future *D* is refused (`_validate_trade_date`). No test checks all channels in one whole run.\n205: - **Open**: Add the whole-run planted-marker test as a required CI check.\n206: - **Out of scope (stated, not tested)**: The model's own training data may contain events after *D*. A report for a historical *D* should state this limitation.\n207: - **Priority**: Must\n208: - **Tradeoff**: Historical runs see less data than a live run would.\n209: - **Status**: partial\n210: \n211: ### REQ-TA-FR-005 Data gaps and the core-data rule\n212: \n213: - **Type**: functional\n214: - **Statement**: This requirement owns every rule about missing data.\n215:   1. **Core rule.** If core data has any code other than `OK`, the run ends `INCOMPLETE(DATA)`.\n216:   2. **Non-core rule.** A gap in any other channel does not stop the run.\n217:   3. **Disclosure.** Every report has a \"Data coverage\" section that lists each channel with exactly one code from the table below. The section is built from tool results and is never written by the model.\n218: - **Coverage codes**:\n219: \n220:   | Code | Meaning | v0.7.1 signal it maps from |\n221:   |---|---|---|\n222:   | `OK` | Served and fresh | Normal tool result |\n223:   | `UNAVAILABLE` | The vendor was down, throttled or failed, or the feed could not see the requested window. Says nothing about the stock. | `DATA_UNAVAILABLE: …` (`router.vendor_unavailable`); `<… unavailable for …>` (`date_window.coverage_gap`) |\n224:   | `NO_DATA` | Every vendor that answered had no data for this stock | `NO_DATA_AVAILABLE: …` (`router.no_data_available`) |\n225:   | `STALE` | Served, but older than its FR-006 threshold | FR-006 |\n226:   | `WITHHELD` | Live-only data withheld from a historical run | FR-004 withheld notices |\n227:   | `NOT_REACHED` | The run stopped before this channel was called. Appears only in `INCOMPLETE` runs. | — |\n228: \n229: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and 12 fixtures — 8 non-core gaps (2 each for `UNAVAILABLE`, `NO_DATA`, `STALE`, `WITHHELD`), 3 core gaps (price `UNAVAILABLE`, `NO_DATA`, `STALE`) and 1 clean run — when each runs, then: (a) 8/8 non-core fixtures end `COMPLETED` and list the affected channel with the matching code; (b) 3/3 core fixtures end `INCOMPLETE(DATA)`; (c) the clean fixture lists 12/12 channels as `OK`; (d) 0/12 raise; (e) the section is byte-identical when the scripted model's prose is replaced with different prose.\n230: - **Semantic part**: whether the model's own prose avoids claiming an absence (\"no recent news\") for a channel that has a gap is tested in the GOV-001 suite, because a scripted model cannot test it.\n231: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-RUN-001, REQ-TA-FR-004\n232: - **Baseline**: The data layer already tells these cases apart in tool text and tells the model not to invent values (`dataflows/router.py`, `date_window.py`; tests `test_no_data_handling.py`, `test_vendor_errors.py`). But nothing collects them per run; the report does not list them; and a full price outage still ends with a rating, because throttled or unreachable vendors degrade to a text note in every category. Channels 3 and 11 bypass the router.\n233: - **Open**: Collect the codes per run (router plus the two bypass channels), stop on a core gap, and render the section.\n234: - **Priority**: Must\n235: - **Tradeoff**: Every report gains a section, including gaps that a reader may not care about.\n236: - **Status**: partial\n237: \n238: ### REQ-TA-FR-006 Freshness thresholds\n239: \n240: - **Type**: functional\n241: - **Statement**: Each data type shall be judged fresh or stale by the rule in the table below. Stale data is coded `STALE` (FR-005) and handled as the last column says.\n242: \n243:   | Data type | Fresh when | Parameter (Appendix D) | If exceeded |\n244:   |---|---|---|---|\n245:   | Price history | Latest bar is ≤ `STALE_PRICE_DAYS` calendar days before *D* | `STALE_PRICE_DAYS` | Not used; core gap → `INCOMPLETE(DATA)` (FR-005) |\n246:   | Technical indicators | Follows price history | — | Follows price history |\n247:   | Financial statements | Latest statement was filed ≤ `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` days before *D* | `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` | Still shown with its filing date; coded `STALE`; run continues |\n248:   | Ticker news, global news, social posts | Item lies inside the requested window, clamped to *D* (FR-004) | `global_news_lookback_days` (v0.7.1 config) | Item left out. This is not marked `STALE`; an empty window is `NO_DATA` or `UNAVAILABLE`. |\n249:   | Macro indicators, insider transactions | No threshold (releases are monthly or irregular) | — | Each value shown with its own date |\n250:   | Company overview, prediction markets | Live-only | — | `WITHHELD` on historical runs (FR-004) |\n251: \n252: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and 6 boundary fixtures, when each runs, then 6/6 behave as follows: price bar at *D*−`STALE_PRICE_DAYS` → `OK`; at *D*−(`STALE_PRICE_DAYS`+1) → `INCOMPLETE(DATA)`; statement filed at *D*−`STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` → `OK`; at *D*−(`STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS`+1) → `STALE` and still shown; news item on the window's first day → included; one day before it → left out.\n253: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-FR-005\n254: - **Baseline**: The price rule already exists: a frame whose latest row is more than 10 days before the requested date is refused as stale (`MAX_OHLCV_STALE_DAYS = 10`, `dataflows/vendors/yahoo/ohlcv.py`; `test_yfinance_stale_ohlcv_guard.py`). News and social windows exist (FR-004). There is no statement-age rule.\n255: - **Open**: Add the statement-age rule and the `STALE` code; confirm `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` (provisional).\n256: - **Priority**: Should\n257: - **Tradeoff**: A fixed statement threshold suits some filing schedules better than others. Hong Kong half-yearly filers are the reason for the provisional 200 days.\n258: - **Status**: partial\n259: \n260: ### REQ-TA-FR-007 Rating meaning and no ownership wording\n261: \n262: - **Type**: functional\n263: - **Statement**:\n264:   1. **Meaning.** The five ratings describe how strongly the evidence favours the instrument, from strongest positive (Buy) to strongest negative (Sell). **Hold** means the evidence is balanced, or too thin to favour either direction. No rating is an instruction about the user's account.\n265:   2. **Labels.** Reports label the three model judgments separately: \"Final rating (Portfolio Manager)\", \"Research recommendation (Research Manager, intermediate)\" and \"Trader proposal (Buy / Hold / Sell, intermediate)\". Only the Portfolio Manager's output is called the final rating, and only it fills `rating` in the run record.\n266:   3. **No ownership wording.** Prompts and reports shall not state or assume that the user holds the instrument. The minimum banned list is `fixtures/fr007/ownership_phrases.txt`: \"your position\", \"current position\", \"maintain the position\", \"add to your position\", \"exit your position\", \"your holdings\", \"you own\".\n267: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, when (a) the Research Manager and Portfolio Manager prompt templates are scanned, then 2/2 contain 0 banned phrases and define Hold with the sentence in part 1; (b) one report is rendered, then it contains all 3 labels (3/3) and exactly 1 \"Final rating\"; (c) 3 scripted final decisions that each contain one banned phrase are checked, then 3/3 get `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding R3, and 1 clean decision gets `PASSED`.\n268: - **Semantic part**: live-model wording is tested in the GOV-001 suite.\n269: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-ARCH-002, REQ-TA-RUN-001\n270: - **Baseline**: Both manager prompts define ratings as account actions: `research_manager.py` line 32 \"Hold: … recommend maintaining the current position\"; `portfolio_manager.py` line 53 \"Hold: Maintain current position, no action needed\", plus \"enter or add to position\" and \"Exit position\". v0.7.1 keeps the three judgments as separate fields (`ResearchPlan.recommendation`, `TraderProposal.action`, `PortfolioDecision.rating` in `agents/schemas.py`).\n271: - **Open**: Reword both prompts, add the labels, and add rule R3 to the output check.\n272: - **Priority**: Must\n273: - **Tradeoff**: Without account wording, the rating reads less like direct advice. That is intended in a research-only scope.\n274: - **Status**: proposed\n275: \n276: ### REQ-TA-FR-008 Sentiment score and confidence consistent with available data\n277: \n278: - **Type**: functional\n279: - **Statement**: The Sentiment Analyst's model-chosen band, score and confidence shall follow the rules below, applied by the output check. Any agent that later gets a confidence field shall follow the same confidence rule.\n280: \n281:   | Rule | Check | Kind |\n282:   |---|---|---|\n283:   | R4 | `overall_score` lies in its band's range: Bullish [6.5, 10]; Mildly Bullish [5.5, 6.5); Neutral and Mixed [4.5, 5.5); Mildly Bearish [3.5, 4.5); Bearish [0, 3.5). These are the schema's own guideline ranges, made exact. | Blocking |\n284:   | R5 | If any of the analyst's 3 sources (news, StockTwits, Reddit) is not `OK`, confidence is at most `low`. A higher value is lowered, and both the original and the new value are recorded. | Corrected |\n285:   | R6 | If none of the 3 sources is `OK`, the band must be Neutral | Blocking |\n286: \n287: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and 6 fixtures, when each is checked, then 6/6 match: (1) the team's example — Bullish, score 0, high, all 3 sources unavailable → R4 and R6 blocking, R5 lowers confidence to low → `NEEDS_REVIEW`; (2) Mildly Bullish, 6.0, high, all sources `OK` → `PASSED`, confidence stays high; (3) Bullish, 7.0, high, Reddit `UNAVAILABLE` → `PASSED`, confidence lowered to low and recorded; (4) Bearish, 5.0 → R4 → `NEEDS_REVIEW`; (5) Bullish, 6.5 → passes R4; (6) Mildly Bullish, 6.5 → fails R4.\n288: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-FR-005, REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n289: - **Baseline**: `SentimentReport` (`agents/schemas.py`) enforces only the 0–10 bounds and the allowed labels. The band–score ranges and the \"low when a source is missing\" rule are guidance text the model may ignore. The team confirmed the schema accepts Bullish + 0 + High.\n290: - **Open**: Add R4–R6 to the output check.\n291: - **Priority**: Should\n292: - **Tradeoff**: Lowering confidence automatically can understate a strong signal from the two sources that did work.\n293: - **Status**: proposed\n294: \n295: ---\n296: \n297: ## Non-functional requirements\n298: \n299: ### REQ-TA-NFR-001 Fail safely on external failures\n300: \n301: - **Type**: quality (reliability)\n302: - **Statement**: No vendor or model failure shall crash the process.
