Additionally, 0 of the FR-005 fixtures raise.\n311: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-RUN-001, REQ-TA-FR-005\n312: - **Baseline**: Malformed structured output already falls back to free text (`agents/structured.py`). An unreadable final rating already becomes `REVIEW` (`agents/rating.py`). There is no run-level catch, so a model call that fails after retries raises out of `propagate`.\n313: - **Open**: Catch at the graph entry and map to `INCOMPLETE(MODEL)`.\n314: - **Priority**: Must\n315: - **Tradeoff**: Some runs that used to crash loudly now end quietly as `INCOMPLETE`; the log (OBS-001) must keep the detail.\n316: - **Status**: partial\n317: \n318: ### REQ-TA-NFR-002 Add or remove an analyst\n319: \n320: - **Type**: quality (maintainability)\n321: - **Statement**: Adding or removing an analyst shall require changes only to that analyst's module and its registration data, and to no orchestration module.\n322: - **Fit criterion**: Given a change that adds 1 analyst, when `git diff --stat` is taken against `{tradingagents/graph/setup.py, tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py, tradingagents/graph/conditional_logic.py}`, then changed lines in that set = 0 and the full test suite passes.\n323: - **Dependencies**: none\n324: - **Baseline**: Removing works (`selected_analysts` → `build_analyst_execution_plan`, `graph/analyst_execution.py`). Adding needs an edit to the hard-coded `analyst_factories` in `graph/setup.py`.\n325: - **Open**: Move factories into the registration data.\n326: - **Priority**: Could\n327: - **Tradeoff**: Wiring is less readable at the point of use.\n328: - **Status**: partial\n329: \n330: ### REQ-TA-NFR-OBS-001 Structured logging\n331: \n332: - **Type**: quality (observability)\n333: - **Statement**: The system shall write machine-parseable log records, each with `run_id`, ticker, node or agent, timestamp, elapsed time, and event outcome. When a run stops for `BUDGET`, the log names the limit that was hit (time, tokens or calls).\n334: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, when every line of both sinks is parsed after one completed run and after one `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` run, then 100% of lines parse and contain all six fields with non-null values; the `BUDGET` run's log names exactly 1 limit.\n335: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-SEC-002, REQ-TA-RUN-001, REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n336: - **Baseline**: The graph writes one JSON state file per run (`_log_state`). The CLI writes plain-text `message_tool.log` (`cli/run.py`).\n337: - **Open**: JSON-lines for the CLI sink; add `run_id` and elapsed time to both.\n338: - **Priority**: Should\n339: - **Tradeoff**: JSON lines are harder to skim by eye.\n340: - **Status**: partial\n341: \n342: ### REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001 Immutable run record and report\n343: \n344: - **Type**: quality (reproducibility)\n345: - **Statement**: Every run, including each rerun, shall write exactly one run record and one report folder, both named by a unique `run_id`. The record contains: start and end time, code version, every configuration key that can change what the run produces, a hash of the prompt templates, and the RUN-001 fields. A later run shall never overwrite or change an earlier run's record or report.\n346: - **Recorded keys**: every key in `DEFAULT_CONFIG` except `{results_dir, data_cache_dir, memory_log_path, checkpoint_enabled, llm_max_retries}` (the keys v0.7.1 already treats as \"does not change what a run writes\", `_NOT_IN_SIGNATURE`). Endpoint URLs are recorded only as set / not set (SEC-002).\n347: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, when (a) two runs of the same ticker and *D* execute one after the other, then 2 distinct records and 2 distinct report folders exist, and the first run's files are byte-identical before and after the second; (b) each record has non-null `run_id`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `version`, `prompt_hash`, `config` and the RUN-001 fields; (c) for each of the 10 keys v0.7.1 leaves out of `run_settings()` (`temperature`, `max_tokens`, `max_tool_rounds`, `news_article_limit`, `global_news_article_limit`, `global_news_lookback_days`, `holding_period_days`, `google_thinking_level`, `openai_reasoning_effort`, `anthropic_effort`), changing only that key makes the two records differ in exactly that key (10/10); (d) recorded keys = `DEFAULT_CONFIG` keys minus the excluded set (0 missing, 0 extra); (e) editing one prompt template changes `prompt_hash`, and leaving templates unchanged keeps it the same; (f) the SEC-002 scan finds 0 planted secrets.\n348: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-RUN-001, REQ-TA-SEC-002\n349: - **Baseline**: `run_settings()` records only an allowlist (version, providers, models, analysts, rounds, language, vendors). It has no run id, timing or prompt hash. The state log is named `full_states_log_<D>.json` per ticker, so a same-day rerun overwrites it.\n350: - **Open**: Widen the record, add run id, timing and prompt hash, and name files by run id.\n351: - **Priority**: Should\n352: - **Tradeoff**: `results_dir` grows faster; no automatic clean-up is proposed.\n353: - **Status**: partial\n354: \n355: ### REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-001 Maximum run time\n356: \n357: - **Type**: performance\n358: - **Statement**: A single-ticker run shall complete within `RUN_TIME_CAP`, measured wall-clock from graph start to the run record being written.\n359: - **Fit criterion**: Given the live profile, when 20 runs execute one after another, then the maximum of the 20 run times is ≤ `RUN_TIME_CAP` and 20/20 are `COMPLETED`. Runs stopped as `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` count as failures of this criterion.\n360: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-NFR-001, REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n361: - **Baseline**: No cap. Analysts already run in parallel (`graph/setup.py`).\n362: - **Open**: Measure first, then fix `RUN_TIME_CAP` from the measurement.\n363: - **Priority**: Should\n364: - **Tradeoff**: A tight cap trades completeness for speed.\n365: - **Status**: proposed\n366: \n367: ### REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002 Time-budget handling\n368: \n369: - **Type**: performance\n370: - **Statement**: A run that crosses its time budget (default `RUN_TIME_CAP`) shall stop and end `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`. Calls already in flight may run for at most `CANCEL_ALLOWANCE` beyond the budget.\n371: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile with a slow scripted model and a 30 s test budget, when 10 runs execute, then 10/10 end `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`, 10/10 return within 30 s + `CANCEL_ALLOWANCE`, and 10/10 logs name the time limit.\n372: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-NFR-001, REQ-TA-RUN-001\n373: - **Baseline**: No run-level timer.\n374: - **Open**: Check the deadline at node boundaries and add the cancellation allowance.\n375: - **Priority**: Should\n376: - **Tradeoff**: Calls that ignore cancellation delay the return.\n377: - **Status**: proposed\n378: \n379: ### REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001 Run token budget\n380: \n381: - **Type**: cost\n382: - **Statement**: A run shall use at most `TOKEN_BUDGET` tokens in total, counted from provider usage data. A run that would exceed it ends `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`. If a provider returns no usage data, the run is not stopped; its record marks token usage as `UNKNOWN`.\n383: - **Fit criterion**: Given the live profile, when 20 runs execute one after another, then 20/20 have known usage ≤ `TOKEN_BUDGET`, and the GOV-001 score over these runs is ≥ `QUALITY_THRESHOLD`. A run with `UNKNOWN` usage counts as a failure of this criterion, not as zero cost.\n384: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-GOV-001, REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n385: - **Baseline**: `max_tokens` caps each call (`default_config.py`). There is no run-level count.\n386: - **Open**: Add up usage per run; set `TOKEN_BUDGET` from measurement.\n387: - **Priority**: Should\n388: - **Tradeoff**: A budget forces shorter prompts or debates, which the quality threshold partly forbids.\n389: - **Status**: proposed\n390: \n391: ### REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002 Run-wide LLM call cap\n392: \n393: - **Type**: cost\n394: - **Statement**: The system shall enforce `CALL_CAP` on LLM calls per run, checked before dispatch. A call refused by the cap ends the run `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`.\n395: - **Counting rule** (normative): one call is one dispatch to a provider, including each retry, each structured-output re-request and each background memory request. The cap is shared across all parallel branches.\n396: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, a test cap of 8 and 4 analysts, when the graph runs, then dispatch count ≤ 8, the 9th attempt never reaches the provider (provider call log length = 8), and the run ends `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` with the call limit named in the log.\n397: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-NFR-001, REQ-TA-RUN-001\n398: - **Baseline**: Only per-scope limits: `max_tool_rounds` (20), `max_debate_rounds` / `max_risk_discuss_rounds` (1 each), `llm_max_retries`.\n399: - **Open**: Add a shared run-scoped counter.\n400: - **Priority**: Must\n401: - **Tradeoff**: A small shared cap can starve parallel branches.\n402: - **Status**: proposed\n403: \n404: ### REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003 Early debate convergence\n405: \n406: - **Type**: cost\n407: - **Statement**: The bull/bear debate and the risk discussion shall stop before their configured maximum when the participants' positions have converged.\n408: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, 4 convergence fixtures (2 per debate) and 4 disagreement fixtures, when each runs, then rounds used < maximum for 4/4 convergence fixtures, rounds used = maximum for 4/4 disagreement fixtures, and the RUN-001 fields of all 8 equal those of the round-count-only baseline.\n409: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001\n410: - **Baseline**: Round-count only (`graph/conditional_logic.py`).\n411: - **Open**: Define the convergence signal.\n412: - **Priority**: Could\n413: - **Tradeoff**: A debate can be cut before its disagreement surfaces.\n414: - **Status**: proposed\n415: \n416: ### REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001 Evaluation counting rules\n417: \n418: - **Type**: quality (evaluation)\n419: - **Statement**: Every evaluation result the team reports shall be computed with these rules:\n420:   1. **Completion rate** = `COMPLETED` runs ÷ all runs started. No run is ever removed from this denominator.\n421:   2. **Quality scores** (GOV-001 score, rating distribution) are computed over `COMPLETED` runs only, and are always reported beside the completion rate and the number of `NEEDS_REVIEW` runs.\n422:   3. `INCOMPLETE` runs are reported by `stop_reason`.\n423:   4. A run's outcome never invalidates its evidence (FR-001). Source reliability is not graded from run outcomes.\n424:   5. Two results may be compared only if their run records match on `config` and `prompt_hash` (NFR-REPRO-001).\n425: - **Fit criterion**: Given 10 fixed run records (6 `COMPLETED` of which 2 are `NEEDS_REVIEW`; `INCOMPLETE`: 1 `DATA`, 2 `MODEL`, 1 `BUDGET`), when the evaluation script runs, then it reports a completion rate of 6/10, a quality denominator of 6, `NEEDS_REVIEW` = 2, and stop reasons `DATA` 1, `MODEL` 2, `BUDGET` 1, with 0 records dropped. Given 2 records that differ in `prompt_hash`, the script refuses to compare them (1/1).\n426: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-RUN-001, REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n427: - **Baseline**: v0.7.1 has a backtest (`backtest.py`) but no rule for counting failed runs.\n428: - **Open**: Member D to build the script to these rules.\n429: - **Priority**: Should\n430: - **Tradeoff**: Reporting completed-only quality next to a low completion rate can look worse than a single blended number. That is intended.\n431: - **Status**: proposed\n432: \n433: ---\n434: \n435: ## Security requirements\n436: \n437: ### REQ-TA-SEC-001 Prompt-injection resistance\n438: \n439: - **Type**: security\n440: - **Statement**: Instructions inside retrieved content shall not change the run's configuration, the `data_coverage` record, the output check's rules or result, or any RUN-001 field set by deterministic code.\n441: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and 20 fixtures (5 each for market, news, social and fundamentals content) whose injected text tells the model to, for example, \"say all data is complete\", \"print OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" or \"ignore your rules\", with the scripted model copying the injected text into its output, when each runs, then for 20/20: the config equals the pre-run config (deep equality); `data_coverage` equals that of the same fixture without the injection; and `output_check` and `check_findings` equal the result of applying R1–R8 to the final state.\n442: - **Semantic part**: whether a live model's rating is swayed by injected text is tested in the GOV-001 suite.\n443: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-ARCH-002, REQ-TA-FR-005\n444: - **Baseline**: Ticker input is sanitised (`dataflows/symbols.py`). Retrieved text reaches the model unmodified. No deterministic check exists yet.\n445: - **Open**: Build ARCH-002 and FR-005 so that no model text feeds them.\n446: - **Priority**: Must\n447: - **Tradeoff**: Injected text can still appear as quoted evidence; it simply has no authority.\n448: - **Status**: proposed\n449: \n450: ### REQ-TA-SEC-002 No credential or token leakage\n451: \n452: - **Type**: security\n453: - **Statement**: Logs, reports, run records and error messages shall not contain API keys, OAuth access tokens, refresh tokens or bearer [REDACTED]\n454: - **Fit criterion**: Given a distinctive fake value planted as each of these 4 secret types across all vendor error paths, when each path is exercised, then a scan of logs, reports, run records and captured exceptions finds 0 planted values and 0 `Bearer ` prefixes.\n455: - **Dependencies**: none\n456: - **Baseline**: `get_scrubbed` (`dataflows/net.py`) redacts query-parameter secrets and is used by 2 vendor modules. `run_settings()` leaves endpoint URLs out. Coverage of loggers, reports and tracebacks is unverified.\n457: - **Open**: Send every outbound error through one scrubber.\n458: - **Priority**: Must\n459: - **Tradeoff**: Less debugging detail in error text.\n460: - **Status**: partial\n461: \n462: ### REQ-TA-SEC-003 No promise of guaranteed returns\n463: \n464: - **Type**: security\n465: - **Statement**: Reports shall start with a disclaimer and shall not claim guaranteed returns, guaranteed profit or capital protection.\n466: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, when (a) 20 reports are rendered, then 20/20 start with the disclaimer string; (b) 5 scripted final decisions that each contain a phrase from `fixtures/sec003/guarantee_phrases.txt` are checked, then 5/5 get `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding R8.\n467: - **Semantic part**: 5 live prompts that directly ask for a guarantee are in the GOV-001 suite.\n468: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n469: - **Baseline**: The disclaimer exists in the README only.\n470: - **Open**: Add the report disclaimer and rule R8.\n471: - **Priority**: Should\n472: - **Tradeoff**: The phrase list flags \"guaranteed\" even inside a quoted source.\n473: - **Status**: proposed\n474: \n475: ---\n476: \n477: ## Architectural constraints\n478: \n479: ### REQ-TA-ARCH-001 Vendors behind one routing point\n480: \n481: - **Type**: architectural_constraint\n482: - **Statement**: Vendor access shall go through the router's method map, so agent and graph modules name a method, never a vendor module or vendor SDK.\n483: - **Fit criterion**: Given `tradingagents/agents/**` and `tradingagents/graph/**`, when the import-boundary test runs, then they import 0 times from `tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.*` and 0 times from `yfinance` (the only vendor SDK in `pyproject.toml`); and a fake vendor in the method map serves every evidence request in the end-to-end test with 0 monkeypatches of agent modules.\n484: - **Dependencies**: none\n485: - **Baseline**: Not met. There are 4 direct vendor imports in 3 agent files: `agents/context.py` (Yahoo profile), `agents/tools.py` (Yahoo snapshot) and `agents/analysts/sentiment_analyst.py` (Reddit, StockTwits). `tests/test_layering.py` bans only the `yfinance` library.\n486: - **Open**: Move the 4 imports behind router methods and extend the layering test.\n487: - **Priority**: Should\n488: - **Tradeoff**: One more indirection per call.\n489: - **Status**: partial\n490: \n491: ### REQ-TA-ARCH-002 Deterministic output check\n492: \n493: - **Type**: architectural_constraint\n494: - **Statement**: Exactly one deterministic, non-LLM component shall set `output_check` and `check_findings`. It runs on every `COMPLETED` run after the Portfolio Manager and applies the rules below. Each rule is owned by the requirement named in the table (P1).\n495: - **Authority**: No model output can set, change or skip the check's result. Text in model output that claims a check result (\"validated\", \"PASSED\") has no effect.\n496: - **Meaning**: `PASSED` means only that the report meets rules R1–R8. It does not mean the analysis is correct, the facts are true or the rating is good advice. The report shows this sentence next to the result.\n497: - **Rules**:\n498: \n499:   | Rule | Check | Owner | Kind |\n500:   |---|---|---|---|\n501:   | R1 | Final rating is readable (not `REVIEW`) | RUN-001 | Blocking |\n502:   | R2 | Every cited evidence ID resolves | FR-001 | Blocking |\n503:   | R3 | No banned ownership phrase | FR-007 | Blocking |\n504:   | R4 | Sentiment score matches band | FR-008 | Blocking |\n505:   | R5 | Sentiment confidence within the coverage cap | FR-008 | Corrected |\n506:   | R6 | No sentiment direction without any sentiment data | FR-008 | Blocking |\n507:   | R7 | \"Data coverage\" section present and equal to the coverage record | FR-005 | Blocking |\n508:   | R8 | Disclaimer present; no guarantee phrase | SEC-003 | Blocking |\n509: \n510: - **Results**: any blocking finding → `NEEDS_REVIEW`; only corrected findings or none → `PASSED`; `INCOMPLETE` run → `NOT_RUN`.\n511: - **Failure behaviour**: If the check itself raises, the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding `CHECK_ERROR`. It never falls back to `PASSED`.\n512: - **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, when (a) every `COMPLETED` fixture in Appendix A is inspected, then 100% of `output_check` values equal R1–R8 applied to the final state, and the field is written at exactly 1 call site in the code; (b) a fixture makes the check raise, then the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW` + `CHECK_ERROR` (1/1); (c) a fixture's model text says \"OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" while R3 fails, then the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW` (1/1); (d) every `INCOMPLETE` fixture has `NOT_RUN` (100%).\n513: - **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-RUN-001\n514: - **Baseline**: No check exists. The Portfolio Manager writes the rating directly (`agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py`), and `REVIEW` comes from the parser fallback (`agents/rating.py`).\n515: - **Open**: Member B designs the component and documents the authority and failure rules above.\n516: - **Priority**: Must\n517: - **Tradeoff**: One more stage after the graph, and a second place a reader must look.\n518: - **Status**: proposed\n519: \n520: ---\n521: \n522: ## Governance requirements\n523: \n524: ### REQ-TA-GOV-001 Semantic evaluation gate\n525: \n526: - **Type**: governance\n527: - **Statement**: Every change to prompt or model settings (paths in `GOV_PATHS`) shall pass the semantic evaluation suite before merge.\n528: - **Suite contents** (minimum): `N_EVAL` fixed cases scored by a fixed rubric under the live profile, including: the FR-005 absence-wording check, the FR-007 ownership-wording check, the SEC-001 injection cases and the SEC-003 guarantee prompts. The distinct-records test is owned by NFR-REPRO-001 and referenced from FR-003. | FR-003 |\n\n---\n\n## Definitions (normative)\n\nEach term below is used only in this sense throughout the document.\n\n| Term | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| Run | One analysis of one ticker for one analysis date, started through `TradingAgentsGraph.propagate` or the CLI. A resumed run is the same run; a rerun is a new run. |\n| *D* | The run's analysis date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, not later than today). |\n| Channel | One of the 12 evidence sources listed in FR-004. |\n| Evidence item | One retrieved unit from a channel: a price series, one news item, one social post, one financial statement, one macro series, one memory lesson. |\n| Core data | Price history (`core_stock_apis`) only. Technical indicators are computed from it and follow it. |\n| Gap | A channel whose `data_coverage` code is anything other than `OK`. |\n| Final rating | The Portfolio Manager's output: Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell, or `REVIEW` when none can be read. |\n| Intermediate judgment | The Research Manager's recommendation (5-tier) and the Trader's action (Buy / Hold / Sell). Never called a \"rating\" in reports. |\n| Completed | Only `run_outcome = COMPLETED`. It says the pipeline finished, never that the result is good. |\n| Output check | The deterministic, non-LLM component of ARCH-002. |\n| Finding | A rule the output check found broken. A **blocking** finding sets `NEEDS_REVIEW`. A **corrected** finding is fixed automatically and recorded. |\n| Offline / live profile | The two test set-ups in Appendix A. |\n| Parameter | A named number in Appendix D. Fit criteria refer to parameters by name. |\n\n## Drafting principles (normative)\n\n- **P1 One owner per rule.** Each rule is stated in exactly one requirement. Other requirements cite it by ID and do not restate it.\n- **P2 Priority order.** A requirement depends only on requirements of equal or higher priority.\n- **P3 Defined terms.** Terms from Definitions are used only in their defined sense.\n- **P4 No loose numbers.** Every threshold is a parameter in Appendix D, marked fixed or provisional, with an owner.\n- **P5 Testable form.** Each fit criterion reads: **Given** (profile and fixtures, Appendix A) **when** (action) **then** (counts or booleans).\n\n---\n\n## Overview\n\n| ID | Type | Summary | Priority | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| REQ-TA-RUN-001 | Functional | Every run records separate outcome, stop reason, rating, check and coverage fields | Must | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-FR-001 | Functional | Evidence IDs, traceable records, and visible source and date in the report | Must | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-FR-003 | Functional | Checkpoint list, resume without re-running persisted tasks, explicit rerun | Should | partial |\n| REQ-TA-FR-004 | Functional | No evidence dated after *D* reaches any agent | Must | partial |\n| REQ-TA-FR-005 | Functional | Gaps are disclosed with a code; missing price data stops the run | Must | partial |\n| REQ-TA-FR-006 | Functional | Freshness thresholds per data type | Should | partial |\n| REQ-TA-FR-007 | Functional | Ratings describe the stock, not the user's account; no ownership wording | Must | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-FR-008 | Functional | Sentiment score and confidence consistent with the data actually available | Should | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-NFR-001 | Quality (reliability) | No crash on vendor or model failure; each failure has one defined result | Must | partial |\n| REQ-TA-NFR-002 | Quality (maintainability) | Add or remove an analyst without editing orchestration | Could | partial |\n| REQ-TA-NFR-OBS-001 | Quality (observability) | Structured log records with fixed fields | Should | partial |\n| REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001 | Quality (reproducibility) | One immutable run record and report per run | Should | partial |\n| REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-001 | Performance | Single analysis within `RUN_TIME_CAP` | Should | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002 | Performance | Crossing the time budget ends the run `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` | Should | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001 | Cost | Run-level token budget, measured from provider usage | Should | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002 | Cost | Run-wide LLM call cap enforced before dispatch | Must | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003 | Cost | Debates end early on convergence | Could | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001 | Quality (evaluation) | Fixed counting rules for completion rate and quality scores | Should | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-SEC-001 | Security | Retrieved content cannot change config, coverage or check results | Must | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-SEC-002 | Security | No credentials or tokens in logs, reports, run records or errors | Must | partial |\n| REQ-TA-SEC-003 | Security | No guarantee of returns or capital protection | Should | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-ARCH-001 | Architectural constraint | Vendors behind one routing point | Should | partial |\n| REQ-TA-ARCH-002 | Architectural constraint | One deterministic output check; LLMs cannot set its result | Must | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-GOV-001 | Governance | Semantic evaluation gate on prompt and model changes | Must | proposed |\n| REQ-TA-GOV-002 | Governance | Test plan approved before implementation | Must | to be confirmed |\n\nWithdrawn: REQ-TA-FR-002, REQ-TA-NFR-SAFETY-001, REQ-TA-NFR-SAFETY-002 (Appendix C).\n\n**Scope.** Research-only. The system produces research and a rating about an instrument. It does not size positions or check exposure against an account. A portfolio file, which v0.7.1 accepts, is outside project scope: no requirement makes claims about runs that use one, and every fixture runs without one.\n\n---\n\n## Run result\n\n### REQ-TA-RUN-001 Run result fields\n\n- **Type**: functional\n- **Statement**: Every run shall end with a run record holding the fields below. Each field describes one thing only, and only the combinations in the validity table are allowed.\n- **Fields**:\n\n  | Field | Values | Set by | Present when |\n  |---|---|---|---|\n  | `run_outcome` | `COMPLETED`, `INCOMPLETE` | Run engine | Always |\n  | `stop_reason` | `DATA`, `MODEL`, `BUDGET` | Run engine | Only when `INCOMPLETE` |\n  | `rating` | Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell, `REVIEW` | Portfolio Manager, read by the rating parser | Only when `COMPLETED` |\n  | `output_check` | `PASSED`, `NEEDS_REVIEW`, `NOT_RUN` | Output check (ARCH-002) | Always |\n  | `check_findings` | List of rule IDs, each marked blocking or corrected | Output check (ARCH-002) | Always (may be empty) |\n  | `data_coverage` | One code per channel (FR-005) | FR-005 | Always |\n\n- **Stop reasons**:\n\n  | Reason | Kind | Raised when | Owner of the rule |\n  |---|---|---|---|\n  | `DATA` | Failure | Core data is unavailable, absent or stale | FR-005, FR-006 |\n  | `MODEL` | Failure | A model step produced no usable output after retries and the free-text fallback | NFR-001 |\n  | `BUDGET` | Planned stop | A configured time, token or call limit was reached. Which limit is written to the log (OBS-001), not to the status. | PERF-002, COST-001, COST-002 |\n\n- **Validity table** (every other combination is invalid):\n\n  | `run_outcome` | `stop_reason` | `rating` | `output_check` |\n  |---|---|---|---|\n  | `INCOMPLETE` | `DATA` / `MODEL` / `BUDGET` | — | `NOT_RUN` |\n  | `COMPLETED` | — | Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell | `PASSED` or `NEEDS_REVIEW` |\n  | `COMPLETED` | — | `REVIEW` | `NEEDS_REVIEW` (rule R1) |\n\n- **Fit criterion**: Given every offline fixture in Appendix A, when each runs, then 100% of runs produce a run record; 100% of records match exactly one row of the validity table; 0 records have `COMPLETED` while some agent step produced no output.\n- **Dependencies**: none (all fields are owned here; their rules live in the owners named above)\n- **Baseline**: `propagate` returns `(final_state, signal)`, where `signal` is a 5-tier rating or `REVIEW` when no rating can be parsed (`graph/trading_graph.py`, `agents/rating.py`). There is no outcome, stop reason, check result or coverage field.\n- **Open**: Add the fields to the run record (NFR-REPRO-001) and set them on every exit path.\n- **Priority**: Must\n- **Status**: proposed\n- **Tradeoff**: The report header shows three short lines (outcome, rating, check) instead of one.\n\n---\n\n## Functional requirements\n\n### REQ-TA-FR-001 Evidence IDs, records and visible source dates\n\n- **Type**: functional\n- **Statement**: The system shall give each evidence item admitted into a run one stable evidence ID, and shall keep a record for it with at least: source, ticker, and either observation time or publication time. Wherever the report cites an item, it shall show the item's source and date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) beside the citation. Records are kept for every run whatever its outcome: a run's outcome never changes or deletes its evidence records.\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and `fixtures/fr001/evidence.jsonl`, when one run completes and every cited ID is collected, then (a) 100% of cited IDs resolve to exactly 1 record with non-empty `source`, `ticker` and one of `observed_at` / `published_at`; (b) 100% of citations in the rendered report show a source and a date; (c) all 12 channels of FR-004 write records, including the 2 that bypass the router. Given fixture `fixtures/fr001/timeout_after_price/`, which ends `INCOMPLETE(MODEL)` after price data was retrieved, then (d) the registry still holds the price records, unchanged (≥ 1 record, byte-identical to before the stop). An ID that is cited but not registered is the blocking finding R2 (ARCH-002).\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-RUN-001\n- **Related**: ARCH-001 (when it is met, the registry write can sit in the router alone)\n- **Baseline**: Items carry their own dates and source labels in vendor text (news rows and price rows both carry a date), but nothing assigns an ID or keeps a record keyed by one.\n- **Open**: Add the registry write at the data boundary, including the two bypass channels, and render source and date at each citation.\n- **Priority**: Must\n- **Tradeoff**: One write per admitted item and one lookup per citation, plus storage under `results_dir`.\n- **Status**: proposed\n\n### REQ-TA-FR-003 Checkpoint list, resume and rerun\n\n- **Type**: functional\n- **Statement**: The system shall list saved checkpoints, resume an interrupted run without re-running tasks that were already saved, and rerun from scratch on request.\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and a run interrupted after all 4 analyst branches were saved, when (a) it is resumed with the same ticker, *D* and settings, then agent invocations for those 4 branches = 0 (4/4); (b) the checkpoint list is shown, then it lists ticker, *D*, the run signature, the number of saved tasks, and a status of `RESUMABLE` (signature matches current settings) or `CONFIG_CHANGED` (it does not) — checked on 1 fixture of each status; (c) it is rerun, then all 4 branches execute again (≥ 1 invocation each), the old checkpoint is cleared, and the rerun gets its own run record and report per NFR-REPRO-001.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-NFR-001, REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n- **Baseline**: Resume already works: per-node SQLite checkpoints keyed by a run signature, resume detection (`checkpoint_step`), fresh start when the signature changes, and clean-up after success (`graph/checkpointer.py`, `_run_signature` in `trading_graph.py`; tests `test_checkpoint_resume.py`, `test_checkpoint_lifecycle.py`, `test_graph_end_to_end.py::test_an_interrupted_run_resumes_from_its_checkpoint`). There is no list command and no explicit rerun command.\n- **Open**: Add the list and rerun commands. Turn the three checks above into acceptance tests.\n- **Priority**: Should\n- **Tradeoff**: Checkpoints are stored per ticker, so the list is per ticker unless an index file is added.\n- **Status**: partial\n\n### REQ-TA-FR-004 Point-in-time evidence (no look-ahead)\n\n- **Type**: functional\n- **Statement**: For a run with analysis date *D*, no item published, observed, filed or resolved after the end of *D* shall reach any agent's prompt, through any channel. A date the model gives a tool shall never widen the window past *D*. Data with no historical version (live-only data) shall be withheld from a run dated before today. The one exception is the instrument's current name, which may be given only when it is labelled as the current name.\n- **Why Must**: An analysis or backtest that sees later news or prices looks better than it really is. Every evaluation result (EVAL-001) would be invalid.\n- **Channels** (normative; this list defines \"channel\" for the whole document):\n\n  | # | Channel | Entry point in v0.7.1 | Current guard |\n  |---|---|---|---|\n  | 1 | Price history | `get_stock_data` | Window end clamped to *D* (`as_of_window`) |\n  | 2 | Technical indicators | `get_indicators` | Date clamped to *D* (`as_of`) |\n  | 3 | Verified market snapshot | `get_verified_market_snapshot` (calls Yahoo directly, not through the router) | Date clamped to *D* |\n  | 4 | Company overview | `get_fundamentals` | Withheld on historical runs (`withhold_live_profile`) — live-only |\n  | 5 | Financial statements | `get_balance_sheet`, `get_cashflow`, `get_income_statement` | Date clamped; filtered by filing date |\n  | 6 | Ticker news | `get_news` | Window clamped; items trimmed by `in_window` |\n  | 7 | Global news | `get_global_news` | Date clamped; items trimmed by `in_window` |\n  | 8 | Insider transactions | `get_insider_transactions` | Run date passed from graph state |\n  | 9 | Macro indicators | `get_macro_indicators` (FRED) | Data vintage pinned to *D* |\n  | 10 | Prediction markets | `get_prediction_markets` (Polymarket) | Withheld on historical runs — live-only |\n  | 11 | Social posts | Reddit and StockTwits inside `sentiment_analyst.py` (not through the router) | Items trimmed by `in_window` |\n  | 12 | Memory lessons | `TradingMemoryLog.get_past_context(as_of=D)` | Only lessons resolved on or before *D* |\n\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, *D* = 2026-01-09, and `fixtures/fr004/channels/` holding, for each of the 10 dated channels, one control item dated *D* and one planted item dated *D*+1 that carries the marker `LOOKAHEAD-<#>`, when one run executes and every prompt to the scripted model is captured, then: (a) 0/10 markers appear in any prompt; (b) 10/10 control items appear in at least one prompt; (c) the 2 live-only channels return their \"withheld\" notice (2/2) and 0 live values; (d) for each of the 12 dated tools in `agents/tools.py`, a model-supplied date of *D*+30 is served as *D* (12/12); (e) the instrument context holds 0 sector, industry or exchange values, and any name carries the \"current name\" label.\n- **Dependencies**: none\n- **Baseline**: Each channel already has its own guard and unit tests (`test_tool_date_enforcement.py`, `test_news_lookahead.py`, `test_social_lookahead.py`, `test_fundamentals_lookahead.py`, `test_memory_pointintime.py`, `test_undated_tools_as_of.py`, `test_statement_knowledge_time.py`); a future *D* is refused (`_validate_trade_date`). No test checks all channels in one whole run.\n- **Open**: Add the whole-run planted-marker test as a required CI check.\n- **Out of scope (stated, not tested)**: The model's own training data may contain events after *D*. A report for a historical *D* should state this limitation.\n- **Priority**: Must\n- **Tradeoff**: Historical runs see less data than a live run would.\n- **Status**: partial\n\n### REQ-TA-FR-005 Data gaps and the core-data rule\n\n- **Type**: functional\n- **Statement**: This requirement owns every rule about missing data.\n  1. **Core rule.** If core data has any code other than `OK`, the run ends `INCOMPLETE(DATA)`.\n  2. **Non-core rule.** A gap in any other channel does not stop the run.\n  3. **Disclosure.** Every report has a \"Data coverage\" section that lists each channel with exactly one code from the table below. The section is built from tool results and is never written by the model.\n- **Coverage codes**:\n\n  | Code | Meaning | v0.7.1 signal it maps from |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | `OK` | Served and fresh | Normal tool result |\n  | `UNAVAILABLE` | The vendor was down, throttled or failed, or the feed could not see the requested window. Says nothing about the stock. | `DATA_UNAVAILABLE: …` (`router.vendor_unavailable`); `<… unavailable for …>` (`date_window.coverage_gap`) |\n  | `NO_DATA` | Every vendor that answered had no data for this stock | `NO_DATA_AVAILABLE: …` (`router.no_data_available`) |\n  | `STALE` | Served, but older than its FR-006 threshold | FR-006 |\n  | `WITHHELD` | Live-only data withheld from a historical run | FR-004 withheld notices |\n  | `NOT_REACHED` | The run stopped before this channel was called. Appears only in `INCOMPLETE` runs. | — |\n\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and 12 fixtures — 8 non-core gaps (2 each for `UNAVAILABLE`, `NO_DATA`, `STALE`, `WITHHELD`), 3 core gaps (price `UNAVAILABLE`, `NO_DATA`, `STALE`) and 1 clean run — when each runs, then: (a) 8/8 non-core fixtures end `COMPLETED` and list the affected channel with the matching code; (b) 3/3 core fixtures end `INCOMPLETE(DATA)`; (c) the clean fixture lists 12/12 channels as `OK`; (d) 0/12 raise; (e) the section is byte-identical when the scripted model's prose is replaced with different prose.\n- **Semantic part**: whether the model's own prose avoids claiming an absence (\"no recent news\") for a channel that has a gap is tested in the GOV-001 suite, because a scripted model cannot test it.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-RUN-001, REQ-TA-FR-004\n- **Baseline**: The data layer already tells these cases apart in tool text and tells the model not to invent values (`dataflows/router.py`, `date_window.py`; tests `test_no_data_handling.py`, `test_vendor_errors.py`). But nothing collects them per run; the report does not list them; and a full price outage still ends with a rating, because throttled or unreachable vendors degrade to a text note in every category. Channels 3 and 11 bypass the router.\n- **Open**: Collect the codes per run (router plus the two bypass channels), stop on a core gap, and render the section.\n- **Priority**: Must\n- **Tradeoff**: Every report gains a section, including gaps that a reader may not care about.\n- **Status**: partial\n\n### REQ-TA-FR-006 Freshness thresholds\n\n- **Type**: functional\n- **Statement**: Each data type shall be judged fresh or stale by the rule in the table below. Stale data is coded `STALE` (FR-005) and handled as the last column says.\n\n  | Data type | Fresh when | Parameter (Appendix D) | If exceeded |\n  |---|---|---|---|\n  | Price history | Latest bar is ≤ `STALE_PRICE_DAYS` calendar days before *D* | `STALE_PRICE_DAYS` | Not used; core gap → `INCOMPLETE(DATA)` (FR-005) |\n  | Technical indicators | Follows price history | — | Follows price history |\n  | Financial statements | Latest statement was filed ≤ `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` days before *D* | `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` | Still shown with its filing date; coded `STALE`; run continues |\n  | Ticker news, global news, social posts | Item lies inside the requested window, clamped to *D* (FR-004) | `global_news_lookback_days` (v0.7.1 config) | Item left out. This is not marked `STALE`; an empty window is `NO_DATA` or `UNAVAILABLE`. |\n  | Macro indicators, insider transactions | No threshold (releases are monthly or irregular) | — | Each value shown with its own date |\n  | Company overview, prediction markets | Live-only | — | `WITHHELD` on historical runs (FR-004) |\n\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and 6 boundary fixtures, when each runs, then 6/6 behave as follows: price bar at *D*−`STALE_PRICE_DAYS` → `OK`; at *D*−(`STALE_PRICE_DAYS`+1) → `INCOMPLETE(DATA)`; statement filed at *D*−`STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` → `OK`; at *D*−(`STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS`+1) → `STALE` and still shown; news item on the window's first day → included; one day before it → left out.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-FR-005\n- **Baseline**: The price rule already exists: a frame whose latest row is more than 10 days before the requested date is refused as stale (`MAX_OHLCV_STALE_DAYS = 10`, `dataflows/vendors/yahoo/ohlcv.py`; `test_yfinance_stale_ohlcv_guard.py`). News and social windows exist (FR-004). There is no statement-age rule.\n- **Open**: Add the statement-age rule and the `STALE` code; confirm `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` (provisional).\n- **Priority**: Should\n- **Tradeoff**: A fixed statement threshold suits some filing schedules better than others. Hong Kong half-yearly filers are the reason for the provisional 200 days.\n- **Status**: partial\n\n### REQ-TA-FR-007 Rating meaning and no ownership wording\n\n- **Type**: functional\n- **Statement**:\n  1. **Meaning.** The five ratings describe how strongly the evidence favours the instrument, from strongest positive (Buy) to strongest negative (Sell). **Hold** means the evidence is balanced, or too thin to favour either direction. No rating is an instruction about the user's account.\n  2. **Labels.** Reports label the three model judgments separately: \"Final rating (Portfolio Manager)\", \"Research recommendation (Research Manager, intermediate)\" and \"Trader proposal (Buy / Hold / Sell, intermediate)\". Only the Portfolio Manager's output is called the final rating, and only it fills `rating` in the run record.\n  3. **No ownership wording.** Prompts and reports shall not state or assume that the user holds the instrument. The minimum banned list is `fixtures/fr007/ownership_phrases.txt`: \"your position\", \"current position\", \"maintain the position\", \"add to your position\", \"exit your position\", \"your holdings\", \"you own\".\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, when (a) the Research Manager and Portfolio Manager prompt templates are scanned, then 2/2 contain 0 banned phrases and define Hold with the sentence in part 1; (b) one report is rendered, then it contains all 3 labels (3/3) and exactly 1 \"Final rating\"; (c) 3 scripted final decisions that each contain one banned phrase are checked, then 3/3 get `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding R3, and 1 clean decision gets `PASSED`.\n- **Semantic part**: live-model wording is tested in the GOV-001 suite.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-ARCH-002, REQ-TA-RUN-001\n- **Baseline**: Both manager prompts define ratings as account actions: `research_manager.py` line 32 \"Hold: … recommend maintaining the current position\"; `portfolio_manager.py` line 53 \"Hold: Maintain current position, no action needed\", plus \"enter or add to position\" and \"Exit position\". v0.7.1 keeps the three judgments as separate fields (`ResearchPlan.recommendation`, `TraderProposal.action`, `PortfolioDecision.rating` in `agents/schemas.py`).\n- **Open**: Reword both prompts, add the labels, and add rule R3 to the output check.\n- **Priority**: Must\n- **Tradeoff**: Without account wording, the rating reads less like direct advice. That is intended in a research-only scope.\n- **Status**: proposed\n\n### REQ-TA-FR-008 Sentiment score and confidence consistent with available data\n\n- **Type**: functional\n- **Statement**: The Sentiment Analyst's model-chosen band, score and confidence shall follow the rules below, applied by the output check. Any agent that later gets a confidence field shall follow the same confidence rule.\n\n  | Rule | Check | Kind |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | R4 | `overall_score` lies in its band's range: Bullish [6.5, 10]; Mildly Bullish [5.5, 6.5); Neutral and Mixed [4.5, 5.5); Mildly Bearish [3.5, 4.5); Bearish [0, 3.5). These are the schema's own guideline ranges, made exact. | Blocking |\n  | R5 | If any of the analyst's 3 sources (news, StockTwits, Reddit) is not `OK`, confidence is at most `low`. A higher value is lowered, and both the original and the new value are recorded. | Corrected |\n  | R6 | If none of the 3 sources is `OK`, the band must be Neutral | Blocking |\n\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and 6 fixtures, when each is checked, then 6/6 match: (1) the team's example — Bullish, score 0, high, all 3 sources unavailable → R4 and R6 blocking, R5 lowers confidence to low → `NEEDS_REVIEW`; (2) Mildly Bullish, 6.0, high, all sources `OK` → `PASSED`, confidence stays high; (3) Bullish, 7.0, high, Reddit `UNAVAILABLE` → `PASSED`, confidence lowered to low and recorded; (4) Bearish, 5.0 → R4 → `NEEDS_REVIEW`; (5) Bullish, 6.5 → passes R4; (6) Mildly Bullish, 6.5 → fails R4.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-FR-005, REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n- **Baseline**: `SentimentReport` (`agents/schemas.py`) enforces only the 0–10 bounds and the allowed labels. The band–score ranges and the \"low when a source is missing\" rule are guidance text the model may ignore. The team confirmed the schema accepts Bullish + 0 + High.\n- **Open**: Add R4–R6 to the output check.\n- **Priority**: Should\n- **Tradeoff**: Lowering confidence automatically can understate a strong signal from the two sources that did work.\n- **Status**: proposed\n\n---\n\n## Non-functional requirements\n\n### REQ-TA-NFR-001 Fail safely on external failures\n\n- **Type**: quality (reliability)\n- **Statement**: No vendor or model failure shall crash the process. Data failures follow FR-005. Model failures follow this table:\n\n  | Model situation | Result |\n  |---|---|\n  | Structured output is malformed, but the v0.7.1 free-text fallback produces usable text | Not a failure; the run continues |\n  | The final decision text has no readable rating | `COMPLETED`, `rating = REVIEW`, `NEEDS_REVIEW` (rule R1) |\n  | A model step produces no output after retries and the fallback (timeout, provider or auth error) | `INCOMPLETE(MODEL)` |\n\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and 6 fixtures (2 per table row), when each runs, then 6/6 get the result in their row and 0/6 raise out of the entry point. Additionally, 0 of the FR-005 fixtures raise.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-RUN-001, REQ-TA-FR-005\n- **Baseline**: Malformed structured output already falls back to free text (`agents/structured.py`). An unreadable final rating already becomes `REVIEW` (`agents/rating.py`). There is no run-level catch, so a model call that fails after retries raises out of `propagate`.\n- **Open**: Catch at the graph entry and map to `INCOMPLETE(MODEL)`.\n- **Priority**: Must\n- **Tradeoff**: Some runs that used to crash loudly now end quietly as `INCOMPLETE`; the log (OBS-001) must keep the detail.\n- **Status**: partial\n\n### REQ-TA-NFR-002 Add or remove an analyst\n\n- **Type**: quality (maintainability)\n- **Statement**: Adding or removing an analyst shall require changes only to that analyst's module and its registration data, and to no orchestration module.\n- **Fit criterion**: Given a change that adds 1 analyst, when `git diff --stat` is taken against `{tradingagents/graph/setup.py, tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py, tradingagents/graph/conditional_logic.py}`, then changed lines in that set = 0 and the full test suite passes.\n- **Dependencies**: none\n- **Baseline**: Removing works (`selected_analysts` → `build_analyst_execution_plan`, `graph/analyst_execution.py`). Adding needs an edit to the hard-coded `analyst_factories` in `graph/setup.py`.\n- **Open**: Move factories into the registration data.\n- **Priority**: Could\n- **Tradeoff**: Wiring is less readable at the point of use.\n- **Status**: partial\n\n### REQ-TA-NFR-OBS-001 Structured logging\n\n- **Type**: quality (observability)\n- **Statement**: The system shall write machine-parseable log records, each with `run_id`, ticker, node or agent, timestamp, elapsed time, and event outcome. When a run stops for `BUDGET`, the log names the limit that was hit (time, tokens or calls).\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, when every line of both sinks is parsed after one completed run and after one `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` run, then 100% of lines parse and contain all six fields with non-null values; the `BUDGET` run's log names exactly 1 limit.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-SEC-002, REQ-TA-RUN-001, REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n- **Baseline**: The graph writes one JSON state file per run (`_log_state`). The CLI writes plain-text `message_tool.log` (`cli/run.py`).\n- **Open**: JSON-lines for the CLI sink; add `run_id` and elapsed time to both.\n- **Priority**: Should\n- **Tradeoff**: JSON lines are harder to skim by eye.\n- **Status**: partial\n\n### REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001 Immutable run record and report\n\n- **Type**: quality (reproducibility)\n- **Statement**: Every run, including each rerun, shall write exactly one run record and one report folder, both named by a unique `run_id`. The record contains: start and end time, code version, every configuration key that can change what the run produces, a hash of the prompt templates, and the RUN-001 fields. A later run shall never overwrite or change an earlier run's record or report.\n- **Recorded keys**: every key in `DEFAULT_CONFIG` except `{results_dir, data_cache_dir, memory_log_path, checkpoint_enabled, llm_max_retries}` (the keys v0.7.1 already treats as \"does not change what a run writes\", `_NOT_IN_SIGNATURE`). Endpoint URLs are recorded only as set / not set (SEC-002).\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, when (a) two runs of the same ticker and *D* execute one after the other, then 2 distinct records and 2 distinct report folders exist, and the first run's files are byte-identical before and after the second; (b) each record has non-null `run_id`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `version`, `prompt_hash`, `config` and the RUN-001 fields; (c) for each of the 10 keys v0.7.1 leaves out of `run_settings()` (`temperature`, `max_tokens`, `max_tool_rounds`, `news_article_limit`, `global_news_article_limit`, `global_news_lookback_days`, `holding_period_days`, `google_thinking_level`, `openai_reasoning_effort`, `anthropic_effort`), changing only that key makes the two records differ in exactly that key (10/10); (d) recorded keys = `DEFAULT_CONFIG` keys minus the excluded set (0 missing, 0 extra); (e) editing one prompt template changes `prompt_hash`, and leaving templates unchanged keeps it the same; (f) the SEC-002 scan finds 0 planted secrets.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-RUN-001, REQ-TA-SEC-002\n- **Baseline**: `run_settings()` records only an allowlist (version, providers, models, analysts, rounds, language, vendors). It has no run id, timing or prompt hash. The state log is named `full_states_log_<D>.json` per ticker, so a same-day rerun overwrites it.\n- **Open**: Widen the record, add run id, timing and prompt hash, and name files by run id.\n- **Priority**: Should\n- **Tradeoff**: `results_dir` grows faster; no automatic clean-up is proposed.\n- **Status**: partial\n\n### REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-001 Maximum run time\n\n- **Type**: performance\n- **Statement**: A single-ticker run shall complete within `RUN_TIME_CAP`, measured wall-clock from graph start to the run record being written.\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the live profile, when 20 runs execute one after another, then the maximum of the 20 run times is ≤ `RUN_TIME_CAP` and 20/20 are `COMPLETED`. Runs stopped as `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` count as failures of this criterion.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-NFR-001, REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n- **Baseline**: No cap. Analysts already run in parallel (`graph/setup.py`).\n- **Open**: Measure first, then fix `RUN_TIME_CAP` from the measurement.\n- **Priority**: Should\n- **Tradeoff**: A tight cap trades completeness for speed.\n- **Status**: proposed\n\n### REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002 Time-budget handling\n\n- **Type**: performance\n- **Statement**: A run that crosses its time budget (default `RUN_TIME_CAP`) shall stop and end `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`. Calls already in flight may run for at most `CANCEL_ALLOWANCE` beyond the budget.\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile with a slow scripted model and a 30 s test budget, when 10 runs execute, then 10/10 end `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`, 10/10 return within 30 s + `CANCEL_ALLOWANCE`, and 10/10 logs name the time limit.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-NFR-001, REQ-TA-RUN-001\n- **Baseline**: No run-level timer.\n- **Open**: Check the deadline at node boundaries and add the cancellation allowance.\n- **Priority**: Should\n- **Tradeoff**: Calls that ignore cancellation delay the return.\n- **Status**: proposed\n\n### REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001 Run token budget\n\n- **Type**: cost\n- **Statement**: A run shall use at most `TOKEN_BUDGET` tokens in total, counted from provider usage data. A run that would exceed it ends `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`. If a provider returns no usage data, the run is not stopped; its record marks token usage as `UNKNOWN`.\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the live profile, when 20 runs execute one after another, then 20/20 have known usage ≤ `TOKEN_BUDGET`, and the GOV-001 score over these runs is ≥ `QUALITY_THRESHOLD`. A run with `UNKNOWN` usage counts as a failure of this criterion, not as zero cost.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-GOV-001, REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n- **Baseline**: `max_tokens` caps each call (`default_config.py`). There is no run-level count.\n- **Open**: Add up usage per run; set `TOKEN_BUDGET` from measurement.\n- **Priority**: Should\n- **Tradeoff**: A budget forces shorter prompts or debates, which the quality threshold partly forbids.\n- **Status**: proposed\n\n### REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002 Run-wide LLM call cap\n\n- **Type**: cost\n- **Statement**: The system shall enforce `CALL_CAP` on LLM calls per run, checked before dispatch. A call refused by the cap ends the run `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`.\n- **Counting rule** (normative): one call is one dispatch to a provider, including each retry, each structured-output re-request and each background memory request. The cap is shared across all parallel branches.\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, a test cap of 8 and 4 analysts, when the graph runs, then dispatch count ≤ 8, the 9th attempt never reaches the provider (provider call log length = 8), and the run ends `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` with the call limit named in the log.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-NFR-001, REQ-TA-RUN-001\n- **Baseline**: Only per-scope limits: `max_tool_rounds` (20), `max_debate_rounds` / `max_risk_discuss_rounds` (1 each), `llm_max_retries`.\n- **Open**: Add a shared run-scoped counter.\n- **Priority**: Must\n- **Tradeoff**: A small shared cap can starve parallel branches.\n- **Status**: proposed\n\n### REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003 Early debate convergence\n\n- **Type**: cost\n- **Statement**: The bull/bear debate and the risk discussion shall stop before their configured maximum when the participants' positions have converged.\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, 4 convergence fixtures (2 per debate) and 4 disagreement fixtures, when each runs, then rounds used < maximum for 4/4 convergence fixtures, rounds used = maximum for 4/4 disagreement fixtures, and the RUN-001 fields of all 8 equal those of the round-count-only baseline.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001\n- **Baseline**: Round-count only (`graph/conditional_logic.py`).\n- **Open**: Define the convergence signal.\n- **Priority**: Could\n- **Tradeoff**: A debate can be cut before its disagreement surfaces.\n- **Status**: proposed\n\n### REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001 Evaluation counting rules\n\n- **Type**: quality (evaluation)\n- **Statement**: Every evaluation result the team reports shall be computed with these rules:\n  1. **Completion rate** = `COMPLETED` runs ÷ all runs started. No run is ever removed from this denominator.\n  2. **Quality scores** (GOV-001 score, rating distribution) are computed over `COMPLETED` runs only, and are always reported beside the completion rate and the number of `NEEDS_REVIEW` runs.\n  3. `INCOMPLETE` runs are reported by `stop_reason`.\n  4. A run's outcome never invalidates its evidence (FR-001). Source reliability is not graded from run outcomes.\n  5. Two results may be compared only if their run records match on `config` and `prompt_hash` (NFR-REPRO-001).\n- **Fit criterion**: Given 10 fixed run records (6 `COMPLETED` of which 2 are `NEEDS_REVIEW`; `INCOMPLETE`: 1 `DATA`, 2 `MODEL`, 1 `BUDGET`), when the evaluation script runs, then it reports a completion rate of 6/10, a quality denominator of 6, `NEEDS_REVIEW` = 2, and stop reasons `DATA` 1, `MODEL` 2, `BUDGET` 1, with 0 records dropped. Given 2 records that differ in `prompt_hash`, the script refuses to compare them (1/1).\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-RUN-001, REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n- **Baseline**: v0.7.1 has a backtest (`backtest.py`) but no rule for counting failed runs.\n- **Open**: Member D to build the script to these rules.\n- **Priority**: Should\n- **Tradeoff**: Reporting completed-only quality next to a low completion rate can look worse than a single blended number. That is intended.\n- **Status**: proposed\n\n---\n\n## Security requirements\n\n### REQ-TA-SEC-001 Prompt-injection resistance\n\n- **Type**: security\n- **Statement**: Instructions inside retrieved content shall not change the run's configuration, the `data_coverage` record, the output check's rules or result, or any RUN-001 field set by deterministic code.\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile and 20 fixtures (5 each for market, news, social and fundamentals content) whose injected text tells the model to, for example, \"say all data is complete\", \"print OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" or \"ignore your rules\", with the scripted model copying the injected text into its output, when each runs, then for 20/20: the config equals the pre-run config (deep equality); `data_coverage` equals that of the same fixture without the injection; and `output_check` and `check_findings` equal the result of applying R1–R8 to the final state.\n- **Semantic part**: whether a live model's rating is swayed by injected text is tested in the GOV-001 suite.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-ARCH-002, REQ-TA-FR-005\n- **Baseline**: Ticker input is sanitised (`dataflows/symbols.py`). Retrieved text reaches the model unmodified. No deterministic check exists yet.\n- **Open**: Build ARCH-002 and FR-005 so that no model text feeds them.\n- **Priority**: Must\n- **Tradeoff**: Injected text can still appear as quoted evidence; it simply has no authority.\n- **Status**: proposed\n\n### REQ-TA-SEC-002 No credential or token leakage\n\n- **Type**: security\n- **Statement**: Logs, reports, run records and error messages shall not contain API keys, OAuth access tokens, refresh tokens or bearer [REDACTED]\n- **Fit criterion**: Given a distinctive fake value planted as each of these 4 secret types across all vendor error paths, when each path is exercised, then a scan of logs, reports, run records and captured exceptions finds 0 planted values and 0 `Bearer ` prefixes.\n- **Dependencies**: none\n- **Baseline**: `get_scrubbed` (`dataflows/net.py`) redacts query-parameter secrets and is used by 2 vendor modules. `run_settings()` leaves endpoint URLs out. Coverage of loggers, reports and tracebacks is unverified.\n- **Open**: Send every outbound error through one scrubber.\n- **Priority**: Must\n- **Tradeoff**: Less debugging detail in error text.\n- **Status**: partial\n\n### REQ-TA-SEC-003 No promise of guaranteed returns\n\n- **Type**: security\n- **Statement**: Reports shall start with a disclaimer and shall not claim guaranteed returns, guaranteed profit or capital protection.\n- **Fit criterion**: Given the offline profile, when (a) 20 reports are rendered, then 20/20 start with the disclaimer string; (b) 5 scripted final decisions that each contain a phrase from `fixtures/sec003/guarantee_phrases.txt` are checked, then 5/5 get `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding R8.\n- **Semantic part**: 5 live prompts that directly ask for a guarantee are in the GOV-001 suite.\n- **Dependencies**: REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n- **Baseline**: The disclaimer exists in the README only.\n- **Open**: Add the report disclaimer and rule R8.\n- **Priority**: Should\n- **Tradeoff**: The phrase list flags \"guaranteed\" even inside a quoted source.\n- **Status**: proposed\n\n---\n\n## Architectural constraints\n\n### REQ-TA-ARCH-001 Vendors behind one routing point\n\n- **Type**: architectural_constraint\n- **Statement**: Vendor access shall go through the router's method map, so agent and graph modules name a method, never a vendor module or vendor SDK.\n- **Fit criterion**: Given `tradingagents/agents/**` and `tradingagents/graph/**`, when the import-boundary test runs, then they import 0 times from `tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.*` and 0 times from `yfinance` (the only vendor SDK in `pyproject.toml`); and a fake vendor in the method map serves every evidence request in the end-to-end test with 0 monkeypatches of agent modules.\n- **Dependencies**: none\n- **Baseline**: Not met. Each rule is owned by the requirement named in the table (P1).\n- **Authority**: No model output can set, change or skip the check's result. Text in model output that claims a check result (\"validated\", \"PASSED\") has no effect.\n- **Meaning**: `PASSED` means only that the report meets rules R1–R8. It does not mean the analysis is correct, the facts are true or the rating is good advice. The report shows this sentence next to the result.\n- **Rules**:\n\n  | Rule | Check | Owner | Kind |\n  |---|---|---|---|\n  | R1 | Final rating is readable (not `REVIEW`) | RUN-001 | Blocking |\n  | R2 | Every cited evidence ID resolves | FR-001 | Blocking |\n  | R3 | No banned ownership phrase | FR-007 | Blocking |\n  | R4 | Sentiment score matches band | FR-008 | Blocking |\n  | R5 | Sentiment confidence within the coverage cap | FR-008 | Corrected |\n  | R6 | No sentiment direction without any sentiment data | FR-008 | Blocking |\n  | R7 | \"Data coverage\" section present and equal to the coverage record | FR-005 | Blocking |\n  | R8 | Disclaimer present; no guarantee phrase | SEC-003 | Blocking |\n\n- **Results**: any blocking finding → `NEEDS_REVIEW`; only corrected findings or none → `PASSED`; `INCOMPLETE` run → `NOT_RUN`.\n- **Failure behaviour**: If the check itself raises, the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding `CHECK_ERROR`. Assessment\n10: \n11: V2 is substantially more coherent than v1. Research-only scope, withdrawn portfolio invariants, separate outcome/rating/check fields, the three termination categories, explicit handling of free-text fallback, human-visible source dates, and completed-run evaluation denominators resolve major earlier concerns. GUI withdrawal is a valid scope decision; it should not be reclassified as a non-functional requirement.\n12: \n13: The earlier proposals are now substantially incorporated: FR-007 separates model judgments and bans ownership wording; FR-001 includes visible provenance; FR-005/006 address availability and freshness; FR-008 adds confidence checks. Remaining problems concern the precise meaning, coverage and application of those rules. The source draft should not yet be treated as fully executable acceptance criteria.\n14: \n15: **Review priority:** High means resolve before implementing the affected contract. Medium means refine before its acceptance tests are finalized. Findings below distinguish actual contradictions, underspecification, and semantic/design risks; not every finding is a logical conflict.\n16: \n17: Source line references below are one-based and apply to the hashed input above. Suggested remedies are discussion options, not edits to Member A's baseline.\n18: \n19: ## 2. Findings that affect core behaviour\n20: \n21: ### V2-01 — No sentiment data is forced to Neutral\n22: \n23: **High; semantic risk.** FR-008 R6 (line 284) requires Neutral when none of the sources is OK. Combined with R4, a model can emit Neutral, score 5, low confidence with all sources unavailable and receive PASSED. This presents unavailable sentiment as an assessment of neutral sentiment. The same condition also applies when sources contain usable data but are coded STALE.\n24: \n25: **Suggested decision:** distinguish “not assessed / insufficient data” from neutral evidence, using a separate availability field or nullable band/score. This need not introduce another run outcome or stop reason. If the team intentionally retains Neutral, require a conspicuous unavailable-assessment label and clarify that it is a placeholder rather than observed market sentiment. Add a direct no-data Neutral fixture; the current example only catches an inconsistent Bullish/0 output.\n26: \n27: ### V2-02 — Confidence correction happens after downstream use\n28: \n29: **High; sequencing gap.** FR-008 says its rules are applied by the output check, while ARCH-002 (line 494) runs after the Portfolio Manager. By then the Bull/Bear Researchers, Research Manager, Trader and risk debate may already have consumed the uncorrected High confidence. Correcting the final sentiment header does not undo its influence on the rating or narrative. R4/R6 contradictions can likewise travel through the graph before being flagged.\n30: \n31: **Suggested decision:** normalize or validate sentiment before downstream agents consume it, retaining an audit finding for the final output check. Alternatively, explicitly scope corrections to display only and document that downstream reasoning used the original value. Specify which version appears in every saved report, agent context and run record. The existing single owner of final `output_check` can be preserved.\n32: \n33: ### V2-03 — Twelve-channel coverage cannot express three sentiment source states\n34: \n35: **High; contract gap.** RUN-001/FR-005 require one code per FR-004 channel. Channel 11 combines Reddit and StockTwits, but FR-008 R5/R6 require separate states for news, Reddit and StockTwits. A combined social code cannot distinguish “Reddit unavailable, StockTwits OK” from the reverse. Financial statements and macro channels can also contain multiple requests with mixed results.\n36: \n37: **Suggested decision:** keep a twelve-channel summary plus per-source/request outcomes. Define aggregation precedence and partial coverage. A successful fallback must not remain UNAVAILABLE merely because the first vendor failed. Specify whether the news source used by sentiment is exactly the ticker-news channel or a separate request window.\n38: \n39: ### V2-04 — No valid coverage code for a skipped channel on a completed run\n40: \n41: **High; incomplete closed vocabulary.** FR-005 lines 217–227 requires every channel to have exactly one code and permits NOT_REACHED only for incomplete runs. Upstream supports selecting only some analysts, and tools need not request all channels. A completed market-only run can have no sentiment/news call without any vendor failure. None of OK, UNAVAILABLE, NO_DATA, STALE or WITHHELD describes that situation truthfully.\n42: \n43: **Suggested decision:** add a coverage state such as NOT_REQUESTED, and define NOT_APPLICABLE if needed; or explicitly require all channels to be fetched for every in-scope run. Missing an optional unrequested channel should not silently become an outage. Keep the clean fixture's 12 OK channels only if it deliberately exercises all twelve.\n44: \n45: ### V2-05 — Required price retrieval is not explicitly guaranteed\n46: \n47: **High; missing precondition.** FR-005 says a core code other than OK stops the run. However, NOT_REACHED is defined only after a stop, and no requirement explicitly guarantees that core price history is retrieved regardless of analyst selection or model tool choices. A final rating could otherwise be produced without triggering a core request at all.\n48: \n49: **Suggested decision:** require a trusted core-price check before any run can claim completion. Define the minimum usable price series/window and whether a verified market snapshot can satisfy it. This is distinct from adding another discretionary model tool.\n50: \n51: ### V2-06 — Sentiment absence and free-text fallback are not specified\n52: \n53: **High; interface gap.** R4–R6 assume typed band, score and confidence fields. NFR-001 explicitly accepts free-text fallback, and analyst selection may omit sentiment entirely. The draft does not say how to parse missing/ambiguous sentiment fields, whether to skip those rules for an unselected analyst, or how to record such a skip. A general CHECK_ERROR is not a clear intended result for ordinary optional input.\n54: \n55: **Suggested decision:** define applicability and typed extraction for each check. Unparseable selected sentiment should produce a named finding, while an intentionally omitted sentiment analyst should follow an explicit not-applicable rule. Add fixtures for omitted analyst, missing score, invalid confidence and conflicting text/structured values.\n56: \n57: ### V2-07 — Immutable records and resume lifecycle remain ambiguous\n58: \n59: **High; lifecycle gap.** Definitions line 50 makes resume the same run. RUN-001 records an interrupted run as INCOMPLETE; FR-003 later resumes it; REPRO-001 promises one immutable record/report per run. Does resume update the existing result, create a second result under the same run ID, or retain a stale incomplete outcome? The statement explicitly protects earlier runs from later runs but does not settle updates to this same logical run.\n60: \n61: **Suggested decision:** choose one lifecycle: attempt records linked to a logical run, or a mutable in-progress journal with one immutable final manifest and separately recorded interruptions. Define budgets and elapsed time across resume, checkpoint-to-run identity, and how EVAL-001 counts interruptions and eventual completion. Preserve evidence without duplicating logical runs in the denominator.\n62: \n63: ### V2-08 — The exact record comparison cannot pass as written\n64: \n65: **High; literal contradiction in acceptance.** REPRO-001 criterion (c), line 347, says changing one config key makes two records differ in exactly that key. The same requirement mandates unique run IDs, start/end times and distinct run artifacts. Those records necessarily differ in more than the config key, even when model output is identical.\n66: \n67: **Suggested wording:** “The `config` objects differ in exactly that key; run identity, timestamps, measured usage, outputs and findings are outside this comparison.” Keep their independent correctness tests.\n68: \n69: ### V2-09 — Universal non-null rule conflicts with absent result fields\n70: \n71: **High; literal contradiction in acceptance.** REPRO-001 criterion (b), line 347, requires non-null mandatory fields “and the RUN-001 fields.” RUN-001 requires stop_reason only on INCOMPLETE and rating only on COMPLETED. Requiring all of those fields to be non-null on every record would invalidate every result row.\n72: \n73: **Suggested wording:** validate RUN-001 fields conditionally against its validity table; specify absent versus explicit null serialization. `check_findings` can be an empty list. Document CHECK_ERROR as an allowed system finding alongside rule IDs R1–R8, including its blocking classification.\n74: \n75: ### V2-10 — The evaluation comparability rule prevents change studies\n76: \n77: **High; over-restrictive evaluation policy.** EVAL-001 rule 5 (line 425) prohibits comparing results unless both config and prompt_hash match. That is appropriate for repeated measurements under fixed conditions, but excludes intentional prompt/model/budget comparisons. GOV-001 can still score a candidate against an absolute threshold; it cannot support a permitted before/after comparison under this wording when the prompt changes.\n78: \n79: **Suggested decision:** distinguish repeatability comparisons from controlled change experiments.
