Proposed schema/interface (NEW; UNAPPROVED)\n89: \n90: First slice modules (out-of-tree standalone acceptable; paths proposed):\n91: \n92: - `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/__init__.py` — package (NEW; D implements, B contract, C tests, E wiring).\n93: - `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/facts.py` — `TrustedFact`/`FactBundle` + precision/unit policy (NEW).\n94: - `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/calculator.py` — registered relations over `Decimal` (NEW).\n95: - `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/claims.py` — claim model + (fixture-supplied) claim set (NEW).\n96: - `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/audit.py` — standalone audit over saved artifacts + supplied fixture (NEW).\n97: \n98: No existing production module is modified by the first slice.\n99: \n100: ### 4.1 `TrustedFact` / `FactBundle`\n101: \n102: ```\n103: FactSource = Literal[\n104:   \"supplied_run_fixture\",        # explicitly supplied, run-bound typed inputs (first slice)\n105:   \"verified_market_snapshot\",    # later: typed values derived from snapshot.py\n106:   \"fundamentals_statement\",      # later: statement facts with period/availability date\n107:   \"trader_proposed_level\",       # later: the Trader's *proposed* level (NOT verified market truth)\n108:   \"portfolio_user_supplied\",     # user-supplied holdings/cash (unverified)\n109: ]\n110: \n111: TrustedFact {\n112:   name: str\n113:   value: Decimal | None          # None = unknown (never coerced to 0)\n114:   unit: Literal[\"price\",\"points\",\"shares\",\"currency\",\"multiple\",\"percent\",\"ratio\"]\n115:   source: FactSource\n116:   source_id: str                 # e.g. snapshot row id / statement ref / \"user_input\"\n117:   availability_date: str         # ISO date the fact became knowable (must be <= run analysis date)\n118:   period: str | None             # explicit statement period end/label (not the run date)\n119:   run_analysis_date: str         # the run's analysis date\n120:   declared_precision: int        # digits after decimal the claim may rely on\n121:   verified: bool                 # True only for externally-verifiable sources; user/model inputs are False\n122: }\n123: \n124: FactBundle {\n125:   run_id: str; ticker: str; analysis_date: str\n126:   fingerprint_sha256: str | None # frozen portfolio fingerprint when portfolio-derived (else None)\n127:   source_revision: str; prompt_hash: str\n128:   facts: list[TrustedFact]\n129: }\n130: ```\n131: \n132: Rules: unknown `value` is `None` (never `0`); `availability_date` must be `<=` the run analysis date (a post-cutoff fact is excluded); `period` and `availability_date` are distinct from the run date; `verified=False` for user-supplied holdings and for model-proposed levels. Portfolio **quantity is user-supplied/unverified**. The bundle binds to the frozen `RunContext` (provenance per [INV-04/05](../invariants.md)).\n133: \n134: ### 4.2 `NumericClaim` (a detected relation) and calculator operations\n135: \n136: ```\n137: ClaimClass = Literal[\n138:   \"price_distance\",\"price_direction\",\"atr_distance\",\"atr_band\",\n139:   \"percent_with_denominator\",\"position_notional\",\"risk_reward\"\n140: ]\n141: \n142: OperandRef {\n143:   fact: str                      # fact name in the bundle\n144:   role: Literal[\"anchor\",\"level\",\"atr\",\"minuend\",\"subtrahend\",\"numerator\",\n145:                 \"denominator\",\"factor_min\",\"factor_max\",\"quantity\",\"price\"]\n146: }\n147: \n148: NumericClaim {\n149:   claim_id: str\n150:   class: ClaimClass\n151:   operands: list[OperandRef]     # roles make the relation explicit\n152:   asserted_unit: \"price|points|currency|percent|ratio|multiple\"\n153:   asserted_value: Decimal | None # single stated number, or...\n154:   asserted_range: tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None\n155:   asserted_direction: \"above|below|none\"   # for distance/direction claims\n156:   claim_precision: int           # digits after decimal the *claim* was stated at\n157:   anchor_evidence: str | None    # trusted reference linking a claim to its anchor claim, if any\n158:   stage: str                     # \"trader\" | \"portfolio_manager\" | \"research_manager\" | ...\n159:   stage_text_sha256: str         # hash of the stage prose the span indexes into\n160:   text_span: tuple[int,int]      # offsets into that stage prose (evidence; never rewritten)\n161:   extraction_provenance: \"supplied\" | \"deterministic\" | \"llm_assisted\"\n162: }\n163: ```\n164: \n165: A relation whose class is not registered, or whose operands cannot be bound, is `UNSUPPORTED` (the class exists as a typed marker even if the *specific* relation is unregistered; no impossible enum value). A claim with ambiguous extraction, unknown `claim_precision`, or missing `anchor_evidence` for an associated band is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n166: \n167: **Operations (fixed registry):** `subtract(minuend, subtrahend)`, `abs_distance(anchor, level)`, `direction(anchor, level)`, `divide_positive(numerator, denominator)` (denominator must be `> 0`), `scaled_band(factor_min, factor_max, atr)`. Each op declares its operand roles and result unit. The calculator **verifies the relation relative to the specified operands**; it does not assert that those operands are the true or complete facts.\n168: \n169: ### 4.3 `ComputedResult` (proposal; NOT Q1–Q4)\n170: \n171: ```\n172: CoverageStatus = Literal[\"VERIFIED\",\"MISMATCH\",\"NOT_VERIFIABLE\",\"UNSUPPORTED\"]\n173: \n174: ComputedResult {\n175:   claim_id: str\n176:   computed_value: Decimal | None\n177:   computed_range: tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None\n178:   computed_unit: ...\n179:   expected_at_claim_precision: Decimal | tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None  # round-half-up of computed at claim_precision\n180:   status: CoverageStatus\n181:   source_facts: list[str]\n182:   notes: str     # e.g. \"missing atr\" / \"ambiguous 1.5 role\" / \"unregistered relation\"\n183: }\n184: ```\n185: \n186: **Do not reuse `CHECK_ERROR`** for a numerical semantic mismatch and **do not create a Q5 silently.** A later, A/C-approved change may add a proposal-only finding type (`NumericFinding { rule: \"NUMERIC\", ... }`); until then results live only in the standalone audit file.\n187: \n188: ### 4.4 Precision / rounding / tolerance policy (exact for the first slice)\n189: \n190: - **Arithmetic:** Python `Decimal` at **context precision 28**; no binary float in the calculator.\n191: - **Comparison rule (first slice): NO tolerance.** Compute exactly, **round half-up to the claim's declared `claim_precision`**, and require **equality** with the asserted value/range endpoints. A different rounded value is `MISMATCH`.\n192: - **Precision bounds per class (frozen; a claim outside its bound is rejected as `NOT_VERIFIABLE`):**\n193:   - `price_distance`, `atr_band` → allow `claim_precision` in `{0,1,2}`.\n194:   - `atr_distance` (multiple) → allow `claim_precision` in `{1,2,3,4}`.\n195:   - `price_direction` → no numeric precision (boolean).\n196: - **Unknown/ambiguous precision** (the prose does not state enough digits to pin `claim_precision`) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n197: - **Units:** the calculator refuses to combine operands of incompatible unit roles (e.g. a `factor_*` (multiple) with a `points` asserted unit) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE` unless trusted `anchor_evidence` explicitly links them as the same range claim, in which case they are compared as that claim (§4.5).\n198: - No caller-chosen wide tolerances are permitted in the first slice.\n199: \n200: ### 4.5 Worked examples under this policy (document examples, exact)\n201: \n202: - **Distance/direction (positive):** `anchor=258.47`, `level=255.33`, ATR `4.39`. `abs(258.47 − 255.33) = 3.14`; direction: `255.33 < 258.47` ⇒ **below**. Prose “≈3.14 points below” at `claim_precision=2` → expected `3.14` → `VERIFIED`.\n203: - **Direction (negative):** same anchors, prose says “above” → computed **below** ⇒ `asserted_direction` mismatch ⇒ `MISMATCH`.\n204: - **ATR multiple (positive at 2 dp):** `3.14 / 4.39 = 0.7152619576…`; round half-up to `claim_precision=2` → `0.72`. Prose “0.72×ATR” → `VERIFIED`.\n205: - **ATR multiple (boundary negative):** same, but prose “0.7153×ATR” at `claim_precision=4` → expected `0.7153` (round-half-up of `0.71526195…`) → `VERIFIED`; prose “0.72×ATR” is only valid at `claim_precision=2`. A prose that states `0.72` but declares precision 4 is inconsistent → `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (ambiguous precision), **not** silently accepted. This resolves the earlier `0.7153` vs `0.72` contradiction: the two are **different declared precisions**, compared by equality only at each claim's own precision.\n206: - **ATR band (positive):** `factor_min=1.5`, `factor_max=2`, `atr=4.39` → `1.5 × 4.39 = 6.585`, `2 × 4.39 = 8.78`. At `claim_precision=2`, round-half-up → expected band `(6.59, 8.78)`. Prose “6.59–8.78 points” → `VERIFIED`; prose “6.585–8.78” at precision 3 is outside the frozen bound for `atr_band` (max 2) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n207: - **ATR band (boundary negative):** prose “6.6–8.8 points” at `claim_precision=1`: expected (round-half-up) `(6.6, 8.8)` → `VERIFIED`; the **same** numbers claimed at precision 2 → expected `(6.59, 8.78)` ≠ `(6.60, 8.80)` → `MISMATCH`. Precision is part of the claim.\n208: - **PM band “1.5–8.8 points below the fill” (observed):** parsed literally, both endpoints are `points`, giving range `(1.5, 8.8)` points. If trusted `anchor_evidence` links it to the preceding `1.5–2×ATR` claim, compare against the expected band `(6.59, 8.78)` at precision 2 → `MISMATCH` (lower endpoint `1.5` ≠ `6.59`). If no trusted association exists, the first endpoint's role is ambiguous (`1.5` could be a factor) ⇒ `NOT_VERIFIABLE`. It is **not** universally a dimensional error; the auditor reports `MISMATCH`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE` for review and never rewrites the text or fails the run.\n209: - **C2 ATR multiple (observed):** `anchor=258.47`, `level=250.94`, `atr=4.39` → `7.53`; `7.53 / 4.39 = 1.71526195…`; at `claim_precision=1` round-half-up → `1.7`. Prose “roughly 1×ATR” ⇒ `MISMATCH` (also outside any integer rounding), surfaced for review.\n210: - **Unsupported:** effective tax rate from `net_income / operating_income` when `pretax_income`/`tax_expense` absent ⇒ `UNSUPPORTED`.\n211: - **Not verifiable:** ATR missing or `≤ 0` ⇒ ATR multiple/band `NOT_VERIFIABLE`; unknown cash ⇒ any affordability/notional claim needing cash `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (no `0`).\n212: \n213: ---\n214: \n215: ## 5. Integration stages\n216: \n217: **Stage 0 — standalone post-run audit (first slice; no live-path change).** A separate tool reads **saved** stage artifacts plus an **explicitly supplied, run-bound typed fact fixture**, evaluates only the first-slice relations, and writes its **own** audit file at a caller-chosen location **outside** the finalized run directory. It does **not** modify saved artifacts, the manifest or its hashes, and its retention/integrity (`audit.json` + its own checksum) is **distinct** from the authoritative report/manifest. It changes no `Finding`/`output_check`/`run_outcome`/rendering. Coverage is reported **inside the audit file only**, never in the published report/UI.\n218: \n219: **Stage 1 — later: automatic typed fact projection + staging integration (needs named seams and approval).** Extracting typed facts directly from `snapshot.py`/graph, writing the audit into the staging area, or surfacing coverage in the report requires touching these existing modules, with separate review:\n220: `tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/snapshot.py`, `tradingagents/agents/state.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/persist.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py::_prompt_hash` (source inventory).\n221: \n222: **Stage 2 — optional render/gating (separately unapproved).** Only if A/C approve a schema/interface/quality-rule change: map a `MISMATCH` on a registered relation to `NEEDS_REVIEW` via a **new, named** finding type (never a reused `CHECK_ERROR`, never a silent Q5) and/or communicate coverage in the report without implying whole-narrative certification. Would also require edits to `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` §3.1–3.6/§6, `docs/architecture/invariants.md` INV-03/04/08/11, `docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md`, `docs/architecture/memory-design.md`, `permission-model.md`, and the `docs/verification/*` registry.\n223: \n224: **Q1–Q4 remains unchanged until such approval.** Undetected/unregistered numerical prose remains uncounted; the audit states coverage as “N of M **detected registered** claims checked”, never a whole-narrative certification.\n225: \n226: ---\n227: \n228: ## 6. Acceptance plan\n229: \n230: ### 6.0 Optional small first slice (price distance/direction + ATR band only)\n231: \n232: Fixture: a supplied typed fact packet for one saved run (e.g. `close=258.47`, `stop=255.33`, `atr=4.39`, `as_of=2026-01-09`) and a small set of supplied claims with roles/precision. Scenarios:\n233: \n234: | ID | Fixture | Expected | Seam |\n235: |---|---|---|---|\n236: | NVA-01 | prose “≈3.14 points below” | `VERIFIED` (distance+direction) | calculator `abs_distance`/`direction` |\n237: | NVA-02 | same anchors; prose says “above” | `MISMATCH` (direction) | `direction` |\n238: | NVA-03 | same anchors; prose correctly says “below” (reverse of NVA-02) | `VERIFIED` (direction) | `direction` |\n239: | NVA-04 | prose “6.59–8.78 points” at precision 2 | `VERIFIED` (ATR band) | `scaled_band` |\n240: | NVA-05 | prose “0.72×ATR” at precision 2 and “0.7153×ATR” at precision 4 | both `VERIFIED`; a `0.72` claim declared at precision 4 | `NOT_VERIFIABLE` | `divide_positive` + precision policy |\n241: | NVA-06 | ATR missing / `0` / nonfinite | `NOT_VERIFIABLE`, no `0`, no divide-by-zero | `divide_positive`/`scaled_band` |\n242: \n243: The slice stops there; it does **not** validate any frozen report. ESTIMATE for this slice: **~1–2 working days** for a standalone tool + fixture + these scenarios, **if** the team wants it before the deadline; otherwise it should be deferred. This estimate is not a promise.\n244: \n245: ### 6.1 Full roadmap scenarios (beyond the first slice, needing later approval)\n246: \n247: | ID | Fixture | Expected | Seam |\n248: |---|---|---|---|\n249: | NVA-07 | notional: supplied quantity `40` and supplied price `258.47` → `10338.80`; separately, an “affordability” claim needing **cash** (unknown) | notional `VERIFIED` (from supplied qty×price); affordability `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (cash unknown, not `0`) | `position_notional` vs affordability inputs |\n250: | NVA-08 | explicit-empty vs NO_PORTFOLIO portfolios | distinct; flat not asserted where unknown | fact bundle |\n251: | NVA-09 | wrong ticker/date/source/fingerprint binding | claim `NOT_VERIFIABLE`/excluded, never `VERIFIED` | fact run-binding |\n252: | NVA-10 | unregistered relation (tax rate from net/operating income; weighted EPS) | `UNSUPPORTED`, never `VERIFIED` | registry |\n253: | NVA-11 | precision boundaries (6.585 vs “6.6”; 0.7153 vs “0.72”; declared vs claimed precision) | exact per §4.4; wrong precision `NOT_VERIFIABLE`, wrong rounded value `MISMATCH` | calculator precision |\n254: | NVA-12 | standalone run over saved artifacts | audit file written **outside** the run dir; saved report/manifest bytes and hashes unchanged | Stage 0 standalone |\n255: | NVA-13 | partial coverage (some `UNSUPPORTED`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE`) | audit summary reports counts; **no** published report/UI coverage and **no** whole-narrative verified claim | audit summary only |\n256: | NVA-14 | PM band “1.5–8.8 points” with and without trusted anchor linkage | `MISMATCH` (linked) / `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (unlinked); review-needed, never auto-rewritten | claims `anchor_evidence` |\n257: | NVA-L | after any Stage-1/2 change: live fixed replay | registered relations evaluated against real facts; coverage internal; independent human/C review | integration |\n258: \n259: Where a class is unregistered or a relation's operands cannot be bound, the result is `UNSUPPORTED` (represented via `extraction_provenance`/notes), never an impossible `ClaimClass` value.\n260: \n261: **Independent human review / C scoring is still required** for: whether a `VERIFIED` relation is the *right* claim to make, narrative quality, ownership/challenge semantics, and any promotion from audit-only to gating. No numeric threshold constitutes C acceptance or F8 recovery.\n262: \n263: ---\n264: \n265: ## 7. Work split, prerequisites, estimates, migration, risks\n266: \n267: ### 7.1 Handoff (recorded team allocation; not universal course roles)\n268: \n269: - **B (architecture):** propose `NVR-` scope, the fact/claim/status contract, units/precision policy and Stage-1/2 deltas.\n270: - **A (requirements):** adopt (or not) any `NVR-` item and any Stage-2 gating; A owns requirement adoption.\n271: - **C (independent tests/evaluation):** own NVA acceptance, a real cohort and semantic judgement. C owns acceptance; D does not define it.\n272: - **D (implementation):** build the standalone first slice; later, the typed projection, calculator and claim extraction.\n273: - **E (integration/governance):** prompt-hash/source-inventory, staging/sink/privacy, report and registry edits — only after approval.\n274: \n275: No approvals are asserted or invented here.\n276: \n277: ### 7.2 Prerequisites and genuinely pending choices\n278: \n279: Pending: whether to do the optional first slice before the deadline or defer; adopt B (vs B+detection aid); exact precision bounds if more classes are added; where trusted facts come from (supplied fixture now; `snapshot.py`-derived projection later); whether/when any render/gating is wanted; who owns semantic acceptance.\n280: \n281: ### 7.3 Estimates (ESTIMATE; no measurements, no promise)\n282: \n283: - Optional first slice (standalone, supplied fixture, 3 relations, §6.0): **~1–2 working days**.\n284: - Full Stage-0/1 typed projection + more classes + tests: **~4–7 working days** (beyond the immediate deadline; not proposed as a necessary immediate fix).\n285: - Stage-2 render/gating + contract review + live replay: **~3–6 working days**, plus A/C review.\n286: \n287: ### 7.4 Migration / rollback\n288: \n289: - **Migration:** the first slice is fully standalone and additive; no live-path, enum, manifest or rendering change; it reads saved artifacts and writes its own file.\n290: - **Rollback:** delete/ignore the standalone tool and its audit file; saved run artifacts and manifest hashes are untouched, so rollback is simply not running the tool.\n291: \n292: ### 7.5 Risks\n293: \n294: - **False assurance:** `VERIFIED` must not read as “whole report correct”. Mitigation: coverage counts of detected registered claims only; no whole-narrative badge; explicit `UNSUPPORTED`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n295: - **Bounded coverage / detection:** only registered detected relations are scored; undetected prose is uncounted and stated.\n296: - **Fact provenance:** facts must be from a supplied or externally-verifiable source; model-proposed levels and user-supplied holdings are unverified inputs, never “truth”.\n297: - **Detection aid errors:** LLM/regex extraction is unverified; it cannot yield `VERIFIED` and must not include clearly different relations that happen to compute.\n298: - **Scope creep:** Stage-1/2 touches check authority and contracts; keep separately approved and beyond the immediate deadline.\n299: \n300: ---\n301: \n302: ## 8. Status and next step\n303: \n304: This is a **plan for review**, not implementation, not approval, and not a claim that any current report is validated. Brian authorized only drafting it. Implementation, tests, canonical-requirement adoption and any render/gating wait for A/B/C/D/E scope, design and test approval. The coordinator-observed examples (L1 historical arithmetic, the PM band wording, the C2 ATR multiple) are retained as design evidence; they are not reclassified as passed, and the optional first slice does not rescue them before review. The broader roadmap is **beyond** this immediately approved drafting work.\n305: \n306: PLAN_READY_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW — /home/brian/projects/CS5351/docs/architecture/proposals/numeric-validation-extension-plan-2026-11-21.md\n\n(End of file - total 306 lines)\n</content>",

        "text": "# Numeric-validation extension plan (PROPOSAL, unapproved)\n\nStatus: **PROPOSAL only.** Prepared 2026-11-21, Asia/Hong_Kong, by the OpenCode repair session at Brian's request (“Prepare a numeric-validation extension plan”, Codex call `call_2908c9d302df46eebfbf787d3853dcf3`). This authorizes **drafting a plan**, not implementing a validator, checker, schema, test, code change, canonical-requirement adoption or approval. Nothing here is an accepted requirement, a measured result, an independent score, or a Member C acceptance. Requirement IDs below use a separate **`NVR-`** prefix and are explicitly **UNAPPROVED**; they do not modify or renumber any `SEL-TA-*` ID.\n\nRelated existing documents (unchanged): [interface contracts](../interface-contracts.md), [invariants](../invariants.md), [runtime policy catalog](../runtime-policy-catalog.md), [ADR 001](../adr/001-portfolio-aware-cli.md), [memory design](../memory-design.md), [permission model](../permission-model.md), and the approved bounded prompt plans [`live-trader-numeric-test-plan-2026-11-21.md`](../../verification/proposals/live-trader-numeric-test-plan-2026-11-21.md) (L1) and [`live-fundamentals-vintage-test-plan-2026-11-21.md`](../../verification/proposals/live-fundamentals-vintage-test-plan-2026-11-21.md) (L2).\n\n---\n\n## 0. Deadline context and an optional small first slice\n\nThe course deadline is **26 Nov 2026, 23:59 Hong Kong**. The full programme in §7 is **not** proposed as an immediate, necessary fix and cannot be promised before the deadline. The frozen current-source live cohort and its source inventory must not be disturbed by this work; it is a separate, post-run audit proposal.\n\nAn **optional, small, bounded first slice** (see §6.0) is offered only if the team wants *something* reviewable quickly: a **standalone, post-run audit** run over already-saved artifacts, using an **explicitly supplied, run-bound typed input fixture**, covering only **price distance** and **price direction** and **ATR band**. It excludes LLM extraction, automatic typed extraction from the graph/snapshot, any staging integration, any report/UI change and any gating. It does **not** claim that any frozen report is already validated. Everything broader (§7 roadmap) is clearly **beyond** this immediately approved drafting work.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Problem statement\n\nPrompt instructions alone (L1/L2) reduce but cannot certify free-text financial arithmetic. The coordinator observed on the current frozen source (not re-run by this drafting session):\n\n- **L1 historical arithmetic (already mitigated by prompt, retained as history):** before the L1 prompt fix, the Trader described stop `255.33` as “roughly 1.5×ATR (6.6 points) below” a `258.47` close with ATR `4.39`; the real difference is `258.47 − 255.33 = 3.14` ≈ `0.7153×ATR`. L1 now yields the correct `3.14`/about `0.72×ATR` and “below” on the targeted fixtures.\n- **PM band wording (a unit/definition, not pure price arithmetic):** full C1 `20261121T101520Z-52544e6d` (deepseek profile) PM prose says a `1.5–2×ATR` stop is “~6.6–8.8 points (ATR 4.39)” and later writes **“anchor the stop 1.5–8.8 points below the fill.”** Both ends of the later phrase read as “points”; text alone cannot prove the leading `1.5` was meant as a multiplier. This is a **range mismatch against the explicitly anchored preceding `1.5–2×ATR` claim** *only if* trusted context establishes that association; otherwise it is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n- **C2 ATR multiple (observed multiple error):** the final C2 PM described downside from `258.47` to `250.94` as “roughly 1×ATR” with ATR `4.39`. The actual move is `258.47 − 250.94 = 7.53`, and `7.53 / 4.39 ≈ 1.7153×ATR` — the “roughly 1×” wording does not match.\n\nThese are coordinator-observed examples used as **design coverage**, not an assertion that every claim in any report was independently audited, and not a re-run by this drafting session.\n\nBroader financial definitions also matter and are **not** trivially certifiable: EPS is not generally safely additive across quarters; an effective tax rate cannot be certified from net income / operating income when pretax income and tax expense are absent. A calculator can check a **relation relative to specified operands**; it cannot certify the truth, semantics or exhaustive extraction of financial prose.\n\n### 1.1 Proposed (UNAPPROVED) requirement IDs\n\nSeparate `NVR-` prefix; not canonical requirements.\n\n- **NVR-001 — Typed supplied facts first.** Numeric inputs are supplied to the auditor as a typed, run-bound fact bundle (ticker, analysis date, source identifier and availability date, period, units, declared precision) rather than parsed from prose. Automatic typed extraction from the graph/snapshot is a **later** change (§7), not part of the first slice.\n- **NVR-002 — Registered relations only.** A deterministic calculator evaluates only **registered** relations (see §4.2 roles) over `Decimal` (precision 28), with fixed units and defined rounding. No `eval`, no model-authored expected values. It verifies a relation against the **specified operands**; it does not certify the operands' truth or that the operand set is complete.\n- **NVR-003 — Bounded relation-class coverage.** The first slice covers only price distance, price direction and ATR band; the broader roadmap adds percentages with an explicit denominator, position notional from supplied quantities, and risk/reward with explicit anchors. Out-of-scope financial definitions (tax-rate from net/operating income, weighted-EPS derivation) are **`UNSUPPORTED`**, never “verified” merely because a formula runs.\n- **NVR-004 — Coverage-honest status.** Each **detected, registered** claim gets a status from `{VERIFIED, MISMATCH, NOT_VERIFIABLE, UNSUPPORTED}` (§4.3); there is **no** fifth per-claim `UNVERIFIED` status. Prose spans that are not detected/registered are counted separately, not scored. The denominator is only the **detected registered claims**, not every statement in the report. Partial coverage never yields a whole-narrative “verified” claim.\n- **NVR-005 — Standalone audit first.** The first slice runs **outside** the live run: a standalone post-run tool reads saved artifacts and a separately supplied typed fixture, and writes its own audit file (not into the finalized run directory). It changes **no** `output_check`, `run_outcome`, Q1–Q4, public enum, manifest or rendered report. Any staging integration, render/gating or public status change is separately unapproved.\n- **NVR-006 — Provenance and immutability.** Facts and claims bind to run id, ticker, analysis date, source identifier, source availability date, period, input fingerprint, unit and stage text hash+offset; unknown is never `0`; saved run artifacts are read-only. The audit's own retention/integrity is distinct from the authoritative report/manifest (which it never alters).\n\n### 1.2 Preserved decisions (not reopened)\n\nTwo input modes; five research ratings and three Trader actions; Q1–Q4 unchanged; user-supplied/unverified holdings/cash; no orders; source-date constraints; report+manifest critical, terminal-append best-effort; the frozen `RunContext`/fingerprint; no reliance on the raw low-level primitive. This plan does **not** restart the ADR 001 C1/C2/C3 architecture decision.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Candidate approaches (design comparison; ESTIMATE, no measurements)\n\nEstimates are design judgements labelled **ESTIMATE**. No measured latency/cost/accuracy is claimed.\n\n### 2.1 A — Expanded prompts only (status quo + more instructions)\n\n- **Rationale:** cheapest; no new modules. L1/L2 already show prompt wording changes behaviour.\n- **Coverage:** cannot certify arithmetic; unit/definition wording (e.g. the PM band, C2 multiple) can recur; no machine-readable coverage.\n- **Cost:** ESTIMATE ~0.2–0.5 day; low value as a correctness claim.\n- **Verdict:** necessary but insufficient; keep L1/L2, do not extend as the solution.\n\n### 2.2 B — Typed supplied-fact bundle + deterministic relation calculator + claim ledger (recommended)\n\n- **Rationale:** separates *facts* (typed, run-bound, supplied or later projected), *claims* (detected relations) and *computed results* (deterministic). A claim is checked **against the specified operands**; unregistered relations are `UNSUPPORTED`; missing/unknown/ambiguous inputs are `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n- **Coverage gaps:** undetected prose stays uncounted; semantic financial definitions remain `UNSUPPORTED`; coverage is bounded to the registered relations.\n- **Integration cost:** first slice (standalone, supplied fixture, three relations) small; automatic extraction, more classes and any staging/gating are later.\n- **Verdict:** recommended bounded design; do **not** restart C1/C2/C3.\n\n### 2.3 C — Prose parsing / second-LLM critique\n\n- **Rationale:** flexible; can “explain” arithmetic in arbitrary prose.\n- **Coverage:** a regex cannot universally verify financial prose; a second LLM is non-deterministic, adds cost/latency, can hallucinate agreement, and is itself unverifiable. It can at most **triage or extract candidate claims**, never certify.\n- **Cost:** ESTIMATE ~2–4 days plus per-call cost/latency; weak auditability.\n- **Verdict:** acceptable only as a *detection aid*; its output is always an `UNSUPPORTED`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE`-until-confirmed suggestion and never yields `VERIFIED` by itself (wrong operands/formula that happen to compute must not certify the prose).\n\n**Recommendation:** **B**. Do not restart C1/C2/C3.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Actual code seams inspected (read-only)\n\n- **Graph state holds prose, not structured numbers.** `tradingagents/agents/state.py` (`AgentState`) carries prose reports and a rendered `portfolio_context` string; there is **no** typed numeric-facts field.\n- **The verified market snapshot is rendered text, computed transiently.** `tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/snapshot.py::build_verified_market_snapshot` computes latest OHLCV + indicators deterministically but **returns a markdown string**; the structured values are not exposed to state. Tool: `tradingagents/agents/tools.py::get_verified_market_snapshot`.\n- **Some structured numeric fields exist for the Trader only.** `tradingagents/agents/schemas.py::TraderProposal` has `entry_price`, `stop_loss` and free-text `position_sizing`; the PM `PortfolioDecision.price_target` is similar. **These are the model's proposed levels, not verified external market truth.**\n- **Portfolio facts are caller input, not market data.** `tradingagents/portfolio.py::PortfolioContext` (user-supplied, **unverified**) and the frozen `RunContext`/`FrozenSnapshot` in `tradingagents/runapi/context.py` (fingerprint, as-of) are the only canonical account snapshot.\n- **Checks and result enums.** `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py::OutputChecker` implements Q1–Q4 only; `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` defines `Finding` rules `Q1|Q2|Q3|Q4|CHECK_ERROR` and `OutputCheck = PASSED|NEEDS_REVIEW|NOT_RUN`.\n- **Envelope/report assembly.** `tradingagents/runapi/reporting.py` builds the trusted envelope; `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py` builds the final markdown/HTML; `tradingagents/reporting.py::_report_parts` selects prose sections.\n\n**Consequence:** the code does **not** already expose a trusted structured numeric projection for price/ATR/position facts. A **new** projection (or, for the first slice, an explicitly supplied typed fixture) is **required**; this plan does not invent an existing canonical snapshot. A separate post-run audit can read the **saved** prose artifacts without touching the live path.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Proposed schema/interface (NEW; UNAPPROVED)\n\nFirst slice modules (out-of-tree standalone acceptable; paths proposed):\n\n- `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/__init__.py` — package (NEW; D implements, B contract, C tests, E wiring).\n- `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/facts.py` — `TrustedFact`/`FactBundle` + precision/unit policy (NEW).\n- `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/calculator.py` — registered relations over `Decimal` (NEW).\n- `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/claims.py` — claim model + (fixture-supplied) claim set (NEW).\n- `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/audit.py` — standalone audit over saved artifacts + supplied fixture (NEW).\n\nNo existing production module is modified by the first slice.\n\n### 4.1 `TrustedFact` / `FactBundle`\n\n```\nFactSource = Literal[\n  \"supplied_run_fixture\",        # explicitly supplied, run-bound typed inputs (first slice)\n  \"verified_market_snapshot\",    # later: typed values derived from snapshot.py\n  \"fundamentals_statement\",      # later: statement facts with period/availability date\n  \"trader_proposed_level\",       # later: the Trader's *proposed* level (NOT verified market truth)\n  \"portfolio_user_supplied\",     # user-supplied holdings/cash (unverified)\n]\n\nTrustedFact {\n  name: str\n  value: Decimal | None          # None = unknown (never coerced to 0)\n  unit: Literal[\"price\",\"points\",\"shares\",\"currency\",\"multiple\",\"percent\",\"ratio\"]\n  source: FactSource\n  source_id: str                 # e.g. snapshot row id / statement ref / \"user_input\"\n  availability_date: str         # ISO date the fact became knowable (must be <= run analysis date)\n  period: str | None             # explicit statement period end/label (not the run date)\n  run_analysis_date: str         # the run's analysis date\n  declared_precision: int        # digits after decimal the claim may rely on\n  verified: bool                 # True only for externally-verifiable sources; user/model inputs are False\n}\n\nFactBundle {\n  run_id: str; ticker: str; analysis_date: str\n  fingerprint_sha256: str | None # frozen portfolio fingerprint when portfolio-derived (else None)\n  source_revision: str; prompt_hash: str\n  facts: list[TrustedFact]\n}\n```\n\nRules: unknown `value` is `None` (never `0`); `availability_date` must be `<=` the run analysis date (a post-cutoff fact is excluded); `period` and `availability_date` are distinct from the run date; `verified=False` for user-supplied holdings and for model-proposed levels. Portfolio **quantity is user-supplied/unverified**. The bundle binds to the frozen `RunContext` (provenance per [INV-04/05](../invariants.md)).\n\n### 4.2 `NumericClaim` (a detected relation) and calculator operations\n\n```\nClaimClass = Literal[\n  \"price_distance\",\"price_direction\",\"atr_distance\",\"atr_band\",\n  \"percent_with_denominator\",\"position_notional\",\"risk_reward\"\n]\n\nOperandRef {\n  fact: str                      # fact name in the bundle\n  role: Literal[\"anchor\",\"level\",\"atr\",\"minuend\",\"subtrahend\",\"numerator\",\n                \"denominator\",\"factor_min\",\"factor_max\",\"quantity\",\"price\"]\n}\n\nNumericClaim {\n  claim_id: str\n  class: ClaimClass\n  operands: list[OperandRef]     # roles make the relation explicit\n  asserted_unit: \"price|points|currency|percent|ratio|multiple\"\n  asserted_value: Decimal | None # single stated number, or...\n  asserted_range: tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None\n  asserted_direction: \"above|below|none\"   # for distance/direction claims\n  claim_precision: int           # digits after decimal the *claim* was stated at\n  anchor_evidence: str | None    # trusted reference linking a claim to its anchor claim, if any\n  stage: str                     # \"trader\" | \"portfolio_manager\" | \"research_manager\" | ...\n  stage_text_sha256: str         # hash of the stage prose the span indexes into\n  text_span: tuple[int,int]      # offsets into that stage prose (evidence; never rewritten)\n  extraction_provenance: \"supplied\" | \"deterministic\" | \"llm_assisted\"\n}\n```\n\nA relation whose class is not registered, or whose operands cannot be bound, is `UNSUPPORTED` (the class exists as a typed marker even if the *specific* relation is unregistered; no impossible enum value). A claim with ambiguous extraction, unknown `claim_precision`, or missing `anchor_evidence` for an associated band is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n\n**Operations (fixed registry):** `subtract(minuend, subtrahend)`, `abs_distance(anchor, level)`, `direction(anchor, level)`, `divide_positive(numerator, denominator)` (denominator must be `> 0`), `scaled_band(factor_min, factor_max, atr)`. Each op declares its operand roles and result unit. The calculator **verifies the relation relative to the specified operands**; it does not assert that those operands are the true or complete facts.\n\n### 4.3 `ComputedResult` (proposal; NOT Q1–Q4)\n\n```\nCoverageStatus = Literal[\"VERIFIED\",\"MISMATCH\",\"NOT_VERIFIABLE\",\"UNSUPPORTED\"]\n\nComputedResult {\n  claim_id: str\n  computed_value: Decimal | None\n  computed_range: tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None\n  computed_unit: ...\n  expected_at_claim_precision: Decimal | tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None  # round-half-up of computed at claim_precision\n  status: CoverageStatus\n  source_facts: list[str]\n  notes: str     # e.g. \"missing atr\" / \"ambiguous 1.5 role\" / \"unregistered relation\"\n}\n```\n\n**Do not reuse `CHECK_ERROR`** for a numerical semantic mismatch and **do not create a Q5 silently.** A later, A/C-approved change may add a proposal-only finding type (`NumericFinding { rule: \"NUMERIC\", ... }`); until then results live only in the standalone audit file.\n\n### 4.4 Precision / rounding / tolerance policy (exact for the first slice)\n\n- **Arithmetic:** Python `Decimal` at **context precision 28**; no binary float in the calculator.\n- **Comparison rule (first slice): NO tolerance.** Compute exactly, **round half-up to the claim's declared `claim_precision`**, and require **equality** with the asserted value/range endpoints. A different rounded value is `MISMATCH`.\n- **Precision bounds per class (frozen; a claim outside its bound is rejected as `NOT_VERIFIABLE`):**\n  - `price_distance`, `atr_band` → allow `claim_precision` in `{0,1,2}`.\n  - `atr_distance` (multiple) → allow `claim_precision` in `{1,2,3,4}`.\n  - `price_direction` → no numeric precision (boolean).\n- **Unknown/ambiguous precision** (the prose does not state enough digits to pin `claim_precision`) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n- **Units:** the calculator refuses to combine operands of incompatible unit roles (e.g. a `factor_*` (multiple) with a `points` asserted unit) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE` unless trusted `anchor_evidence` explicitly links them as the same range claim, in which case they are compared as that claim (§4.5).\n- No caller-chosen wide tolerances are permitted in the first slice.\n\n### 4.5 Worked examples under this policy (document examples, exact)\n\n- **Distance/direction (positive):** `anchor=258.47`, `level=255.33`, ATR `4.39`. `abs(258.47 − 255.33) = 3.14`; direction: `255.33 < 258.47` ⇒ **below**. Prose “≈3.14 points below” at `claim_precision=2` → expected `3.14` → `VERIFIED`.\n- **Direction (negative):** same anchors, prose says “above” → computed **below** ⇒ `asserted_direction` mismatch ⇒ `MISMATCH`.\n- **ATR multiple (positive at 2 dp):** `3.14 / 4.39 = 0.7152619576…`; round half-up to `claim_precision=2` → `0.72`. Prose “0.72×ATR” → `VERIFIED`.\n- **ATR multiple (boundary negative):** same, but prose “0.7153×ATR” at `claim_precision=4` → expected `0.7153` (round-half-up of `0.71526195…`) → `VERIFIED`; prose “0.72×ATR” is only valid at `claim_precision=2`. A prose that states `0.72` but declares precision 4 is inconsistent → `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (ambiguous precision), **not** silently accepted. This resolves the earlier `0.7153` vs `0.72` contradiction: the two are **different declared precisions**, compared by equality only at each claim's own precision.\n- **ATR band (positive):** `factor_min=1.5`, `factor_max=2`, `atr=4.39` → `1.5 × 4.39 = 6.585`, `2 × 4.39 = 8.78`. At `claim_precision=2`, round-half-up → expected band `(6.59, 8.78)`. Prose “6.59–8.78 points” → `VERIFIED`; prose “6.585–8.78” at precision 3 is outside the frozen bound for `atr_band` (max 2) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n- **ATR band (boundary negative):** prose “6.6–8.8 points” at `claim_precision=1`: expected (round-half-up) `(6.6, 8.8)` → `VERIFIED`; the **same** numbers claimed at precision 2 → expected `(6.59, 8.78)` ≠ `(6.60, 8.80)` → `MISMATCH`. Precision is part of the claim.\n- **PM band “1.5–8.8 points below the fill” (observed):** parsed literally, both endpoints are `points`, giving range `(1.5, 8.8)` points. If trusted `anchor_evidence` links it to the preceding `1.5–2×ATR` claim, compare against the expected band `(6.59, 8.78)` at precision 2 → `MISMATCH` (lower endpoint `1.5` ≠ `6.59`). If no trusted association exists, the first endpoint's role is ambiguous (`1.5` could be a factor) ⇒ `NOT_VERIFIABLE`. It is **not** universally a dimensional error; the auditor reports `MISMATCH`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE` for review and never rewrites the text or fails the run.\n- **C2 ATR multiple (observed):** `anchor=258.47`, `level=250.94`, `atr=4.39` → `7.53`; `7.53 / 4.39 = 1.71526195…`; at `claim_precision=1` round-half-up → `1.7`. Prose “roughly 1×ATR” ⇒ `MISMATCH` (also outside any integer rounding), surfaced for review.\n- **Unsupported:** effective tax rate from `net_income / operating_income` when `pretax_income`/`tax_expense` absent ⇒ `UNSUPPORTED`.\n- **Not verifiable:** ATR missing or `≤ 0` ⇒ ATR multiple/band `NOT_VERIFIABLE`; unknown cash ⇒ any affordability/notional claim needing cash `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (no `0`).\n\n---\n\n## 5. Integration stages\n\n**Stage 0 — standalone post-run audit (first slice; no live-path change).** A separate tool reads **saved** stage artifacts plus an **explicitly supplied, run-bound typed fact fixture**, evaluates only the first-slice relations, and writes its **own** audit file at a caller-chosen location **outside** the finalized run directory. It does **not** modify saved artifacts, the manifest or its hashes, and its retention/integrity (`audit.json` + its own checksum) is **distinct** from the authoritative report/manifest. It changes no `Finding`/`output_check`/`run_outcome`/rendering. Coverage is reported **inside the audit file only**, never in the published report/UI.\n\n**Stage 1 — later: automatic typed fact projection + staging integration (needs named seams and approval).** Extracting typed facts directly from `snapshot.py`/graph, writing the audit into the staging area, or surfacing coverage in the report requires touching these existing modules, with separate review:\n`tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/snapshot.py`, `tradingagents/agents/state.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/persist.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py::_prompt_hash` (source inventory).\n\n**Stage 2 — optional render/gating (separately unapproved).** Only if A/C approve a schema/interface/quality-rule change: map a `MISMATCH` on a registered relation to `NEEDS_REVIEW` via a **new, named** finding type (never a reused `CHECK_ERROR`, never a silent Q5) and/or communicate coverage in the report without implying whole-narrative certification. Would also require edits to `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` §3.1–3.6/§6, `docs/architecture/invariants.md` INV-03/04/08/11, `docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md`, `docs/architecture/memory-design.md`, `permission-model.md`, and the `docs/verification/*` registry.\n\n**Q1–Q4 remains unchanged until such approval.** Undetected/unregistered numerical prose remains uncounted; the audit states coverage as “N of M **detected registered** claims checked”, never a whole-narrative certification.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Acceptance plan\n\n### 6.0 Optional small first slice (price distance/direction + ATR band only)\n\nFixture: a supplied typed fact packet for one saved run (e.g. `close=258.47`, `stop=255.33`, `atr=4.39`, `as_of=2026-01-09`) and a small set of supplied claims with roles/precision. Scenarios:\n\n| ID | Fixture | Expected | Seam |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| NVA-01 | prose “≈3.14 points below” | `VERIFIED` (distance+direction) | calculator `abs_distance`/`direction` |\n| NVA-02 | same anchors; prose says “above” | `MISMATCH` (direction) | `direction` |\n| NVA-03 | same anchors; prose correctly says “below” (reverse of NVA-02) | `VERIFIED` (direction) | `direction` |\n| NVA-04 | prose “6.59–8.78 points” at precision 2 | `VERIFIED` (ATR band) | `scaled_band` |\n| NVA-05 | prose “0.72×ATR” at precision 2 and “0.7153×ATR” at precision 4 | both `VERIFIED`; a `0.72` claim declared at precision 4 | `NOT_VERIFIABLE` | `divide_positive` + precision policy |\n| NVA-06 | ATR missing / `0` / nonfinite | `NOT_VERIFIABLE`, no `0`, no divide-by-zero | `divide_positive`/`scaled_band` |\n\nThe slice stops there; it does **not** validate any frozen report. ESTIMATE for this slice: **~1–2 working days** for a standalone tool + fixture + these scenarios, **if** the team wants it before the deadline; otherwise it should be deferred. This estimate is not a promise.\n\n### 6.1 Full roadmap scenarios (beyond the first slice, needing later approval)\n\n| ID | Fixture | Expected | Seam |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| NVA-07 | notional: supplied quantity `40` and supplied price `258.47` → `10338.80`; separately, an “affordability” claim needing **cash** (unknown) | notional `VERIFIED` (from supplied qty×price); affordability `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (cash unknown, not `0`) | `position_notional` vs affordability inputs |\n| NVA-08 | explicit-empty vs NO_PORTFOLIO portfolios | distinct; flat not asserted where unknown | fact bundle |\n| NVA-09 | wrong ticker/date/source/fingerprint binding | claim `NOT_VERIFIABLE`/excluded, never `VERIFIED` | fact run-binding |\n| NVA-10 | unregistered relation (tax rate from net/operating income; weighted EPS) | `UNSUPPORTED`, never `VERIFIED` | registry |\n| NVA-11 | precision boundaries (6.585 vs “6.6”; 0.7153 vs “0.72”; declared vs claimed precision) | exact per §4.4; wrong precision `NOT_VERIFIABLE`, wrong rounded value `MISMATCH` | calculator precision |\n| NVA-12 | standalone run over saved artifacts | audit file written **outside** the run dir; saved report/manifest bytes and hashes unchanged | Stage 0 standalone |\n| NVA-13 | partial coverage (some `UNSUPPORTED`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE`) | audit summary reports counts; **no** published report/UI coverage and **no** whole-narrative verified claim | audit summary only |\n| NVA-14 | PM band “1.5–8.8 points” with and without trusted anchor linkage | `MISMATCH` (linked) / `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (unlinked); review-needed, never auto-rewritten | claims `anchor_evidence` |\n| NVA-L | after any Stage-1/2 change: live fixed replay | registered relations evaluated against real facts; coverage internal; independent human/C review | integration |\n\nWhere a class is unregistered or a relation's operands cannot be bound, the result is `UNSUPPORTED` (represented via `extraction_provenance`/notes), never an impossible `ClaimClass` value.\n\n**Independent human review / C scoring is still required** for: whether a `VERIFIED` relation is the *right* claim to make, narrative quality, ownership/challenge semantics, and any promotion from audit-only to gating. No numeric threshold constitutes C acceptance or F8 recovery.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Work split, prerequisites, estimates, migration, risks\n\n### 7.1 Handoff (recorded team allocation; not universal course roles)\n\n- **B (architecture):** propose `NVR-` scope, the fact/claim/status contract, units/precision policy and Stage-1/2 deltas.\n- **A (requirements):** adopt (or not) any `NVR-` item and any Stage-2 gating; A owns requirement adoption.\n- **C (independent tests/evaluation):** own NVA acceptance, a real cohort and semantic judgement. C owns acceptance; D does not define it.\n- **D (implementation):** build the standalone first slice; later, the typed projection, calculator and claim extraction.\n- **E (integration/governance):** prompt-hash/source-inventory, staging/sink/privacy, report and registry edits — only after approval.\n\nNo approvals are asserted or invented here.\n\n### 7.2 Prerequisites and genuinely pending choices\n\nPending: whether to do the optional first slice before the deadline or defer; adopt B (vs B+detection aid); exact precision bounds if more classes are added; where trusted facts come from (supplied fixture now; `snapshot.py`-derived projection later); whether/when any render/gating is wanted; who owns semantic acceptance.\n\n### 7.3 Estimates (ESTIMATE; no measurements, no promise)\n\n- Optional first slice (standalone, supplied fixture, 3 relations, §6.0): **~1–2 working days**.\n- Full Stage-0/1 typed projection + more classes + tests: **~4–7 working days** (beyond the immediate deadline; not proposed as a necessary immediate fix).\n- Stage-2 render/gating + contract review + live replay: **~3–6 working days**, plus A/C review.\n\n### 7.4 Migration / rollback\n\n- **Migration:** the first slice is fully standalone and additive; no live-path, enum, manifest or rendering change; it reads saved artifacts and writes its own file.\n- **Rollback:** delete/ignore the standalone tool and its audit file; saved run artifacts and manifest hashes are untouched, so rollback is simply not running the tool.\n\n### 7.5 Risks\n\n- **False assurance:** `VERIFIED` must not read as “whole report correct”. Mitigation: coverage counts of detected registered claims only; no whole-narrative badge; explicit `UNSUPPORTED`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n- **Bounded coverage / detection:** only registered detected relations are scored; undetected prose is uncounted and stated.\n- **Fact provenance:** facts must be from a supplied or externally-verifiable source; model-proposed levels and user-supplied holdings are unverified inputs, never “truth”.\n- **Detection aid errors:** LLM/regex extraction is unverified; it cannot yield `VERIFIED` and must not include clearly different relations that happen to compute.\n- **Scope creep:** Stage-1/2 touches check authority and contracts; keep separately approved and beyond the immediate deadline.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Status and next step\n\nThis is a **plan for review**, not implementation, not approval, and not a claim that any current report is validated. Brian authorized only drafting it. Implementation, tests, canonical-requirement adoption and any render/gating wait for A/B/C/D/E scope, design and test approval. The coordinator-observed examples (L1 historical arithmetic, the PM band wording, the C2 ATR multiple) are retained as design evidence; they are not reclassified as passed, and the optional first slice does not rescue them before review. A band whose factors are *claimed as points* (rather than dimensionless multipliers) without the registered `scaled_band` multiplication is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`; an ambiguous operand/anchor unit is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n+\n ### 4.3 `ComputedResult` (proposal; NOT Q1–Q4)\n \n ```\n CoverageStatus = Literal[\"VERIFIED\",\"MISMATCH\",\"NOT_VERIFIABLE\",\"UNSUPPORTED\"]\n",

````text
The modified source/test files are pre-existing approved changes from earlier turns; this turn edited **only** the plan document (and created no other file). All six corrections are applied.

## Corrections applied (plan-only)

1. **`ClaimClass` is now `str` + `REGISTERED_CLASSES` registry.** Arbitrary named unregistered classes (`tax_rate`, `weighted_eps`) → `UNSUPPORTED`; removed the contradictory “impossible enum value” explanation; `extraction_provenance`/`notes` explicitly not a class discriminator.
2. **First slice truly limited to distance/direction/ATR band.** The ATR-multiple fixture moved to the roadmap (§6.1 NVA-11). New first-slice **NVA-05** is the PM band: `MISMATCH` with trusted `anchor_evidence` vs `NOT_VERIFIABLE` without. **NVA-03** now reverses the level/anchor (`level=261.61`, `anchor=258.47` ⇒ above) with prose “below” ⇒ `MISMATCH`. The malformed table (extra column) is fixed, and the first slice now includes **immutability/hash-binding (NVA-07)**, **wrong-binding (NVA-08)** and **invalid/unknown-input (NVA-09)** tests rather than deferring trust rules.
3. **Precision coherent.** ATR multiple allowed `0..4` dp in the roadmap registry, so literal “roughly 1×ATR” compares at 0 dp (`1.715…→2`, `2≠1` ⇒ `MISMATCH`); a literal `1` is not assumed `1.0`. PM `1.5–8.8 points` compares at 1 dp `(6.6,8.8)`; `6.60–8.80` compares at 2 dp `(6.59,8.78)` ⇒ `MISMATCH`; the same text cannot be re-declared at arbitrary precision. The negative boundary is now an actual wrong value at the **same** precision (`6.6–8.7` vs `6.6–8.8`). `claim_precision` is nullable (`int | None`) matching the schema.
4. **Units fixed.** `scaled_band` **multiplies** dimensionless factors by ATR-points → points and is valid (not rejected); a factor *claimed as points* without the registered multiplication is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`; named unit algebra per op; ambiguous anchor → `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.
5. **C4 trial 2 residual added** (`20261121T101520Z-3680051f`: “$4.47…below today's low of $255.33” — actual low−stop `1.33≈0.303×ATR`, `4.47=258.47−254`), stating L1 corrected only the observed fixture cases and the full narrative still has a wrong-anchor error — not “all price math fixed”.
6. **Fact bundle hardened.** Unique `fact_id`s; `stage_text_sha256`+`text_span` correspondence; explicit trusted `anchor_evidence` binding (never inferred); `period` (actuals) and `availability_date` both ≤ cutoff; first-slice facts are manually supplied/unverified source truth unless evidence-backed; `VERIFIED` = relation-verified only.

All examples/tables were re-checked for internal arithmetic consistency; links unchanged and resolve; `git diff --check` clean. No tests/live/subagents; no other files touched; no new measurements or approvals.

`PLAN_READY_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW` — `/home/brian/projects/CS5351/docs/architecture/proposals/numeric-validation-extension-plan-2026-11-21.md`

Advisory versus authoritative data\n \n | Data | Nature | Authority |\n |---|---|---|\n | Model narrative, ratings text, recommendations | **Advisory** | Cannot set `output_check`/`run_outcome`/provenance |\n | Final rating (Buy/Overweight/Hold/Underweight/Sell/REVIEW) | Derived deterministically from the PM output | Reported, but check Q1 only *reads* readability |\n | Frozen snapshot metadata (mode, basename, fingerprint, as-of) | **Authoritative** (trusted state) | Built by input service; used by header/result/check |\n | `output_check` (PASSED/NEEDS_REVIEW/NOT_RUN) + findings | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutputChecker` only |\n | `run_outcome` (COMPLETED/INCOMPLETE) + `stop_reason` | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutcomeFinalizer` only |\n \n The disclaimer and no-portfolio notice are **frozen strings** (selected-requirements §1) and are treated as trusted content, excluded from Q4 phrase scanning.\n \n ---\n \n ## 5. Workflow (selected C2)\n \n 1. **Discover** eligible `.json` files (non-recursive, sorted, symlinks excluded) from `PORTFOLIO_DIR` — or accept explicit `--portfolio PATH` (outside dir allowed; parent not scanned).\n 2. **Select** one file, or choose no-portfolio, or cancel.\n 3. **Validate/precheck** the frozen bytes; reuse upstream model validation after explicit shape/type/as-of prechecks. Empty positions is valid (flat); no silent fallback.\n 4. **Freeze** → `RunContext` (deeply immutable value tuples; full-64 canonical fingerprint; as-of/basis recorded). Consent state `FROZEN`.\n 5. **Notice** (portfolio mode; §6) then **confirm** → `CONFIRMED` (default No). Non-interactive: valid flags are the consent expression.\n 6. **Run** via the **shared execution service** (`runapi/execution.py`): rejects any `RunContext` not `CONFIRMED`. Holdings reach the provider **only after** confirmation.\n 7. **Render body → scrub → single check (Q1–Q4; Q2 inspects the pre-check provenance fragment against explicit trusted metadata) → finalize → build trusted envelope → stage report+manifest (critical) → one atomic directory commit; terminal JSONL append is best-effort.** Incomplete runs bypass the checker and get `NOT_RUN`. The checked body is delivered unchanged; the envelope adds only trusted metadata. Terminal-event durability is decided before the manifest is staged but does not block publication; a terminal-append failure preserves the logical outcome and records `durable=false`. (§ interface-contracts §6–§7).\n 8. Pre-run cancellation/rejection starts **no graph, zero LLM calls, no completed run**; a critical persistence failure yields a typed INCOMPLETE result that never contradicts a returned success.\n \n Detailed state machine, schemas, canonicalization, ordering and failure simulations: `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md`.\n \n ### 5.1 Synthetic input-mode walkthrough (document example, not a passing test)\n - **Interactive, portfolio:** user sees `a.json`, `b.json`; selects `b.json`; precheck passes; freezes `b` (fingerprint Fb); notice shows basename `b.json`, date D, as-of basis, provider-transmission statement; user answers Yes → `CONFIRMED`; run transmits frozen `b` after consent; report header carries Fb and mode `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED`.\n - **Interactive, no portfolio:** empty directory → no-portfolio confirmation with frozen notice; Yes → `CONFIRMED` with `portfolio=None`; header shows `NO_PORTFOLIO`, null file/fingerprint/as-of.\n - **Noninteractive:** `--portfolio b.json --portfolio-as-of D` → freezes b, consent via flags, no prompt. `--without-portfolio` → `NO_PORTFOLIO`. Neither/both → `InputError`, zero calls.\n - **Cancelled:** user answers No at consent → zero graph/LLM, no completed run, counted as a pre-run attempt (NFR-006).\n \n ---\n \n ## 6. Permissions and consent\n \n - Interactive discovery/selection/consent lives **only** in the CLI (`cli/`). Agents and the engine never prompt.\n - **Consent gate** is an explicit coordinator transition between freeze and run. A frozen snapshot is a *candidate input*, **not** a confirmed selection; immutability alone does **not** prevent bypass. Only a coordinator transition to `CONFIRMED` permits run entry (see interface-contracts §4, ADR §Consent).\n - Mandatory execution, exception mapping, checks and artifact finalization sit behind a **shared application boundary** (`tradingagents/runapi/execution.py: run_analysis_api`) usable without terminal prompts. The upstream Python API signature is **preserved**; the supported project API routes through `run_analysis_api` (full requirement coverage). A raw low-level engine primitive (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run`) remains available but **does not** traverse the boundary and **does not** satisfy FR-006/FR-007/NFR-002/003/004; its scope is declared and product reliance requires **A's approval** (residual risk R-API, pending A). See `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` §5.\n - Coding-agent file permissions (separate concern) are in `docs/architecture/permission-model.md`; E implements enforcement.\n \n ---\n \n ## 7. Observability\n \n - New lifecycle event sink: UTF-8 JSONL; fixed fields `run_id, ticker, node, ts(UTC), elapsed_ms, event, event_outcome`. Console stays human-readable. Raw provider payload logging disabled by default. Progress vocabulary is separate from terminal `run_outcome`.\n - Existing sinks are adapted, not silently trusted: see memory-design §Sinks and runtime-policy-catalog.\n \n ---\n \n-## 8. Selection made by Brian (human) 2026-11-12; awaiting team/instructor reconciliation. Not implementation.\n+- Status: **Proposed (architecture draft; implementation-aligned 2026-11-24)**. Selection made by Brian (human) 2026-11-12; awaiting team/instructor reconciliation. The C2 boundary is **implemented** at `a62b801` (verified); this ADR records the decision and its as-built status, not an approval.\n - Deciders: Brian (selection), Member B (author), pending A (requirements coherence), E (governance/assembly).\n-- Scope: `SEL-TA-FR-001..007`, `SEL-TA-NFR-001..006`, `SEL-TA-GOV-006` (permission design contribution).\n+- Scope: `SEL-TA-FR-001..007`, `SEL-TA-NFR-001..006`, `SEL-TA-GOV-006` (permission design contribution). Broader `REQ-TA-*` extensions are recorded as proposed impacts in §\"Proposed broader requirements\", not adopted here.\n - Supersedes: none. Does not modify v2 requirements or the D1 registry (A owns).\n \n > Estimates in this ADR are labelled **ESTIMATE** and are design judgements. No measurement or verification is claimed.\n \n ## Context\n \n TradingAgents v0.7.1 already has an optional `--portfolio PATH` that loads a `PortfolioContext` and renders it into decision-agent prompts (`cli/main.py:50-55`, `tradingagents/portfolio.py`, `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py:293-307`). The selected requirements extend this into a discovery + explicit-consent + frozen-provenance + deterministic-check workflow, with distinct `NO_PORTFOLIO`/`PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED` semantics. The course additionally requires a **layered agent context** design, context assembly and compaction constraints, which this ADR records.\n \n Constraints from the current selection (treated as fixed working decisions): CLI-only UI; `PORTFOLIO_DIR=<root>/portfolios`; `--without-portfolio`; `--portfolio-as-of`; consent behaviour; full normalized-content SHA-256 fingerprint; no silent fallback; no invented zero holdings/cash; model cannot assign checks.\n \n ## Course-required layered context (design)\n \n | Layer | Content (bounded application context) | Source |\n |---|---|---|\n | Identity | Instrument/ticker + resolved identity context | `agents/context.py:build_instrument_context` |\n | Standing constraints | Advisory-only role; no execution; rating vocabulary; disclaimer requirement; \"no account ownership assumed\" | prompts + frozen strings |\n | Knowledge | Analyst reports, research/trader plans, risk debate | graph state |\n | History | Memory-log lessons from prior decisions | `tradingagents/memory/` |\n | State | Input mode, selected basename, as-of/basis, fingerprint (safe projection) | `RunContext` |\n | Current task | The run's instruction to produce a rating + decision | node prompt |\n \n ### Context assembly pipeline (application-bound)\n `deduplicate → prioritize (identity/constraints first) → budget (per-agent token cap) → compact (summarize low-priority narrative; never drop mode/snapshot identity/output authority/critical constraints) → assemble (final prompt)`.\n \n #### Operational budget and compaction design (B3-07, F6; proposed, unmeasured)\n All numbers are **proposed design values (ESTIMATE)**, not measured. C/D later verify/measure.\n \n - **Estimator:** token counts approximated by `ceil(len(prompt_chars)/4)` (cheap, provider-agnostic; **explicitly estimated**, no guarantee against provider tokenizer; no tokenizer dependency added).\n - **Per-agent context cap** `C_cap = 24,000` estimated tokens (proposed): bounds the **assembled prompt context** for one agent, not an aggregate run budget.\n - **Critical reserve** `R_reserve = 4,000` estimated tokens (proposed) planned for identity + standing constraints + state/authority + frozen notice/disclaimer; never compacted.\n - **Compaction threshold** `T_compact = floor(0.8 · C_cap) = floor(19,200) = 19,200`; compact when estimated context exceeds `T_compact`; hard stop at `C_cap`. (Arithmetic corrected: 0.8 × 24,000 = **19,200**, not 20,000.)\n - **Protected-context overflow (actual estimate, not the constant):** let `P` be the **measured estimate of the protected layers** (identity + constraints + state/authority + notice/disclaimer) at assembly time. If `P + (minimum irreducible task/history context) > C_cap`, or more simply if `P > C_cap − C_min_task` (where `C_min_task` is the minimum needed for the current task), **fail closed** (typed `INTERNAL_ERROR`, redacted). The guard compares the **actual protected estimate `P`**, never merely `R_reserve` (which by construction is ≤ `C_cap` and could never overflow).\n - **Compaction termination:** compaction reduces only low-priority narrative (debate prose, redundant analyst text) until total ≤ `T_compact` or until the only remaining reducible content is protected; if compacting all reducible narrative still leaves total > `C_cap`, **fail closed**. Available narrative budget = `C_cap − P`; stop when narrative reaches that bound.\n - **Compaction method:** summarize/trim **low-priority narrative layers only**; deterministic truncation with an explicit \"(compacted)\" marker is the baseline. If a summarizing **model call** is used it is an **explicitly disclosed extra provider call** logged as `event=context.compact` — not silent network behaviour. Default design = deterministic truncation (no extra model; consistent with the note that these corrections imply **no new summarizing provider call**).\n - **Re-injection:** after compaction re-inject identity, mode, snapshot identity (fingerprint/basename/as-of), output authority and frozen disclaimer/notice.\n - **Where:** node-prompt assembly in the agent context layer (`tradingagents/agents/context.py` + prompt builders); **not** OpenCode's internal context.\n - **Temporal guards:** memory/context retrieval keeps upstream as-of/time guards; compaction must not reintroduce out-of-window history.\n - **Illustrative over-cap (document example; arithmetic verified):** assembled estimate = 26,000 tokens; protected `P ≈ 3,200` (identity/constraints/state/notice). Reducible narrative ≈ 22,800. Compaction truncates older bull/bear debate prose (~6,500 → ~500, saving ~6,000) giving 26,000 − 6,000 = **20,000**, still > `T_compact`=19,200, so further low-priority narrative is trimmed (e.g., another ~800) to reach ≈ **19,200** ≤ `T_compact`; protected `P` and current task survive. If instead `P` were 23,000, then `C_cap − P = 1,000` narrative budget, and it fails closed when the minimum task context cannot fit.\n - **Distinction:** bounded **application-context** design; not OpenCode internal management; **not** an aggregate run-token/time/call budget (deferred).\n \n ## Decision\n \n Adopt **C2: an input-service + deeply immutable `RunContext` boundary with a small explicit CLI lifecycle coordinator and a shared execution service.**\n \n - `PortfolioInputService` (`tradingagents/runapi/input_service.py`): the sole discoverer/validator/freezer; produces a `RunContext`.\n - `RunContext`/`FrozenSnapshot` (`runapi/context.py`): deeply immutable value tuples + mode + full-64 canonical SHA-256 + as-of/basis + consent_state; read-only provenance source.\n - **Shared execution service** (`runapi/execution.py: run_analysis_api`): the **common application entry** for CLI and supported project API; rejects non-`CONFIRMED` contexts; owns execution, exception mapping, checks, finalize, staging/publish and terminal event; prompt-free.\n - `RunLifecycleCoordinator` (CLI layer): interactive selection/consent transitions; no LLM; no broad orchestration rewrite; no backtest/resume.\n - `OutputChecker` and `OutcomeFinalizer` are the sole assigners of `output_check`/`run_outcome`.\n - Upstream engine signature preserved; the raw primitive is a declared reduced-coverage path whose product reliance requires A's approval (R-API).\n \n ## Alternatives considered (actual, preserved)\n \n - **C1 — Minimal baseline extension.** Inline discovery/validation (sole shared module, thin inline adapter); header lines appended in reporting; small checker; inline manifest. Pros: smallest footprint. Cons: lifecycle sequencing inline; higher risk of provenance drift if reporting re-derives from `final_state` (latent FR-006/007 risk); weakest typed failure behaviour. Score 3.30.\n - **C2 — Input-service + `RunContext` + small coordinator + shared execution service (selected).** Pros: explicit input/snapshot boundary; clean test seams; shared provenance; typed outcomes; full-coverage API path. Cons: more modules than C1. Score 4.65.\n - **C3 — Phased single-run orchestrator façade.** Same service/context, plus a façade over the whole single-run lifecycle. Pros: strong phase testing. Cons: broader `cli/run.py` change; highest coupling/surface; scope-creep risk. Score 3.75.\n \n ## Human selection rationale (recorded verbatim in substance)\n \n Brian selected **C2** because of its **explicit input/snapshot boundary, test seams and shared provenance, without C3's broader orchestration change.** This is a **human design choice based on estimated tradeoffs**, explicitly **not** a claim of verified superiority.\n \n ## Consequences\n \n Positive: single provenance source; deterministic check authority; consent is an explicit transition; shared execution service gives full-coverage API path; preserved engine signature.\n Negative/risks: the raw low-level engine primitive can bypass the boundary and its product use requires A's approval (R-API); full-64 fingerprint canonicalization must be exactly implemented (`interface-contracts.md` §2.2); prompt/context wording changes are required (not optional).\n+Scope note: the implemented optional-portfolio flow is retained here. The broader `REQ-TA-*` candidate's scope statement excludes portfolio files while its fixture profiles include them; that replacement-scope disagreement is **unresolved (A/C/team)** and does not change this ADR's decision.\n \n ## Repairs (2026-11-21, R1–R5)\n \n These bounded repairs keep the selected architecture; see [remediation record](../../reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md).\n \n - **R4:** the Research Manager now receives the same protected `get_portfolio_context_from_state` block as the Trader and Portfolio Manager, so its investment plan cannot assert a nonexistent position or treat unknown input as flat. It adds a stage-appropriate instruction to correct conflicting upstream ownership premises; the five-tier research vocabulary and three-action Trader vocabulary are unchanged and no rating is forced.\n - **R5:** publication stages a private tentative terminal on the `EventSink` and only commits the caller-visible terminal after the single directory rename succeeds; a critical publication failure exposes exactly one matching `INCOMPLETE` terminal. Terminal-append failure alone still preserves the logical outcome with `terminal_event.durable=false`; report/manifest remain critical and the single-terminal rule is preserved.\n \n+## Implementation status at `a62b801` (verified 2026-11-24)\n+\n+The C2 boundary is present in the checkout, not merely designed:\n+\n+- `runapi/input_service.py` (`PortfolioInputService`, `freeze_explicit`, `freeze_no_portfolio`), `runapi/context.py` (`RunContext`, `FrozenSnapshot`, `ConsentState`), `runapi/execution.py` (`run_analysis_api`, rejects non-`CONFIRMED` at `:149`), `runapi/checks.py` (`OutputChecker`, Q1–Q4), `runapi/finalize.py` (`classify_exception`, `OutcomeFinalizer`), `runapi/persist.py` (single `os.rename` publication at `:154`), `runapi/events.py` (stage-private tentative terminal), `runapi/result.py` (`RunResult`/`CheckResult`/`Finding`), `runapi/reporting.py` (`build_envelope`, `verify_envelope_header_matches`), `runapi/redact.py`.\n+- R1–R5 repairs are implemented (`agents/structured.py` applies the shared `Redactor` to its fallback warnings). Independent acceptance of these repairs remains **pending (C)**; the implementation's own remediation record is `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.\n+- The C-owned tests under `tests/member_c_verification/offline/` define the seams; passing status is C's to report, not this ADR's.\n+\n+## Proposed broader requirements — impact, **not** implemented\n+\n+The uploaded `requirements.yaml` (`status: proposed_for_adoption`) and A's later correspondence would extend the as-built system. If adopted, the following are architecture impacts, documented but **not** designed as accepted decisions here:\n+\n+- **`BUDGET` stop reason** and a run-wide **single-use call-reservation** controller (`REQ-TA-RUN-001`, `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002`): would add a sixth serialized `StopReason`, a shared budget component consulted before every model dispatch, and updates to every reader. The current five-value literal (`runapi/result.py:12-14`) has no `BUDGET`.\n+- **R1–R8 output check** (`REQ-TA-ARCH-002`) and **corrected-only `PASSED`** (R5): R2 (evidence-ID resolution) and R4–R7 (sentiment/coverage) require new data fields and registry components the checker does not inspect; R5 would change `Finding.status`/`CheckResult` so `PASSED` can carry corrected findings — a coordinated type change across checks/report/scorer if retained.\n+- **Evidence and coverage registries** (`REQ-TA-FR-001`, `REQ-TA-FR-005`, `REQ-TA-INV-002/007`), **aggregate budgets/resume** (`REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002`, `COST-001/002`, D-5): new components and a resume contract that currently conflicts with `INV-11`/`INV-12`.\n+- **`REQ-TA-INV-014` / `REQ-TA-GOV-004`** are pending publication; the existing design already covers input freezing (`INV-04/05/05b`) and treats schema validation as a governance/CI boundary, so their absence does not change C2's data flow.\n+\n ## Reopening conditions\n \n - Instructor mandates a single orchestration façade → revisit C3.\n - File-count/scope constraints favour C1 → revisit.\n - Real test evidence (C) shows C1's inline path is cleanly testable with no provenance drift → re-score.\n - Any change to consent semantics, provenance identity or check authority requires a new ADR.\n \n ## Related\n \n - Canonical blueprint: [../../../architecture-blueprint.md](../../../architecture-blueprint.md)\n - [../interface-contracts.md](../interface-contracts.md), [../evaluation-table.md](../evaluation-table.md), [../evaluation-logbook.md](../evaluation-logbook.md), [../risk-list.md](../risk-list.md), [../option-ledger.md](../option-ledger.md), [../invariants.md](../invariants.md), [../memory-design.md](../memory-design.md), [../runtime-policy-catalog.md](../runtime-policy-catalog.md), [../permission-model.md](../permission-model.md), [../traceability-inputs-member-b.md](../traceability-inputs-member-b.md).\n",

Candidates (neutral)\n \n - **C1 — Minimal baseline extension.** Sole shared `portfolio_input` module (discover/validate/freeze) with a **thin inline adapter** in `cli/main.py`; header lines appended in reporting; small checker; inline manifest. Disqualifying constraints pre-screen (DQ1–DQ10)\n \n | # | Constraint | C1 | Rationale | C2 | Rationale | C3 | Rationale |\n |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n | DQ1 | No prompts in agents/engine | Pass | Discovery/consent in CLI entry; agents untouched | Pass | Service/coordinator in CLI layer; engine API unchanged | Pass | Façade is CLI-layer coordinator |\n | DQ2 | No silent default file pick | Pass | Inline requires explicit choice | Pass | `discover()` returns sorted list; explicit selection | Pass | Same service |\n | DQ3 | Absent ≠ flat; missing cash ≠ 0 | Pass | Reuses `PortfolioContext` semantics | Pass | `RunContext` explicit mode + None vs empty | Pass | Same as C2 |\n | DQ4 | Recoverable sentinel not fatal | Pass | Outcome finalizer module | Pass | Finalizer consumes typed exceptions | Pass | Delegates to same finalizer |\n | DQ5 | Model cannot set check/outcome | Pass | Checker separate; header from frozen state | Pass | `RunContext`+`OutputChecker` authoritative | Pass | Same authority objects |\n | DQ6 | No full portfolio payload to new sinks | Pass | Single redactor; discipline required | Pass | Provenance/`SafeRunMetadata` only; redactor at sink | Pass | Same |\n | DQ7 | Reusable input-service boundary | Pass | **Sole shared-service ownership with thin inline adapter** (resolved: one validator/discoverer; reporting reads only returned frozen context) | Pass | One service+immutable context | Pass | Same service+context |\n | DQ8 | Mode-aware prompt/context wording | Pass | Manager prompt edits required | Pass | Same edits via rendered context | Pass | Same |\n | DQ9 | Redaction across sinks | Pass | One helper at each sink | Pass | Redactor at sink boundary | Pass | Same |\n | DQ10 | No backtest/resume scope creep | Pass | CLI single-run only | Pass | Coordinator scoped to one fresh run | Pass | Façade strictly single-run |\n \n All three are eligible.
