Authoritative, non-LLM. | `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py` | additive |\n| `OutcomeFinalizer` | Maps graph return/exceptions/attempted critical-persistence failure to `run_outcome` + `stop_reason`. | `tradingagents/runapi/finalize.py` | additive |\n| `Redactor` | Central masking (keys/tokens/bearer, unsafe diagnostics) at every sink. | `tradingagents/runapi/redact.py` | additive |\n| `EventSink` (JSONL) | Fixed-field structured events. | `tradingagents/runapi/events.py` | additive |\n| Persistence/Manifest | Staging (report+manifest **critical**; terminal event **best-effort**) → single atomic directory commit; manifest via `SafeRunMetadata`; `terminal_event.durable` decided pre-commit without blocking publication. | `tradingagents/runapi/persist.py` | additive |\n| Result schemas | `RunResult`, `CheckResult`, `Finding`, `InputError`, `SafeInputMetadata`, `SafeRunMetadata`, `EffectiveConfig`. | `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` | additive |\n| CLI input UI | Interactive discovery/consent **only** here. | `cli/input_ui.py` | additive |\n| CLI adapter | Thin wiring; adds `--without-portfolio`, `--portfolio-as-of`; suppresses prompts under flags. | `cli/main.py` | adapted |\n| Prompt/context semantics | Mode-aware rating-scale legend; no-portfolio Hold meaning; user-supplied/unverified wording. | `tradingagents/agents/context.py`, manager/trader prompts | adapted |\n| Reporting boundary | Renders checked **body** + trusted **envelope header** from `SafeRunMetadata`; stage labels. | `tradingagents/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/report_html.py` | adapted |\n| Existing loader/model | `PortfolioContext`/`Position` validation and rendering; alias matching. | `tradingagents/portfolio.py` (preserved) | unchanged semantics |\n| Raw engine primitive | `TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run/create_run_state` signature preserved; **does not** traverse the boundary (reduced scope, A approval for product use). | `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` | signature preserved |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Advisory versus authoritative data\n\n| Data | Nature | Authority |\n|---|---|---|\n| Model narrative, ratings text, recommendations | **Advisory** | Cannot set `output_check`/`run_outcome`/provenance |\n| Final rating (Buy/Overweight/Hold/Underweight/Sell/REVIEW) | Derived deterministically from the PM output | Reported, but check Q1 only *reads* readability |\n| Frozen snapshot metadata (mode, basename, fingerprint, as-of) | **Authoritative** (trusted state) | Built by input service; used by header/result/check |\n| `output_check` (PASSED/NEEDS_REVIEW/NOT_RUN) + findings | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutputChecker` only |\n| `run_outcome` (COMPLETED/INCOMPLETE) + `stop_reason` | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutcomeFinalizer` only |\n\nThe disclaimer and no-portfolio notice are **frozen strings** (selected-requirements §1) and are treated as trusted content, excluded from Q4 phrase scanning.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Workflow (selected C2)\n\n1. **Discover** eligible `.json` files (non-recursive, sorted, symlinks excluded) from `PORTFOLIO_DIR` — or accept explicit `--portfolio PATH` (outside dir allowed; parent not scanned).\n2. **Select** one file, or choose no-portfolio, or cancel.\n3. **Validate/precheck** the frozen bytes; reuse upstream model validation after explicit shape/type/as-of prechecks. Empty positions is valid (flat); no silent fallback.\n4. **Freeze** → `RunContext` (deeply immutable value tuples; full-64 canonical fingerprint; as-of/basis recorded). Consent state `FROZEN`.\n5. **Notice** (portfolio mode; §6) then **confirm** → `CONFIRMED` (default No). Non-interactive: valid flags are the consent expression.\n6. **Run** via the **shared execution service** (`runapi/execution.py`): rejects any `RunContext` not `CONFIRMED`. Holdings reach the provider **only after** confirmation.\n7. **Render body → scrub → single check (Q1–Q4; Q2 inspects the pre-check provenance fragment against explicit trusted metadata) → finalize → build trusted envelope → stage report+manifest (critical) → one atomic directory commit; terminal JSONL append is best-effort.** Incomplete runs bypass the checker and get `NOT_RUN`. The checked body is delivered unchanged; the envelope adds only trusted metadata. Terminal-event durability is decided before the manifest is staged but does not block publication; a terminal-append failure preserves the logical outcome and records `durable=false`. (§ interface-contracts §6–§7).\n8. Pre-run cancellation/rejection starts **no graph, zero LLM calls, no completed run**; a critical persistence failure yields a typed INCOMPLETE result that never contradicts a returned success.\n\nDetailed state machine, schemas, canonicalization, ordering and failure simulations: `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md`.\n\n### 5.1 Synthetic input-mode walkthrough (document example, not a passing test)\n- **Interactive, portfolio:** user sees `a.json`, `b.json`; selects `b.json`; precheck passes; freezes `b` (fingerprint Fb); notice shows basename `b.json`, date D, as-of basis, provider-transmission statement; user answers Yes → `CONFIRMED`; run transmits frozen `b` after consent; report header carries Fb and mode `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED`.\n- **Interactive, no portfolio:** empty directory → no-portfolio confirmation with frozen notice; Yes → `CONFIRMED` with `portfolio=None`; header shows `NO_PORTFOLIO`, null file/fingerprint/as-of.\n- **Noninteractive:** `--portfolio b.json --portfolio-as-of D` → freezes b, consent via flags, no prompt. `--without-portfolio` → `NO_PORTFOLIO`. Neither/both → `InputError`, zero calls.\n- **Cancelled:** user answers No at consent → zero graph/LLM, no completed run, counted as a pre-run attempt (NFR-006).\n\n---\n\n## 6. Permissions and consent\n\n- Interactive discovery/selection/consent lives **only** in the CLI (`cli/`). Agents and the engine never prompt.\n- **Consent gate** is an explicit coordinator transition between freeze and run. A frozen snapshot is a *candidate input*, **not** a confirmed selection; immutability alone does **not** prevent bypass. Only a coordinator transition to `CONFIRMED` permits run entry (see interface-contracts §4, ADR §Consent).\n- Mandatory execution, exception mapping, checks and artifact finalization sit behind a **shared application boundary** (`tradingagents/runapi/execution.py: run_analysis_api`) usable without terminal prompts. The upstream Python API signature is **preserved**; the supported project API routes through `run_analysis_api` (full requirement coverage). A raw low-level engine primitive (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run`) remains available but **does not** traverse the boundary and **does not** satisfy FR-006/FR-007/NFR-002/003/004; its scope is declared and product reliance requires **A's approval** (residual risk R-API, pending A). See `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` §5.\n- Coding-agent file permissions (separate concern) are in `docs/architecture/permission-model.md`; E implements enforcement.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Observability\n\n- New lifecycle event sink: UTF-8 JSONL; fixed fields `run_id, ticker, node, ts(UTC), elapsed_ms, event, event_outcome`. Console stays human-readable. Raw provider payload logging disabled by default. Progress vocabulary is separate from terminal `run_outcome`.\n- Existing sinks are adapted, not silently trusted: see memory-design §Sinks and runtime-policy-catalog.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Verification strategy (design-level only)\n\n- **Testability seams** (for C): `PortfolioInputService` (discover/validate/freeze), `RunContext` identity, `OutputChecker` (Q1–Q4 with injected model claims), `OutcomeFinalizer` (typed exceptions), redaction at each sink, manifest atomicity, same-date isolation.\n- **Observable positive/negative seams** are listed per requirement in `docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md` for C. B does not write test code or claim results.\n- **Document consistency checks** (this session) are **not** application verification.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Change policy\n\n- ADRs required for safety-affecting changes (`GOV-006`); changes to provenance identity, check authority, redaction boundary or consent transitions require a new/updated ADR.\n- Preserve upstream `tradingagents/`, `cli/`, `pyproject.toml` and tests unless an approved layout decision changes this.\n- Intentional CLI/type-validation changes are documented in the ADR; they are not treated as accidental compatibility failures.\n- Later architecture revisions based on real test evidence must cite that evidence (not manufactured now).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Requirement allocation summary\n\nFull per-ID allocation (enforced-by component, fallback, other-owner/deferred) is in `docs/architecture/invariants.md` and `docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md`. Summary:\n\n- FR-001/002/003/004 → `PortfolioInputService` + `RunContext` + prompt semantics + coordinator consent.\n- FR-005 → reporting stage labels; reuse `tradingagents/agents/rating.py` (REVIEW ≠ Hold).\n- FR-006/FR-007 → provenance projection + `OutputChecker` (authoritative).\n- NFR-001 → `runapi/finalize.py`; NFR-002 → `runapi/events.py`; NFR-003 → `runapi/redact.py`; NFR-004 → `runapi/persist.py` + fresh run ID; NFR-005 → `runapi/execution.py` shared service + preserved signature; NFR-006 → `RunRecord` accounting (interface-contracts §10).\n- GOV-001..006 → allocated to C/E/A/human; B contributes permission model for `GOV-006`.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Selection made by Brian (human) 2026-11-12; awaiting team/instructor reconciliation. Not implementation.\n4: - Deciders: Brian (selection), Member B (author), pending A (requirements coherence), E (governance/assembly).\n5: - Scope: `SEL-TA-FR-001..007`, `SEL-TA-NFR-001..006`, `SEL-TA-GOV-006` (permission design contribution).\n6: - Supersedes: none. Does not modify v2 requirements or the D1 registry (A owns).\n7: \n8: > Estimates in this ADR are labelled **ESTIMATE** and are design judgements. No measurement or verification is claimed.\n9: \n10: ## Context\n11: \n12: TradingAgents v0.7.1 already has an optional `--portfolio PATH` that loads a `PortfolioContext` and renders it into decision-agent prompts (`cli/main.py:50-55`, `tradingagents/portfolio.py`, `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py:293-307`). The selected requirements extend this into a discovery + explicit-consent + frozen-provenance + deterministic-check workflow, with distinct `NO_PORTFOLIO`/`PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED` semantics. The course additionally requires a **layered agent context** design, context assembly and compaction constraints, which this ADR records.\n13: \n14: Constraints from the current selection (treated as fixed working decisions): CLI-only UI; `PORTFOLIO_DIR=<root>/portfolios`; `--without-portfolio`; `--portfolio-as-of`; consent behaviour; full normalized-content SHA-256 fingerprint; no silent fallback; no invented zero holdings/cash; model cannot assign checks.\n15: \n16: ## Course-required layered context (design)\n17: \n18: | Layer | Content (bounded application context) | Source |\n19: |---|---|---|\n20: | Identity | Instrument/ticker + resolved identity context | `agents/context.py:build_instrument_context` |\n21: | Standing constraints | Advisory-only role; no execution; rating vocabulary; disclaimer requirement; \"no account ownership assumed\" | prompts + frozen strings |\n22: | Knowledge | Analyst reports, research/trader plans, risk debate | graph state |\n23: | History | Memory-log lessons from prior decisions | `tradingagents/memory/` |\n24: | State | Input mode, selected basename, as-of/basis, fingerprint (safe projection) | `RunContext` |\n25: | Current task | The run's instruction to produce a rating + decision | node prompt |\n26: \n27: ### Context assembly pipeline (application-bound)\n28: `deduplicate → prioritize (identity/constraints first) → budget (per-agent token cap) → compact (summarize low-priority narrative; never drop mode/snapshot identity/output authority/critical constraints) → assemble (final prompt)`.\n29: \n30: #### Operational budget and compaction design (B3-07, F6; proposed, unmeasured)\n31: All numbers are **proposed design values (ESTIMATE)**, not measured. C/D later verify/measure.\n32: \n33: - **Estimator:** token counts approximated by `ceil(len(prompt_chars)/4)` (cheap, provider-agnostic; **explicitly estimated**, no guarantee against provider tokenizer; no tokenizer dependency added).\n34: - **Per-agent context cap** `C_cap = 24,000` estimated tokens (proposed): bounds the **assembled prompt context** for one agent, not an aggregate run budget.\n35: - **Critical reserve** `R_reserve = 4,000` estimated tokens (proposed) planned for identity + standing constraints + state/authority + frozen notice/disclaimer; never compacted.\n36: - **Compaction threshold** `T_compact = floor(0.8 · C_cap) = floor(19,200) = 19,200`; compact when estimated context exceeds `T_compact`; hard stop at `C_cap`. (Arithmetic corrected: 0.8 × 24,000 = **19,200**, not 20,000.)\n37: - **Protected-context overflow (actual estimate, not the constant):** let `P` be the **measured estimate of the protected layers** (identity + constraints + state/authority + notice/disclaimer) at assembly time. If `P + (minimum irreducible task/history context) > C_cap`, or more simply if `P > C_cap − C_min_task` (where `C_min_task` is the minimum needed for the current task), **fail closed** (typed `INTERNAL_ERROR`, redacted). The guard compares the **actual protected estimate `P`**, never merely `R_reserve` (which by construction is ≤ `C_cap` and could never overflow).\n38: - **Compaction termination:** compaction reduces only low-priority narrative (debate prose, redundant analyst text) until total ≤ `T_compact` or until the only remaining reducible content is protected; if compacting all reducible narrative still leaves total > `C_cap`, **fail closed**. Available narrative budget = `C_cap − P`; stop when narrative reaches that bound.\n39: - **Compaction method:** summarize/trim **low-priority narrative layers only**; deterministic truncation with an explicit \"(compacted)\" marker is the baseline. If a summarizing **model call** is used it is an **explicitly disclosed extra provider call** logged as `event=context.compact` — not silent network behaviour. Default design = deterministic truncation (no extra model; consistent with the note that these corrections imply **no new summarizing provider call**).\n40: - **Re-injection:** after compaction re-inject identity, mode, snapshot identity (fingerprint/basename/as-of), output authority and frozen disclaimer/notice.\n41: - **Where:** node-prompt assembly in the agent context layer (`tradingagents/agents/context.py` + prompt builders); **not** OpenCode's internal context.\n42: - **Temporal guards:** memory/context retrieval keeps upstream as-of/time guards; compaction must not reintroduce out-of-window history.\n43: - **Illustrative over-cap (document example; arithmetic verified):** assembled estimate = 26,000 tokens; protected `P ≈ 3,200` (identity/constraints/state/notice). Reducible narrative ≈ 22,800. Compaction truncates older bull/bear debate prose (~6,500 → ~500, saving ~6,000) giving 26,000 − 6,000 = **20,000**, still > `T_compact`=19,200, so further low-priority narrative is trimmed (e.g., another ~800) to reach ≈ **19,200** ≤ `T_compact`; protected `P` and current task survive. If instead `P` were 23,000, then `C_cap − P = 1,000` narrative budget, and it fails closed when the minimum task context cannot fit.\n44: - **Distinction:** bounded **application-context** design; not OpenCode internal management; **not** an aggregate run-token/time/call budget (deferred).\n45: \n46: ## Decision\n47: \n48: Adopt **C2: an input-service + deeply immutable `RunContext` boundary with a small explicit CLI lifecycle coordinator and a shared execution service.**\n49: \n50: - `PortfolioInputService` (`tradingagents/runapi/input_service.py`): the sole discoverer/validator/freezer; produces a `RunContext`.\n51: - `RunContext`/`FrozenSnapshot` (`runapi/context.py`): deeply immutable value tuples + mode + full-64 canonical SHA-256 + as-of/basis + consent_state; read-only provenance source.\n52: - **Shared execution service** (`runapi/execution.py: run_analysis_api`): the **common application entry** for CLI and supported project API; rejects non-`CONFIRMED` contexts; owns execution, exception mapping, checks, finalize, staging/publish and terminal event; prompt-free.\n53: - `RunLifecycleCoordinator` (CLI layer): interactive selection/consent transitions; no LLM; no broad orchestration rewrite; no backtest/resume.\n54: - `OutputChecker` and `OutcomeFinalizer` are the sole assigners of `output_check`/`run_outcome`.\n55: - Upstream engine signature preserved; the raw primitive is a declared reduced-coverage path whose product reliance requires A's approval (R-API).\n56: \n57: ## Alternatives considered (actual, preserved)\n58: \n59: - **C1 — Minimal baseline extension.** Inline discovery/validation (sole shared module, thin inline adapter); header lines appended in reporting; small checker; inline manifest. Pros: smallest footprint. Cons: lifecycle sequencing inline; higher risk of provenance drift if reporting re-derives from `final_state` (latent FR-006/007 risk); weakest typed failure behaviour. An explicitly supplied empty `positions` list is a **flat** snapshot, not missing input.\n43: \n44: ### 2.2 Canonical fingerprint bytes (B3-03, F2)\n45: The new provenance fingerprint is **SHA-256 (64 lowercase hex chars)** over a **canonical JSON byte string** of the normalized snapshot. Exact rules:\n46: \n47: 1. **Normalized object** contains exactly: `{\"cash\":…,\"currency\":…,\"positions\":[{\"ticker\":…,\"quantity\":…,\"average_price\":…}, …]}`. No other keys participate.\n48: 2. **Key order:** lexicographic ascending at every object level (`sort_keys=True`).\n49: 3. **Encoding:** UTF-8, **no BOM**, **no trailing newline**; bytes are `json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(\",\", \":\"), ensure_ascii=False).encode(\"utf-8\")`.\n50: 4. **Separators:** `,` and `:` with **no whitespace** (`separators=(\",\", \":\")`).\n51: 5. **String escaping:** JSON string escaping only (`ensure_ascii=False`, so non-ASCII tickers are emitted as UTF-8, not `\\uXXXX`); no additional escaping. Tickers are trimmed and uppercased before serialization.\n52: 6. **Null/default handling:** an absent optional field and an explicit JSON `null` are the **same** and are serialized as the JSON token `null` (`average_price`, `cash`, `currency`).\n53: 7. **Number-token serialization (exact):** every numeric field is first converted by `to_canonical_number(x)`:\n54:    - reject non-finite (`NaN`/`±Inf`) at validation (never reach canonicalization);\n55:    - normalize `-0.0` to `0.0`;\n56:    - if the value is integral and `|x| < 2**53`, emit the **integer token** (e.g., `10`, `1`, `0`), so `1` and `1.0` → token `1`;\n57:    - otherwise emit Python `float.__repr__` (shortest round-trippable decimal, e.g., `150.5`, `0.1`).\n58:    This defines the exact byte token; it is not \"whatever JSON does\".\n59: 8. **Positions sort — total order (no `None`/float comparison):** sort the canonical **row objects** by the composite key `(ticker_upper, to_canonical_number(quantity), price_key)` where `price_key = (0, 0.0)` when `average_price is None` and `(1, to_canonical_number(average_price))` otherwise (a tagged tuple: null sorts **before** any number; numeric compares numerically). Because `ticker_upper` is a string and is part of the key, **two different broker spellings that normalize to the same symbol but differ in spelling sort by their hashed spelling**, and a full-row tie is impossible unless all three hashed fields are equal (identical rows are interchangeable, so input order cannot change the digest). This is a **total order over every field that participates in the digest**, so reordering input never changes the digest and no valid portfolio is rejected by sorting.\n60: 9. **Symbol spelling:** `ticker` is hashed using the **original spelling** as supplied (trimmed, uppercased). Holdings keep their spelling (`portfolio.py:40-68`); alias matching is a runtime concern, not identity. Two files differing only by broker alias spelling are **different** provenance and therefore **different** digests (both are accepted; ordering above remains total).\n61: 10. **Excluded fields:** `basename`, filesystem path, mtime, `portfolio_as_of`, `as_of_basis`, `mode` are recorded separately in metadata, **not** in the content digest.\n62: \n63: > Invariant: INV-05. Upstream truncated 12-char checkpoint fingerprint (`portfolio.py:70-72`, `trading_graph.py:158`) is **preserved unchanged** and unrelated to this digest.\n64: \n65: #### 2.2.1 Exact canonical-byte examples (verified against the rules above)\n66: Row order after sorting is shown; bytes are exactly the string inside quotes.\n67: \n68: - **Reason A — null vs numeric price (reversed input):**\n69:   - Input `[(\"AAPL\",10,None),(\"AAPL\",10,2.0)]` and reversed `[(\"AAPL\",10,2.0),(\"AAPL\",10,None)]` both serialize to\n70:     `{\"cash\":null,\"currency\":null,\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":null,\"quantity\":10,\"ticker\":\"AAPL\"},{\"average_price\":2,\"quantity\":10,\"ticker\":\"AAPL\"}]}` → **equal digest** (null sorts before numeric; `10`/`2` are integer tokens).\n71: - **Reason B — broker-alias tie (reversed input):**\n72:   - Input `[(\"BRK.B\",5,100.0),(\"BRK-B\",5,100.0)]` and reversed both serialize to\n73:     `{\"cash\":null,\"currency\":null,\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":100,\"quantity\":5,\"ticker\":\"BRK-B\"},{\"average_price\":100,\"quantity\":5,\"ticker\":\"BRK.B\"}]}` → **equal digest** (`\"BRK-B\"` < `\"BRK.B\"`; spelling is part of the sort key). Reindexing the **spelling** (e.g., `BRK.B`→`BRK-B` on the other row) is a **different** portfolio by rule 9 and yields a different digest.\n74: - **Reason C — numeric `1` vs `1.0`:**\n75:   - `[(\"MSFT\",1,50)]` cash `1` and `[(\"MSFT\",1.0,50.0)]` cash `1.0` both serialize to\n76:     `{\"cash\":1,\"currency\":null,\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":50,\"quantity\":1,\"ticker\":\"MSFT\"}]}` → **equal digest**.\n77: - **Reason D — missing vs explicit null:** a position with absent `average_price` and one with explicit `null` serialize identically (`\"average_price\":null`) → **equal digest**.\n78: - **Reason E — full example with cash:** `[(\"AAPL\",10,150.5),(\"MSFT\",5,None)]`, cash `2500.0`, currency `\"USD\"` →\n79:   `{\"cash\":2500,\"currency\":\"USD\",\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":150.5,\"quantity\":10,\"ticker\":\"AAPL\"},{\"average_price\":null,\"quantity\":5,\"ticker\":\"MSFT\"}]}`\n80:   → SHA-256 `45f07d9eb3359b059525da0cee26f8a9810269dad11ffb4c42e1dcc7072cef72`.\n81: - **Expected difference:** changing `quantity` from `10` to `10.5`, adding a position, or altering cash/currency changes the digest.\n82: \n83: These are **document examples** checked against the written rules, not passing application tests.\n84: \n85: ### 2.3 Deep immutability (B3-03)\n86: Upstream `PortfolioContext` holds a mutable `list[Position]` of mutable model instances. `RunContext` immutability alone is insufficient. Design:\n87: \n88: - The frozen snapshot is stored as **immutable value tuples**:\n89:   ```\n90:   FrozenPositions = tuple[tuple[str, float, float | None], ...]   # (ticker, quantity, average_price)\n91:   FrozenSnapshot = (basename, cash: float|None, currency: str|None,\n92:                     positions: FrozenPositions, fingerprint_sha256, portfolio_as_of)\n93:   ```\n94: - `RunContext` is a frozen dataclass holding these tuples; it exposes **no mutable accessor**.\n95: - When agents need a `PortfolioContext`, the boundary **constructs a fresh `PortfolioContext`** from the frozen tuples (defensive copy) on each use; it never hands out a shared mutable object. Mutation of that constructed object cannot affect the stored identity.\n96: - The canonical bytes are computed from the frozen tuples, so they are stable regardless of later copies.\n97: \n98: ### 2.4 `RunContext`\n99: ```\n100: RunContext (frozen dataclass) {\n101:   run_id: str\n102:   ticker: str\n103:   analysis_date: str\n104:   mode: InputMode\n105:   snapshot: FrozenSnapshot | None      # None ⇔ NO_PORTFOLIO\n106:   unverified_holdings: bool\n107:   provider_transmission_disclosed: bool\n108:   consent_state: FROZEN | CONFIRMED    # see §4\n109: }\n110: ```\n111: `snapshot is None` **iff** `mode == NO_PORTFOLIO`. `consent_state=FROZEN` ⇒ run not authorized; a snapshot existing does **not** authorize (B3-01, §4).\n112: \n113: ---\n114: \n115: ## 3. Complete schemas and conditional fields (addresses B3-02)\n116: \n117: All projections below are **separately defined** and **never** serialize the portfolio payload or full `RunContext`. Field names use the selected spelling.\n118: \n119: ### 3.1 `InputError`\n120: ```\n121: InputError {\n122:   kind: \"MALFORMED_JSON\" | \"MISSING_POSITIONS\" | \"MISSING_QUANTITY\" | \"NONFINITE_NUMBER\"\n123:         | \"WRONG_SCALAR_TYPE\" | \"UNREADABLE_PATH\" | \"AS_OF_MISMATCH\" | \"FLAG_CONFLICT\"\n124:   basename: str | null          # null when path unreadable before basename known\n125:   field: str | null             # e.g. \"positions[2].quantity\"\n126:   detail: str                   # redacted, no file contents/credentials\n127: }\n128: ```\n129: \n130: ### 3.2 `Finding`\n131: ```\n132: Finding {\n133:   rule: \"Q1\" | \"Q2\" | \"Q3\" | \"Q4\" | \"CHECK_ERROR\"\n134:   status: \"BLOCKING\"\n135:   detail: str                   # redacted\n136: }\n137: ```\n138: \n139: ### 3.3 `CheckResult` (F3 — case table)\n140: ```\n141: CheckResult {\n142:   output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\"\n143:   findings: Finding[]\n144: }\n145: ```\n146: Authoritative case table (**checker is invoked only on the completed path**, §6):\n147: \n148: | Case | `output_check` | `findings` | When |\n149: |---|---|---|---|\n150: | All rules hold | `PASSED` | `[]` (exactly empty) | Completed run; Q1–Q4 all hold |\n151: | Any rule broken OR checker exception | `NEEDS_REVIEW` | **≥ 1** blocking finding (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4, or a single `CHECK_ERROR` on exception) | Completed run |\n152: | Run incomplete | `NOT_RUN` | `[]` (exactly empty) | Checker **not invoked**; assigned by finalizer branch (§6) |\n153: \n154: Invariants (H2 — empty-findings equivalence qualified to **completed** runs): **Completed** ⇒ `PASSED ⇔ findings==[]` and `NEEDS_REVIEW ⇒ findings≠[]`; **Incomplete** ⇒ `NOT_RUN` with `findings==[]` (checker not invoked). There is no global `PASSED ⇔ findings==[]` — `NOT_RUN` also has empty findings.\n155: \n156: ### 3.4 `RunResult` (returned to caller)\n157: ```\n158: RunResult {\n159:   run_id: str\n160:   ticker: str\n161:   analysis_date: str\n162:   input_mode: InputMode\n163:   run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\"\n164:   stop_reason: null | \"MODEL_FAILURE\" | \"DATA_FAILURE\" | \"INTERNAL_ERROR\"\n165:                | \"PERSISTENCE_ERROR\" | \"INTERRUPTED\"\n166:   final_rating: null | \"Buy\" | \"Overweight\" | \"Hold\" | \"Underweight\" | \"Sell\" | \"REVIEW\"\n167:   output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\"\n168:   findings: Finding[]\n169:   manifest_path: str | null     # non-null iff the run directory was published (§7)\n170:   report_path: str | null       # non-null iff the report was published (§7)\n171: }\n172: ```\n173: **Conditional fields (enforced by finalizer):**\n174: - `COMPLETED` ⇒ `final_rating != null` and `stop_reason == null`.\n175: - `INCOMPLETE` ⇒ `final_rating == null`, `output_check == \"NOT_RUN\"`, `findings == []`, `stop_reason != null`.\n176: \n177: ### 3.5 Safe input metadata projection (for sinks; never the payload)\n178: ```\n179: SafeInputMetadata {\n180:   run_id, ticker, analysis_date,\n181:   input_mode: InputMode,\n182:   basename: str | null,                 # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n183:   fingerprint_sha256: str | null,       # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO (64 hex)\n184:   portfolio_as_of: str | null,          # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n185:   as_of_basis: \"USER_CONFIRMED\" | null  # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n186: }\n187: ```\n188: The `null` conditions are **portfolio-only** (mode-dependent); distinct from **outcome-conditional** `RunResult` fields.\n189: \n190: ### 3.6 `SafeRunMetadata` (durable run record; never the payload) — F3\n191: ```\n192: SafeRunMetadata {\n193:   schema_version: \"1\",\n194:   run_id, ticker, analysis_date, input_mode,\n195:   basename: str|null, fingerprint_sha256: str|null, portfolio_as_of: str|null, as_of_basis: \"USER_CONFIRMED\"|null,\n196:   run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\",\n197:   stop_reason: ... | null,               # §3.4 conditional\n198:   final_rating: ... | null,              # §3.4 conditional — NOW CARRIED IN THE DURABLE RECORD\n199:   output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\",\n200:   findings: Finding[],\n201:   code_version: str,                     # tradingagents.__version__\n202:   source_revision: str | null,           # separate source identifier, e.g. git describe or \"unknown\" (§3.7)\n203:   prompt_hash: str,                      # §3.8\n204:   effective_config: EffectiveConfig,     # §3.7\n205:   start_ts_utc: str, end_ts_utc: str     # ISO-8601 UTC; set once at finalize\n206: }\n207: ```\n208: The **same** `final_rating` spelling/conditional rules as `RunResult` apply. Timestamps are captured once at finalize and are never mutated later.\n209: \n210: ### 3.7 `EffectiveConfig` (safe, behaviour-relevant; secrets/endpoints omitted) — F3\n211: ```\n212: EffectiveConfig {\n213:   llm_provider, deep_think_provider, deep_think_llm, quick_think_provider, quick_think_llm,\n214:   analysts: str[], max_debate_rounds: int, max_risk_discuss_rounds: int,\n215:   output_language: str,\n216:   temperature: float | null, max_tokens: int | null,          # behaviour-affecting (baseline keys if set)\n217:   context_cap_tokens: int, compaction_threshold_tokens: int,  # the designed context budget (ADR §Context)\n218:   data_vendors: map, tool_vendors: map\n219: }\n220: ```\n221: Derived from `run_settings()` (`trading_graph.py:255-275`) **plus** the behaviour-affecting keys this design introduces (`temperature`, `max_tokens`, context cap/threshold). `backend_url`, keys, OAuth tokens, local paths are **never** included. `source_revision` is recorded **separately** from `code_version` (upstream `version` stays `0.7.1`; the revision id identifies the actual source state and is `\"unknown\"` when unavailable).\n222: \n223: ### 3.8 `prompt_hash` (deterministic input spec) — F3\n224: - Inventory: the **template set** actually used = (a) identity/context instruction templates, (b) selected analyst templates, (c) trader + research/portfolio-manager templates, (d) frozen notice/disclaimer strings, (e) the mode-aware legend variants selected for this run.\n225: - Serialization: an ordered list `[(template_id, template_text), …]` sorted by `template_id`; each entry serialized as `template_id + \"\\n\" + template_text`; entries joined by `\"\\n\\n\"`; UTF-8, no BOM, no trailing newline; `prompt_hash = SHA-256(bytes)` (64 hex).\n226: - **Dynamic holdings/evidence are excluded** (they vary per run and are captured by the fingerprint/state, not the prompt template). Editing any template or frozen string changes `prompt_hash`. `template_id` values are stable identifiers (e.g., `analyst.market`, `trader`, `manager.portfolio`, `frozen.disclaimer`, `legend.no_portfolio`).\n227: \n228: ### 3.9 `Event` (JSONL)\n229: ```\n230: Event {\n231:   run_id, ticker,\n232:   node: \"input\" | \"engine\" | \"output\",\n233:   ts: str (UTC ISO-8601),\n234:   elapsed_ms: int (>=0, monotonic),\n235:   event: str,                 # e.g. input.selection, input.consent, run.terminal, output.check, output.persist\n236:   event_outcome: str          # progress vocabulary, separate from run_outcome\n237: }\n238: ```\n239: Exactly one `event=run.terminal` logical decision per run (§7.5).\n240: \n241: ### 3.10 Final manifest (`manifest.json`) — F1/F3\n242: ```\n243: Manifest = SafeRunMetadata + {\n244:   report_paths: { markdown: str|null, html: str|null },\n245:   terminal_event: { logical: \"run.terminal\", durable: bool }   # durable = JSONL terminal write succeeded before publication\n246: }\n247: ```\n248: The manifest is written **once**, atomically, **as part of the single publication commit** (§7), and contains **no** positions/cash/other-position list and no secrets. `terminal_event.durable` is known **before** publication because the terminal event is written **before** the commit (or its outcome is decided then) — a later append never changes the immutable manifest.\n249: \n250: #### 3.10.1 Manifest examples (document examples; values illustrative)\n251: Completed, portfolio-provided (fingerprint from §2.2.1 Reason E):\n252: ```\n253: {\"schema_version\":\"1\",\"run_id\":\"20261112T101500Z-ab12cd\",\"ticker\":\"AAPL\",\"analysis_date\":\"2026-11-12\",\n254:  \"input_mode\":\"PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED\",\"basename\":\"b.json\",\n255:  \"fingerprint_sha256\":\"45f07d9eb3359b059525da0cee26f8a9810269dad11ffb4c42e1dcc7072cef72\",\n256:  \"portfolio_as_of\":\"2026-11-12\",\"as_of_basis\":\"USER_CONFIRMED\",\n257:  \"run_outcome\":\"COMPLETED\",\"stop_reason\":null,\"final_rating\":\"Overweight\",\"output_check\":\"PASSED\",\"findings\":[],\n258:  \"code_version\":\"0.7.1\",\"source_revision\":\"git:abc1234\",\"prompt_hash\":\"<64hex>\",\n259:  \"effective_config\":{\"llm_provider\":\"openai\",\"deep_think_llm\":\"gpt-x\",\"quick_think_llm\":\"gpt-y\",\"analysts\":[\"market\",\"news\"],\"max_debate_rounds\":2,\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\":2,\"output_language\":\"English\",\"temperature\":0.2,\"max_tokens\":4096,\"context_cap_tokens\":24000,\"compaction_threshold_tokens\":19200,\"data_vendors\":{},\"tool_vendors\":{}},\n260:  \"start_ts_utc\":\"2026-11-12T10:15:00Z\",\"end_ts_utc\":\"2026-11-12T10:18:22Z\",\n261:  \"report_paths\":{\"markdown\":\"reports/complete_report.md\",\"html\":\"reports/complete_report.html\"},\n262:  \"terminal_event\":{\"logical\":\"run.terminal\",\"durable\":true}}\n263: ```\n264: Incomplete, no-portfolio (persistence failure example):\n265: ```\n266: {\"schema_version\":\"1\",\"run_id\":\"20261112T090000Z-ef34gh\",\"ticker\":\"NVDA\",\"analysis_date\":\"2026-11-12\",\n267:  \"input_mode\":\"NO_PORTFOLIO\",\"basename\":null,\"fingerprint_sha256\":null,\"portfolio_as_of\":null,\"as_of_basis\":null,\n268:  \"run_outcome\":\"INCOMPLETE\",\"stop_reason\":\"PERSISTENCE_ERROR\",\"final_rating\":null,\"output_check\":\"NOT_RUN\",\"findings\":[],\n269:  \"code_version\":\"0.7.1\",\"source_revision\":\"git:abc1234\",\"prompt_hash\":\"<64hex>\",\n270:  \"effective_config\":{...},\"start_ts_utc\":\"2026-11-12T09:00:00Z\",\"end_ts_utc\":\"2026-11-12T09:03:10Z\",\n271:  \"report_paths\":{\"markdown\":null,\"html\":null},\"terminal_event\":{\"logical\":\"run.terminal\",\"durable\":true}}\n272: ```\n273: (Conditional rules hold: COMPLETED has a rating and `stop_reason=null`; INCOMPLETE has `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`, a `stop_reason`, and null report paths.)\n274: \n275: ---\n276: \n277: ## 4. Input-mode state machine (addresses B3-08; both modes complete)\n278: \n279: Interactive discovery/consent lives only in `cli/input_ui.py`. The **noninteractive service** (`input_service.py`) accepts explicit inputs/paths.\n280: \n281: ```\n282: START\n283:  ├─ explicit --portfolio PATH ─────────────► VALIDATING_EXPLICIT\n284:  ├─ explicit --without-portfolio ──────────► NO_PORTFOLIO_FREEZE\n285:  └─ interactive, no explicit flags ────────► DISCOVERING\n286: DISCOVERING\n287:  ├─ eligible files present ──► SELECTING ──cancel──► CANCELLED\n288:  ├─ missing or empty dir ────► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM   (never described as \"empty\" if errored)\n289:  └─ directory read error ────► DIR_ERROR ──retry──► DISCOVERING\n290:                               └──choose no-portfolio──► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM\n291:                               └──cancel──► CANCELLED\n292: SELECTING ──file chosen──► VALIDATING\n293: VALIDATING ──invalid──► INVALID ──reselect──► SELECTING / ──cancel──► CANCELLED\n294: VALIDATING_EXPLICIT ──(noninteractive: --portfolio-as-of D required, D == analysis date)──►\n295:    ──valid──► PORTFOLIO_FREEZE   ──invalid/as-of-mismatch/flags-conflict──► INPUT_ERROR (zero run)\n296: VALIDATING ──valid──► PORTFOLIO_FREEZE\n297: PORTFOLIO_FREEZE  (freeze bytes → FrozenSnapshot; consent_state=FROZEN)\n298:    ──interactive: show notice (basename, D, unverified/as-of, provider-transmission)──► AWAITING_CONSENT\n299:    ──noninteractive: explicit --portfolio already expresses consent──► CONFIRMED\n300: AWAITING_CONSENT ──yes──► CONFIRMED ; ──no/EOF──► CANCELLED\n301: NO_PORTFOLIO_FREEZE\n302:    ──interactive: show frozen no-portfolio notice──► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM\n303:    ──noninteractive: --without-portfolio expresses consent──► CONFIRMED\n304: NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM ──yes──► CONFIRMED ; ──no/EOF──► CANCELLED\n305: CONFIRMED ──► RUNNING\n306: CANCELLED / INPUT_ERROR → zero graph, zero LLM, no completed run\n307: ```\n308: \n309: - **Both modes** reach a frozen candidate and explicit confirmation (interactive) or explicit flag consent (noninteractive).\n310: - **Noninteractive flag rules:** neither `--portfolio` nor `--without-portfolio` ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR` (zero calls); **both** ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR`; `--portfolio` without `--portfolio-as-of` ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR`; `--portfolio-as-of` with `--without-portfolio` ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR`; `--portfolio-as-of D` ≠ analysis date ⇒ `AS_OF_MISMATCH`.\n311: \n312: ### 4.1 Consent as explicit transitions (B3-01; immutability ≠ bypass prevention)\n313: | From | Trigger | To | Guard |\n314: |---|---|---|---|\n315: | `FROZEN` (PORTFOLIO_FREEZE/NO_PORTFOLIO_FREEZE) | interactive Yes, or valid explicit flag | `CONFIRMED` | notice for portfolio shown first (interactive) |\n316: | `FROZEN` | interactive No/EOF/cancel | `CANCELLED` | zero run |\n317: | `CONFIRMED` | (any) | `RUNNING` | **only** path to `execution.run` |\n318: \n319: `execution.run_analysis_api` **rejects** a `RunContext` whose `consent_state != CONFIRMED`. A frozen snapshot existing does **not** authorize execution; the transition does.\n320: \n321: - **No silent reread:** after freeze the file is never reopened; frozen bytes are the sole input.\n322: - **Disclosure sequencing:** only the **notice** precedes consent; holdings are transmitted to the provider **only after** `CONFIRMED` (during `RUNNING`). No provider transmission before consent.\n323: \n324: ---\n325: \n326: ## 5. Shared CLI/API execution boundary (addresses B3-01, B3-10)\n327: \n328: The **common application entry service** routes **every supported entry point** through the mandatory checks/finalization/persistence:\n329: \n330: ```\n331: # tradingagents/runapi/execution.py  (prompt-free; no cli import)\n332: run_analysis_api(\n333:     run_context: RunContext,          # consent_state must be CONFIRMED\n334:     graph_factory: Callable[..., Engine],  # injectable for tests; default TradingAgentsGraph\n335:     event_sink: EventSink,\n336:     redactor: Redactor,\n337: ) -> RunResult\n338: sequence: validate_consent → engine.stream_run(portfolio or None)\n339:           → render_body → check → finalize → stage → publish → terminal event\n340: ```\n341: \n342: ### 5.1 Entry points and which boundary they traverse\n343: | Entry point | Interaction | Boundary traversal | Requirement coverage |\n344: |---|---|---|---|\n345: | CLI interactive (`cli/main.py`) | prompts in `cli/input_ui.py` | freezes+confirm → `run_analysis_api` | Full (FR/NFR) |\n346: | CLI noninteractive (flags) | none | flags → freeze → `run_analysis_api` | Full |\n347: | **Supported project API** (`tradingagents.runapi.execution.run_analysis_api`) | none | supplies a `RunContext` (built via input service or explicit `portfolio`/`None`) → `run_analysis_api` | Full |\n348: | Low-level engine primitive (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run`) | none | **raw**; **does not** traverse the boundary | **Reduced** — see §5.3 |\n349: \n350: ### 5.2 Supported project API signature\n351: The upstream engine signature is **preserved** (`trading_graph.py:167,293`: `portfolio=None|PortfolioContext`). A programmatic caller wanting the full contract uses:\n352: ```\n353: from tradingagents.runapi.execution import run_analysis_api\n354: from tradingagents.runapi.input_service import freeze_explicit  # builds a FROZEN RunContext\n355: ctx_frozen = freeze_explicit(ticker, analysis_date, portfolio=PortfolioContext(...) | None)  # no prompt; consent_state=FROZEN\n356: ctx_confirmed = ctx_frozen.confirm()                      # explicit programmatic consent transition\n357: result: RunResult = run_analysis_api(ctx_confirmed, event_sink=..., redactor=...)\n358: ```\n359: - **Consent is consistent across all entry points:** `freeze_explicit` **always** returns `consent_state=FROZEN`; a programmatic caller must perform an explicit `confirm()` transition (the programmatic expression of consent; no prompt, no provider transmission before `run_analysis_api`). This matches the CLI/interactive rule that a frozen context is not executable.\n360: - `freeze_explicit(..., portfolio=None)` ⇒ `NO_PORTFOLIO` RunContext with `basename/fingerprint/as_of=null`. `portfolio=PortfolioContext(...)` (in-memory) ⇒ frozen snapshot with **synthetic provenance**: `basename=\"<in-memory>\"`, `fingerprint_sha256=<64-hex over §2.2 canonical bytes>`, `portfolio_as_of=<analysis_date>`, `as_of_basis=\"USER_CONFIRMED\"` (the caller asserts the in-memory book is intended for that date).\n361: - This path runs checks/finalization/redaction/single-commit publication — no compliance gap (B3-01 resolved at design level).\n362: \n363: ### 5.3 Low-level primitive (precise scope; A approval required for reduced coverage)\n364: `TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run/create_run_state` remain available unchanged for baseline compatibility and upstream tests. They **do not** provide the output checker, outcome finalizer, redaction, manifest or events. Scope and honesty:\n365: - Use is legitimate for baseline/existing upstream behaviour and for engine-level tests only.\n366: - A caller using **only** the raw primitive **does not** satisfy FR-006/FR-007/NFR-002/003/004. This is a **declared, scoped low-level compatibility path**; **A must approve** any excluded requirement coverage if a product-facing path relies on it (R-API, pending A). It is not a D design task; only A's acceptance of reduced coverage is pending.\n367: - **Mandatory CLI traversal:** the CLI (`cli/main.py`, `cli/run.py`) **must** call `run_analysis_api` for all product runs; it may not call the raw primitive directly. The raw primitive is not a product entry point.\n368: \n369: ---\n370: \n371: ## 6. Render / check / final envelope ordering (addresses B3-04)\n372: \n373: **Problem fixed:** the check must run on content that does *not* yet contain its own result, yet the delivered header must display the check result. Resolution: separate the **immutable checked body** from the **trusted final envelope**.\n374: \n375: ### 6.1 Two-part document\n376: - **Body** (model-generated sections + trusted frozen notice/disclaimer): rendered once from `final_state` + `RunContext`, **redacted before check**.\n377: - **Pre-check provenance fragment** (trusted, deterministic): the exact header lines Q2 will inspect — analysis date, input mode, basename, full-64 fingerprint, as-of/basis — rendered from `SafeInputMetadata` **before** the check. This is the object Q2 compares; it is not the checker comparing metadata to itself, because it is an independently produced text fragment.\n378: - **Envelope** (trusted): the final delivered header, built **after** the check from `SafeRunMetadata` (which now includes outcome/check). It must byte-match the pre-check provenance fragment for its Q2 fields (verified again before publication, §6.4).\n379: \n380: ### 6.2 Single authoritative check — completed path only (F4)\n381: ```\n382: 1. final_state  (or an exception → go to 6.3 INCOMPLETE branch; checker NOT called)\n383: 2. body = render_body(final_state, RunContext)                 # trusted strings inserted\n384: 3. body = redactor.scrub(body)                                 # redaction BEFORE check\n385: 4. provenance_fragment = render_provenance(SafeInputMetadata)  # trusted header text Q2 inspects\n386: 5. final_rating = run_rating(final_state)  |  REVIEW           # deterministic\n387: 6. CheckResult = OutputChecker.evaluate(                        # ONE authoritative call\n388:         trusted: SafeInputMetadata,     # Q2 authoritative expected values (explicit argument)\n389:         provenance_fragment: str,       # Q2 subject (independently rendered trusted text, compared to `trusted`)\n390:         final_rating: str,              # Q1 subject\n391:         rendered_body: str)             # Q3/Q4 subject (disclaimer excluded from Q4)\n392:    # if the checker raises → CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[CHECK_ERROR]} (fail closed, single decision)\n393: 7. result = OutcomeFinalizer.finalize(graph_returned=True, final_rating, exc=None)  # COMPLETED\n394: 8. envelope = build_envelope(SafeRunMetadata(result, CheckResult))   # uses the FROZEN CheckResult; no second verdict\n395: 9. verify_envelope_header_matches(envelope, trusted)     # publication-time guard vs AUTHORITATIVE metadata (§6.4)\n396: 10. final_doc_md = envelope + body ; final_doc_html = render_html(envelope, body)\n397: 11. stage → single publication commit (§7)\n398: ```\n399: - The checker is invoked **exactly once** on the completed path; the envelope consumes the **frozen** `CheckResult`.\n400: - **Q2 has a real subject and explicit trusted values:** Q2 compares `provenance_fragment` (independently rendered pre-check text) against the **explicitly supplied trusted `SafeInputMetadata`** argument. A fragment whose basename/fingerprint/as-of differs from trusted metadata produces a **Q2** finding, not a guaranteed pass. The trusted metadata is a call argument, not ambient state.\n401: \n402: ### 6.3 Incomplete branch — checker bypassed (F4)\n403: ```\n404: 1. engine raised OR graph did not return a usable final_state\n405: 2. result = OutcomeFinalizer.finalize(graph_returned=False, final_rating=None, exc=exc)\n406: 3. CheckResult = CheckResult{output_check:\"NOT_RUN\", findings:[]}   # assigned directly; checker NOT invoked\n407: 4. envelope = build_envelope(SafeRunMetadata(result, CheckResult))   # INCOMPLETE, NOT_RUN, no rating\n408: 5. no successful report body is published as PASSED; partial artifacts labelled INCOMPLETE (§7)\n409: ```\n410: The checker signature never receives graph-returned data on this path, so there is no contradictory double verdict.\n411: \n412: ### 6.4 Envelope verification and source-of-truth (F4, H3)\n413: - `OutputChecker.evaluate(trusted, provenance_fragment, final_rating, rendered_body)` calls no provider. Q1 = rating readable; **Q2 = every Q2 field in `provenance_fragment` equals the explicit trusted `SafeInputMetadata`** argument; Q3 = disclaimer present in body; Q4 = prohibited phrases absent in body (disclaimer excluded).\n414: - **Publication-time guard — against authoritative metadata:** before the commit, the build verifies that the envelope's Q2 fields equal the **trusted `SafeInputMetadata`** (the same authoritative expected values). The guard does **not** compare the envelope to the possibly-defective `provenance_fragment`; it validates both the fragment's finding (already recorded by the checker) and the delivered envelope against the authoritative values.\n415: - **Q2-defect path (consistent):** if the fragment disagrees with trusted metadata, the checker records a `Q2` finding (`NEEDS_REVIEW`) and that finding is **retained**; the envelope is built from trusted metadata (a **corrected** header) and passes the guard because it matches authoritative values. The run delivers the corrected header labelled `NEEDS_REVIEW` with the original Q2 finding — it is neither silently marked clean nor claimed to have equal-but-unequal values.\n416: - **Single source for the disclaimer:** the disclaimer is rendered **once** into the body from the frozen string; the envelope references its presence (Q3) rather than re-emitting a second copy, avoiding body/envelope duplication mismatch.\n417: - **Redaction precedes checks**, so a checked artifact cannot later be invalidated by redaction.\n418: \n419: ### 6.5 Walkthroughs (synthetic; document examples; verified against §6.2–§6.4)\n420: - **Completed-PASS (no-portfolio):** `final_rating=\"Hold\"`; `provenance_fragment` renders `input_mode=NO_PORTFOLIO`, basename/fingerprint/as-of `null`; body has disclaimer, no prohibited phrase → `CheckResult{PASSED,[]}`; `RunResult{COMPLETED, stop_reason=null, final_rating=\"Hold\", output_check=PASSED}`; envelope shows PASSED; guard passes (envelope matches trusted metadata).\n421: - **Completed-REVIEW (Q2 defect):** renderer bug renders `basename=\"c.json\"` in the `provenance_fragment` while trusted `SafeInputMetadata.basename=\"b.json\"` → Q2 fails on the single checker call → `CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[Q2]}` (finding retained); `RunResult{COMPLETED, output_check=NEEDS_REVIEW}`; the envelope is built from trusted metadata (`b.json`, corrected) and the guard passes because it matches the **authoritative** metadata; the delivered header shows `b.json` and the retained Q2 finding, outcome not silently clean.\n422: - **Completed-REVIEW (Q4):** body contains `guaranteed profit` outside disclaimer → `Finding{Q4}`; `NEEDS_REVIEW`.\n423: - **Checker-error:** checker raises on the single call → `CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[CHECK_ERROR]}`; graph returned so `COMPLETED`; `output_check=NEEDS_REVIEW`; no second call to disagree.\n424: - **Graph-failure (INCOMPLETE):** exception → INCOMPLETE branch; **checker not invoked**; `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `final_rating=null`, `stop_reason` set; nothing published as PASSED.\n425: \n426: ### 6.6 Rendering order for agents (identity vs display)\n427: Canonicalization sorts positions for hashing; `PortfolioContext.render()` keeps upstream ordering for the prompt. Identity and display are intentionally separate; neither mutates the frozen tuple.\n428: \n429: ---\n430: \n431: ## 7. Staging, single publication commit, and terminal-event ordering (addresses F1)\n432: \n433: ### 7.1 Single publication commit point\n434: The run directory is the unit of atomic publication on the same filesystem:\n435: ```\n436: STAGING dir: <results>/_staging/<run_id>/         # not visible as a successful run\n437:   reports/complete_report.md  (and .html if enabled)   # final envelope + checked body\n438:   manifest.json                                        # fully populated incl. terminal_event.durable\n439: COMMIT:  os.replace/rename  <results>/_staging/<run_id>  ->  <results>/<ticker>/<run_id>/\n440: ```\n441: - **One commit point.** Everything the manifest describes (report MD/HTML, manifest itself) is written into the **staging** directory **first**; the **only** publication action is a single atomic directory rename. Before the rename, nothing exists at the published path; after it, a complete, self-consistent run directory exists.\n442: - **No success is visible before the commit.** There is no earlier `rename` of the report into the published location; the \"report staged but unpublished\" state is real because the report lives only under `_staging`.\n443: - **Terminal event ordering (truthful durability):** the **logical** terminal decision is computed before commit. The **JSONL terminal event is appended to the staging `events.jsonl` before the commit**, so its success/failure is **known before** the manifest is finalized. `terminal_event.durable = (jsonl terminal append succeeded)`. A later event append is **not** part of the immutable manifest's claim; best-effort events written after commit are separate and cannot change `manifest.json`.\n444: - **Caller-visible terminal is resolved on commit (R5).** The terminal is first **staged privately** on the `EventSink` (included in the staged `events.jsonl` for durability, but not in the caller-inspectable `events`). Only after the single directory rename succeeds is the tentative terminal **committed** into the caller-visible event list (`commit_terminal`). If the critical report/manifest staging or the rename fails, the tentative terminal is **discarded** and `run_analysis_api` emits exactly one matching `INCOMPLETE` terminal, so a caller-owned sink can never retain a COMPLETED terminal for an unpublished run. The post-rename reveal is a **best-effort callback**: its failure does not revise the already-published logical outcome. Normal completed and engine-incomplete runs still expose exactly one matching terminal. The single-terminal rule is preserved. A legacy sink without the staging protocol has the terminal written into the staged file (truthful `durable`) and the one terminal emitted after the rename.\n445: - **Reader behaviour:** a run directory is a valid published run iff it exists at `<results>/<ticker>/<run_id>/` (the rename completed). `_staging/**` is never treated as a published run. Readers may ignore `_staging`.\n446: \n447: ### 7.2 Sink criticality\n448: | Sink | Criticality | Rule (with single-commit) |\n449: |---|---|---|\n450: | Report MD (and HTML if enabled) | **Critical** | Written to staging; part of the commit unit |\n451: | Manifest | **Critical** | Written to staging with final `terminal_event.durable`; part of the commit unit |\n452: | JSONL terminal event | **Best-effort (not critical)** | Appended to staging **before** commit; its outcome sets `terminal_event.durable` but **does not** block publication and does **not** change the logical outcome |\n453: | Other JSONL progress events | Best-effort | May be appended pre- or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; never changes the immutable manifest |\n454: | State JSON / message log | Best-effort | Written to staging or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip a completed decision |\n455: \n456: ### 7.3 Failure mapping (one per path)\n457: - **Critical staging write fails** (report or manifest) **before commit:** no rename performed; nothing appears at the published path; result `INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`. Staging dir is cleaned or left under `_staging` (not published).\n458: - **Commit rename fails:** same as above — nothing published; typed `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.\n459: - **Best-effort sink fails (progress event / state log / message log):** the commit still proceeds; outcome is unchanged (`COMPLETED`/…); a redacted note is recorded; `terminal_event.durable` reflects the **terminal** append only.\n460: - **Terminal-event append to staging fails (best-effort):** the **logical outcome is preserved** (`COMPLETED` if the graph returned); `terminal_event.durable=false` is recorded in the staging manifest **before** commit; the run directory is still published (report+manifest valid). This is **not** a critical failure and does **not** return `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.\n461: - **Logical outcome revision:** `OutcomeFinalizer` produces the logical outcome; only a **critical report/manifest staging-or-commit** failure (before any publication) revises the returned result to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`. Since nothing is published before commit, no published PASSED/COMPLETED can contradict the returned result. On such a failure the stage-private tentative terminal is discarded and exactly one `INCOMPLETE` terminal is emitted to the caller sink (R5).\n462: - **Full-disk/power-loss durability:** out of scope; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.\n463: \n464: ### 7.4 Reconciliation with earlier finalization\n465: `OutcomeFinalizer` sends the logical outcome and `terminal_event.durable` into the staging manifest **before** commit. If critical persistence fails, the **returned** result is revised to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` (satisfying INV-08); nothing was published, so there is no stale success artifact.\n466: \n467: ### 7.5 Chronological failure walkthroughs (document examples; states verified against §7.1–§7.4)\n468: Legend: `VISIBLE` = present at published path; `STAGED` = under `_staging` only.\n469: \n470: - **(a) Report staging write fails:** after staging the manifest is attempted? **No** — report write fails first → abort; no manifest, no commit. `STAGED`: partial report maybe; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, rating null, NOT_RUN, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`.\n471: - **(b) Manifest staging write fails:** report written to staging; manifest write fails → abort before commit; `STAGED`: report; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. No published COMPLETED exists.\n472: - **(c) Final publication (rename) fails:** staging complete (report+manifest+terminal event); rename fails → `STAGED`: full run; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. Reader sees no published run.\n473: - **(d) Best-effort JSONL progress write fails (after terminal already staged):** commit proceeds; `VISIBLE`: full run with `manifest.terminal_event.durable=true` (terminal append succeeded); returned `COMPLETED/…`; a redacted note about the dropped progress event. Immutable manifest unchanged by the dropped progress event.\n474: - **(e) Terminal-event append to staging fails (best-effort):** `terminal_event.durable=false` recorded in the staging manifest **before** commit; commit still publishes the run directory (report+manifest valid); returned outcome is the **logical outcome** (COMPLETED if graph returned) — **not** PERSISTENCE_ERROR; a redacted note. The manifest truthfully states the terminal event is **not durable**; no later append alters it.\n475: \n476: No walkthrough publishes a report that contradicts the returned terminal result.\n477: \n478: ---\n479: \n480: ## 8. CLI / API contract changes (intentional)\n481: - Added: `--without-portfolio`; `--portfolio-as-of D`. Preserved: `--portfolio PATH` (may be outside `PORTFOLIO_DIR`; parent not scanned).\n482: - Prompts suppressed under explicit flags; conflicts ⇒ `InputError` (no default). Intentional CLI changes (FR-002) recorded in ADR; not accidental compatibility failures.\n483: \n484: ## 9. Escaping and provenance values\n485: - HTML escapes all model/file/provenance values (`report_html.py:10,226,255`); envelope values escaped too. Header uses `SafeInputMetadata`, never the payload.\n486: \n487: ## 10. Evaluation population interface (addresses B3-11)\n488: \n489: NFR-006 requires completion accounting over **started fresh runs**, with pre-run cancellations counted separately and **zero-completed ⇒ insufficient evidence**. Defined interface (owner component: evaluation data model, proposed `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` `RunRecord`; aggregation is a reporting concern for C/D):\n490: \n491: ```\n492: RunRecord (one per attempt; persisted only in evaluation datasets, NOT in the run manifest)\n493:   attempt_id: str\n494:   category: \"STARTED\" | \"PRE_RUN_REJECTED\" | \"PRE_RUN_CANCELLED\"\n495:   run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\" | null   # null for pre-run categories\n496:   output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\" | null\n497:   stop_reason: ... | null\n498:   controlled_change: {factor: str, value: str} | null   # for before/after experiments\n499: ```\n500: Aggregation (design):\n501: - `completion_fraction = count(category=STARTED and run_outcome=COMPLETED) / count(category=STARTED)` (pre-run categories excluded from the denominator but reported separately).\n502: - Report `completed_count`, `needs_review_count`, `incomplete_reason_counts`, `pre_run_rejected`, `pre_run_cancelled`.\n503: - `completed_count == 0` ⇒ **insufficient evidence** (never a passing quality result).\n504: - A pre-run attempt records **no** `run_outcome`, creates **no** completed artifact, and is never counted as a started run.\n505: - Controlled before/after experiments carry `controlled_change` and are labelled as changed-factor comparisons; repeated fixed-condition benchmarks require matching controls. Exact scoring/threshold is C/A's (pending).\n506: \n507: ## 11.
