Module map and ownership (addresses B3-10)\n\nConcrete planned paths so D does not invent architecture. Names are **proposed**; ownership is by team role.\n\n| Planned path (new unless marked) | Responsibility | Owner (design / implement / test / enforce) |\n|---|---|---|\n| `tradingagents/runapi/__init__.py` | Package for the shared application boundary; **no `cli` import** | B / D / C / E |\n| `tradingagents/runapi/context.py` | `RunContext`, `FrozenSnapshot`, canonicalization, deep immutability | B / D / C / E |\n| `tradingagents/runapi/input_service.py` | `PortfolioInputService` (discover/precheck/freeze) — **noninteractive**, prompt-free | B / D / C / E |\n| `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py` | `OutputChecker` (Q1–Q4, deterministic) | B / D / C / E |\n| `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` | `RunResult`, `CheckResult`, findings, `InputError` schemas | B / D / C / E |\n| `tradingagents/runapi/finalize.py` | `OutcomeFinalizer`, exception mapping | B / D / C / E |\n| `tradingagents/runapi/persist.py` | Staging, commit, manifest, publication ordering | B / D / C / E |\n| `tradingagents/runapi/events.py` | JSONL `EventSink` | B / D / C / E |\n| `tradingagents/runapi/redact.py` | Central `Redactor` (sink boundary) | B / D / C / E |\n| `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py` | **Shared application entry service** `run_analysis_api(...)` (see §5) | B / D / C / E |\n| `cli/input_ui.py` | Interactive discovery/consent UI (prompts **only** here) | B / D / C / E |\n| `cli/main.py`, `cli/run.py` (existing) | Thin adapters: call `execution.run_analysis_api` with confirmed input | adapted |\n| `tradingagents/portfolio.py` (existing) | `PortfolioContext` model + `render`; upstream loader unchanged | preserved |\n| `tradingagents/agents/context.py`, manager/trader prompts (existing) | Mode-aware wording; no-portfolio Hold meaning | adapted |\n| `tradingagents/reporting.py`, `report_html.py` (existing) | Body rendering + final envelope header; projection-driven | adapted |\n\n**Dependency rule:** `cli/*` → `tradingagents/runapi/*` → (engine, agents, portfolio, reporting). `tradingagents/runapi/*` must **not** import `cli`. This keeps the shared boundary usable without a terminal (B3-01, B3-10).\n\n---\n\n## 2. Design types and canonicalization (addresses B3-02, B3-03)\n\n### 2.1 `InputMode`\n```\nInputMode = NO_PORTFOLIO | PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED\n```\n- `NO_PORTFOLIO`: holdings/cash unknown; nothing assumed.\n- `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED`: an explicitly selected, validated, frozen snapshot. An explicitly supplied empty `positions` list is a **flat** snapshot, not missing input.\n\n### 2.2 Canonical fingerprint bytes (B3-03, F2)\nThe new provenance fingerprint is **SHA-256 (64 lowercase hex chars)** over a **canonical JSON byte string** of the normalized snapshot. Exact rules:\n\n1. **Normalized object** contains exactly: `{\"cash\":…,\"currency\":…,\"positions\":[{\"ticker\":…,\"quantity\":…,\"average_price\":…}, …]}`. No other keys participate.\n2. **Key order:** lexicographic ascending at every object level (`sort_keys=True`).\n3. **Encoding:** UTF-8, **no BOM**, **no trailing newline**; bytes are `json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(\",\", \":\"), ensure_ascii=False).encode(\"utf-8\")`.\n4. **Separators:** `,` and `:` with **no whitespace** (`separators=(\",\", \":\")`).\n5. **String escaping:** JSON string escaping only (`ensure_ascii=False`, so non-ASCII tickers are emitted as UTF-8, not `\\uXXXX`); no additional escaping. Tickers are trimmed and uppercased before serialization.\n6. **Null/default handling:** an absent optional field and an explicit JSON `null` are the **same** and are serialized as the JSON token `null` (`average_price`, `cash`, `currency`).\n7. **Number-token serialization (exact):** every numeric field is first converted by `to_canonical_number(x)`:\n   - reject non-finite (`NaN`/`±Inf`) at validation (never reach canonicalization);\n   - normalize `-0.0` to `0.0`;\n   - if the value is integral and `|x| < 2**53`, emit the **integer token** (e.g., `10`, `1`, `0`), so `1` and `1.0` → token `1`;\n   - otherwise emit Python `float.__repr__` (shortest round-trippable decimal, e.g., `150.5`, `0.1`).\n   This defines the exact byte token; it is not \"whatever JSON does\".\n8. **Positions sort — total order (no `None`/float comparison):** sort the canonical **row objects** by the composite key `(ticker_upper, to_canonical_number(quantity), price_key)` where `price_key = (0, 0.0)` when `average_price is None` and `(1, to_canonical_number(average_price))` otherwise (a tagged tuple: null sorts **before** any number; numeric compares numerically). Because `ticker_upper` is a string and is part of the key, **two different broker spellings that normalize to the same symbol but differ in spelling sort by their hashed spelling**, and a full-row tie is impossible unless all three hashed fields are equal (identical rows are interchangeable, so input order cannot change the digest). This is a **total order over every field that participates in the digest**, so reordering input never changes the digest and no valid portfolio is rejected by sorting.\n9. **Symbol spelling:** `ticker` is hashed using the **original spelling** as supplied (trimmed, uppercased). Holdings keep their spelling (`portfolio.py:40-68`); alias matching is a runtime concern, not identity. Two files differing only by broker alias spelling are **different** provenance and therefore **different** digests (both are accepted; ordering above remains total).\n10. **Excluded fields:** `basename`, filesystem path, mtime, `portfolio_as_of`, `as_of_basis`, `mode` are recorded separately in metadata, **not** in the content digest.\n\n> Invariant: INV-05. Upstream truncated 12-char checkpoint fingerprint (`portfolio.py:70-72`, `trading_graph.py:158`) is **preserved unchanged** and unrelated to this digest.\n\n#### 2.2.1 Exact canonical-byte examples (verified against the rules above)\nRow order after sorting is shown; bytes are exactly the string inside quotes.\n\n- **Reason A — null vs numeric price (reversed input):**\n  - Input `[(\"AAPL\",10,None),(\"AAPL\",10,2.0)]` and reversed `[(\"AAPL\",10,2.0),(\"AAPL\",10,None)]` both serialize to\n    `{\"cash\":null,\"currency\":null,\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":null,\"quantity\":10,\"ticker\":\"AAPL\"},{\"average_price\":2,\"quantity\":10,\"ticker\":\"AAPL\"}]}` → **equal digest** (null sorts before numeric; `10`/`2` are integer tokens).\n- **Reason B — broker-alias tie (reversed input):**\n  - Input `[(\"BRK.B\",5,100.0),(\"BRK-B\",5,100.0)]` and reversed both serialize to\n    `{\"cash\":null,\"currency\":null,\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":100,\"quantity\":5,\"ticker\":\"BRK-B\"},{\"average_price\":100,\"quantity\":5,\"ticker\":\"BRK.B\"}]}` → **equal digest** (`\"BRK-B\"` < `\"BRK.B\"`; spelling is part of the sort key). Reindexing the **spelling** (e.g., `BRK.B`→`BRK-B` on the other row) is a **different** portfolio by rule 9 and yields a different digest.\n- **Reason C — numeric `1` vs `1.0`:**\n  - `[(\"MSFT\",1,50)]` cash `1` and `[(\"MSFT\",1.0,50.0)]` cash `1.0` both serialize to\n    `{\"cash\":1,\"currency\":null,\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":50,\"quantity\":1,\"ticker\":\"MSFT\"}]}` → **equal digest**.\n- **Reason D — missing vs explicit null:** a position with absent `average_price` and one with explicit `null` serialize identically (`\"average_price\":null`) → **equal digest**.\n- **Reason E — full example with cash:** `[(\"AAPL\",10,150.5),(\"MSFT\",5,None)]`, cash `2500.0`, currency `\"USD\"` →\n  `{\"cash\":2500,\"currency\":\"USD\",\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":150.5,\"quantity\":10,\"ticker\":\"AAPL\"},{\"average_price\":null,\"quantity\":5,\"ticker\":\"MSFT\"}]}`\n  → SHA-256 `45f07d9eb3359b059525da0cee26f8a9810269dad11ffb4c42e1dcc7072cef72`.\n- **Expected difference:** changing `quantity` from `10` to `10.5`, adding a position, or altering cash/currency changes the digest.\n\nThese are **document examples** checked against the written rules, not passing application tests.\n\n### 2.3 Deep immutability (B3-03)\nUpstream `PortfolioContext` holds a mutable `list[Position]` of mutable model instances. `RunContext` immutability alone is insufficient. Design:\n\n- The frozen snapshot is stored as **immutable value tuples**:\n  ```\n  FrozenPositions = tuple[tuple[str, float, float | None], ...]   # (ticker, quantity, average_price)\n  FrozenSnapshot = (basename, cash: float|None, currency: str|None,\n                    positions: FrozenPositions, fingerprint_sha256, portfolio_as_of)\n  ```\n- `RunContext` is a frozen dataclass holding these tuples; it exposes **no mutable accessor**.\n- When agents need a `PortfolioContext`, the boundary **constructs a fresh `PortfolioContext`** from the frozen tuples (defensive copy) on each use; it never hands out a shared mutable object. Mutation of that constructed object cannot affect the stored identity.\n- The canonical bytes are computed from the frozen tuples, so they are stable regardless of later copies.\n\n### 2.4 `RunContext`\n```\nRunContext (frozen dataclass) {\n  run_id: str\n  ticker: str\n  analysis_date: str\n  mode: InputMode\n  snapshot: FrozenSnapshot | None      # None ⇔ NO_PORTFOLIO\n  unverified_holdings: bool\n  provider_transmission_disclosed: bool\n  consent_state: FROZEN | CONFIRMED    # see §4\n}\n```\n`snapshot is None` **iff** `mode == NO_PORTFOLIO`. `consent_state=FROZEN` ⇒ run not authorized; a snapshot existing does **not** authorize (B3-01, §4).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Complete schemas and conditional fields (addresses B3-02)\n\nAll projections below are **separately defined** and **never** serialize the portfolio payload or full `RunContext`. Field names use the selected spelling.\n\n### 3.1 `InputError`\n```\nInputError {\n  kind: \"MALFORMED_JSON\" | \"MISSING_POSITIONS\" | \"MISSING_QUANTITY\" | \"NONFINITE_NUMBER\"\n        | \"WRONG_SCALAR_TYPE\" | \"UNREADABLE_PATH\" | \"AS_OF_MISMATCH\" | \"FLAG_CONFLICT\"\n  basename: str | null          # null when path unreadable before basename known\n  field: str | null             # e.g. \"positions[2].quantity\"\n  detail: str                   # redacted, no file contents/credentials\n}\n```\n\n### 3.2 `Finding`\n```\nFinding {\n  rule: \"Q1\" | \"Q2\" | \"Q3\" | \"Q4\" | \"CHECK_ERROR\"\n  status: \"BLOCKING\"\n  detail: str                   # redacted\n}\n```\n\n### 3.3 `CheckResult` (F3 — case table)\n```\nCheckResult {\n  output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\"\n  findings: Finding[]\n}\n```\nAuthoritative case table (**checker is invoked only on the completed path**, §6):\n\n| Case | `output_check` | `findings` | When |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| All rules hold | `PASSED` | `[]` (exactly empty) | Completed run; Q1–Q4 all hold |\n| Any rule broken OR checker exception | `NEEDS_REVIEW` | **≥ 1** blocking finding (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4, or a single `CHECK_ERROR` on exception) | Completed run |\n| Run incomplete | `NOT_RUN` | `[]` (exactly empty) | Checker **not invoked**; assigned by finalizer branch (§6) |\n\nInvariants (H2 — empty-findings equivalence qualified to **completed** runs): **Completed** ⇒ `PASSED ⇔ findings==[]` and `NEEDS_REVIEW ⇒ findings≠[]`; **Incomplete** ⇒ `NOT_RUN` with `findings==[]` (checker not invoked). There is no global `PASSED ⇔ findings==[]` — `NOT_RUN` also has empty findings.\n\n### 3.4 `RunResult` (returned to caller)\n```\nRunResult {\n  run_id: str\n  ticker: str\n  analysis_date: str\n  input_mode: InputMode\n  run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\"\n  stop_reason: null | \"MODEL_FAILURE\" | \"DATA_FAILURE\" | \"INTERNAL_ERROR\"\n               | \"PERSISTENCE_ERROR\" | \"INTERRUPTED\"\n  final_rating: null | \"Buy\" | \"Overweight\" | \"Hold\" | \"Underweight\" | \"Sell\" | \"REVIEW\"\n  output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\"\n  findings: Finding[]\n  manifest_path: str | null     # non-null iff the run directory was published (§7)\n  report_path: str | null       # non-null iff the report was published (§7)\n}\n```\n**Conditional fields (enforced by finalizer):**\n- `COMPLETED` ⇒ `final_rating != null` and `stop_reason == null`.\n- `INCOMPLETE` ⇒ `final_rating == null`, `output_check == \"NOT_RUN\"`, `findings == []`, `stop_reason != null`.\n\n### 3.5 Safe input metadata projection (for sinks; never the payload)\n```\nSafeInputMetadata {\n  run_id, ticker, analysis_date,\n  input_mode: InputMode,\n  basename: str | null,                 # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n  fingerprint_sha256: str | null,       # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO (64 hex)\n  portfolio_as_of: str | null,          # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n  as_of_basis: \"USER_CONFIRMED\" | null  # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n}\n```\nThe `null` conditions are **portfolio-only** (mode-dependent); distinct from **outcome-conditional** `RunResult` fields.\n\n### 3.6 `SafeRunMetadata` (durable run record; never the payload) — F3\n```\nSafeRunMetadata {\n  schema_version: \"1\",\n  run_id, ticker, analysis_date, input_mode,\n  basename: str|null, fingerprint_sha256: str|null, portfolio_as_of: str|null, as_of_basis: \"USER_CONFIRMED\"|null,\n  run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\",\n  stop_reason: ... | null,               # §3.4 conditional\n  final_rating: ... | null,              # §3.4 conditional — NOW CARRIED IN THE DURABLE RECORD\n  output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\",\n  findings: Finding[],\n  code_version: str,                     # tradingagents.__version__\n  source_revision: str | null,           # separate source identifier, e.g. git describe or \"unknown\" (§3.7)\n  prompt_hash: str,                      # §3.8\n  effective_config: EffectiveConfig,     # §3.7\n  start_ts_utc: str, end_ts_utc: str     # ISO-8601 UTC; set once at finalize\n}\n```\nThe **same** `final_rating` spelling/conditional rules as `RunResult` apply. Timestamps are captured once at finalize and are never mutated later.\n\n### 3.7 `EffectiveConfig` (safe, behaviour-relevant; secrets/endpoints omitted) — F3\n```\nEffectiveConfig {\n  llm_provider, deep_think_provider, deep_think_llm, quick_think_provider, quick_think_llm,\n  analysts: str[], max_debate_rounds: int, max_risk_discuss_rounds: int,\n  output_language: str,\n  temperature: float | null, max_tokens: int | null,          # behaviour-affecting (baseline keys if set)\n  context_cap_tokens: int, compaction_threshold_tokens: int,  # the designed context budget (ADR §Context)\n  data_vendors: map, tool_vendors: map\n}\n```\nDerived from `run_settings()` (`trading_graph.py:255-275`) **plus** the behaviour-affecting keys this design introduces (`temperature`, `max_tokens`, context cap/threshold). `backend_url`, keys, OAuth tokens, local paths are **never** included. `source_revision` is recorded **separately** from `code_version` (upstream `version` stays `0.7.1`; the revision id identifies the actual source state and is `\"unknown\"` when unavailable).\n\n### 3.8 `prompt_hash` (deterministic input spec) — F3\n- Inventory: the **template set** actually used = (a) identity/context instruction templates, (b) selected analyst templates, (c) trader + research/portfolio-manager templates, (d) frozen notice/disclaimer strings, (e) the mode-aware legend variants selected for this run.\n- Serialization: an ordered list `[(template_id, template_text), …]` sorted by `template_id`; each entry serialized as `template_id + \"\\n\" + template_text`; entries joined by `\"\\n\\n\"`; UTF-8, no BOM, no trailing newline; `prompt_hash = SHA-256(bytes)` (64 hex).\n- **Dynamic holdings/evidence are excluded** (they vary per run and are captured by the fingerprint/state, not the prompt template). Editing any template or frozen string changes `prompt_hash`. `template_id` values are stable identifiers (e.g., `analyst.market`, `trader`, `manager.portfolio`, `frozen.disclaimer`, `legend.no_portfolio`).\n\n### 3.9 `Event` (JSONL)\n```\nEvent {\n  run_id, ticker,\n  node: \"input\" | \"engine\" | \"output\",\n  ts: str (UTC ISO-8601),\n  elapsed_ms: int (>=0, monotonic),\n  event: str,                 # e.g. input.selection, input.consent, run.terminal, output.check, output.persist\n  event_outcome: str          # progress vocabulary, separate from run_outcome\n}\n```\nExactly one `event=run.terminal` logical decision per run (§7.5).\n\n### 3.10 Final manifest (`manifest.json`) — F1/F3\n```\nManifest = SafeRunMetadata + {\n  report_paths: { markdown: str|null, html: str|null },\n  terminal_event: { logical: \"run.terminal\", durable: bool }   # durable = JSONL terminal write succeeded before publication\n}\n```\nThe manifest is written **once**, atomically, **as part of the single publication commit** (§7), and contains **no** positions/cash/other-position list and no secrets. `terminal_event.durable` is known **before** publication because the terminal event is written **before** the commit (or its outcome is decided then) — a later append never changes the immutable manifest.\n\n#### 3.10.1 Manifest examples (document examples; values illustrative)\nCompleted, portfolio-provided (fingerprint from §2.2.1 Reason E):\n```\n{\"schema_version\":\"1\",\"run_id\":\"20261112T101500Z-ab12cd\",\"ticker\":\"AAPL\",\"analysis_date\":\"2026-11-12\",\n \"input_mode\":\"PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED\",\"basename\":\"b.json\",\n \"fingerprint_sha256\":\"45f07d9eb3359b059525da0cee26f8a9810269dad11ffb4c42e1dcc7072cef72\",\n \"portfolio_as_of\":\"2026-11-12\",\"as_of_basis\":\"USER_CONFIRMED\",\n \"run_outcome\":\"COMPLETED\",\"stop_reason\":null,\"final_rating\":\"Overweight\",\"output_check\":\"PASSED\",\"findings\":[],\n \"code_version\":\"0.7.1\",\"source_revision\":\"git:abc1234\",\"prompt_hash\":\"<64hex>\",\n \"effective_config\":{\"llm_provider\":\"openai\",\"deep_think_llm\":\"gpt-x\",\"quick_think_llm\":\"gpt-y\",\"analysts\":[\"market\",\"news\"],\"max_debate_rounds\":2,\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\":2,\"output_language\":\"English\",\"temperature\":0.2,\"max_tokens\":4096,\"context_cap_tokens\":24000,\"compaction_threshold_tokens\":19200,\"data_vendors\":{},\"tool_vendors\":{}},\n \"start_ts_utc\":\"2026-11-12T10:15:00Z\",\"end_ts_utc\":\"2026-11-12T10:18:22Z\",\n \"report_paths\":{\"markdown\":\"reports/complete_report.md\",\"html\":\"reports/complete_report.html\"},\n \"terminal_event\":{\"logical\":\"run.terminal\",\"durable\":true}}\n```\nIncomplete, no-portfolio (persistence failure example):\n```\n{\"schema_version\":\"1\",\"run_id\":\"20261112T090000Z-ef34gh\",\"ticker\":\"NVDA\",\"analysis_date\":\"2026-11-12\",\n \"input_mode\":\"NO_PORTFOLIO\",\"basename\":null,\"fingerprint_sha256\":null,\"portfolio_as_of\":null,\"as_of_basis\":null,\n \"run_outcome\":\"INCOMPLETE\",\"stop_reason\":\"PERSISTENCE_ERROR\",\"final_rating\":null,\"output_check\":\"NOT_RUN\",\"findings\":[],\n \"code_version\":\"0.7.1\",\"source_revision\":\"git:abc1234\",\"prompt_hash\":\"<64hex>\",\n \"effective_config\":{...},\"start_ts_utc\":\"2026-11-12T09:00:00Z\",\"end_ts_utc\":\"2026-11-12T09:03:10Z\",\n \"report_paths\":{\"markdown\":null,\"html\":null},\"terminal_event\":{\"logical\":\"run.terminal\",\"durable\":true}}\n```\n(Conditional rules hold: COMPLETED has a rating and `stop_reason=null`; INCOMPLETE has `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`, a `stop_reason`, and null report paths.)\n\n---\n\n## 4. Input-mode state machine (addresses B3-08; both modes complete)\n\nInteractive discovery/consent lives only in `cli/input_ui.py`. The **noninteractive service** (`input_service.py`) accepts explicit inputs/paths.\n\n```\nSTART\n ├─ explicit --portfolio PATH ─────────────► VALIDATING_EXPLICIT\n ├─ explicit --without-portfolio ──────────► NO_PORTFOLIO_FREEZE\n └─ interactive, no explicit flags ────────► DISCOVERING\nDISCOVERING\n ├─ eligible files present ──► SELECTING ──cancel──► CANCELLED\n ├─ missing or empty dir ────► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM   (never described as \"empty\" if errored)\n └─ directory read error ────► DIR_ERROR ──retry──► DISCOVERING\n                              └──choose no-portfolio──► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM\n                              └──cancel──► CANCELLED\nSELECTING ──file chosen──► VALIDATING\nVALIDATING ──invalid──► INVALID ──reselect──► SELECTING / ──cancel──► CANCELLED\nVALIDATING_EXPLICIT ──(noninteractive: --portfolio-as-of D required, D == analysis date)──►\n   ──valid──► PORTFOLIO_FREEZE   ──invalid/as-of-mismatch/flags-conflict──► INPUT_ERROR (zero run)\nVALIDATING ──valid──► PORTFOLIO_FREEZE\nPORTFOLIO_FREEZE  (freeze bytes → FrozenSnapshot; consent_state=FROZEN)\n   ──interactive: show notice (basename, D, unverified/as-of, provider-transmission)──► AWAITING_CONSENT\n   ──noninteractive: explicit --portfolio already expresses consent──► CONFIRMED\nAWAITING_CONSENT ──yes──► CONFIRMED ; ──no/EOF──► CANCELLED\nNO_PORTFOLIO_FREEZE\n   ──interactive: show frozen no-portfolio notice──► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM\n   ──noninteractive: --without-portfolio expresses consent──► CONFIRMED\nNO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM ──yes──► CONFIRMED ; ──no/EOF──► CANCELLED\nCONFIRMED ──► RUNNING\nCANCELLED / INPUT_ERROR → zero graph, zero LLM, no completed run\n```\n\n- **Both modes** reach a frozen candidate and explicit confirmation (interactive) or explicit flag consent (noninteractive).\n- **Noninteractive flag rules:** neither `--portfolio` nor `--without-portfolio` ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR` (zero calls); **both** ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR`; `--portfolio` without `--portfolio-as-of` ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR`; `--portfolio-as-of` with `--without-portfolio` ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR`; `--portfolio-as-of D` ≠ analysis date ⇒ `AS_OF_MISMATCH`.\n\n### 4.1 Consent as explicit transitions (B3-01; immutability ≠ bypass prevention)\n| From | Trigger | To | Guard |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `FROZEN` (PORTFOLIO_FREEZE/NO_PORTFOLIO_FREEZE) | interactive Yes, or valid explicit flag | `CONFIRMED` | notice for portfolio shown first (interactive) |\n| `FROZEN` | interactive No/EOF/cancel | `CANCELLED` | zero run |\n| `CONFIRMED` | (any) | `RUNNING` | **only** path to `execution.run` |\n\n`execution.run_analysis_api` **rejects** a `RunContext` whose `consent_state != CONFIRMED`. A frozen snapshot existing does **not** authorize execution; the transition does.\n\n- **No silent reread:** after freeze the file is never reopened; frozen bytes are the sole input.\n- **Disclosure sequencing:** only the **notice** precedes consent; holdings are transmitted to the provider **only after** `CONFIRMED` (during `RUNNING`). No provider transmission before consent.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Shared CLI/API execution boundary (addresses B3-01, B3-10)\n\nThe **common application entry service** routes **every supported entry point** through the mandatory checks/finalization/persistence:\n\n```\n# tradingagents/runapi/execution.py  (prompt-free; no cli import)\nrun_analysis_api(\n    run_context: RunContext,          # consent_state must be CONFIRMED\n    graph_factory: Callable[..., Engine],  # injectable for tests; default TradingAgentsGraph\n    event_sink: EventSink,\n    redactor: Redactor,\n) -> RunResult\nsequence: validate_consent → engine.stream_run(portfolio or None)\n          → render_body → check → finalize → stage → publish → terminal event\n```\n\n### 5.1 Entry points and which boundary they traverse\n| Entry point | Interaction | Boundary traversal | Requirement coverage |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| CLI interactive (`cli/main.py`) | prompts in `cli/input_ui.py` | freezes+confirm → `run_analysis_api` | Full (FR/NFR) |\n| CLI noninteractive (flags) | none | flags → freeze → `run_analysis_api` | Full |\n| **Supported project API** (`tradingagents.runapi.execution.run_analysis_api`) | none | supplies a `RunContext` (built via input service or explicit `portfolio`/`None`) → `run_analysis_api` | Full |\n| Low-level engine primitive (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run`) | none | **raw**; **does not** traverse the boundary | **Reduced** — see §5.3 |\n\n### 5.2 Supported project API signature\nThe upstream engine signature is **preserved** (`trading_graph.py:167,293`: `portfolio=None|PortfolioContext`). A programmatic caller wanting the full contract uses:\n```\nfrom tradingagents.runapi.execution import run_analysis_api\nfrom tradingagents.runapi.input_service import freeze_explicit  # builds a FROZEN RunContext\nctx_frozen = freeze_explicit(ticker, analysis_date, portfolio=PortfolioContext(...) | None)  # no prompt; consent_state=FROZEN\nctx_confirmed = ctx_frozen.confirm()                      # explicit programmatic consent transition\nresult: RunResult = run_analysis_api(ctx_confirmed, event_sink=..., redactor=...)\n```\n- **Consent is consistent across all entry points:** `freeze_explicit` **always** returns `consent_state=FROZEN`; a programmatic caller must perform an explicit `confirm()` transition (the programmatic expression of consent; no prompt, no provider transmission before `run_analysis_api`). This matches the CLI/interactive rule that a frozen context is not executable.\n- `freeze_explicit(..., portfolio=None)` ⇒ `NO_PORTFOLIO` RunContext with `basename/fingerprint/as_of=null`. `portfolio=PortfolioContext(...)` (in-memory) ⇒ frozen snapshot with **synthetic provenance**: `basename=\"<in-memory>\"`, `fingerprint_sha256=<64-hex over §2.2 canonical bytes>`, `portfolio_as_of=<analysis_date>`, `as_of_basis=\"USER_CONFIRMED\"` (the caller asserts the in-memory book is intended for that date).\n- This path runs checks/finalization/redaction/single-commit publication — no compliance gap (B3-01 resolved at design level).\n\n### 5.3 Low-level primitive (precise scope; A approval required for reduced coverage)\n`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run/create_run_state` remain available unchanged for baseline compatibility and upstream tests. They **do not** provide the output checker, outcome finalizer, redaction, manifest or events. Scope and honesty:\n- Use is legitimate for baseline/existing upstream behaviour and for engine-level tests only.\n- A caller using **only** the raw primitive **does not** satisfy FR-006/FR-007/NFR-002/003/004. This is a **declared, scoped low-level compatibility path**; **A must approve** any excluded requirement coverage if a product-facing path relies on it (R-API, pending A). It is not a D design task; only A's acceptance of reduced coverage is pending.\n- **Mandatory CLI traversal:** the CLI (`cli/main.py`, `cli/run.py`) **must** call `run_analysis_api` for all product runs; it may not call the raw primitive directly. The raw primitive is not a product entry point.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Render / check / final envelope ordering (addresses B3-04)\n\n**Problem fixed:** the check must run on content that does *not* yet contain its own result, yet the delivered header must display the check result. Resolution: separate the **immutable checked body** from the **trusted final envelope**.\n\n### 6.1 Two-part document\n- **Body** (model-generated sections + trusted frozen notice/disclaimer): rendered once from `final_state` + `RunContext`, **redacted before check**.\n- **Pre-check provenance fragment** (trusted, deterministic): the exact header lines Q2 will inspect — analysis date, input mode, basename, full-64 fingerprint, as-of/basis — rendered from `SafeInputMetadata` **before** the check. This is the object Q2 compares; it is not the checker comparing metadata to itself, because it is an independently produced text fragment.\n- **Envelope** (trusted): the final delivered header, built **after** the check from `SafeRunMetadata` (which now includes outcome/check). It must byte-match the pre-check provenance fragment for its Q2 fields (verified again before publication, §6.4).\n\n### 6.2 Single authoritative check — completed path only (F4)\n```\n1. final_state  (or an exception → go to 6.3 INCOMPLETE branch; checker NOT called)\n2. body = render_body(final_state, RunContext)                 # trusted strings inserted\n3. body = redactor.scrub(body)                                 # redaction BEFORE check\n4. provenance_fragment = render_provenance(SafeInputMetadata)  # trusted header text Q2 inspects\n5. final_rating = run_rating(final_state)  |  REVIEW           # deterministic\n6. CheckResult = OutputChecker.evaluate(                        # ONE authoritative call\n        trusted: SafeInputMetadata,     # Q2 authoritative expected values (explicit argument)\n        provenance_fragment: str,       # Q2 subject (independently rendered trusted text, compared to `trusted`)\n        final_rating: str,              # Q1 subject\n        rendered_body: str)             # Q3/Q4 subject (disclaimer excluded from Q4)\n   # if the checker raises → CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[CHECK_ERROR]} (fail closed, single decision)\n7. result = OutcomeFinalizer.finalize(graph_returned=True, final_rating, exc=None)  # COMPLETED\n8. envelope = build_envelope(SafeRunMetadata(result, CheckResult))   # uses the FROZEN CheckResult; no second verdict\n9. verify_envelope_header_matches(envelope, trusted)     # publication-time guard vs AUTHORITATIVE metadata (§6.4)\n10. final_doc_md = envelope + body ; final_doc_html = render_html(envelope, body)\n11. stage → single publication commit (§7)\n```\n- The checker is invoked **exactly once** on the completed path; the envelope consumes the **frozen** `CheckResult`.\n- **Q2 has a real subject and explicit trusted values:** Q2 compares `provenance_fragment` (independently rendered pre-check text) against the **explicitly supplied trusted `SafeInputMetadata`** argument. A fragment whose basename/fingerprint/as-of differs from trusted metadata produces a **Q2** finding, not a guaranteed pass. The trusted metadata is a call argument, not ambient state.\n\n### 6.3 Incomplete branch — checker bypassed (F4)\n```\n1. engine raised OR graph did not return a usable final_state\n2. result = OutcomeFinalizer.finalize(graph_returned=False, final_rating=None, exc=exc)\n3. CheckResult = CheckResult{output_check:\"NOT_RUN\", findings:[]}   # assigned directly; checker NOT invoked\n4. envelope = build_envelope(SafeRunMetadata(result, CheckResult))   # INCOMPLETE, NOT_RUN, no rating\n5. no successful report body is published as PASSED; partial artifacts labelled INCOMPLETE (§7)\n```\nThe checker signature never receives graph-returned data on this path, so there is no contradictory double verdict.\n\n### 6.4 Envelope verification and source-of-truth (F4, H3)\n- `OutputChecker.evaluate(trusted, provenance_fragment, final_rating, rendered_body)` calls no provider. Q1 = rating readable; **Q2 = every Q2 field in `provenance_fragment` equals the explicit trusted `SafeInputMetadata`** argument; Q3 = disclaimer present in body; Q4 = prohibited phrases absent in body (disclaimer excluded).\n- **Publication-time guard — against authoritative metadata:** before the commit, the build verifies that the envelope's Q2 fields equal the **trusted `SafeInputMetadata`** (the same authoritative expected values). The guard does **not** compare the envelope to the possibly-defective `provenance_fragment`; it validates both the fragment's finding (already recorded by the checker) and the delivered envelope against the authoritative values.\n- **Q2-defect path (consistent):** if the fragment disagrees with trusted metadata, the checker records a `Q2` finding (`NEEDS_REVIEW`) and that finding is **retained**; the envelope is built from trusted metadata (a **corrected** header) and passes the guard because it matches authoritative values. The run delivers the corrected header labelled `NEEDS_REVIEW` with the original Q2 finding — it is neither silently marked clean nor claimed to have equal-but-unequal values.\n- **Single source for the disclaimer:** the disclaimer is rendered **once** into the body from the frozen string; the envelope references its presence (Q3) rather than re-emitting a second copy, avoiding body/envelope duplication mismatch.\n- **Redaction precedes checks**, so a checked artifact cannot later be invalidated by redaction.\n\n### 6.5 Walkthroughs (synthetic; document examples; verified against §6.2–§6.4)\n- **Completed-PASS (no-portfolio):** `final_rating=\"Hold\"`; `provenance_fragment` renders `input_mode=NO_PORTFOLIO`, basename/fingerprint/as-of `null`; body has disclaimer, no prohibited phrase → `CheckResult{PASSED,[]}`; `RunResult{COMPLETED, stop_reason=null, final_rating=\"Hold\", output_check=PASSED}`; envelope shows PASSED; guard passes (envelope matches trusted metadata).\n- **Completed-REVIEW (Q2 defect):** renderer bug renders `basename=\"c.json\"` in the `provenance_fragment` while trusted `SafeInputMetadata.basename=\"b.json\"` → Q2 fails on the single checker call → `CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[Q2]}` (finding retained); `RunResult{COMPLETED, output_check=NEEDS_REVIEW}`; the envelope is built from trusted metadata (`b.json`, corrected) and the guard passes because it matches the **authoritative** metadata; the delivered header shows `b.json` and the retained Q2 finding, outcome not silently clean.\n- **Completed-REVIEW (Q4):** body contains `guaranteed profit` outside disclaimer → `Finding{Q4}`; `NEEDS_REVIEW`.\n- **Checker-error:** checker raises on the single call → `CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[CHECK_ERROR]}`; graph returned so `COMPLETED`; `output_check=NEEDS_REVIEW`; no second call to disagree.\n- **Graph-failure (INCOMPLETE):** exception → INCOMPLETE branch; **checker not invoked**; `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `final_rating=null`, `stop_reason` set; nothing published as PASSED.\n\n### 6.6 Rendering order for agents (identity vs display)\nCanonicalization sorts positions for hashing; `PortfolioContext.render()` keeps upstream ordering for the prompt. Identity and display are intentionally separate; neither mutates the frozen tuple.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Staging, single publication commit, and terminal-event ordering (addresses F1)\n\n### 7.1 Single publication commit point\nThe run directory is the unit of atomic publication on the same filesystem:\n```\nSTAGING dir: <results>/_staging/<run_id>/         # not visible as a successful run\n  reports/complete_report.md  (and .html if enabled)   # final envelope + checked body\n  manifest.json                                        # fully populated incl. terminal_event.durable\nCOMMIT:  os.replace/rename  <results>/_staging/<run_id>  ->  <results>/<ticker>/<run_id>/\n```\n- **One commit point.** Everything the manifest describes (report MD/HTML, manifest itself) is written into the **staging** directory **first**; the **only** publication action is a single atomic directory rename. Before the rename, nothing exists at the published path; after it, a complete, self-consistent run directory exists.\n- **No success is visible before the commit.** There is no earlier `rename` of the report into the published location; the \"report staged but unpublished\" state is real because the report lives only under `_staging`.\n- **Terminal event ordering (truthful durability):** the **logical** terminal decision is computed before commit. The **JSONL terminal event is appended to the staging `events.jsonl` before the commit**, so its success/failure is **known before** the manifest is finalized. `terminal_event.durable = (jsonl terminal append succeeded)`. A later event append is **not** part of the immutable manifest's claim; best-effort events written after commit are separate and cannot change `manifest.json`.\n- **Caller-visible terminal is resolved on commit (R5).** The terminal is first **staged privately** on the `EventSink` (included in the staged `events.jsonl` for durability, but not in the caller-inspectable `events`). Only after the single directory rename succeeds is the tentative terminal **committed** into the caller-visible event list (`commit_terminal`). If the critical report/manifest staging or the rename fails, the tentative terminal is **discarded** and `run_analysis_api` emits exactly one matching `INCOMPLETE` terminal, so a caller-owned sink can never retain a COMPLETED terminal for an unpublished run. The post-rename reveal is a **best-effort callback**: its failure does not revise the already-published logical outcome. Normal completed and engine-incomplete runs still expose exactly one matching terminal. The single-terminal rule is preserved. A legacy sink without the staging protocol has the terminal written into the staged file (truthful `durable`) and the one terminal emitted after the rename.\n- **Reader behaviour:** a run directory is a valid published run iff it exists at `<results>/<ticker>/<run_id>/` (the rename completed). `_staging/**` is never treated as a published run. Readers may ignore `_staging`.\n\n### 7.2 Sink criticality\n| Sink | Criticality | Rule (with single-commit) |\n|---|---|---|\n| Report MD (and HTML if enabled) | **Critical** | Written to staging; part of the commit unit |\n| Manifest | **Critical** | Written to staging with final `terminal_event.durable`; part of the commit unit |\n| JSONL terminal event | **Best-effort (not critical)** | Appended to staging **before** commit; its outcome sets `terminal_event.durable` but **does not** block publication and does **not** change the logical outcome |\n| Other JSONL progress events | Best-effort | May be appended pre- or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; never changes the immutable manifest |\n| State JSON / message log | Best-effort | Written to staging or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip a completed decision |\n\n### 7.3 Failure mapping (one per path)\n- **Critical staging write fails** (report or manifest) **before commit:** no rename performed; nothing appears at the published path; result `INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`. Staging dir is cleaned or left under `_staging` (not published).\n- **Commit rename fails:** same as above — nothing published; typed `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.\n- **Best-effort sink fails (progress event / state log / message log):** the commit still proceeds; outcome is unchanged (`COMPLETED`/…); a redacted note is recorded; `terminal_event.durable` reflects the **terminal** append only.\n- **Terminal-event append to staging fails (best-effort):** the **logical outcome is preserved** (`COMPLETED` if the graph returned); `terminal_event.durable=false` is recorded in the staging manifest **before** commit; the run directory is still published (report+manifest valid). This is **not** a critical failure and does **not** return `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.\n- **Logical outcome revision:** `OutcomeFinalizer` produces the logical outcome; only a **critical report/manifest staging-or-commit** failure (before any publication) revises the returned result to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`. Since nothing is published before commit, no published PASSED/COMPLETED can contradict the returned result. On such a failure the stage-private tentative terminal is discarded and exactly one `INCOMPLETE` terminal is emitted to the caller sink (R5).\n- **Full-disk/power-loss durability:** out of scope; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.\n\n### 7.4 Reconciliation with earlier finalization\n`OutcomeFinalizer` sends the logical outcome and `terminal_event.durable` into the staging manifest **before** commit. If critical persistence fails, the **returned** result is revised to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` (satisfying INV-08); nothing was published, so there is no stale success artifact.\n\n### 7.5 Chronological failure walkthroughs (document examples; states verified against §7.1–§7.4)\nLegend: `VISIBLE` = present at published path; `STAGED` = under `_staging` only.\n\n- **(a) Report staging write fails:** after staging the manifest is attempted? **No** — report write fails first → abort; no manifest, no commit. `STAGED`: partial report maybe; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, rating null, NOT_RUN, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`.\n- **(b) Manifest staging write fails:** report written to staging; manifest write fails → abort before commit; `STAGED`: report; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. No published COMPLETED exists.\n- **(c) Final publication (rename) fails:** staging complete (report+manifest+terminal event); rename fails → `STAGED`: full run; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. Reader sees no published run.\n- **(d) Best-effort JSONL progress write fails (after terminal already staged):** commit proceeds; `VISIBLE`: full run with `manifest.terminal_event.durable=true` (terminal append succeeded); returned `COMPLETED/…`; a redacted note about the dropped progress event. Immutable manifest unchanged by the dropped progress event.\n- **(e) Terminal-event append to staging fails (best-effort):** `terminal_event.durable=false` recorded in the staging manifest **before** commit; commit still publishes the run directory (report+manifest valid); returned outcome is the **logical outcome** (COMPLETED if graph returned) — **not** PERSISTENCE_ERROR; a redacted note. The manifest truthfully states the terminal event is **not durable**; no later append alters it.\n\nNo walkthrough publishes a report that contradicts the returned terminal result.\n\n---\n\n## 8. CLI / API contract changes (intentional)\n- Added: `--without-portfolio`; `--portfolio-as-of D`. Preserved: `--portfolio PATH` (may be outside `PORTFOLIO_DIR`; parent not scanned).\n- Prompts suppressed under explicit flags; conflicts ⇒ `InputError` (no default). Intentional CLI changes (FR-002) recorded in ADR; not accidental compatibility failures.\n\n## 9. Escaping and provenance values\n- HTML escapes all model/file/provenance values (`report_html.py:10,226,255`); envelope values escaped too. Header uses `SafeInputMetadata`, never the payload.\n\n## 10. Evaluation population interface (addresses B3-11)\n\nNFR-006 requires completion accounting over **started fresh runs**, with pre-run cancellations counted separately and **zero-completed ⇒ insufficient evidence**. Defined interface (owner component: evaluation data model, proposed `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` `RunRecord`; aggregation is a reporting concern for C/D):\n\n```\nRunRecord (one per attempt; persisted only in evaluation datasets, NOT in the run manifest)\n  attempt_id: str\n  category: \"STARTED\" | \"PRE_RUN_REJECTED\" | \"PRE_RUN_CANCELLED\"\n  run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\" | null   # null for pre-run categories\n  output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\" | null\n  stop_reason: ... | null\n  controlled_change: {factor: str, value: str} | null   # for before/after experiments\n```\nAggregation (design):\n- `completion_fraction = count(category=STARTED and run_outcome=COMPLETED) / count(category=STARTED)` (pre-run categories excluded from the denominator but reported separately).\n- Report `completed_count`, `needs_review_count`, `incomplete_reason_counts`, `pre_run_rejected`, `pre_run_cancelled`.\n- `completed_count == 0` ⇒ **insufficient evidence** (never a passing quality result).\n- A pre-run attempt records **no** `run_outcome`, creates **no** completed artifact, and is never counted as a started run.\n- Controlled before/after experiments carry `controlled_change` and are labelled as changed-factor comparisons; repeated fixed-condition benchmarks require matching controls. Exact scoring/threshold is C/A's (pending).\n\n## 11. Pending (external owners)\nFinal D1/schema (A); C's test IDs, rubric/threshold, and independent evidence; E enforcement; instructor layout. A must approve any reliance on the reduced-coverage low-level primitive (§5.3).",

This selection does **not** introduce automatic deletion or a cross-run catalogue (deferred). **Deletion owner:** the end user (application role); E/ops may define a later retention policy but must not silently delete user artifacts.\n- **Retrieval policy:** reads for provenance/console use the redacted `SafeInputMetadata`/`SafeRunMetadata`; the portfolio source file is not re-read after freeze; no full payload is retrieved from manifests/logs.\n- **Redaction ≠ suppression:** masking secrets (NFR-003) is **distinct** from suppressing raw holdings/prompt dumps. Both are required: raw portfolio bytes, full `RunContext`, raw provider prompts/payloads are **not persisted** in new sinks regardless of redaction.\n- **Provider retention:** holdings **transmitted to the provider after consent** are subject to the **provider's own retention/logging policy, outside application control**; the notice states this is intentional provider transmission. The application is not represented as local-only.\n- **Secrets:** never persisted; redaction boundary at every sink (§5).\n- **Source files:** portfolio source files are kept **read-only**; their bytes are not copied into manifests/transcripts.\n\n## 5. Sink handling (existing + new)\n\nEach sink: decision (retain/adapt/disable/replace), output location, run-ID isolation, overwrite prevention, permitted content, redaction boundary, raw-payload suppression, failure handling, responsible component. Criticality and ordering are in `interface-contracts.md` §7.\n\n| Sink | Decision | Output location | Run-ID isolation & overwrite prevention | Permitted content | Redaction boundary | Raw payload suppression | Failure handling | Responsible component |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `message_tool.log` (`cli/run.py:139-164`) | **Adapt** | per-run results dir (`results_dir/<ticker>/<run_id>/message_tool.log`) | Under run-ID-isolated dir; never append across runs | Model/system narrative; no raw portfolio bytes/other-position dump | `Redactor` per line | Yes | **Best-effort:** failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip COMPLETED (not a promised artifact) | Persist + Redactor |\n| Graph state JSON `full_states_log_{trade_date}.json` (`trading_graph.py:472`) | **Adapt (replace path keying)** | per-run results dir | **Legacy date-keyed overwrites same ticker+date.** Replace with run-ID-qualified filename; refuse-if-exists | Existing narrative fields + safe provenance projection; never raw payload | `Redactor` on serialized entry | Yes | **Best-effort:** failure ⇒ redacted note; prior run preserved | Persist (path) + Redactor |\n| Markdown report (`reporting.py`) | **Adapt** | per-run dir (`reports/complete_report.md`) | Run-ID-qualified; **critical**: written to `_staging`, published only by the single directory commit (§interface-contracts §7); refuse silent overwrite | Checked body + trusted envelope from safe projection | Redact body **before** check; escape/redact provenance | Yes | **Critical:** staging/commit failure ⇒ INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR; no success exposed (§7) | reporting + Persist |\n| HTML report (`report_html.py`) | **Retain escaping, adapt provenance source** | alongside MD (`complete_report.html`) | Same as MD (critical when enabled) | Same checked body + escaped envelope | Already escapes (`:10,226,255`); extend to provenance | Yes | Same as MD | reporting + Persist |\n| **Manifest (new)** | **New** | per-run dir (`manifest.json`) | Run-ID-qualified; **written into `_staging` before the single commit**; immutable after commit; refuse overwrite | `Manifest` (`SafeRunMetadata` + paths + `terminal_event.durable`, decided pre-commit); **no payload/secret endpoints** | `Redactor` before staging write | Yes | **Critical:** staging/commit failure ⇒ INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR; nothing published | Persist |\n| **JSONL event sink (new)** | **New** | per-run dir (`events.jsonl`) | Run-ID-qualified; **terminal event appended to `_staging` before commit (sets `durable`)**; other progress events best-effort | Fixed fields (§interface-contracts §3.9) | `Redactor` per event | Yes | **Best-effort, non-critical: terminal append failure ⇒ `terminal_event.durable=false` (manifest states it) but the logical outcome is preserved and the run is published; progress-event failure ⇒ redacted note, never changes the immutable manifest** | EventSink + Persist |\n\n**Disclosure distinction:** decision-agent narrative necessarily receives provider-summarized context **after consent** (intentional disclosure). This is distinct from copying **raw portfolio bytes / full provider payloads** into manifests/logs/events/state JSON, which is prohibited (INV-06).\n\n## 6. Non-goals\nNo resume/checkpoint redesign, no cross-run catalogue, no aggregate budget persistence. Upstream checkpoint fingerprint (12-char) remains a checkpoint concern, preserved unchanged.",

Lifecycle sequencing stays inline.\n- **C2 — Input-service + immutable `RunContext` + small lifecycle coordinator (SELECTED).** One `PortfolioInputService` → `RunContext`; CLI `RunLifecycleCoordinator` with explicit consent transitions; `OutputChecker`; `OutcomeFinalizer`; redaction; JSONL events; atomic manifest. Single-run scope only.\n- **C3 — Phased single-run orchestrator façade.** Same service/context as C2 plus a façade over the whole single-run lifecycle; no backtest/resume.\n\n## 2. Disqualifying constraints pre-screen (DQ1–DQ10)\n\n| # | Constraint | C1 | Rationale | C2 | Rationale | C3 | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| DQ1 | No prompts in agents/engine | Pass | Discovery/consent in CLI entry; agents untouched | Pass | Service/coordinator in CLI layer; engine API unchanged | Pass | Façade is CLI-layer coordinator |\n| DQ2 | No silent default file pick | Pass | Inline requires explicit choice | Pass | `discover()` returns sorted list; explicit selection | Pass | Same service |\n| DQ3 | Absent ≠ flat; missing cash ≠ 0 | Pass | Reuses `PortfolioContext` semantics | Pass | `RunContext` explicit mode + None vs empty | Pass | Same as C2 |\n| DQ4 | Recoverable sentinel not fatal | Pass | Outcome finalizer module | Pass | Finalizer consumes typed exceptions | Pass | Delegates to same finalizer |\n| DQ5 | Model cannot set check/outcome | Pass | Checker separate; header from frozen state | Pass | `RunContext`+`OutputChecker` authoritative | Pass | Same authority objects |\n| DQ6 | No full portfolio payload to new sinks | Pass | Single redactor; discipline required | Pass | Provenance/`SafeRunMetadata` only; redactor at sink | Pass | Same |\n| DQ7 | Reusable input-service boundary | Pass | **Sole shared-service ownership with thin inline adapter** (resolved: one validator/discoverer; reporting reads only returned frozen context) | Pass | One service+immutable context | Pass | Same service+context |\n| DQ8 | Mode-aware prompt/context wording | Pass | Manager prompt edits required | Pass | Same edits via rendered context | Pass | Same |\n| DQ9 | Redaction across sinks | Pass | One helper at each sink | Pass | Redactor at sink boundary | Pass | Same |\n| DQ10 | No backtest/resume scope creep | Pass | CLI single-run only | Pass | Coordinator scoped to one fresh run | Pass | Façade strictly single-run |\n\nAll three are eligible. C1's DQ7 pass depends on the discipline that reporting/report code never re-derives provenance from `final_state` (latent FR-006/007 risk if violated — recorded as a C1 risk in `risk-list.md`).\n\n## 3. Score matrix (design estimates) with rationale + uncertainty\n\nScores 1–5 (5 best). Every score is a design estimate.\n\n| Criterion (weight) | C1 | Rationale / uncertainty | C2 | Rationale / uncertainty | C3 | Rationale / uncertainty |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Testability / independent seams (25%) | 3 | Shared module helps; inline `main.py` branches harder to isolate. Uncertainty: medium (seams unknown until C plans) | 5 | Service+RunContext+checker cleanly mockable; identity testable independently. Uncertainty: low | 4 | Phased façade testable per phase; more states. Uncertainty: medium |\n| Change surface / coupling / maintainability (25%) | 4 | Small footprint; scattered-edit drift risk. Uncertainty: medium-high | 4 | Bounded cohesive modules; small report/manager touch. Uncertainty: low-medium | 2 | Broad `cli/run.py` lifecycle change. Uncertainty: high |\n| Auditability / provenance (20%) | 3 | Provenance fragmented across main/reporting. Uncertainty: medium | 5 | Centralized in RunContext; single source for result/header/manifest/events. Uncertainty: low | 5 | Same centralization via façade. Uncertainty: low |\n| Failure behaviour (15%) | 2 | Inline path risks untyped escapes; finalizer bolted on. Uncertainty: medium-high | 5 | Coordinator+finalizer enforce typed mapping at every phase. Uncertainty: low | 5 | Façade owns phase failure. Uncertainty: low |\n| Compatibility w/ intentional changes (10%) | 4 | Required CLI changes intentional; minor scattered edits. Uncertainty: low | 5 | Clean flag additions; documented intended changes. Uncertainty: low | 4 | More churn in run path. Uncertainty: medium |\n| Effort/token estimate (5%) | 5 | ESTIMATE: lowest. Uncertainty: high (may grow) | 3 | ESTIMATE: medium — module map now lists ~10 `runapi` modules (supersedes \"~4\"). Uncertainty: medium | 2 | ESTIMATE: medium-high; façade rewrite. Uncertainty: high |\n\n## 4. Weighted totals (baseline weights)\n\nBaseline weights: testability 25 · change 25 · auditability 20 · failure 15 · compat 10 · effort 5 = 100.\n\n- **C1** = .25·3 + .25·4 + .20·3 + .15·2 + .10·4 + .05·5 = 0.75+1.00+0.60+0.30+0.40+0.25 = **3.300**\n- **C2** = .25·5 + .25·4 + .20·5 + .15·5 + .10·5 + .05·3 = 1.25+1.00+1.00+0.75+0.50+0.15 = **4.650**\n- **C3** = .25·4 + .25·2 + .20·5 + .15·5 + .10·4 + .05·2 = 1.00+0.50+1.00+0.75+0.40+0.10 = **3.750**\n\n## 5. Sensitivity analysis (both scenarios normalized to 100%)\n\n### Scenario (a) — change-surface–favouring (exact normalized weights)\ntestability 12.5 · change 37.5 · auditability 20 · failure 15 · compat 10 · effort 5 = **100**.\n\n- C1 = .125·3 + .375·4 + .20·3 + .15·2 + .10·4 + .05·5 = 0.375+1.500+0.600+0.300+0.400+0.250 = **3.425**\n- C2 = .125·5 + .375·4 + .20·5 + .15·5 + .10·5 + .05·3 = 0.625+1.500+1.000+0.750+0.500+0.150 = **4.525**\n- C3 = .125·4 + .375·2 + .20·5 + .15·5 + .10·4 + .05·2 = 0.500+0.750+1.000+0.750+0.400+0.100 = **3.500**\n\n### Scenario (b) — testability-favouring (exact normalized weights)\ntestability 44.4 · change 11.1 · auditability 17.8 · failure 13.3 · compat 8.9 · effort 4.4 (fractions of 100; sum 99.9 → exact fractions used below).\nExact: testability 50/112.5=0.44444 · change 12.5/112.5=0.11111 · audit 20/112.5=0.17778 · failure 15/112.5=0.13333 · compat 10/112.5=0.08889 · effort 5/112.5=0.04444 (sum = 1.00000).\n\n- **C1** = .44444·3 + .11111·4 + .17778·3 + .13333·2 + .08889·4 + .04444·5 = 1.3333+0.4444+0.5333+0.2667+0.3556+0.2222 = **3.156** ✓\n- **C2** = .44444·5 + .11111·4 + .17778·5 + .13333·5 + .08889·5 + .04444·3 = 2.2222+0.4444+0.8889+0.6667+0.4444+0.1333 = **4.800** ✓\n- **C3** = .44444·4 + .11111·2 + .17778·5 + .13333·5 + .08889·4 + .04444·2 = 1.7778+0.2222+0.8889+0.6667+0.3556+0.0889 = **4.000** ✓\n\n(Scenario (b) totals: 3.156 / 4.800 / 4.000, as required.)\n\n## 6. Interpretation and limits\nRanking across baseline and both normalized scenarios: **C2 > C3 > C1**. This consistency is **a property of the chosen weights and the assigned design-estimate scores, not independent evidence of correctness**. Scores carry stated uncertainty; a different plausible set (e.g., C1 change-surface 5, C1 testability 4) narrows the C1 gap. Reopening conditions: instructor mandates a façade (favours C3); file-count constraint (favours C1/C3); real test evidence (C) shows C1 cleanly testable without provenance drift.\n\n## 7. Selection\n**C2 selected by Brian (human)**, rationale: explicit input/snapshot boundary, test seams and shared provenance without C3's broader orchestration change. Recorded in `adr/001-portfolio-aware-cli.md`; process in `evaluation-logbook.md`.",

Status: working selection authorized for architecture exploration by Brian; pending Member A/team approval as a final registry. This is not the final D1 YAML deliverable. IDs `SEL-TA-*` belong to this selection and do not silently modify/reuse the wider v2 IDs.\n4: \n5: ## 1. Scope and baseline\n6: \n7: Target TradingAgents v0.7.1; extend its existing terminal UI, Python/LangGraph workflow, portfolio loader and Markdown/HTML reports. No new web GUI, broker connection, order execution, exposure certification or guaranteed investment outcome. Preserve baseline code/import structure until an approved layout decision.\n8: \n9: This deliberately revises v2's exclusion of portfolio input. Both modes are supported: `NO_PORTFOLIO` (unknown holdings/cash) and `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED` (explicit user-selected snapshot). An explicitly supplied empty positions list is a flat snapshot, not missing input. Reported holdings are user-supplied context, not independently verified account facts.\n10: \n11: Existing v0.7.1: CLI `--portfolio PATH` calls `tradingagents.portfolio.load_portfolio`; its optional context reaches the graph and decision agents. No option means no context. It does not offer the proposed automatic folder picker/confirmation flow. Relevant sources: `cli/main.py`, `cli/run.py`, `tradingagents/portfolio.py`, `tradingagents/agents/context.py`, `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py`.\n12: \n13: ### Fixed working decisions\n14: \n15: - Interface is the current CLI. `PORTFOLIO_DIR` defaults to `<project-root>/portfolios`; do not search the home directory, credentials or arbitrary folders. Interactive discovery is non-recursive and lists regular `.json` files in deterministic filename order; symlinks are excluded from discovery.\n16: - Explicit `--portfolio PATH` remains supported, including a deliberately supplied path outside PORTFOLIO_DIR. Do not silently pick the newest/first file. Explicit paths are not an instruction to scan their parent directory.\n17: - Noninteractive use requires either `--portfolio PATH` or a new explicit `--without-portfolio` flag. Neither means input error; both means input error. The ordinary Python API remains usable with `portfolio=None` and does not prompt. CLI flags express the consent that an unattended process cannot give interactively.\n18: - A run begins only after input selection/validation/confirmation. Cancelled/rejected input starts no graph, makes zero LLM calls and creates no completed run. A fresh invocation creates a fresh run ID. Checkpoint resume, backtest changes, deadlines/token/call budgets and convergence changes are deferred from this selection.\n19: - Snapshot timing: user confirms that selected holdings are intended for analysis date D; record `portfolio_as_of=D` and `as_of_basis=USER_CONFIRMED`. Never infer timing from file modification time or claim historical accuracy was verified. Noninteractive `--portfolio` users must supply `--portfolio-as-of D` matching the requested analysis date. Existing upstream loader schema stays unchanged; these are wrapper metadata.\n20: - Selection reads the chosen file once, validates those bytes and freezes the normalized context for that run. Subsequent file changes cannot silently change the snapshot. Do not persist the full portfolio or other-position list in new report headers/logs/manifests; upstream decision prompts necessarily receive context and the provider disclosure is made before confirmation. Context-dependent generated narrative is still possible.\n21: \n22: ### Result and check contract\n23: \n24: Every started run returns `run_outcome=COMPLETED|INCOMPLETE`. Completed means the workflow returned; its final `rating` is Buy/Overweight/Hold/Underweight/Sell or REVIEW. Incomplete has no final rating and has `stop_reason=MODEL_FAILURE|DATA_FAILURE|INTERNAL_ERROR|PERSISTENCE_ERROR|INTERRUPTED`. Use MODEL_FAILURE only for exhausted model/provider output failures; DATA_FAILURE for an unrecovered raised vendor/data exception; preserve baseline recoverable non-core unavailable-data behaviour. INTERRUPTED covers cooperative cancellation, not an impossible promise to persist through power loss.\n25: \n26: `output_check=PASSED|NEEDS_REVIEW|NOT_RUN`; incomplete always NOT_RUN. A deterministic component owns the check. Rules: Q1 final rating readable, Q2 header matches trusted input snapshot metadata, Q3 disclaimer present, Q4 prohibited guarantee phrases absent. Each broken rule is a blocking finding; checker exception yields blocking CHECK_ERROR. No findings means PASSED. PASSED certifies only these checks, not factual accuracy or account suitability. This selection does not introduce global source-confidence scoring, sentiment correction or twelve-channel availability grading.\n27: \n28: Frozen strings: no-portfolio notice = `Holdings and cash were not provided; no account ownership is assumed.` Disclaimer = `Research output only. User-supplied holdings are unverified. No order is placed and no return is guaranteed.` Q4 checks the model-generated narrative for case-insensitive phrases `guaranteed profit`, `guaranteed returns`, `capital protection is guaranteed`. The trusted disclaimer is excluded. These limited phrase checks are complemented by SEL-TA-GOV-004 semantic evaluation and are not claimed to prove universal absence of paraphrased guarantees.\n29: \n30: ## 2. Functional requirements\n31: \n32: Each criterion below is a proposed acceptance obligation, not an existing test/result. All offline tests use isolated folders, a scripted model and no network. C owns actual test IDs, files and procedures.\n33: \n34: ### SEL-TA-FR-001 Discover and select a portfolio file\n35: \n36: - Type: functional. Priority: Must. Source: Brian's new holdings workflow; extends v2 FR-007 scope.\n37: - Statement: In interactive mode without an explicit input-mode flag, the CLI lists eligible filenames from PORTFOLIO_DIR and offers select one, continue without portfolio, or cancel. A missing/empty directory proceeds to the explicit no-portfolio confirmation; a directory read error is shown and offers retry, explicit no-portfolio confirmation, or cancel. It is never described as an empty directory.\n38: - Fit: With eligible `a.json`, `b.json`, a nested JSON, symlink and text file, exactly a/b appear once in sorted order; selecting b passes only b to validation. Separate empty/missing/unreadable fixtures follow their declared branch; cancelling dispatches zero LLM calls. One invalid selection does not pick a default.\n39: - Baseline: --portfolio exists; picker is new. Tradeoff: an extra interaction prevents silent selection.\n40: \n41: ### SEL-TA-FR-002 Explicit mode confirmation\n42: \n43: - Type: functional. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-001.\n44: - Statement: Interactive no-portfolio choice shows the frozen notice and asks to proceed, default No. File choice shows basename, analysis date, unverified/as-of statement, and that holdings will be sent to the configured model provider; it asks to proceed, default No. Confirming without holdings passes actual None, not an empty PortfolioContext. Automated invocation follows the flag rules above; an explicit flag is consent and prompts are suppressed.\n45: - Fit: Yes/No/EOF fixtures for each mode: only Yes starts one graph. No/EOF starts zero and exits cleanly. Noninteractive neither/both flags produce a readable input error and zero graph/LLM calls; valid --without-portfolio starts once with None.\n46: - Tradeoff: adds confirmation while preserving deliberate unattended use. API calls do not gain interactive prompts.\n47: \n48: ### SEL-TA-FR-003 Validate and freeze the selected snapshot\n49: \n50: - Type: functional. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-001/002.\n51: - Statement: Require top-level JSON object with explicit `positions` list. Each position has ticker and finite numeric quantity; optional average_price and cash are null or finite JSON numbers (booleans and numeric strings are rejected). Optional currency is a string or null. Reuse upstream model validation after these input prechecks. Empty positions is valid; malformed/missing fields, NaN/Infinity, unreadable paths and as-of mismatch stop input before dispatch. Explain filename plus bad field/path without exposing file contents or credentials. Permit reselect/cancel; no silent no-portfolio fallback.\n52: - Fit: Valid populated, explicit empty and null-cash fixtures load; six invalid classes (bad JSON, missing positions, missing quantity, nonfinite number, wrong scalar type, unreadable file) and as-of mismatch each dispatch zero calls with a field/file diagnostic. Editing the file after confirmation does not change the context used or fingerprint recorded.\n53: - Baseline: upstream validates many invalid files; explicit shape/type/as-of and freezing are project extensions. Tradeoff: previously permissive `{}` input is rejected to avoid treating absent data as an intentionally empty book.\n54: \n55: ### SEL-TA-FR-004 Propagate explicit context without inventing holdings\n56: \n57: - Type: functional. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-003.\n58: - Statement: Pass exactly the frozen validated snapshot through the existing portfolio argument to the decision agents. Retain upstream instrument alias matching. Missing cash is not zero; absent context is not a flat book. No-portfolio prompts do not refer to the user's existing position. Portfolio-provided prompts may refer only to explicitly supplied facts, labelled as user-supplied; they do not claim account verification.\n59: - Fit: Capture Trader/Portfolio Manager prompts for no portfolio, explicit flat, held ticker, broker-alias ticker and null-cash fixtures. All five preserve their distinct state; missing cash renders no invented number. Assert selected fixture values occur, another file's unique marker does not, and no-portfolio calls contain the frozen notice.\n60: - Baseline: optional rendering/alias distinctions already exist; unified confirmation-to-report identity and strengthened wording are new. Tradeoff: preserving unknowns limits account-specific conclusions.\n61: \n62: ### SEL-TA-FR-005 Distinguish ratings and actions\n63: \n64: - Type: functional. Priority: Must. Source: v2 FR-007.\n65: - Statement: Label final Portfolio Manager rating, intermediate Research Manager recommendation and intermediate Trader action separately. First two use five-tier research vocabulary; Trader uses three actions. REVIEW means unreadable rating, never Hold. No-portfolio Hold means balanced/insufficient evidence supporting no new directional action, not keeping an assumed position. Portfolio context does not convert research into an executable account instruction.\n66: - Fit: Fixtures cover all five final ratings, all three Trader actions, REVIEW and differing intermediate/final judgments. Each completed report has exactly one final-rating header and all three labelled stages. A REVIEW fixture remains REVIEW; no-portfolio Hold includes the defined meaning and no ownership assertion.\n67: - Tradeoff: stage labels take space but prevent conflating recommendation and proposal.\n68: \n69: ### SEL-TA-FR-006 Deterministic input provenance in every report\n70: \n71: - Type: functional. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-002/003/005.\n72: - Statement: Header is built from trusted state and contains run ID, ticker, D, input mode, selected basename and a full normalized-content SHA-256 fingerprint when supplied, user-confirmed as-of date/basis, outcome/check and disclaimer. No-portfolio uses explicit null for file/fingerprint/as-of and the frozen notice. Partial artifacts say INCOMPLETE and contain no final rating. Basename/fingerprint are provenance, not proof of truthful holdings. Do not automatically export the full portfolio payload in this header.\n73: - Fit: Changing scripted model prose leaves provenance identical. Selecting b yields b's frozen fingerprint in returned result, manifest and report, never a's. None and explicit empty portfolio produce distinct modes/fingerprints. HTML escapes file/model text, including script-like names.\n74: - Tradeoff: adds metadata; holdings fingerprints are privacy-sensitive and remain local by default.\n75: \n76: ### SEL-TA-FR-007 Deterministic output-check authority\n77: \n78: - Type: functional/invariant. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-006.\n79: - Statement: One non-LLM component assigns output_check and findings using Q1-Q4; model text cannot assign, bypass or overwrite them. Header/result/check refer to the same frozen data. On check error retain COMPLETED if the graph returned, but use NEEDS_REVIEW with CHECK_ERROR. Render check meaning next to the result.\n80: - Fit: Positive fixture passes; four single-rule failures each produce its matching finding and NEEDS_REVIEW; injected model claim `OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED` cannot override a failing rule. Check exception fails closed; every incomplete fixture is NOT_RUN. Output check calls no provider.\n81: - Tradeoff: limited deterministic checks do not assess truth. Concrete fallback: mark review-needed, suppress any success badge and retain readable diagnostics for human review.\n82: \n83: ## 3. Non-functional requirements\n84: \n85: ### SEL-TA-NFR-001 Reliable external-failure handling\n86: \n87: - Type: reliability. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-007.\n88: - Statement: Preserve usable free-text fallback after structured-output failure. Exhausted model failures, unrecovered raised data failures and ordinary internal exceptions return typed incomplete results rather than escaping the public CLI/application entry point. A workflow returning unreadable final text completes with REVIEW and NEEDS_REVIEW. Do not reclassify a recoverable optional-data sentinel as a fatal error.\n89: - Fit: Two usable-fallback, two unreadable-final, two exhausted-model and one raised-data fixture all follow the contract; zero exceptions escape. An ordinary injected internal exception returns INTERNAL_ERROR. Diagnostics are redacted. Tradeoff: predictable failure results require preserving causes for debugging.\n90: \n91: ### SEL-TA-NFR-002 Structured observability\n92: \n93: - Type: observability. Priority: Should. Depends: NFR-001/003.\n94: - Statement: The new lifecycle event sink is UTF-8 JSONL. Every event contains run_id, ticker, node (`input`/`engine`/`output` for non-agent events), UTC timestamp, nonnegative monotonic elapsed_ms, event and event_outcome. Progress vocabulary is separate from terminal run_outcome. Console presentation may remain human-readable; raw provider payload logging is disabled by default in this selection.\n95: - Fit: Parse every line from one completed and one incomplete run: 100% parse, required fields non-null and elapsed nonnegative. Exactly one terminal event per run. No full portfolio payload or planted secret appears. Existing upstream state snapshots are not falsely described as JSONL. Tradeoff: machine-readable logs need a human-friendly console view.\n96: \n97: ### SEL-TA-NFR-003 Credential and holdings privacy\n98: \n99: - Type: security/privacy. Priority: Must.\n100: - Statement: Central output/error redaction covers the selected CLI, model/data exception messages, new events, report headers and manifests. Never emit API keys, OAuth access/refresh tokens or bearer [REDACTED] values. Keep portfolio source files read-only. Do not copy raw portfolio bytes into manifests/transcripts or print other-position lists in the selection UI. The confirmed disclosure to the model provider is intentional, not represented as local-only processing.\n101: - Fit: Four planted secret types across each named sink and model/data error path yield zero values; marker for an unrelated holding does not appear in UI/header/events/manifest. Source bytes are unchanged after success/failure. Secret leakage inside arbitrary generated narratives is also scanned; redact before delivery. Tradeoff: diagnostic detail is reduced. C expands the named-path inventory as integrations grow.\n102: \n103: ### SEL-TA-NFR-004 Distinct immutable fresh-run artifacts\n104: \n105: - Type: reproducibility. Priority: Should. Depends: FR-006, NFR-003.\n106: - Statement: Each started fresh run gets a unique ID and its own report directory and final manifest. Write manifest atomically once after artifact/check finalization. Record times, code version/source identifier, prompt hash, safe effective config, input provenance and result fields. Do not serialize secret endpoints; record safe provider identifiers. Failed runs keep available partial artifacts. Durable records during total disk failure/power loss are not promised; return a redacted persistence diagnostic if commit fails.\n107: - Fit: Two same-ticker/date runs produce two directories; first hashes remain unchanged. Config-only comparison of two manifests differing in one selected config key finds exactly that config difference; IDs/timing/results are excluded from that assertion. Prompt edit changes hash. Required result fields are validated conditionally: incomplete has no rating, completed has no stop_reason. Resume is deferred, not implemented by mutating a final record.\n108: - Tradeoff: extra storage; no automatic deletion in this selection.\n109: \n110: ### SEL-TA-NFR-005 Cohesive, compatible integration\n111: \n112: - Type: maintainability. Priority: Should. Depends: FR-003/004.\n113: - Statement: One reusable selection/input service and one shared result/reporting boundary support CLI without putting interactive prompts inside agents or the Python engine API. Reuse the upstream portfolio model/rendering and selected graph contract. Do not replace the baseline or duplicate independent JSON validators in every agent. Preserve upstream tests and explicitly document intentional CLI/type-validation changes.\n114: - Fit: One mocked API call with portfolio=None completes without terminal reads; explicit valid portfolio CLI call invokes selection service once and graph once. Structural check finds zero terminal prompt imports in tradingagents/agents/** and graph/**. Full prior offline suite has zero unapproved regressions. Tradeoff: added adapter boundary in exchange for testability.\n115: \n116: ### SEL-TA-NFR-006 Transparent evaluation population\n117: \n118: - Type: evaluation quality. Priority: Should. Depends: NFR-004.\n119: - Statement: Completion fraction counts all started fresh runs; pre-run rejected/cancelled inputs are counted separately. Quality summaries use completed runs and show count, NEEDS_REVIEW count and incomplete-reason counts alongside scores. Zero completed samples means insufficient evidence, never a passing quality result. Controlled before/after experiments may differ in declared changed factors; repeated fixed-condition benchmarks require matching controls.\n120: - Fit: Ten started records (six completed, two of those review-needed; four incomplete) plus two pre-run cancellations produce completion 6/10, review-needed 2, cancellations 2 and no dropped starts. Zero-completed fixture returns insufficient evidence. Changed prompt experiment is labelled as such, not rejected merely for its hash. Tradeoff: denominators expose unavailable delivery rather than hide it.\n121: \n122: ## 4. Mandatory process requirements (additional to the seven FRs/six NFRs)\n123: \n124: These follow the course brief, not optional v2 startup exemptions. Accountable owners are separate from the implementation designer.\n125: \n126: | ID | Type / priority | Statement and fit criterion | Owner |\n127: |---|---|---|---|\n128: | SEL-TA-GOV-001 | Governance / Must | Before implementation, record attributable approval of the independent test plan. An implementation PR with no prior approval fails its required check. | C plan; E enforcement; human approver |\n129: | SEL-TA-GOV-002 | Governance / Must | Registry validates against its schema. One valid/one invalid registry fixture proves pass/fail. A supplies final YAML/schema; this working Markdown is not substituted for them. | A/E |\n130: | SEL-TA-GOV-003 | Governance / Must | Prior tests run with zero unapproved regression; lint/type/dependency checks run on commits; safety PRs also run contract/security/API/permission checks. Introduced negative fixtures fail the matching required check. | C/E |\n131: | SEL-TA-GOV-004 | Governance / Must | Prompt/model changes replay fixed semantic cases against human-approved quality thresholds before production. Cases cover conditional ownership, rating/action distinction, guarantee language and injection. Below threshold or no valid samples cannot pass. C freezes rubric/population/threshold with A; D measures; E enforces. No unapproved non-blocking startup claim. | C/D/E |\n132: | SEL-TA-GOV-005 | Governance / Must | Code/prompt PR without AI-use log update is blocked. Demonstrate one rejected and one accepted fixture/change. Record real tools/model/session/interventions only. | E/all |\n133: | SEL-TA-GOV-006 | Governance/invariant / Must | Branch protection requires passing checks and human review plus ADR for safety changes; agent file access follows approved default-deny whitelists. A denied write attempt is blocked and logged without changing the file. | E with B permission design |\n134: \n135: ## 5. Test profile, ownership and deferred scope\n136: \n137: Pinned offline workload: isolated temporary directories, fake portfolio files (no real holdings/keys), scripted models following v0.7.1 test seams, no network and no provider billing. A/C turn the acceptance sketches into an approved fixture inventory and executable tests; they must not assert tests exist/pass yet. API/CLI/Markdown/HTML paths are distinct integration obligations. Exact semantic scoring threshold is an open C/A decision and must be fixed before semantic approval, not invented by an architecture agent.\n138: \n139: B designs enforcing components, contracts, invariant fallbacks, state/privacy and permission boundaries. D implements via supervised OpenCode. C owns test code and independent verification. E owns enforcement/packaging; A owns final requirements. All selected runtime requirements are Must or Should with dependencies no lower in priority. Mandatory minimal result persistence belongs to FR-006; optional richer experiment metadata belongs to NFR-004.\n140: \n141: Deferred: web GUI; exposure caps/position validation; automatic broker discovery; order execution; full stable-evidence registry across twelve channels; new historical filtering/freshness rules; global source-confidence grades; R4-R6 sentiment correction; resume/catalogue redesign; aggregate time/token/call limits; debate convergence; analyst plugin redesign. Preserve upstream safeguards while deferring their extension. Do not claim deferred v2 requirements are satisfied by this selection.\n142: \n143: Open items do not authorize silent improvisation: final D1 approval, semantic rubric/threshold, exact source/test layout accepted by instructor and the governance setup are unresolved. They do not prevent design candidate exploration; implementation/production gates remain real. Use the working decisions above for architecture unless a direct contradiction is found.\n144: \n145: Change log: 2026-11-12 +08:00 - Initial seven-FR/six-NFR/six-governance working selection, incorporating explicitly confirmed optional holdings.
