A missing/empty directory proceeds to the explicit no-portfolio confirmation; a directory read error is shown and offers retry, explicit no-portfolio confirmation, or cancel. It is never described as an empty directory.\n- Fit: With eligible `a.json`, `b.json`, a nested JSON, symlink and text file, exactly a/b appear once in sorted order; selecting b passes only b to validation. Separate empty/missing/unreadable fixtures follow their declared branch; cancelling dispatches zero LLM calls. One invalid selection does not pick a default.\n- Baseline: --portfolio exists; picker is new. Tradeoff: an extra interaction prevents silent selection.\n\n### SEL-TA-FR-002 Explicit mode confirmation\n\n- Type: functional. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-001.\n- Statement: Interactive no-portfolio choice shows the frozen notice and asks to proceed, default No. File choice shows basename, analysis date, unverified/as-of statement, and that holdings will be sent to the configured model provider; it asks to proceed, default No. Confirming without holdings passes actual None, not an empty PortfolioContext. Automated invocation follows the flag rules above; an explicit flag is consent and prompts are suppressed.\n- Fit: Yes/No/EOF fixtures for each mode: only Yes starts one graph. No/EOF starts zero and exits cleanly. Noninteractive neither/both flags produce a readable input error and zero graph/LLM calls; valid --without-portfolio starts once with None.\n- Tradeoff: adds confirmation while preserving deliberate unattended use. API calls do not gain interactive prompts.\n\n### SEL-TA-FR-003 Validate and freeze the selected snapshot\n\n- Type: functional. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-001/002.\n- Statement: Require top-level JSON object with explicit `positions` list. Each position has ticker and finite numeric quantity; optional average_price and cash are null or finite JSON numbers (booleans and numeric strings are rejected). Optional currency is a string or null. Reuse upstream model validation after these input prechecks. Empty positions is valid; malformed/missing fields, NaN/Infinity, unreadable paths and as-of mismatch stop input before dispatch. Explain filename plus bad field/path without exposing file contents or credentials. Permit reselect/cancel; no silent no-portfolio fallback.\n- Fit: Valid populated, explicit empty and null-cash fixtures load; six invalid classes (bad JSON, missing positions, missing quantity, nonfinite number, wrong scalar type, unreadable file) and as-of mismatch each dispatch zero calls with a field/file diagnostic. Editing the file after confirmation does not change the context used or fingerprint recorded.\n- Baseline: upstream validates many invalid files; explicit shape/type/as-of and freezing are project extensions. Tradeoff: previously permissive `{}` input is rejected to avoid treating absent data as an intentionally empty book.\n\n### SEL-TA-FR-004 Propagate explicit context without inventing holdings\n\n- Type: functional. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-003.\n- Statement: Pass exactly the frozen validated snapshot through the existing portfolio argument to the decision agents. Retain upstream instrument alias matching. Missing cash is not zero; absent context is not a flat book. No-portfolio prompts do not refer to the user's existing position. Portfolio-provided prompts may refer only to explicitly supplied facts, labelled as user-supplied; they do not claim account verification.\n- Fit: Capture Trader/Portfolio Manager prompts for no portfolio, explicit flat, held ticker, broker-alias ticker and null-cash fixtures. All five preserve their distinct state; missing cash renders no invented number. Assert selected fixture values occur, another file's unique marker does not, and no-portfolio calls contain the frozen notice.\n- Baseline: optional rendering/alias distinctions already exist; unified confirmation-to-report identity and strengthened wording are new. Tradeoff: preserving unknowns limits account-specific conclusions.\n\n### SEL-TA-FR-005 Distinguish ratings and actions\n\n- Type: functional. Priority: Must. Source: v2 FR-007.\n- Statement: Label final Portfolio Manager rating, intermediate Research Manager recommendation and intermediate Trader action separately. First two use five-tier research vocabulary; Trader uses three actions. REVIEW means unreadable rating, never Hold. No-portfolio Hold means balanced/insufficient evidence supporting no new directional action, not keeping an assumed position. Portfolio context does not convert research into an executable account instruction.\n- Fit: Fixtures cover all five final ratings, all three Trader actions, REVIEW and differing intermediate/final judgments. Each completed report has exactly one final-rating header and all three labelled stages. A REVIEW fixture remains REVIEW; no-portfolio Hold includes the defined meaning and no ownership assertion.\n- Tradeoff: stage labels take space but prevent conflating recommendation and proposal.\n\n### SEL-TA-FR-006 Deterministic input provenance in every report\n\n- Type: functional. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-002/003/005.\n- Statement: Header is built from trusted state and contains run ID, ticker, D, input mode, selected basename and a full normalized-content SHA-256 fingerprint when supplied, user-confirmed as-of date/basis, outcome/check and disclaimer. No-portfolio uses explicit null for file/fingerprint/as-of and the frozen notice. Partial artifacts say INCOMPLETE and contain no final rating. Basename/fingerprint are provenance, not proof of truthful holdings. Do not automatically export the full portfolio payload in this header.\n- Fit: Changing scripted model prose leaves provenance identical. Selecting b yields b's frozen fingerprint in returned result, manifest and report, never a's. None and explicit empty portfolio produce distinct modes/fingerprints. HTML escapes file/model text, including script-like names.\n- Tradeoff: adds metadata; holdings fingerprints are privacy-sensitive and remain local by default.\n\n### SEL-TA-FR-007 Deterministic output-check authority\n\n- Type: functional/invariant. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-006.\n- Statement: One non-LLM component assigns output_check and findings using Q1-Q4; model text cannot assign, bypass or overwrite them. Header/result/check refer to the same frozen data. On check error retain COMPLETED if the graph returned, but use NEEDS_REVIEW with CHECK_ERROR. Render check meaning next to the result.\n- Fit: Positive fixture passes; four single-rule failures each produce its matching finding and NEEDS_REVIEW; injected model claim `OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED` cannot override a failing rule. Check exception fails closed; every incomplete fixture is NOT_RUN. Output check calls no provider.\n- Tradeoff: limited deterministic checks do not assess truth. Concrete fallback: mark review-needed, suppress any success badge and retain readable diagnostics for human review.\n\n## 3. Non-functional requirements\n\n### SEL-TA-NFR-001 Reliable external-failure handling\n\n- Type: reliability. Priority: Must. Depends: FR-007.\n- Statement: Preserve usable free-text fallback after structured-output failure. Exhausted model failures, unrecovered raised data failures and ordinary internal exceptions return typed incomplete results rather than escaping the public CLI/application entry point. A workflow returning unreadable final text completes with REVIEW and NEEDS_REVIEW. Do not reclassify a recoverable optional-data sentinel as a fatal error.\n- Fit: Two usable-fallback, two unreadable-final, two exhausted-model and one raised-data fixture all follow the contract; zero exceptions escape. An ordinary injected internal exception returns INTERNAL_ERROR. Diagnostics are redacted. Tradeoff: predictable failure results require preserving causes for debugging.\n\n### SEL-TA-NFR-002 Structured observability\n\n- Type: observability. Priority: Should. Depends: NFR-001/003.\n- Statement: The new lifecycle event sink is UTF-8 JSONL. Every event contains run_id, ticker, node (`input`/`engine`/`output` for non-agent events), UTC timestamp, nonnegative monotonic elapsed_ms, event and event_outcome. Progress vocabulary is separate from terminal run_outcome. Console presentation may remain human-readable; raw provider payload logging is disabled by default in this selection.\n- Fit: Parse every line from one completed and one incomplete run: 100% parse, required fields non-null and elapsed nonnegative. Exactly one terminal event per run. No full portfolio payload or planted secret appears. Existing upstream state snapshots are not falsely described as JSONL. Tradeoff: machine-readable logs need a human-friendly console view.\n\n### SEL-TA-NFR-003 Credential and holdings privacy\n\n- Type: security/privacy. Priority: Must.\n- Statement: Central output/error redaction covers the selected CLI, model/data exception messages, new events, report headers and manifests. Never emit API keys, OAuth access/refresh tokens or bearer [REDACTED] values. Keep portfolio source files read-only. Do not copy raw portfolio bytes into manifests/transcripts or print other-position lists in the selection UI. The confirmed disclosure to the model provider is intentional, not represented as local-only processing.\n- Fit: Four planted secret types across each named sink and model/data error path yield zero values; marker for an unrelated holding does not appear in UI/header/events/manifest. Source bytes are unchanged after success/failure. Secret leakage inside arbitrary generated narratives is also scanned; redact before delivery. Tradeoff: diagnostic detail is reduced. C expands the named-path inventory as integrations grow.\n\n### SEL-TA-NFR-004 Distinct immutable fresh-run artifacts\n\n- Type: reproducibility. Priority: Should. Depends: FR-006, NFR-003.\n- Statement: Each started fresh run gets a unique ID and its own report directory and final manifest. Write manifest atomically once after artifact/check finalization. Record times, code version/source identifier, prompt hash, safe effective config, input provenance and result fields. Do not serialize secret endpoints; record safe provider identifiers. Failed runs keep available partial artifacts. Durable records during total disk failure/power loss are not promised; return a redacted persistence diagnostic if commit fails.\n- Fit: Two same-ticker/date runs produce two directories; first hashes remain unchanged. Config-only comparison of two manifests differing in one selected config key finds exactly that config difference; IDs/timing/results are excluded from that assertion. Prompt edit changes hash. Required result fields are validated conditionally: incomplete has no rating, completed has no stop_reason. Resume is deferred, not implemented by mutating a final record.\n- Tradeoff: extra storage; no automatic deletion in this selection.\n\n### SEL-TA-NFR-005 Cohesive, compatible integration\n\n- Type: maintainability. Priority: Should. Depends: FR-003/004.\n- Statement: One reusable selection/input service and one shared result/reporting boundary support CLI without putting interactive prompts inside agents or the Python engine API. Reuse the upstream portfolio model/rendering and selected graph contract. Do not replace the baseline or duplicate independent JSON validators in every agent. Preserve upstream tests and explicitly document intentional CLI/type-validation changes.\n- Fit: One mocked API call with portfolio=None completes without terminal reads; explicit valid portfolio CLI call invokes selection service once and graph once. Structural check finds zero terminal prompt imports in tradingagents/agents/** and graph/**. Full prior offline suite has zero unapproved regressions. Tradeoff: added adapter boundary in exchange for testability.\n\n### SEL-TA-NFR-006 Transparent evaluation population\n\n- Type: evaluation quality. Priority: Should. Depends: NFR-004.\n- Statement: Completion fraction counts all started fresh runs; pre-run rejected/cancelled inputs are counted separately. Quality summaries use completed runs and show count, NEEDS_REVIEW count and incomplete-reason counts alongside scores. Zero completed samples means insufficient evidence, never a passing quality result. Controlled before/after experiments may differ in declared changed factors; repeated fixed-condition benchmarks require matching controls.\n- Fit: Ten started records (six completed, two of those review-needed; four incomplete) plus two pre-run cancellations produce completion 6/10, review-needed 2, cancellations 2 and no dropped starts. Zero-completed fixture returns insufficient evidence. Changed prompt experiment is labelled as such, not rejected merely for its hash. Tradeoff: denominators expose unavailable delivery rather than hide it.\n\n## 4. Mandatory process requirements (additional to the seven FRs/six NFRs)\n\nThese follow the course brief, not optional v2 startup exemptions. Accountable owners are separate from the implementation designer.\n\n| ID | Type / priority | Statement and fit criterion | Owner |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| SEL-TA-GOV-001 | Governance / Must | Before implementation, record attributable approval of the independent test plan. An implementation PR with no prior approval fails its required check. | C plan; E enforcement; human approver |\n| SEL-TA-GOV-002 | Governance / Must | Registry validates against its schema. One valid/one invalid registry fixture proves pass/fail. A supplies final YAML/schema; this working Markdown is not substituted for them. | A/E |\n| SEL-TA-GOV-003 | Governance / Must | Prior tests run with zero unapproved regression; lint/type/dependency checks run on commits; safety PRs also run contract/security/API/permission checks. Introduced negative fixtures fail the matching required check. | C/E |\n| SEL-TA-GOV-004 | Governance / Must | Prompt/model changes replay fixed semantic cases against human-approved quality thresholds before production. Cases cover conditional ownership, rating/action distinction, guarantee language and injection. Below threshold or no valid samples cannot pass. C freezes rubric/population/threshold with A; D measures; E enforces. No unapproved non-blocking startup claim. | C/D/E |\n| SEL-TA-GOV-005 | Governance / Must | Code/prompt PR without AI-use log update is blocked. Demonstrate one rejected and one accepted fixture/change. Record real tools/model/session/interventions only. | E/all |\n| SEL-TA-GOV-006 | Governance/invariant / Must | Branch protection requires passing checks and human review plus ADR for safety changes; agent file access follows approved default-deny whitelists. A denied write attempt is blocked and logged without changing the file. | E with B permission design |\n\n## 5. Test profile, ownership and deferred scope\n\nPinned offline workload: isolated temporary directories, fake portfolio files (no real holdings/keys), scripted models following v0.7.1 test seams, no network and no provider billing. A/C turn the acceptance sketches into an approved fixture inventory and executable tests; they must not assert tests exist/pass yet. API/CLI/Markdown/HTML paths are distinct integration obligations. Exact semantic scoring threshold is an open C/A decision and must be fixed before semantic approval, not invented by an architecture agent.\n\nB designs enforcing components, contracts, invariant fallbacks, state/privacy and permission boundaries. D implements via supervised OpenCode. C owns test code and independent verification. E owns enforcement/packaging; A owns final requirements. All selected runtime requirements are Must or Should with dependencies no lower in priority. Mandatory minimal result persistence belongs to FR-006; optional richer experiment metadata belongs to NFR-004.\n\nDeferred: web GUI; exposure caps/position validation; automatic broker discovery; order execution; full stable-evidence registry across twelve channels; new historical filtering/freshness rules; global source-confidence grades; R4-R6 sentiment correction; resume/catalogue redesign; aggregate time/token/call limits; debate convergence; analyst plugin redesign. Preserve upstream safeguards while deferring their extension. Do not claim deferred v2 requirements are satisfied by this selection.\n\nOpen items do not authorize silent improvisation: final D1 approval, semantic rubric/threshold, exact source/test layout accepted by instructor and the governance setup are unresolved. They do not prevent design candidate exploration; implementation/production gates remain real. Use the working decisions above for architecture unless a direct contradiction is found.\n\nChange log: 2026-11-12 +08:00 - Initial seven-FR/six-NFR/six-governance working selection, incorporating explicitly confirmed optional holdings. No v2 source file modified; new input-mode scope awaits A/team adoption.",

        "path": "/home/brian/projects/CS5351/requirements.yaml",
        "text": "- id: REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  title: Run result fields\n  type: functional\n  priority: Must\n  status: proposed\n  statement: \"Every run shall end with a run record holding the fields below. Each field describes one\\\n    \\ thing only, and only the combinations in the validity table are allowed.\\n\\n| Field | Values | Set\\\n    \\ by | Present when |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| `run_outcome` | `COMPLETED`, `INCOMPLETE` | Run engine\\\n    \\ | Always |\\n| `stop_reason` | `MODEL_FAILURE`, `DATA_FAILURE`, `BUDGET`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`,\\\n    \\ `INTERRUPTED` | Run engine | Only when `INCOMPLETE` |\\n| `rating` | Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight,\\\n    \\ Sell, `REVIEW` | Portfolio Manager, read by the rating parser | Only when `COMPLETED` |\\n| `output_check`\\\n    \\ | `PASSED`, `NEEDS_REVIEW`, `NOT_RUN` | Output check (ARCH-002) | Always |\\n| `check_findings` |\\\n    \\ List of rule IDs, each marked blocking or corrected | Output check (ARCH-002) | Always (may be empty)\\\n    \\ |\\n| `data_coverage` | One code per channel (FR-005) | FR-005 | Always |\\n\\n**Stop reasons**:\\n\\n\\\n    | Reason | Kind | Raised when | Owner of the rule |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| `MODEL_FAILURE` | Failure\\\n    \\ | A model step produced no usable output after retries and the free-text fallback; also an authentication\\\n    \\ or provider-configuration error (`runapi/finalize.py:classify_exception` maps `authentication` and\\\n    \\ any `openai`/`anthropic`/`google`/`langchain` exception here) | NFR-001 |\\n| `DATA_FAILURE` | Failure\\\n    \\ | Core data is unavailable, absent or stale | FR-005, FR-006 |\\n| `BUDGET` | Planned stop | A required\\\n    \\ model request is refused by the run budget. A workflow that finishes within budget completes normally;\\\n    \\ which limit was hit goes to the log (OBS-001), not to the status. | PERF-002, COST-001, COST-002\\\n    \\ |\\n| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Failure | A defect or unmapped exception in the system's own code. Never\\\n    \\ used for budget exhaustion. | none (the default for an unclassified exception) |\\n| `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`\\\n    \\ | Failure | Writing or committing the report or manifest failed before publication | NFR-REPRO-001\\\n    \\ |\\n| `INTERRUPTED` | Planned stop | The run was cooperatively cancelled. Not a claim of durability\\\n    \\ through power loss. | FR-003 (resume), D-5 |\\n\\n**Spelling rule** (B2, Member B, 2026-11-23). The\\\n    \\ two failure values keep the spellings the\\nimplementation already serializes: `MODEL_FAILURE` and\\\n    \\ `DATA_FAILURE`. The draft's short forms\\n`MODEL` and `DATA` are human-facing labels only and are\\\n    \\ not values. Renaming a serialized value is a\\nbreaking change for existing evidence, validators\\\n    \\ and readers, so no requirement here asks for one.\\n`BUDGET` is the only addition; adding an enum\\\n    \\ value is not automatically supported by every existing\\nreader, so every reader must be updated\\\n    \\ or it will reject the new value.\\n\\n**Precedence rule** (B, 2026-11-23). Exactly one primary reason\\\n    \\ is recorded. If critical\\nreport-or-manifest publication fails, `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is primary (NFR-REPRO-001,\\\n    \\ INV-14) and the\\ninitiating cause is retained in the safe diagnostic. A budget refusal is never\\\n    \\ reported as\\n`INTERNAL_ERROR`; if a budget stop and a persistence failure occur together, the persistence\\\n    \\ failure\\nis primary and the budget cause is recorded as secondary.\\n\\n**Mapping rule** (exactly\\\n    \\ one reason per run):\\n\\n1. These six values are the complete vocabulary. Every `INCOMPLETE` run\\\n    \\ shall map to exactly one of\\n   them, and a run that ends for an unlisted reason is a defect, not\\\n    \\ a new value.\\n2. Budget exhaustion shall be reported as `BUDGET`. It shall never be relabelled `INTERNAL_ERROR`\\\n    \\ or\\n   reported as a successful run.\\n3. A `BUDGET` or `INTERRUPTED` stop shall not be relabelled\\\n    \\ `MODEL_FAILURE` or `DATA_FAILURE`; those\\n   two describe a failure of the model or the data, not\\\n    \\ of a configured limit or a cancellation.\\n4. A budget refusal must be recognised before the generic\\\n    \\ exception classifier runs, and the memory\\n   settlement step and the structured-output fallback\\\n    \\ must not swallow it.\\n\\n**Validity table** (every other combination is invalid):\\n\\n| `run_outcome`\\\n    \\ | `stop_reason` | `rating` | `output_check` |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| `INCOMPLETE` | any one of the\\\n    \\ six | — | `NOT_RUN` |\\n| `COMPLETED` | — | Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell | `PASSED`\\\n    \\ or `NEEDS_REVIEW` |\\n| `COMPLETED` | — | `REVIEW` | `NEEDS_REVIEW` (rule R1) |\\n\\n**Evidence note.**\\\n    \\ No live attempt in `docs/reviews/evidence/live-verification-2026-11-21/` ends\\n`INCOMPLETE`: all\\\n    \\ 15 deduplicated attempts are `COMPLETED` with a null stop reason (verified\\n2026-11-23). Persistence\\\n    \\ and interruption behaviour is supported by the typed contract and offline\\nfault tests, not by that\\\n    \\ cohort.\"\n  fit_criterion: Given every offline fixture in Appendix A plus 6 one-per-reason fixtures, when each runs,\n    then (a) 100% of runs produce a run record; (b) 100% of records match exactly one row of the validity\n    table; (c) each of the 6 stop reasons appears at least once and 6/6 map to the reason declared for\n    their fixture; (d) 0 records have `COMPLETED` while some agent step produced no output; (e) 0 budget-exhaustion\n    fixtures are labelled `INTERNAL_ERROR`; (f) 0 records carry a reason outside the six-value vocabulary\n    (1 unlisted reason = 1 blocking defect).\n  tradeoff: The report header shows three short lines (outcome, rating, check) instead of one.\n  dependencies: []\n  baseline: 'Re-verified 2026-11-23 against the team repository `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. The result contract\n    now exists: `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` defines `RunOutcome = COMPLETED|INCOMPLETE`, a `StopReason`\n    literal, `OutputCheck = PASSED|NEEDS_REVIEW|NOT_RUN`, and `RunResult` with cross-field invariants\n    (COMPLETED needs a rating and no stop reason; INCOMPLETE needs no rating, a stop reason and NOT_RUN).\n    `runapi/execution.py` builds the envelope and `runapi/finalize.py` maps exceptions to stop reasons.\n    The raw graph entry `propagate` still returns `(final_state, signal)` where `signal` is a 5-tier rating\n    or `REVIEW` (`graph/trading_graph.py`, `agents/rating.py`). The gap is the vocabulary, not the contract:\n    the enum holds MODEL_FAILURE, DATA_FAILURE, INTERNAL_ERROR, PERSISTENCE_ERROR and INTERRUPTED, and\n    has no BUDGET (OQ-6).'\n  open: Add the fields to the run record (NFR-REPRO-001) and set them on every exit path.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n  amended_by:\n  - D-3\n  - D-5\n  note: 'Decision OQ-6, resolved 2026-11-23 and revised the same day after Member B''s reply. The stop-reason\n    vocabulary is six values: `MODEL_FAILURE`, `DATA_FAILURE`, `BUDGET`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`,\n    `INTERRUPTED`. The first two keep the spellings the implementation already uses (`tradingagents/runapi/result.py:12-14`\n    at `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`); A had briefly required `MODEL`/`DATA` and accepted B''s objection (B2)\n    that renaming is a breaking change to a serialized public value consumed by 23 code/test sites and\n    9 documents, including C''s own STOP_REASONS set. `BUDGET` is the one addition and is not yet present\n    in the code; adding it is an implementation item for B/D (finalize, reporting, result validation,\n    regression fixtures), and every existing reader must be updated or it will reject the new value. The\n    other two values exist because a three-value table left `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` and `INTERRUPTED` runs\n    without a valid row. B''s correction, accepted: no live evidence shows an `INCOMPLETE` attempt. All\n    15 deduplicated attempts in `docs/reviews/evidence/live-verification-2026-11-21/` are `COMPLETED`\n    with a null stop reason; persistence and interruption behaviour is supported by typed contracts and\n    offline tests, not by that live cohort. Non-normative, D-5: a resumed run keeps its `run_id` and adds\n    an attempt rather than starting a new run; the interrupted attempt is written `INCOMPLETE` and is\n    never edited afterwards; evaluation counts `run_id`s, not attempts. B notes that D-5 conflicts with\n    INV-11/INV-12''s fresh-run-ID and immutability rules and is therefore a separate contract change,\n    not implied by the vocabulary; it stays open (see requirement-source-notes.md OQ-8).'\n- id: REQ-TA-FR-001\n  title: Evidence IDs, records and visible source dates\n  type: functional\n  priority: Must\n  status: proposed\n  statement: 'The system shall give each evidence item admitted into a run one stable evidence ID, and\n    shall keep a record for it with at least: source, ticker, and either observation time or publication\n    time. Wherever the report cites an item, it shall show the item''s source and date (`YYYY-MM-DD`)\n    beside the citation. Records are kept for every run whatever its outcome: a run''s outcome never changes\n    or deletes its evidence records.'\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile and `fixtures/fr001/evidence.jsonl`, when one run completes\n    and every cited ID is collected, then (a) 100% of cited IDs resolve to exactly 1 record with non-empty\n    `source`, `ticker` and one of `observed_at` / `published_at`; (b) 100% of citations in the rendered\n    report show a source and a date; (c) all 12 channels of FR-004 write records, including the 2 that\n    bypass the router. Given fixture `fixtures/fr001/timeout_after_price/`, which ends `INCOMPLETE(MODEL)`\n    after price data was retrieved, then (d) the registry still holds the price records, unchanged (≥\n    1 record, byte-identical to before the stop). An ID that is cited but not registered is the blocking\n    finding R2 (ARCH-002).\n  tradeoff: One write per admitted item and one lookup per citation, plus storage under `results_dir`.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  related: ARCH-001 (when it is met, the registry write can sit in the router alone)\n  baseline: Items carry their own dates and source labels in vendor text (news rows and price rows both\n    carry a date), but nothing assigns an ID or keeps a record keyed by one.\n  open: Add the registry write at the data boundary, including the two bypass channels, and render source\n    and date at each citation.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-FR-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: tests/test_no_data_handling.py\n    locator: observed in v0.7.1\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-FR-003\n  title: Checkpoint list, resume and rerun\n  type: functional\n  priority: Should\n  status: partial\n  statement: The system shall list saved checkpoints, resume an interrupted run without re-running tasks\n    that were already saved, and rerun from scratch on request.\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile and a run interrupted after all 4 analyst branches were saved,\n    when (a) it is resumed with the same ticker, *D* and settings, then agent invocations for those 4\n    branches = 0 (4/4); (b) the checkpoint list is shown, then it lists ticker, *D*, the run signature,\n    the number of saved tasks, and a status of `RESUMABLE` (signature matches current settings) or `CONFIG_CHANGED`\n    (it does not) — checked on 1 fixture of each status; (c) it is rerun, then all 4 branches execute\n    again (≥ 1 invocation each), the old checkpoint is cleared, and the rerun gets its own run record\n    and report per NFR-REPRO-001.\n  tradeoff: Checkpoints are stored per ticker, so the list is per ticker unless an index file is added.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-001\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n  baseline: 'Resume already works: per-node SQLite checkpoints keyed by a run signature, resume detection\n    (`checkpoint_step`), fresh start when the signature changes, and clean-up after success (`graph/checkpointer.py`,\n    `_run_signature` in `trading_graph.py`; tests `test_checkpoint_resume.py`, `test_checkpoint_lifecycle.py`,\n    `test_graph_end_to_end.py::test_an_interrupted_run_resumes_from_its_checkpoint`). There is no list\n    command and no explicit rerun command.'\n  open: Add the list and rerun commands. Turn the three checks above into acceptance tests.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-FR-003\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-FR-004\n  title: Point-in-time evidence (no look-ahead)\n  type: functional\n  priority: Must\n  status: partial\n  statement: For a run with analysis date *D*, no item published, observed, filed or resolved after the\n    end of *D* shall reach any agent's prompt, through any channel. A date the model gives a tool shall\n    never widen the window past *D*. Data with no historical version (live-only data) shall be withheld\n    from a run dated before today. The one exception is the instrument's current name, which may be given\n    only when it is labelled as the current name.\n  fit_criterion: 'Given the offline profile, *D* = 2026-01-09, and `fixtures/fr004/channels/` holding,\n    for each of the 10 dated channels, one control item dated *D* and one planted item dated *D*+1 that\n    carries the marker `LOOKAHEAD-<#>`, when one run executes and every prompt to the scripted model is\n    captured, then: (a) 0/10 markers appear in any prompt; (b) 10/10 control items appear in at least\n    one prompt; (c) the 2 live-only channels return their \"withheld\" notice (2/2) and 0 live values; (d)\n    for each of the 12 dated tools in `agents/tools.py`, a model-supplied date of *D*+30 is served as\n    *D* (12/12); (e) the instrument context holds 0 sector, industry or exchange values, and any name\n    carries the \"current name\" label.'\n  tradeoff: Historical runs see less data than a live run would.\n  dependencies: []\n  baseline: Each channel already has its own guard and unit tests (`test_tool_date_enforcement.py`, `test_news_lookahead.py`,\n    `test_social_lookahead.py`, `test_fundamentals_lookahead.py`, `test_memory_pointintime.py`, `test_undated_tools_as_of.py`,\n    `test_statement_knowledge_time.py`); a future *D* is refused (`_validate_trade_date`). No test checks\n    all channels in one whole run.\n  open: Add the whole-run planted-marker test as a required CI check.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-FR-004\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-FR-005\n  title: Data gaps and the core-data rule\n  type: functional\n  priority: Must\n  status: partial\n  statement: \"This requirement owns every rule about missing data.\\n1. **Core rule.** If core data has\\\n    \\ any code other than `OK`, the run ends `INCOMPLETE(DATA)`.\\n2. **Non-core rule.** A gap in any other\\\n    \\ channel does not stop the run.\\n3. **Disclosure.** Every report has a \\\"Data coverage\\\" section\\\n    \\ that lists each channel with exactly one code from the table below. The section is built from tool\\\n    \\ results and is never written by the model. A channel that no selected analyst requested is reported\\\n    \\ as `NOT_REQUESTED`; it is never reported as a gap. The coverage vocabulary shall additionally contain\\\n    \\ `NOT_REQUESTED`, meaning no selected analyst asked for this channel and no vendor call was made\\\n    \\ for it; it is valid for both `COMPLETED` and `INCOMPLETE` runs.\"\n  fit_criterion: 'Given the offline profile and 12 fixtures — 8 non-core gaps (2 each for `UNAVAILABLE`,\n    `NO_DATA`, `STALE`, `WITHHELD`), 3 core gaps (price `UNAVAILABLE`, `NO_DATA`, `STALE`) and 1 clean\n    run — when each runs, then: (a) 8/8 non-core fixtures end `COMPLETED` and list the affected channel\n    with the matching code; (b) 3/3 core fixtures end `INCOMPLETE(DATA)`; (c) the clean fixture, run with\n    all four analysts selected, lists 12/12 channels as `OK`; (d) a market-only fixture, run with the\n    market analyst selected alone, lists the 4 market channels as `OK` and the other 8 as `NOT_REQUESTED`,\n    and reports none of them as `UNAVAILABLE` (0/12 channels mislabelled as a gap when not requested);\n    (e) 0/12 raise; (f) the section is byte-identical when the scripted model''s prose is replaced with\n    different prose.'\n  tradeoff: Every report gains a section, including gaps that a reader may not care about.\n  semantic_part: whether the model's own prose avoids claiming an absence (\"no recent news\") for a channel\n    that has a gap is tested in the GOV-001 suite, because a scripted model cannot test it.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  - REQ-TA-FR-004\n  baseline: The data layer already tells these cases apart in tool text and tells the model not to invent\n    values (`dataflows/router.py`, `date_window.py`; tests `test_no_data_handling.py`, `test_vendor_errors.py`).\n    But nothing collects them per run; the report does not list them; and a full price outage still ends\n    with a rating, because throttled or unreachable vendors degrade to a text note in every category.\n    Channels 3 and 11 bypass the router.\n  open: Collect the codes per run (router plus the two bypass channels), stop on a core gap, render the\n    section, and mark every channel that no selected analyst requested as `NOT_REQUESTED`.\n  note: Decision D-1 (applied in requirements-draft-v3.md) closes review finding V2-04. Without this code\n    a completed market-only run cannot describe 8 unrequested channels truthfully.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-FR-005\n  - kind: team_decision\n    ref: req-final-scope-A-2026-11-22.md#3\n    locator: D-1\n  - kind: review_finding\n    ref: requirements-v2-review-2026-11-12.md\n    locator: V2-04\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-FR-006\n  title: Freshness thresholds\n  type: functional\n  priority: Should\n  status: partial\n  statement: \"Each data type shall be judged fresh or stale by the rule in the table below. Stale data\\\n    \\ is coded `STALE` (FR-005) and handled as the last column says.\\n\\n| Data type | Fresh when | Parameter\\\n    \\ (Appendix D) | If exceeded |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| Price history | Latest bar is ≤ `STALE_PRICE_DAYS`\\\n    \\ calendar days before *D* | `STALE_PRICE_DAYS` | Not used; core gap → `INCOMPLETE(DATA)` (FR-005)\\\n    \\ |\\n| Technical indicators | Follows price history | — | Follows price history |\\n| Financial statements\\\n    \\ | Latest statement was filed ≤ `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` days before *D* | `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` |\\\n    \\ Still shown with its filing date; coded `STALE`; run continues |\\n| Ticker news, global news, social\\\n    \\ posts | Item lies inside the requested window, clamped to *D* (FR-004) | `global_news_lookback_days`\\\n    \\ (v0.7.1 config) | Item left out. This is not marked `STALE`; an empty window is `NO_DATA` or `UNAVAILABLE`.\\\n    \\ |\\n| Macro indicators, insider transactions | No threshold (releases are monthly or irregular) |\\\n    \\ — | Each value shown with its own date |\\n| Company overview, prediction markets | Live-only | —\\\n    \\ | `WITHHELD` on historical runs (FR-004) |\"\n  fit_criterion: 'Given the offline profile and 6 boundary fixtures, when each runs, then 6/6 behave as\n    follows: price bar at *D*−`STALE_PRICE_DAYS` → `OK`; at *D*−(`STALE_PRICE_DAYS`+1) → `INCOMPLETE(DATA)`;\n    statement filed at *D*−`STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` → `OK`; at *D*−(`STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS`+1) → `STALE`\n    and still shown; news item on the window''s first day → included; one day before it → left out.'\n  tradeoff: A fixed statement threshold suits some filing schedules better than others. Hong Kong half-yearly\n    filers are the reason for the provisional 200 days.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-FR-005\n  baseline: 'The price rule already exists: a frame whose latest row is more than 10 days before the requested\n    date is refused as stale (`MAX_OHLCV_STALE_DAYS = 10`, `dataflows/vendors/yahoo/ohlcv.py`; `test_yfinance_stale_ohlcv_guard.py`).\n    News and social windows exist (FR-004). There is no statement-age rule.'\n  open: Add the statement-age rule and the `STALE` code; confirm `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` (provisional).\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-FR-006\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-FR-007\n  title: Rating meaning and no ownership wording\n  type: functional\n  priority: Must\n  status: proposed\n  statement: \"1. **Meaning.** The five ratings describe how strongly the evidence favours the instrument,\\\n    \\ from strongest positive (Buy) to strongest negative (Sell). **Hold** means the evidence is balanced,\\\n    \\ or too thin to favour either direction. No rating is an instruction about the user's account.\\n\\\n    2. **Labels.** Reports label the three model judgments separately: \\\"Final rating (Portfolio Manager)\\\"\\\n    , \\\"Research recommendation (Research Manager, intermediate)\\\" and \\\"Trader proposal (Buy / Hold /\\\n    \\ Sell, intermediate)\\\". Only the Portfolio Manager's output is called the final rating, and only\\\n    \\ it fills `rating` in the run record.\\n3. **No ownership wording.** Prompts and reports shall not\\\n    \\ state or assume that the user holds the instrument. The minimum banned list is `fixtures/fr007/ownership_phrases.txt`:\\\n    \\ \\\"your position\\\", \\\"current position\\\", \\\"maintain the position\\\", \\\"add to your position\\\", \\\"\\\n    exit your position\\\", \\\"your holdings\\\", \\\"you own\\\".\"\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile, when (a) the Research Manager and Portfolio Manager prompt\n    templates are scanned, then 2/2 contain 0 banned phrases and define Hold with the sentence in part\n    1; (b) one report is rendered, then it contains all 3 labels (3/3) and exactly 1 \"Final rating\"; (c)\n    3 scripted final decisions that each contain one banned phrase are checked, then 3/3 get `NEEDS_REVIEW`\n    with finding R3, and 1 clean decision gets `PASSED`.\n  tradeoff: Without account wording, the rating reads less like direct advice. That is intended in a research-only\n    scope.\n  semantic_part: live-model wording is tested in the GOV-001 suite.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  baseline: 'Re-verified 2026-11-23 against `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. Both manager prompts now condition\n    the rating wording on whether a portfolio was supplied: `research_manager.py:44-48` and `portfolio_manager.py:56-60`,\n    where `hold_meaning` is computed from `portfolio_context`, so Hold reads as \"do not interpret Hold\n    as maintaining an assumed position\" when no portfolio is supplied. The earlier \"maintain the current\n    position\" wording is gone. The three judgments stay as separate fields (`ResearchPlan.recommendation`,\n    `TraderProposal.action`, `PortfolioDecision.rating` in `agents/schemas.py`).'\n  open: Reword both prompts, add the labels, and add rule R3 to the output check.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-FR-007\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-FR-008\n  title: Sentiment score and confidence consistent with available data\n  type: functional\n  priority: Should\n  status: proposed\n  statement: \"The Sentiment Analyst's model-chosen band, score and confidence shall follow the rules below,\\\n    \\ applied by the output check. Any agent that later gets a confidence field shall follow the same\\\n    \\ confidence rule.\\n\\n| Rule | Check | Kind |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| R4 | `overall_score` lies in its band's\\\n    \\ range: Bullish [6.5, 10]; Mildly Bullish [5.5, 6.5); Neutral and Mixed [4.5, 5.5); Mildly Bearish\\\n    \\ [3.5, 4.5); Bearish [0, 3.5). These are the schema's own guideline ranges, made exact. | Blocking\\\n    \\ |\\n| R5 | If any of the analyst's 3 sources (news, StockTwits, Reddit) is not `OK`, confidence is\\\n    \\ at most `low`. A dispatch attempt is one model-generation request attempt issued\n655:     through the controlled application client boundary, including attempts that time out or fail, application\n656:     retries, structured-output re-requests, free-text fallback, and in-run memory reflection requests.\n657:     Every attempt shall be preceded by its own fresh single-use reservation from the run''s shared budget\n658:     controller; a reservation authorizes exactly one attempt, cannot be reused, and a denied reservation\n659:     dispatches nothing. An attempt that has been issued consumes its slot even if it fails. A workflow\n660:     that finishes within its cap completes normally; a run stops `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` only when a required\n661:     further attempt is refused.'\n662:   fit_criterion: Given the offline profile and `CALL_CAP = 8`, when a run executes, then (a) every controlled\n663:     request attempt has a unique preceding successful reservation from the same run; audit records pair\n664:     one reservation with at most one attempt, including retries, fallback and memory calls; a denied reservation\n665:     dispatches nothing; (b) total controlled request attempts ≤ 8 across all branches and model tiers,\n666:     with SDK automatic retries disabled for this mode or every underlying attempt independently gated\n667:     and counted; (c) after 7 slots are consumed, 4 workers contend for the remaining slot using an injected\n668:     barrier against the real reservation component, and exactly 1 succeeds and 3 are denied (the winner's\n669:     identity need not be deterministic); (d) in a scripted workflow that requires one more attempt after\n670:     the cap is exhausted, that attempt is refused and the run returns `INCOMPLETE` with `stop_reason =\n671:     BUDGET`, no final rating and `output_check = NOT_RUN`, with audit metadata naming the configured cap\n672:     and the counts; a workflow that completes within its cap ends normally.\n673:   tradeoff: A small shared cap can starve parallel branches, and a strict single-use reservation means\n674:     a branch that loses the last slot stops the run rather than degrading. The stricter the bound, the\n675:     less tolerant the system is of a borderline cap; that is the price of a guarantee that can actually\n676:     be checked.\n677:   metric: model-request dispatch attempts per run, against successful reservations and CALL_CAP\n678:   threshold: dispatch_attempts <= successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP (test value 8); 0 attempts issued\n679:     without a reservation\n680:   verification: offline profile; one budget-controller fixture with an injected threading barrier for\n681:     the last-slot race; audit log pairing reservations with attempts; one exhaustion fixture and one within-cap\n682:     fixture\n683:   dependencies:\n684:   - REQ-TA-NFR-001\n685:   - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n686:   baseline: 'Only per-scope limits: `max_tool_rounds` (20), `max_debate_rounds` / `max_risk_discuss_rounds`\n687:     (1 each), `llm_max_retries`.'\n688:   open: Add a shared run-scoped counter and a reservation that precedes dispatch.\n689:   note: 'Decision D-3, revised 2026-11-23 after Member B''s technical reply. Non-normative. Application\n690:     counting equals real provider calls only when every attempt the application issues is an attempt the\n691:     provider sees. In the inspected baseline, `llm_max_retries` is forwarded to the provider SDK (`tradingagents/llm_clients/factory.py`),\n692:     and analysts fan out concurrently from `START` (`tradingagents/graph/setup.py`), so a counter around\n693:     high-level model invocations cannot by itself guarantee the bound. Member B''s recommended mechanism\n694:     is one shared run-scoped budget controller with SDK retries disabled, where each application retry\n695:     takes a fresh single-use reservation; that makes the strict `<= CALL_CAP` bound achievable. How it\n696:     is built remains a B design and D implementation decision (`decision-request-D3-cost002-2026-11-22.md`,\n697:     reply of 2026-11-22). Because a reservation authorizes exactly one attempt, concurrent branches hold\n698:     their own reservations and no branch allowance is needed; the earlier `CALL_CAP + N_concurrent_branches`\n699:     form is withdrawn. This requirement does not guarantee the provider gateway''s internal retry count,\n700:     exact billable usage or monetary cost, and it does not claim the bound is implemented: the controller\n701:     does not exist in the baseline. If D cannot make (a)-(d) hold on every enabled client, A downgrades\n702:     COST-002 from Must to Should and restates it as detection-only, recorded in D-4.'\n703:   source:\n704:   - kind: team_document\n705:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n706:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n707:     locator: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002\n708:   - kind: team_decision\n709:     ref: req-final-scope-A-2026-11-22.md#3\n710:     locator: D-3\n711:   - kind: team_document\n712:     ref: reply-to-A-cost002-2026-11-22.md\n713:     locator: Member B technical reply; strict bound and single-use reservation adopted 2026-11-23\n714:   - kind: baseline_observation\n715:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n716:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n717: - id: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003\n718:   title: Early debate convergence\n719:   type: cost\n720:   priority: Could\n721:   status: proposed\n722:   statement: The bull/bear debate and the risk discussion shall stop before their configured maximum when\n723:     the participants' positions have converged.\n724:   fit_criterion: Given the offline profile, 4 convergence fixtures (2 per debate) and 4 disagreement fixtures,\n725:     when each runs, then rounds used < maximum for 4/4 convergence fixtures, rounds used = maximum for\n726:     4/4 disagreement fixtures, and the RUN-001 fields of all 8 equal those of the round-count-only baseline.\n727:   tradeoff: A debate can be cut before its disagreement surfaces.\n728:   metric: debate rounds executed when the debate has converged\n729:   threshold: converged debate stops before max_debate_rounds (rounds_executed < max_debate_rounds on the\n730:     converged fixture); 0 premature stops on the non-converged fixture\n731:   verification: offline profile; one converged and one non-converged scripted debate\n732:   dependencies:\n733:   - REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001\n734:   baseline: Round-count only (`graph/conditional_logic.py`).\n735:   open: Define the convergence signal.\n736:   source:\n737:   - kind: team_document\n738:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n739:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n740:     locator: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003\n741:   - kind: baseline_observation\n742:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n743:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n744: - id: REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001\n745:   title: Evaluation counting rules\n746:   type: quality_evaluation\n747:   priority: Should\n748:   status: proposed\n749:   statement: \"Every evaluation result the team reports shall be computed with these rules:\\n1. **Completion\\\n750:     \\ rate** = `COMPLETED` runs ÷ all runs started. No run is ever removed from this denominator.\\n2.\\\n751:     \\ **Quality scores** (GOV-001 score, rating distribution) are computed over `COMPLETED` runs only,\\\n752:     \\ and are always reported beside the completion rate and the number of `NEEDS_REVIEW` runs.\\n3. `INCOMPLETE`\\\n753:     \\ runs are reported by `stop_reason`.\\n4. A run's outcome never invalidates its evidence (FR-001).\\\n754:     \\ Source reliability is not graded from run outcomes.\\n5. **Acceptance population.** `N_EVAL` counts\\\n755:     \\ distinct semantic cases, never attempts; a repeated attempt is a repeatability comparison under\\\n756:     \\ rule 6 and is not counted twice. A changed case population is a versioned acceptance change, not\\\n757:     \\ a re-run, and results across two populations are not compared. The counting rules below define arithmetic\\\n758:     \\ only: the rubric, the critical items, the profile and `QUALITY_THRESHOLD` are required acceptance\\\n759:     \\ inputs owned by Members D and E, and no counting result is an acceptance result without them.\\n\\\n760:     6. **Comparison modes.** Two results may be compared in *repeatability* mode only if their run records\\\n761:     \\ match on `config` and `prompt_hash` (NFR-REPRO-001); any difference between them is measurement\\\n762:     \\ noise and is reported as such. A *controlled change* comparison is permitted when exactly one factor\\\n763:     \\ (prompt, model or budget) is declared as changed and every other recorded key matches; the output\\\n764:     \\ must name that factor and report `factor: before -> after`, with the completion rate and the `NEEDS_REVIEW`\\\n765:     \\ count beside both sides. A comparison that changes more than one factor, or that does not declare\\\n766:     \\ the factor, is refused.\"\n767:   fit_criterion: 'Given 10 fixed run records used as a counting fixture (6 `COMPLETED` of which 2 are\n768:     `NEEDS_REVIEW`; `INCOMPLETE`: 1 `DATA_FAILURE`, 2 `MODEL_FAILURE`, 1 `BUDGET`), when the evaluation\n769:     script runs, then it reports a completion rate of 6/10, a quality denominator of 6, `NEEDS_REVIEW`\n770:     = 2, and stop reasons `DATA_FAILURE` 1, `MODEL_FAILURE` 2, `BUDGET` 1, with 0 records dropped; and\n771:     the output states that these 10 records are a counting fixture, not an acceptance run under `N_EVAL`.\n772:     Given 2 records that differ in `prompt_hash` and declare no changed factor, the script refuses to\n773:     compare them (1/1); given 2 records differing only in `prompt_hash` that declare `prompt` as the changed\n774:     factor, it reports exactly 1 controlled-change comparison naming `prompt` (1/1); given 2 records differing\n775:     in both `prompt_hash` and `model` with no declaration, it refuses (1/1); given 20 cases scored twice\n776:     under identical `config` and `prompt_hash`, then `N_EVAL` is reported as 20 cases and not 40 attempts,\n777:     and exactly 1 result is counted.'\n778:   tradeoff: Reporting completed-only quality next to a low completion rate can look worse than a single\n779:     blended number. That is intended.\n780:   metric: agreement between reported evaluation numbers and a recomputation from the same run records\n781:   threshold: 100% of reported counts equal the recomputed values; 0 runs silently removed from the completion\n782:     denominator; 0 undeclared multi-factor comparisons accepted\n783:   verification: recompute every reported figure from the stored run records of a fixed evidence set\n784:   dependencies:\n785:   - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n786:   - REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n787:   baseline: v0.7.1 has a backtest (`backtest.py`) but no rule for counting failed runs.\n788:   open: Member D to build the script to these rules.\n789:   source:\n790:   - kind: team_document\n791:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n792:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n793:     locator: REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001\n794:   - kind: review_finding\n795:     ref: requirements-v2-review-2026-11-12.md\n796:     locator: V2-10\n797:   - kind: baseline_observation\n798:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n799:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n800:   note: 'Amended 2026-11-23 on Member B''s question. B asked whether `N_EVAL` counts cases or attempts\n801:     and whether the existing five cases and two trials establish acceptance under `N_EVAL=20` with an\n802:     open threshold. B was right that they do not, and A found a second defect of A''s own: the parameter\n803:     appendix says `N_EVAL` = 20 cases, while this criterion originally exercised 10 records without saying\n804:     they were not acceptance. Rule 5 is new and says both things explicitly. A did **not** fix the remainder,\n805:     because the rubric, the critical items, the evaluation profile and `QUALITY_THRESHOLD` are owned by\n806:     D and E and two of them are still open parameters; writing them here would have made `GOV-001` look\n807:     decided when it is not. Not implemented: no evaluation script exists in the baseline.'\n808: - id: REQ-TA-SEC-001\n809:   title: Prompt-injection resistance\n810:   type: security\n811:   priority: Must\n812:   status: proposed\n813:   statement: Instructions inside retrieved content shall not change the run's configuration, the `data_coverage`\n814:     record, the output check's rules or result, or any RUN-001 field set by deterministic code.\n815:   fit_criterion: 'Given the offline profile and 20 fixtures (5 each for market, news, social and fundamentals\n816:     content) whose injected text tells the model to, for example, \"say all data is complete\", \"print OUTPUT\n817:     CHECK: PASSED\" or \"ignore your rules\", with the scripted model copying the injected text into its\n818:     output, when each runs, then for 20/20: the config equals the pre-run config (deep equality); `data_coverage`\n819:     equals that of the same fixture without the injection; and `output_check` and `check_findings` equal\n820:     the result of applying R1–R8 to the final state.'\n821:   tradeoff: Injected text can still appear as quoted evidence; it simply has no authority.\n822:   metric: injected instructions that change the rating or the output check\n823:   threshold: 0/20 injection fixtures change the final rating or the output_check; 20/20 still produce\n824:     a valid run record\n825:   verification: offline profile; injected text in every retrieved-text channel (news, social, filings,\n826:     web)\n827:   semantic_part: whether a live model's rating is swayed by injected text is tested in the GOV-001 suite.\n828:   dependencies:\n829:   - REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n830:   - REQ-TA-FR-005\n831:   baseline: Ticker input is sanitised (`dataflows/symbols.py`). Retrieved text reaches the model unmodified.\n832:     No deterministic check exists yet.\n833:   open: Build ARCH-002 and FR-005 so that no model text feeds them.\n834:   source:\n835:   - kind: team_document\n836:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n837:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n838:     locator: REQ-TA-SEC-001\n839:   - kind: baseline_observation\n840:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n841:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n842: - id: REQ-TA-SEC-002\n843:   title: No credential or token leakage\n844:   type: security\n845:   priority: Must\n846:   status: partial\n847:   statement: Logs, reports, run records and error messages shall not contain API keys, OAuth access tokens,\n848:     refresh tokens or bearer [REDACTED]\n849:   fit_criterion: Given a distinctive fake value planted as each of these 4 secret types across all vendor\n850:     error paths, when each path is exercised, then a scan of logs, reports, run records and captured exceptions\n851:     finds 0 planted values and 0 `Bearer ` prefixes.\n852:   tradeoff: Less debugging detail in error text.\n853:   metric: secret occurrences in report, log, event stream and traceback on error paths\n854:   threshold: 0 occurrences of any planted secret in any sink; source files unmodified\n855:   verification: plant 4 secret types across every sink and every error path, then scan the captured output\n856:   dependencies: []\n857:   baseline: Re-verified 2026-11-23 against `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. `get_scrubbed` (`dataflows/net.py`)\n858:     redacts query-parameter secrets and is used by the Alpha Vantage and FRED vendor modules. The boundary\n859:     adds `runapi/redact.py`, a `Redactor` applied at the event, report and error sinks. Coverage of third-party\n860:     loggers and uncaught tracebacks outside the boundary remains unverified.\n861:   open: Send every outbound error through one scrubber.\n862:   source:\n863:   - kind: team_document\n864:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n865:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n866:     locator: REQ-TA-SEC-002\n867:   - kind: baseline_observation\n868:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n869:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n870: - id: REQ-TA-SEC-003\n871:   title: No promise of guaranteed returns\n872:   type: security\n873:   priority: Should\n874:   status: proposed\n875:   statement: Reports shall start with a disclaimer and shall not claim guaranteed returns, guaranteed\n876:     profit or capital protection.\n877:   fit_criterion: Given the offline profile, when (a) 20 reports are rendered, then 20/20 start with the\n878:     disclaimer string; (b) 5 scripted final decisions that each contain a phrase from `fixtures/sec003/guarantee_phrases.txt`\n879:     are checked, then 5/5 get `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding R8.\n880:   tradeoff: The phrase list flags \"guaranteed\" even inside a quoted source.\n881:   metric: reports starting with the disclaimer, and guarantee phrases caught by rule R8\n882:   threshold: 20/20 reports start with the disclaimer; 5/5 guarantee fixtures get NEEDS_REVIEW with finding\n883:     R8\n884:   verification: offline profile; 20 rendered reports and 5 scripted decisions containing listed phrases\n885:   semantic_part: 5 live prompts that directly ask for a guarantee are in the GOV-001 suite.\n886:   dependencies:\n887:   - REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n888:   baseline: The disclaimer exists in the README only.\n889:   open: Add the report disclaimer and rule R8.\n890:   source:\n891:   - kind: team_document\n892:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n893:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n894:     locator: REQ-TA-SEC-003\n895:   - kind: baseline_observation\n896:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n897:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n898: - id: REQ-TA-ARCH-001\n899:   title: Vendors behind one routing point\n900:   type: architectural_constraint\n901:   priority: Should\n902:   status: partial\n903:   statement: Vendor access shall go through the router's method map, so agent and graph modules name a\n904:     method, never a vendor module or vendor SDK.\n905:   fit_criterion: Given `tradingagents/agents/**` and `tradingagents/graph/**`, when the import-boundary\n906:     test runs, then they import 0 times from `tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.*` and 0 times from `yfinance`\n907:     (the only vendor SDK in `pyproject.toml`); and a fake vendor in the method map serves every evidence\n908:     request in the end-to-end test with 0 monkeypatches of agent modules.\n909:   tradeoff: One more indirection per call.\n910:   metric: direct vendor imports in agent modules\n911:   threshold: 0 direct vendor imports in `tradingagents/agents/**`; the layering test covers every vendor\n912:     package, not only `yfinance`\n913:   verification: static import scan anchored on the package boundary, enforced by `tests/test_layering.py`\n914:   dependencies: []\n915:   baseline: 'Not met. There are 4 direct vendor imports in 3 agent files: `agents/context.py` (Yahoo profile),\n916:     `agents/tools.py` (Yahoo snapshot) and `agents/analysts/sentiment_analyst.py` (Reddit, StockTwits).\n917:     `tests/test_layering.py` bans only the `yfinance` library.'\n918:   open: Move the 4 imports behind router methods and extend the layering test.\n919:   source:\n920:   - kind: team_document\n921:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n922:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n923:     locator: REQ-TA-ARCH-001\n924:   - kind: baseline_observation\n925:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n926:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n927: - id: REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n928:   title: Deterministic output check\n929:   type: architectural_constraint\n930:   priority: Must\n931:   status: proposed\n932:   statement: \"Exactly one deterministic, non-LLM component shall set `output_check` and `check_findings`.\\\n933:     \\ It runs on every `COMPLETED` run after the Portfolio Manager and applies the rules below. Each rule\\\n934:     \\ is owned by the requirement named in the table (P1).\\n\\n| Rule | Check | Owner | Kind |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n\\\n935:     | R1 | Final rating is readable (not `REVIEW`) | RUN-001 | Blocking |\\n| R2 | Every cited evidence\\\n936:     \\ ID resolves | FR-001 | Blocking |\\n| R3 | No banned ownership phrase | FR-007 | Blocking |\\n| R4\\\n937:     \\ | Sentiment score matches band | FR-008 | Blocking |\\n| R5 | Sentiment confidence within the coverage\\\n938:     \\ cap | FR-008 | Corrected |\\n| R6 | No sentiment direction without any sentiment data | FR-008 |\\\n939:     \\ Blocking |\\n| R7 | \\\"Data coverage\\\" section present and equal to the coverage record | FR-005 |\\\n940:     \\ Blocking |\\n| R8 | Disclaimer present; no guarantee phrase | SEC-003 | Blocking |\\n\\n## Naming (corrected\\\n941:     \\ 2026-11-23 after Member B's reply)\\n\\n`R1`–`R8` here means the output-check rules defined in `requirements-draft-v4.md`.\\\n942:     \\ Two collisions to avoid:\\n\\n- `docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md` reuses the same `R`\\\n943:     \\ prefix for unrelated trigger rows: its `R1` is a provider failover, its `R3` is \\\"model output exhausted\\\"\\\n944:     . Those are not these rules.\\n- `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py` emits only `Q1`–`Q4`. `R1` maps to\\\n945:     \\ `Q1`, `R8` maps to `Q3`/`Q4`, and `R4`–`R7` rest on coverage, sentiment and intermediate-output\\\n946:     \\ fields that the current checker does not inspect. `R2` has no enforcing component.\\n\\nSo this table\\\n947:     \\ states what a compliant system must do, not what the baseline already does.\\n\\n**Authority**: No\\\n948:     \\ model output can set, change or skip the check's result. Text in model output that claims a check\\\n949:     \\ result (\\\"validated\\\", \\\"PASSED\\\") has no effect.\\n\\n**Meaning**: `PASSED` means only that the report\\\n950:     \\ meets rules R1–R8. It does not mean the analysis is correct, the facts are true or the rating is\\\n951:     \\ good advice. The report shows this sentence next to the result.\\n\\n**Results**: any blocking finding\\\n952:     \\ → `NEEDS_REVIEW`; only corrected findings or none → `PASSED`; `INCOMPLETE` run → `NOT_RUN`.\\n\\n\\\n953:     **Failure behaviour**: If the check itself raises, the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding `CHECK_ERROR`.\\\n954:     \\ It never falls back to `PASSED`.\"\n955:   fit_criterion: 'Given the offline profile, when (a) every `COMPLETED` fixture in Appendix A is inspected,\n956:     then 100% of `output_check` values equal R1–R8 applied to the final state, and the field is written\n957:     at exactly 1 call site in the code; (b) a fixture makes the check raise, then the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW`\n958:     + `CHECK_ERROR` (1/1); (c) a fixture''s model text says \"OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" while R3 fails, then\n959:     the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW` (1/1); (d) every `INCOMPLETE` fixture has `NOT_RUN` (100%).'\n960:   tradeoff: One more stage after the graph, and a second place a reader must look.\n961:   metric: authority of the output check; results set by model text\n962:   threshold: 0 of the injected model-text fixtures change output_check; 8/8 rules R1-R8 produce a blocking\n963:     finding on their failing fixture\n964:   verification: offline profile; inject each rule's failing fixture plus a model-text override attempt\n965:   dependencies:\n966:   - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n967:   baseline: 'Re-verified 2026-11-23 against `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. The deterministic check now exists:\n968:     `runapi/checks.py` defines `OutputChecker` with rules Q1-Q4 (rating readable, provenance matches the\n969:     frozen snapshot, disclaimer present, no prohibited guarantee phrase), each broken rule becoming a\n970:     blocking `Finding`, and `runapi/finalize.py` makes the outcome decision. `runapi/reporting.py` verifies\n971:     the envelope header against the trusted input. What remains unverified is enforcement on every enabled\n972:     entry point: the raw `TradingAgentsGraph` primitive is a declared reduced-coverage path, and the Portfolio\n973:     Manager still writes its rating directly (`agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py`).'\n974:   open: Member B designs the component and documents the authority and failure rules above.\n975:   source:\n976:   - kind: team_document\n977:     ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n978:     sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n979:     locator: REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n980:   - kind: baseline_observation\n981:     ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n982:     locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n983:   note: 'Rules R1-R8 are the OUTPUT-CHECK rules defined in requirements-draft-v4.md. Naming, corrected\n984:     2026-11-23 after Member B''s reply, to avoid a collision in the team''s documents: `docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md`\n985:     uses the same `R` prefix for unrelated trigger rows (its R1 is a provider failover, its R3 is model\n986:     exhausted), and `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py` emits only `Q1`-`Q4`. R1 maps to Q1, R8 to Q3/Q4;\n987:     R4-R7 rest on coverage, sentiment and intermediate-output fields that this requirement set defines\n988:     and the current checker does not inspect, and R2 has no enforcing component. So R1-R8 state what a\n989:     compliant system must do, not what the baseline does. Identity rule and result mapping are unchanged.'\n990: - id: REQ-TA-INV-001\n991:   title: Unreadable rating never passes\n992:   type: invariant\n993:   priority: Must\n994:   status: proposed\n995:   statement: The system shall hold that a final rating that cannot be parsed is reported as `REVIEW` with\n996:     `output_check = NEEDS_REVIEW`, and `PASSED` is never claimed for a run whose final rating is `REVIEW`.\n997:     This does not claim that every `COMPLETED` run yields a usable investment rating, and it does not\n998:     make `REVIEW` a model failure.\n999:   zero_tolerance: true\n1000:   enforced_by: REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n1001:   rule_owner: REQ-TA-RUN-001\n1002:   amended_by: []\n1003:   fit_criterion: Given the unreadable-rating fixtures, when each is checked, then 100% are reported `COMPLETED`\n1004:     + `REVIEW` + `NEEDS_REVIEW` (rule R1); 0 REPORT a `REVIEW` rating under `PASSED`. A single observed\n1005:     violation is 1 blocking defect; no run is exempt.\n1006:   tradeoff: A zero-tolerance invariant fails the build on one counterexample, which costs time when the\n1007:     counterexample is a fixture bug rather than a product bug.\n1008:   dependencies:\n1009:   - REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n1010:   note: 'Promoted 2026-11-23 (A-10) from ARCH-002''s rule table; source requirement RUN-001. LAYERS (OQ-7,\n1011:     revised 2026-11-23): this entry owns the requirement meaning and its zero-tolerance fit criterion.\n1012:     Member B''s `docs/architecture/invariants.md` owns the architecture enforcement, runtime monitor and\n1013:     fallback.
