There is no run-level catch, so a model\n    call that fails after retries raises out of `propagate`.\n  open: Catch at the graph entry and map to `INCOMPLETE(MODEL)`.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-002\n  title: Add or remove an analyst\n  type: quality_maintainability\n  priority: Could\n  status: partial\n  statement: Adding or removing an analyst shall require changes only to that analyst's module and its\n    registration data, and to no orchestration module.\n  fit_criterion: Given a change that adds 1 analyst, when `git diff --stat` is taken against `{tradingagents/graph/setup.py,\n    tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py, tradingagents/graph/conditional_logic.py}`, then changed lines\n    in that set = 0 and the full test suite passes.\n  tradeoff: Wiring is less readable at the point of use.\n  metric: changed lines in the orchestration module set when one analyst is added\n  threshold: changed lines in {graph/setup.py, graph/trading_graph.py, graph/conditional_logic.py} = 0;\n    full test suite passes\n  verification: apply one add-analyst change and take `git diff --stat` against that file set\n  dependencies: []\n  baseline: Removing works (`selected_analysts` → `build_analyst_execution_plan`, `graph/analyst_execution.py`).\n    Adding needs an edit to the hard-coded `analyst_factories` in `graph/setup.py`.\n  open: Move factories into the registration data.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-002\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-OBS-001\n  title: Structured logging\n  type: quality_observability\n  priority: Should\n  status: partial\n  statement: The system shall write machine-parseable log records, each with `run_id`, ticker, node or\n    agent, timestamp, elapsed time, and event outcome. When a run stops for `BUDGET`, the log names the\n    limit that was hit (time, tokens or calls).\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile, when every line of both sinks is parsed after one completed\n    run and after one `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` run, then 100% of lines parse and contain all six fields with\n    non-null values; the `BUDGET` run's log names exactly 1 limit.\n  tradeoff: JSON lines are harder to skim by eye.\n  metric: required log fields present per run, and events emitted on every exit path\n  threshold: 100% of runs emit each required event; 0 runs with a missing required field; 0 secrets in\n    any log line\n  verification: offline profile; parse the event stream of every fixture run, including failure and cancellation\n    fixtures\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-SEC-002\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n  baseline: 'Re-verified 2026-11-23 against `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. The boundary now emits structured\n    events: `runapi/events.py` provides an `EventSink` writing event records (for example `input.consent`,\n    `output.check`, `run.terminal`) alongside each run. The graph still writes one JSON state file per\n    run (`_log_state`, `full_states_log_<D>.json`), and the CLI writes the plain-text `message_tool.log`\n    (`cli/run.py`).'\n  open: JSON-lines for the CLI sink; add `run_id` and elapsed time to both.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-OBS-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n  title: Immutable run record and report\n  type: quality_reproducibility\n  priority: Should\n  status: partial\n  statement: 'Every run, including each rerun, shall write exactly one run record and one report folder,\n    both named by a unique `run_id`. The record contains: start and end time, code version, every configuration\n    key that can change what the run produces, a hash of the prompt templates, and the RUN-001 fields.\n    A later run shall never overwrite or change an earlier run''s record or report.'\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile, when (a) two runs of the same ticker and *D* execute one after\n    the other, then 2 distinct records and 2 distinct report folders exist, and the first run's files\n    are byte-identical before and after the second; (b) each record has non-null `run_id`, `started_at`,\n    `ended_at`, `version`, `prompt_hash`, `config` and the RUN-001 fields; (c) for each of the 10 keys\n    v0.7.1 leaves out of `run_settings()` (`temperature`, `max_tokens`, `max_tool_rounds`, `news_article_limit`,\n    `global_news_article_limit`, `global_news_lookback_days`, `holding_period_days`, `google_thinking_level`,\n    `openai_reasoning_effort`, `anthropic_effort`), changing only that key makes the two records differ\n    in exactly that key (10/10); (d) recorded keys = `DEFAULT_CONFIG` keys minus the excluded set (0 missing,\n    0 extra); (e) editing one prompt template changes `prompt_hash`, and leaving templates unchanged keeps\n    it the same; (f) the SEC-002 scan finds 0 planted secrets.\n  tradeoff: '`results_dir` grows faster; no automatic clean-up is proposed.'\n  metric: run-record fields recorded per run; determinism of the record after publication\n  threshold: 100% of runs have a run record with every listed field non-empty (or explicitly null); 0\n    runs whose record changes after publication\n  verification: offline profile; hash each run record immediately after publication and again after the\n    next run\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  - REQ-TA-SEC-002\n  baseline: 'Re-verified 2026-11-23 against `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. The run boundary now records reproducibility\n    facts in the run manifest: `run_id`, `code_version`, `source_revision`, `prompt_hash`, `effective_config`,\n    `start_ts_utc`/`end_ts_utc` and `fingerprint_sha256` (`runapi/execution.py` `_source_revision`/`_prompt_hash`,\n    `runapi/reporting.py`; see a real manifest under `docs/reviews/evidence/live-verification-2026-11-21/`).\n    The graph-level `run_settings()` (`graph/trading_graph.py`) remains an allowlist with no run id, timing\n    or prompt hash, and the state log is still named `full_states_log_<D>.json`. The baseline closes this\n    requirement at the `runapi` boundary, not in the raw graph path.'\n  open: Widen the record, add run id, timing and prompt hash, and name files by run id.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-001\n  title: Maximum run time\n  type: performance\n  priority: Should\n  status: proposed\n  statement: A single-ticker run shall complete within `RUN_TIME_CAP`, measured wall-clock from graph\n    start to the run record being written.\n  fit_criterion: Given the live profile, when 20 runs execute one after another, then the maximum of the\n    20 run times is ≤ `RUN_TIME_CAP` and 20/20 are `COMPLETED`. Runs stopped as `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` count\n    as failures of this criterion.\n  tradeoff: A tight cap trades completeness for speed.\n  metric: wall-clock time from run start to terminal event\n  threshold: <= RUN_TIME_CAP (provisional 120 s) on the offline profile\n  verification: offline profile; scripted model with recorded latencies; time the run boundary, not the\n    graph alone\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-001\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n  baseline: No cap. Analysts already run in parallel (`graph/setup.py`).\n  open: Measure first, then fix `RUN_TIME_CAP` from the measurement.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002\n  title: Time-budget handling\n  type: performance\n  priority: Should\n  status: proposed\n  statement: A run that crosses its time budget (default `RUN_TIME_CAP`) shall stop and end `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`.\n    Calls already in flight may run for at most `CANCEL_ALLOWANCE` beyond the budget.\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile with a slow scripted model and a 30 s test budget, when 10\n    runs execute, then 10/10 end `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`, 10/10 return within 30 s + `CANCEL_ALLOWANCE`,\n    and 10/10 logs name the time limit.\n  tradeoff: Calls that ignore cancellation delay the return.\n  metric: time from the deadline/cancel signal to the terminal event; terminal outcome\n  threshold: <= CANCEL_ALLOWANCE (2 s) and exactly 1 terminal event naming the budget; workflow within\n    budget completes normally\n  verification: offline profile; fixture that crosses the deadline mid-step and fixture cancelled between\n    steps\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-001\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  baseline: No run-level timer.\n  open: Check the deadline at node boundaries and add the cancellation allowance.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001\n  title: Run token budget\n  type: cost\n  priority: Should\n  status: proposed\n  statement: A run shall use at most `TOKEN_BUDGET` tokens in total, counted from provider usage data.\n    A run that would exceed it ends `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)`. If a provider returns no usage data, the run\n    is not stopped; its record marks token usage as `UNKNOWN`.\n  fit_criterion: Given the live profile, when 20 runs execute one after another, then 20/20 have known\n    usage ≤ `TOKEN_BUDGET`, and the GOV-001 score over these runs is ≥ `QUALITY_THRESHOLD`. A run with\n    `UNKNOWN` usage counts as a failure of this criterion, not as zero cost.\n  tradeoff: A budget forces shorter prompts or debates, which the quality threshold partly forbids.\n  metric: tokens consumed per run against TOKEN_BUDGET\n  threshold: tokens_used <= TOKEN_BUDGET; a run that exhausts the budget ends INCOMPLETE with stop_reason\n    BUDGET\n  verification: offline profile with a scripted model reporting token counts; one within-budget and one\n    exhaustion fixture\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-GOV-001\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n  baseline: '`max_tokens` caps each call (`default_config.py`). There is no run-level count.'\n  open: Add up usage per run; set `TOKEN_BUDGET` from measurement.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002\n  title: Run-wide LLM call cap\n  type: cost\n  priority: Must\n  status: proposed\n  statement: 'The system shall ensure that, per run, the number of model-request dispatch attempts never\n    exceeds the number of successful reservations and never exceeds `CALL_CAP`: `dispatch_attempts <=\n    successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP`. A dispatch attempt is one model-generation request attempt issued\n    through the controlled application client boundary, including attempts that time out or fail, application\n    retries, structured-output re-requests, free-text fallback, and in-run memory reflection requests.\n    Every attempt shall be preceded by its own fresh single-use reservation from the run''s shared budget\n    controller; a reservation authorizes exactly one attempt, cannot be reused, and a denied reservation\n    dispatches nothing. An attempt that has been issued consumes its slot even if it fails. A workflow\n    that finishes within its cap completes normally; a run stops `INCOMPLETE(BUDGET)` only when a required\n    further attempt is refused.'\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile and `CALL_CAP = 8`, when a run executes, then (a) every controlled\n    request attempt has a unique preceding successful reservation from the same run; audit records pair\n    one reservation with at most one attempt, including retries, fallback and memory calls; a denied reservation\n    dispatches nothing; (b) total controlled request attempts ≤ 8 across all branches and model tiers,\n    with SDK automatic retries disabled for this mode or every underlying attempt independently gated\n    and counted; (c) after 7 slots are consumed, 4 workers contend for the remaining slot using an injected\n    barrier against the real reservation component, and exactly 1 succeeds and 3 are denied (the winner's\n    identity need not be deterministic); (d) in a scripted workflow that requires one more attempt after\n    the cap is exhausted, that attempt is refused and the run returns `INCOMPLETE` with `stop_reason =\n    BUDGET`, no final rating and `output_check = NOT_RUN`, with audit metadata naming the configured cap\n    and the counts; a workflow that completes within its cap ends normally.\n  tradeoff: A small shared cap can starve parallel branches, and a strict single-use reservation means\n    a branch that loses the last slot stops the run rather than degrading. The stricter the bound, the\n    less tolerant the system is of a borderline cap; that is the price of a guarantee that can actually\n    be checked.\n  metric: model-request dispatch attempts per run, against successful reservations and CALL_CAP\n  threshold: dispatch_attempts <= successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP (test value 8); 0 attempts issued\n    without a reservation\n  verification: offline profile; one budget-controller fixture with an injected threading barrier for\n    the last-slot race; audit log pairing reservations with attempts; one exhaustion fixture and one within-cap\n    fixture\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-001\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  baseline: 'Only per-scope limits: `max_tool_rounds` (20), `max_debate_rounds` / `max_risk_discuss_rounds`\n    (1 each), `llm_max_retries`.'\n  open: Add a shared run-scoped counter and a reservation that precedes dispatch.\n  note: 'Decision D-3, revised 2026-11-23 after Member B''s technical reply. Non-normative. Application\n    counting equals real provider calls only when every attempt the application issues is an attempt the\n    provider sees. In the inspected baseline, `llm_max_retries` is forwarded to the provider SDK (`tradingagents/llm_clients/factory.py`),\n    and analysts fan out concurrently from `START` (`tradingagents/graph/setup.py`), so a counter around\n    high-level model invocations cannot by itself guarantee the bound. Member B''s recommended mechanism\n    is one shared run-scoped budget controller with SDK retries disabled, where each application retry\n    takes a fresh single-use reservation; that makes the strict `<= CALL_CAP` bound achievable. How it\n    is built remains a B design and D implementation decision (`decision-request-D3-cost002-2026-11-22.md`,\n    reply of 2026-11-22). Because a reservation authorizes exactly one attempt, concurrent branches hold\n    their own reservations and no branch allowance is needed; the earlier `CALL_CAP + N_concurrent_branches`\n    form is withdrawn. This requirement does not guarantee the provider gateway''s internal retry count,\n    exact billable usage or monetary cost, and it does not claim the bound is implemented: the controller\n    does not exist in the baseline. If D cannot make (a)-(d) hold on every enabled client, A downgrades\n    COST-002 from Must to Should and restates it as detection-only, recorded in D-4.'\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002\n  - kind: team_decision\n    ref: req-final-scope-A-2026-11-22.md#3\n    locator: D-3\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: reply-to-A-cost002-2026-11-22.md\n    locator: Member B technical reply; strict bound and single-use reservation adopted 2026-11-23\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003\n  title: Early debate convergence\n  type: cost\n  priority: Could\n  status: proposed\n  statement: The bull/bear debate and the risk discussion shall stop before their configured maximum when\n    the participants' positions have converged.\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile, 4 convergence fixtures (2 per debate) and 4 disagreement fixtures,\n    when each runs, then rounds used < maximum for 4/4 convergence fixtures, rounds used = maximum for\n    4/4 disagreement fixtures, and the RUN-001 fields of all 8 equal those of the round-count-only baseline.\n  tradeoff: A debate can be cut before its disagreement surfaces.\n  metric: debate rounds executed when the debate has converged\n  threshold: converged debate stops before max_debate_rounds (rounds_executed < max_debate_rounds on the\n    converged fixture); 0 premature stops on the non-converged fixture\n  verification: offline profile; one converged and one non-converged scripted debate\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001\n  baseline: Round-count only (`graph/conditional_logic.py`).\n  open: Define the convergence signal.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-COST-003\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001\n  title: Evaluation counting rules\n  type: quality_evaluation\n  priority: Should\n  status: proposed\n  statement: \"Every evaluation result the team reports shall be computed with these rules:\\n1. **Completion\\\n    \\ rate** = `COMPLETED` runs ÷ all runs started. No run is ever removed from this denominator.\\n2.\\\n    \\ **Quality scores** (GOV-001 score, rating distribution) are computed over `COMPLETED` runs only,\\\n    \\ and are always reported beside the completion rate and the number of `NEEDS_REVIEW` runs.\\n3. `INCOMPLETE`\\\n    \\ runs are reported by `stop_reason`.\\n4. A run's outcome never invalidates its evidence (FR-001).\\\n    \\ Source reliability is not graded from run outcomes.\\n5. **Acceptance population.** `N_EVAL` counts\\\n    \\ distinct semantic cases, never attempts; a repeated attempt is a repeatability comparison under\\\n    \\ rule 6 and is not counted twice. A changed case population is a versioned acceptance change, not\\\n    \\ a re-run, and results across two populations are not compared. The counting rules below define arithmetic\\\n    \\ only: the rubric, the critical items, the profile and `QUALITY_THRESHOLD` are required acceptance\\\n    \\ inputs owned by Members D and E, and no counting result is an acceptance result without them.\\n\\\n    6. **Comparison modes.** Two results may be compared in *repeatability* mode only if their run records\\\n    \\ match on `config` and `prompt_hash` (NFR-REPRO-001); any difference between them is measurement\\\n    \\ noise and is reported as such. A *controlled change* comparison is permitted when exactly one factor\\\n    \\ (prompt, model or budget) is declared as changed and every other recorded key matches; the output\\\n    \\ must name that factor and report `factor: before -> after`, with the completion rate and the `NEEDS_REVIEW`\\\n    \\ count beside both sides. A comparison that changes more than one factor, or that does not declare\\\n    \\ the factor, is refused.\"\n  fit_criterion: 'Given 10 fixed run records used as a counting fixture (6 `COMPLETED` of which 2 are\n    `NEEDS_REVIEW`; `INCOMPLETE`: 1 `DATA_FAILURE`, 2 `MODEL_FAILURE`, 1 `BUDGET`), when the evaluation\n    script runs, then it reports a completion rate of 6/10, a quality denominator of 6, `NEEDS_REVIEW`\n    = 2, and stop reasons `DATA_FAILURE` 1, `MODEL_FAILURE` 2, `BUDGET` 1, with 0 records dropped; and\n    the output states that these 10 records are a counting fixture, not an acceptance run under `N_EVAL`.\n    Given 2 records that differ in `prompt_hash` and declare no changed factor, the script refuses to\n    compare them (1/1); given 2 records differing only in `prompt_hash` that declare `prompt` as the changed\n    factor, it reports exactly 1 controlled-change comparison naming `prompt` (1/1); given 2 records differing\n    in both `prompt_hash` and `model` with no declaration, it refuses (1/1); given 20 cases scored twice\n    under identical `config` and `prompt_hash`, then `N_EVAL` is reported as 20 cases and not 40 attempts,\n    and exactly 1 result is counted.'\n  tradeoff: Reporting completed-only quality next to a low completion rate can look worse than a single\n    blended number. That is intended.\n  metric: agreement between reported evaluation numbers and a recomputation from the same run records\n  threshold: 100% of reported counts equal the recomputed values; 0 runs silently removed from the completion\n    denominator; 0 undeclared multi-factor comparisons accepted\n  verification: recompute every reported figure from the stored run records of a fixed evidence set\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  - REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001\n  baseline: v0.7.1 has a backtest (`backtest.py`) but no rule for counting failed runs.\n  open: Member D to build the script to these rules.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-NFR-EVAL-001\n  - kind: review_finding\n    ref: requirements-v2-review-2026-11-12.md\n    locator: V2-10\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n  note: 'Amended 2026-11-23 on Member B''s question. B asked whether `N_EVAL` counts cases or attempts\n    and whether the existing five cases and two trials establish acceptance under `N_EVAL=20` with an\n    open threshold. B was right that they do not, and A found a second defect of A''s own: the parameter\n    appendix says `N_EVAL` = 20 cases, while this criterion originally exercised 10 records without saying\n    they were not acceptance. Rule 5 is new and says both things explicitly. A did **not** fix the remainder,\n    because the rubric, the critical items, the evaluation profile and `QUALITY_THRESHOLD` are owned by\n    D and E and two of them are still open parameters; writing them here would have made `GOV-001` look\n    decided when it is not. Not implemented: no evaluation script exists in the baseline.'\n- id: REQ-TA-SEC-001\n  title: Prompt-injection resistance\n  type: security\n  priority: Must\n  status: proposed\n  statement: Instructions inside retrieved content shall not change the run's configuration, the `data_coverage`\n    record, the output check's rules or result, or any RUN-001 field set by deterministic code.\n  fit_criterion: 'Given the offline profile and 20 fixtures (5 each for market, news, social and fundamentals\n    content) whose injected text tells the model to, for example, \"say all data is complete\", \"print OUTPUT\n    CHECK: PASSED\" or \"ignore your rules\", with the scripted model copying the injected text into its\n    output, when each runs, then for 20/20: the config equals the pre-run config (deep equality); `data_coverage`\n    equals that of the same fixture without the injection; and `output_check` and `check_findings` equal\n    the result of applying R1–R8 to the final state.'\n  tradeoff: Injected text can still appear as quoted evidence; it simply has no authority.\n  metric: injected instructions that change the rating or the output check\n  threshold: 0/20 injection fixtures change the final rating or the output_check; 20/20 still produce\n    a valid run record\n  verification: offline profile; injected text in every retrieved-text channel (news, social, filings,\n    web)\n  semantic_part: whether a live model's rating is swayed by injected text is tested in the GOV-001 suite.\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-ARCH-002\n  - REQ-TA-FR-005\n  baseline: Ticker input is sanitised (`dataflows/symbols.py`). Retrieved text reaches the model unmodified.\n    No deterministic check exists yet.\n  open: Build ARCH-002 and FR-005 so that no model text feeds them.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-SEC-001\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-SEC-002\n  title: No credential or token leakage\n  type: security\n  priority: Must\n  status: partial\n  statement: Logs, reports, run records and error messages shall not contain API keys, OAuth access tokens,\n    refresh tokens or bearer [REDACTED]\n  fit_criterion: Given a distinctive fake value planted as each of these 4 secret types across all vendor\n    error paths, when each path is exercised, then a scan of logs, reports, run records and captured exceptions\n    finds 0 planted values and 0 `Bearer ` prefixes.\n  tradeoff: Less debugging detail in error text.\n  metric: secret occurrences in report, log, event stream and traceback on error paths\n  threshold: 0 occurrences of any planted secret in any sink; source files unmodified\n  verification: plant 4 secret types across every sink and every error path, then scan the captured output\n  dependencies: []\n  baseline: Re-verified 2026-11-23 against `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. `get_scrubbed` (`dataflows/net.py`)\n    redacts query-parameter secrets and is used by the Alpha Vantage and FRED vendor modules. The boundary\n    adds `runapi/redact.py`, a `Redactor` applied at the event, report and error sinks. Coverage of third-party\n    loggers and uncaught tracebacks outside the boundary remains unverified.\n  open: Send every outbound error through one scrubber.\n  source:\n  - kind: team_document\n    ref: requirements-draft-v4.md\n    sha256: 542f382c6ae7040442c075cfe4c8416025af4872dcb62c5b189154c846cab051\n    locator: REQ-TA-SEC-002\n  - kind: baseline_observation\n    ref: Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb\n    locator: baseline statement verified against the team repository\n- id: REQ-TA-SEC-003\n  title: No promise of guaranteed returns\n  type: security\n  priority: Should\n  status: proposed\n  statement: Reports shall start with a disclaimer and shall not claim guaranteed returns, guaranteed\n    profit or capital protection.\n  fit_criterion: Given the offline profile, when (a) 20 reports are rendered, then 20/20 start with the\n    disclaimer string; Those are not these rules.\\n- `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py` emits only `Q1`–`Q4`. `R1` maps to\\\n    \\ `Q1`, `R8` maps to `Q3`/`Q4`, and `R4`–`R7` rest on coverage, sentiment and intermediate-output\\\n    \\ fields that the current checker does not inspect. `R2` has no enforcing component.\\n\\nSo this table\\\n    \\ states what a compliant system must do, not what the baseline already does.\\n\\n**Authority**: No\\\n    \\ model output can set, change or skip the check's result. Text in model output that claims a check\\\n    \\ result (\\\"validated\\\", \\\"PASSED\\\") has no effect.\\n\\n**Meaning**: `PASSED` means only that the report\\\n    \\ meets rules R1–R8. It does not mean the analysis is correct, the facts are true or the rating is\\\n    \\ good advice. The report shows this sentence next to the result.\\n\\n**Results**: any blocking finding\\\n    \\ → `NEEDS_REVIEW`; only corrected findings or none → `PASSED`; `INCOMPLETE` run → `NOT_RUN`.\\n\\n\\\n    **Failure behaviour**: If the check itself raises, the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW` with finding `CHECK_ERROR`.\\\n    \\ It never falls back to `PASSED`.\"\n  fit_criterion: 'Given the offline profile, when (a) every `COMPLETED` fixture in Appendix A is inspected,\n    then 100% of `output_check` values equal R1–R8 applied to the final state, and the field is written\n    at exactly 1 call site in the code; (b) a fixture makes the check raise, then the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW`\n    + `CHECK_ERROR` (1/1); (c) a fixture''s model text says \"OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" while R3 fails, then\n    the result is `NEEDS_REVIEW` (1/1); (d) every `INCOMPLETE` fixture has `NOT_RUN` (100%).'\n  tradeoff: One more stage after the graph, and a second place a reader must look.\n  metric: authority of the output check; results set by model text\n  threshold: 0 of the injected model-text fixtures change output_check; 8/8 rules R1-R8 produce a blocking\n    finding on their failing fixture\n  verification: offline profile; inject each rule's failing fixture plus a model-text override attempt\n  dependencies:\n  - REQ-TA-RUN-001\n  baseline: 'Re-verified 2026-11-23 against `Le-kk/CS5351@c0081cb`. The plan hash is checked against the plan\\\n    \\ at the approved revision. An approval never extends to a materially changed plan or to an unlisted\\\n    \\ feature without renewed approval. No hotfix, single-member or approver-absence exception exists.\\\n    \\ A later passing test run or a CI receipt cannot substitute for a missing prior approval.       "newString": "## Repairs (2026-11-21, R1–R5)\n\nThese bounded repairs keep the selected architecture; see [remediation record](../../reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md).\n\n- **R4:** the Research Manager now receives the same protected `get_portfolio_context_from_state` block as the Trader and Portfolio Manager, so its investment plan cannot assert a nonexistent position or treat unknown input as flat. It adds a stage-appropriate instruction to correct conflicting upstream ownership premises; the five-tier research vocabulary and three-action Trader vocabulary are unchanged and no rating is forced.\n- **R5:** publication stages a private tentative terminal on the `EventSink` and only commits the caller-visible terminal after the single directory rename succeeds; a critical publication failure exposes exactly one matching `INCOMPLETE` terminal. Terminal-append failure alone still preserves the logical outcome with `terminal_event.durable=false`; report/manifest remain critical and the single-terminal rule is preserved.\n\n## Implementation status at `a62b801` (verified 2026-11-24)\n\nThe C2 boundary is present in the checkout, not merely designed:\n\n- `runapi/input_service.py` (`PortfolioInputService`, `freeze_explicit`, `freeze_no_portfolio`), `runapi/context.py` (`RunContext`, `FrozenSnapshot`, `ConsentState`), `runapi/execution.py` (`run_analysis_api`, rejects non-`CONFIRMED` at `:149`), `runapi/checks.py` (`OutputChecker`, Q1–Q4), `runapi/finalize.py` (`classify_exception`, `OutcomeFinalizer`), `runapi/persist.py` (single `os.rename` publication at `:154`), `runapi/events.py` (stage-private tentative terminal), `runapi/result.py` (`RunResult`/`CheckResult`/`Finding`), `runapi/reporting.py` (`build_envelope`, `verify_envelope_header_matches`), `runapi/redact.py`.\n- R1–R5 repairs are implemented (`agents/structured.py` applies the shared `Redactor` to its fallback warnings). Independent acceptance of these repairs remains **pending (C)**; the implementation's own remediation record is `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.\n- The C-owned tests under `tests/member_c_verification/offline/` define the seams; passing status is C's to report, not this ADR's.\n\n## Proposed broader requirements — impact, **not** implemented\n\nThe uploaded `requirements.yaml` (`status: proposed_for_adoption`) and A's later correspondence would extend the as-built system. A must approve any reliance on the reduced-coverage low-level primitive (§5.3). Pending publication of `REQ-TA-INV-014` (immutable input) and `REQ-TA-GOV-004` (schema validation) does not change this contract; input freezing is covered by INV-04/05/05b and schema validation belongs to the governance/CI boundary.\n\n## 12. Implementation status and deviations at `a62b801` (verified 2026-11-24)\n\nThis section records what the checkout **actually implements** relative to the design above. Where the design is broader, the deviation is stated; none of these is a claim that a proposed `REQ-TA-*` obligation is met.\n\n### 12.1 Implemented as designed\n- **Consent gate (§4.1, §5):** `run_analysis_api` rejects any `RunContext` whose `consent_state != CONFIRMED` (`runapi/execution.py:149`); `freeze_explicit`/`freeze_no_portfolio` return `FROZEN` (`runapi/input_service.py`).\n- **Canonical fingerprint (§2.2):** implemented in `runapi/context.py`; `FrozenSnapshot` carries the full-64 digest and `as_of_basis=\"USER_CONFIRMED\"`.\n- **Checker authority & Q1–Q4 (§3.3, §6):** `runapi/checks.py` `OutputChecker.evaluate(trusted, provenance_fragment, final_rating, rendered_body)`; checker exception → `CHECK_ERROR` via `error_result`.\n- **Conditional result fields (§3.4):** enforced by `RunResult.__post_init__` (`runapi/result.py:78-90`): `COMPLETED` requires a rating and no stop reason; `INCOMPLETE` requires no rating, a stop reason, `NOT_RUN` and no findings.\n- **Single publication commit + truthful terminal durability (§7):** `runapi/persist.py` writes report+manifest into `_staging`, appends the terminal event, and publishes with one `os.rename` (`:154`); a terminal-append failure yields `terminal_event.durable=false` without flipping the outcome. Stage-private tentative terminal is in `runapi/events.py` (`stage_tentative_terminal`/`commit_terminal`/`discard_tentative_terminal`).\n- **Envelope + header guard (§6.4):** `runapi/reporting.py` `build_envelope` and `verify_envelope_header_matches`.\n- **Evaluation population interface (§10):** `RunRecord` and `summarize_records` exist in `runapi/result.py` (`INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` when no completed run).\n\n### 12.2 As-built vocabulary (narrower than `REQ-TA-*`)\n- **`StopReason`:** five values — `MODEL_FAILURE`, `DATA_FAILURE`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `INTERRUPTED` (`runapi/result.py:12-14`). **No `BUDGET`.** `classify_exception` maps auth/provider/langchain exceptions to `MODEL_FAILURE`, vendor/data to `DATA_FAILURE`, else `INTERNAL_ERROR`; `KeyboardInterrupt`/`InterruptedError` → `INTERRUPTED`.\n- **`Finding.status`:** only `BLOCKING` (`result.py:39`). **`CheckResult`:** `PASSED` with any findings raises; `NEEDS_REVIEW` requires ≥1 finding; `NOT_RUN` forbids findings (`result.py:51-57`). There is **no corrected-finding state**, so proposed R5 (`PASSED` with corrected-only findings) is **not** supported by the current types.\n- **Checker rules:** Q1–Q4 only; no evidence-ID, sentiment or coverage rules. Proposed `R1–R8` (`REQ-TA-ARCH-002`) are **not** implemented; R1≈Q1, R8≈Q3/Q4, R2/R4–R7 have no enforcing code.\n\n### 12.3 Conditional-semantics corrections (aligned with the 24 November review)\n- **Outcome-dependent fields, not blanket non-null:** `stop_reason` is present **only** for `INCOMPLETE`; `final_rating` is present **only** for `COMPLETED` (§3.4). Any proposed requirement wording that requires both fields non-null in every record is **inconsistent** with this contract and with `REQ-TA-RUN-001`'s own validity table; the correct check validates field presence/nullability per the validity table, not a blanket non-null assertion. (This is the `REQ-TA-NFR-REPRO-001` fit-(b) vs `REQ-TA-RUN-001` tension identified in the review; it is a requirements-wording item, not an architecture change.)\n- **Critical publication failure cannot promise an artifact:** a critical report/manifest failure returns `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` with `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null` (§7.3). The contract does **not** promise an on-disk report/manifest on that path; a reproduction requirement should preserve the returned-logical-result vs artifact-publication distinction.\n- **Fixture shorthand:** `INCOMPLETE(MODEL)` / `INCOMPLETE(DATA)` in fixture prose are human shorthand; serialized values remain `MODEL_FAILURE` / `DATA_FAILURE` (RUN-001 spelling rule).\n\n### 12.4 Optional-portfolio scope (implemented; replacement registry unresolved)\n- The implemented contract supports `NO_PORTFOLIO` and an explicitly confirmed `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED` snapshot, including an explicitly empty (flat) book and a supplied book that lacks the analyzed instrument (`§1`, `§2.1`). This is retained as implemented.\n- The uploaded `REQ-TA-*` candidate's scope statement excludes portfolio files while its fixture profiles include them. That replacement-scope disagreement is **unresolved (A/C/team)**; this document does not adopt either wording.\n\n### 12.5 Proposed extensions (documented impact, **not** implemented)\nRecorded here so adoption cost is visible; each is a design+D+C+E change, not implied by this contract:\n- `BUDGET` enum value + run-wide single-use call-reservation controller (`REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002`), including updating every reader that enumerates `StopReason`.\n- `R1–R8` checker with evidence-ID registry and per-run `data_coverage` record (`REQ-TA-FR-001/005`, `INV-002/007`).\n- Corrected-only `PASSED`: requires adding a non-blocking `Finding` status and relaxing `CheckResult(PASSED)` (`result.py:51-57`) together across checks/report/scorer and their tests.\n- Aggregate time/token budgets and resume identity (D-5), which conflicts with the fresh-run-ID/immutability invariants (INV-11/INV-12).",
      "oldString": "## 11. Pending (external owners)\nFinal D1/schema (A); C's test IDs, rubric/threshold, and independent evidence; E enforcement; instructor layout. A must approve any reliance on the reduced-coverage low-level primitive (§5.3)."

Advisory versus authoritative data\n \n | Data | Nature | Authority |\n |---|---|---|\n | Model narrative, ratings text, recommendations | **Advisory** | Cannot set `output_check`/`run_outcome`/provenance |\n | Final rating (Buy/Overweight/Hold/Underweight/Sell/REVIEW) | Derived deterministically from the PM output | Reported, but check Q1 only *reads* readability |\n | Frozen snapshot metadata (mode, basename, fingerprint, as-of) | **Authoritative** (trusted state) | Built by input service; used by header/result/check |\n | `output_check` (PASSED/NEEDS_REVIEW/NOT_RUN) + findings | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutputChecker` only |\n | `run_outcome` (COMPLETED/INCOMPLETE) + `stop_reason` | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutcomeFinalizer` only |\n \n The disclaimer and no-portfolio notice are **frozen strings** (selected-requirements §1) and are treated as trusted content, excluded from Q4 phrase scanning.\n \n ---\n \n ## 5. Workflow (selected C2)\n \n 1. **Discover** eligible `.json` files (non-recursive, sorted, symlinks excluded) from `PORTFOLIO_DIR` — or accept explicit `--portfolio PATH` (outside dir allowed; parent not scanned).\n 2. **Select** one file, or choose no-portfolio, or cancel.\n 3. **Validate/precheck** the frozen bytes; reuse upstream model validation after explicit shape/type/as-of prechecks. Empty positions is valid (flat); no silent fallback.\n 4. **Freeze** → `RunContext` (deeply immutable value tuples; full-64 canonical fingerprint; as-of/basis recorded). Consent state `FROZEN`.\n 5. **Notice** (portfolio mode; §6) then **confirm** → `CONFIRMED` (default No). Non-interactive: valid flags are the consent expression.\n 6. **Run** via the **shared execution service** (`runapi/execution.py`): rejects any `RunContext` not `CONFIRMED`. Holdings reach the provider **only after** confirmation.\n 7. **Render body → scrub → single check (Q1–Q4; Q2 inspects the pre-check provenance fragment against explicit trusted metadata) → finalize → build trusted envelope → stage report+manifest (critical) → one atomic directory commit; terminal JSONL append is best-effort.** Incomplete runs bypass the checker and get `NOT_RUN`. The checked body is delivered unchanged; the envelope adds only trusted metadata. Terminal-event durability is decided before the manifest is staged but does not block publication; a terminal-append failure preserves the logical outcome and records `durable=false`. (§ interface-contracts §6–§7).\n 8. Pre-run cancellation/rejection starts **no graph, zero LLM calls, no completed run**; a critical persistence failure yields a typed INCOMPLETE result that never contradicts a returned success.\n \n Detailed state machine, schemas, canonicalization, ordering and failure simulations: `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md`.\n \n ### 5.1 Synthetic input-mode walkthrough (document example, not a passing test)\n - **Interactive, portfolio:** user sees `a.json`, `b.json`; selects `b.json`; precheck passes; freezes `b` (fingerprint Fb); notice shows basename `b.json`, date D, as-of basis, provider-transmission statement; user answers Yes → `CONFIRMED`; run transmits frozen `b` after consent; report header carries Fb and mode `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED`.\n - **Interactive, no portfolio:** empty directory → no-portfolio confirmation with frozen notice; Yes → `CONFIRMED` with `portfolio=None`; header shows `NO_PORTFOLIO`, null file/fingerprint/as-of.\n - **Noninteractive:** `--portfolio b.json --portfolio-as-of D` → freezes b, consent via flags, no prompt. `--without-portfolio` → `NO_PORTFOLIO`. Neither/both → `InputError`, zero calls.\n - **Cancelled:** user answers No at consent → zero graph/LLM, no completed run, counted as a pre-run attempt (NFR-006).\n \n ---\n \n ## 6. Permissions and consent\n \n - Interactive discovery/selection/consent lives **only** in the CLI (`cli/`). Agents and the engine never prompt.\n - **Consent gate** is an explicit coordinator transition between freeze and run. A frozen snapshot is a *candidate input*, **not** a confirmed selection; immutability alone does **not** prevent bypass. Only a coordinator transition to `CONFIRMED` permits run entry (see interface-contracts §4, ADR §Consent).\n - Mandatory execution, exception mapping, checks and artifact finalization sit behind a **shared application boundary** (`tradingagents/runapi/execution.py: run_analysis_api`) usable without terminal prompts. The upstream Python API signature is **preserved**; the supported project API routes through `run_analysis_api` (full requirement coverage). A raw low-level engine primitive (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run`) remains available but **does not** traverse the boundary and **does not** satisfy FR-006/FR-007/NFR-002/003/004; its scope is declared and product reliance requires **A's approval** (residual risk R-API, pending A). See `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` §5.\n - Coding-agent file permissions (separate concern) are in `docs/architecture/permission-model.md`; E implements enforcement.\n \n ---\n \n ## 7. Observability\n \n - New lifecycle event sink: UTF-8 JSONL; fixed fields `run_id, ticker, node, ts(UTC), elapsed_ms, event, event_outcome`. Console stays human-readable. Raw provider payload logging disabled by default. Progress vocabulary is separate from terminal `run_outcome`.\n - Existing sinks are adapted, not silently trusted: see memory-design §Sinks and runtime-policy-catalog.\n \n ---\n \n ## 8. Engineering contributions (project-specific design)\n+\n+This section states the team's concrete engineering contributions honestly. The individual mechanisms are **standard software-engineering techniques** (immutability, content hashing, atomic directory replacement, append-before-dispatch ledgers, fail-closed checks). We do **not** claim to have invented them, and a standard technique's use does not by itself establish originality. The contribution is the **problem-specific design, its adaptation across the existing TradingAgents pipeline, and the demonstrated effect** in this application; the professor assesses originality. Each item separates what is **deterministically enforced** from what depends on **model compliance** (pending semantic acceptance).\n+\n+### 8A.1 Protected portfolio facts across Research Manager, Trader and Portfolio Manager\n+\n+- **Concrete problem.** In the baseline the portfolio block reached some decision stages unevenly. A real observed failure (2026-11-18, F9) showed an explicit-empty `PortfolioContext(positions=[])` run completing with deterministic check `PASSED` while the Trader/Portfolio-Manager narrative still spoke of \"reducing/retaining existing exposure\" — an unsupported account claim. Downstream stages could also inherit an ownership premise asserted upstream (the Research Manager's investment plan) without access to the same supplied facts.\n+- **Design decision.** Route the same protected portfolio block through a single helper, `get_portfolio_context_from_state` (`tradingagents/agents/context.py:214`), into **all three** decision stages — Research Manager, Trader, Portfolio Manager — and wrap it in `<protected_context>…</protected_context>` (`protect_context`, `context.py:271`) so context compaction cannot drop it. Absent input yields an explicit \"no account ownership is assumed / unknown, not flat\" notice; explicit-empty carries a no-nonzero-target instruction; a held book carries the supplied quantity. The stage instruction tells the model to correct conflicting upstream ownership premises (R4). The five research ratings and three Trader actions are unchanged; no rating is forced.\n+- **Baseline/team change.** Bounded R4 repair (2026-11-21): equalized the block across all three stages and added the corrective instruction. It is a prompt-grounding change, **not** a new authoritative check.\n+- **Tradeoff.** Prompt text grows slightly and each stage must be kept consistent; grounding reduces but cannot eliminate unsupported narrative. A deterministic ownership check would be a larger change the current Q1–Q4 checker deliberately does not make.\n+- **Implementation status.** **Implemented** (R4). **Deterministically enforced:** the trusted facts are delivered to all three stages and survive compaction (prompt-capture tests). **Not enforced deterministically:** that the model's prose never asserts an unsupported position — that is assessed semantically (pending C, GOV-004).\n+- **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r4_research_manager_context.py` (RM/Trader/PM prompt distinction, shared facts, user-supplied/unverified label surviving compaction, absent≠flat); C seams `tests/member_c_verification/offline/test_fr004_propagation.py`, `test_fr005_ratings.py`. Source: `tradingagents/agents/managers/research_manager.py:27-52`, `portfolio_manager.py:30-51`, `trader/trader.py:34,82-93`, `context.py:214-273`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/evidence/live-diagnostic-2026-11-18.json`; `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.\n+- **Residual limitation.** Prompts cannot guarantee every future narrative; Q1–Q4 does not inspect ownership wording. The concrete demonstration is the **explicit-empty → upstream RM trim error the downstream stages corrected → protected-context repair → fresh RM/Trader/PM prompt evidence** thread recorded in the remediation review (retained diagnostics, not a new experiment run here).\n+\n+### 8A.2 Separation of model advice from authoritative provenance/check results (truthful publication and failure handling)\n+\n+- **Concrete problem.** Model narrative, ratings text and any self-claimed \"OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" are advisory but can be mistaken for authoritative state; and a run can claim success while its artifacts failed to publish, or leave a caller-visible COMPLETED terminal for an unpublished run.\n+- **Design decision.** Advisory model output is separated from authoritative, deterministic state:\n+  - **Provenance** is built only from the frozen `RunContext` and a full 64-char SHA-256 over canonical JSON bytes (`runapi/context.py`), never re-read from the file or `final_state`.\n+  - **Check authority** lives in one non-LLM `OutputChecker` (Q1–Q4); model text cannot set or override `output_check` (`runapi/checks.py`, `test_fr007_output_check.py::test_tc_fr007_c_model_claim_cannot_override`).\n+  - **Outcome** is decided by `OutcomeFinalizer` from typed exceptions (`runapi/finalize.py`).\n+  - **Truthful publication:** report+manifest are **critical** and published by a **single atomic directory rename**; the JSONL terminal event is **best-effort** and its real durability is recorded as `terminal_event.durable` before the immutable manifest is staged (`runapi/persist.py:130-157`). A critical staging/commit failure returns `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` with no artifact promise. A tentative terminal is staged privately and revealed only after the commit; a post-commit callback failure cannot revise a published COMPLETED result (R5).\n+- **Baseline/team change.** Bounded R5 repair plus the C2 boundary (`runapi/` modules). These separate advisory from authoritative status and make publication truthfully conditional.\n+- **Tradeoff.** More modules and a staging directory; best-effort events mean a run can publish with `durable=false` (stated, not hidden). Not a power-loss durability guarantee.\n+- **Implementation status.** **Implemented** (Q1–Q4 + R5). **Deterministically enforced:** check authority, provenance identity, conditional result fields, single-commit publication, truthful `durable`. **Residual:** the checker only covers Q1–Q4, not factual accuracy; terminal append remains best-effort.\n+- **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r5_terminal_visibility.py` (rename-failure exposes INCOMPLETE only, manifest-write consistency, terminal-append keeps logical outcome, tentative not exposed pre-commit, single terminal); C seams `tests/member_c_verification/offline/test_fr006_provenance.py`, `test_fr007_output_check.py`, `test_nfr004_persistence.py`, `test_nfr002_events.py`. Source: `runapi/checks.py`, `runapi/finalize.py`, `runapi/persist.py`, `runapi/events.py`, `runapi/reporting.py`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.\n+- **Residual limitation.** Q1–Q4 certifies only its named rules, not truth or account suitability; publication durability is cooperative, not power-loss-proof. Demonstration: the **publication-failure / counterfeit-terminal negatives** in `test_r5_terminal_visibility.py` (offline regression material, not a new live run).\n+\n+### 8A.3 Evaluation-evidence integrity (case/config/artifact correspondence, counterfeit rejection, unsuccessful-attempt accounting)\n+\n+- **Concrete problem.** A semantic score is only meaningful if each result is bound to the case, configuration and artifact it claims to have come from; a forged or mismatched artifact could otherwise pass, and silently dropping failed or incomplete attempts could inflate completion/quality.\n+- **Design decision.** The C-owned live scorer/harness (`tests/member_c_verification/live/`) enforces:\n+  - **Correspondence:** per case, the trusted `(input_mode, basename, fingerprint, as-of, kind)` is derived from the authoritative case definitions (`score_gov004.py::expected_case_identity`) and compared to the manifest; tier-provider settings must match the fixed configuration (`_tier_providers_match_fixed`); case/config/provenance/result and hash checks bind each report to its record.\n+  - **Counterfeit rejection:** conflicting mirror copies and bare authoritative metadata lines outside the header block are rejected (`_reject_counterfeit_metadata_outside_header`; canonical-record equality for durability mirrors).\n+  - **Unsuccessful-attempt accounting:** `replay_store.claim_start` records an exclusive, durable STARTED before dispatch under a cross-process lock; an unresolved start stays a non-completed denominator entry and blocks ID reuse; the scorer reports all started/completed attempts and separates retries.\n+- **Baseline/team change.** These are C's verification-tooling changes (R2/R3), refined with B's design/B-remediation probes. The application product code is not the evaluator; the ledger and scorer are verification governance.\n+- **Tradeoff.** Binding and duplicate-detection add complexity and refuse convenience shortcuts (e.g., reusing a run ID, or substituting a held-target artifact for an empty case); a stricter scorer can fail an otherwise \"good-looking\" package.\n+- **Implementation status.** **Implemented** as verification tooling (R2/R3). **Deterministically enforced:** case/config/artifact binding, counterfeit rejection, exclusive durable starts, all-start accounting. **Residual:** the scorer cannot authenticate a human reviewer or decide general financial truth; the human score sheet is intentionally unfilled and C's acceptance is **pending**.\n+- **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r2_scorer_correspondence.py`, `test_r2_r3_differential_pins.py`, `test_r3_replay_durability.py` (durable-before-dispatch, later-failure retention, unresolved start stays non-completed, exclusive same-ID claim); C harness `tests/member_c_verification/live/test_score_gov004_exitcodes.py` (PASS/FAIL/PENDING exit codes), `test_harness_selfcheck.py`. Source: `tests/member_c_verification/live/score_gov004.py`, `replay_store.py`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/evidence/live-verification-2026-11-21/` (`gov004_starts.json`, `cohort.json`, `ai-review-proposed-scores.json`, `rescore-results.json`, `integrity.json`).\n+- **Residual limitation.** The retained cohort used a narrow rubric that does **not** test general financial arithmetic; the AI-proposed 28/28 is a proposal, not C acceptance. Demonstration: the **retained live package** is re-scored from the repository; the scorer reports `PENDING` until a real reviewer supplies the score sheet, while a counterfeit/substituted artifact fails (`test_r2_02_held_target_substituted_for_empty_case_fails`, `test_r2_03_*`, `test_r3_04_unresolved_start_stays_noncompleted_and_blocks_reuse`).\n+\n+### 8A.4 Demonstration types and originality claim\n+\n+Three distinct deliverables use this material; they are not interchangeable:\n+\n+- **Video — product demonstration.** Shows before/after behaviour (e.g., optional/empty portfolio, protected facts across stages, advisory-vs-authoritative status, a publication-failure or counterfeit negative) using recorded live **or clearly labelled scripted offline** material. It illustrates the mechanism; it does not itself prove originality or acceptance.\n+- **Original-SE explanation.** Explains the project-specific design decisions above: why these facts must be protected across stages, why advisory text is separated from deterministic authority, and why evaluation evidence must bind case/config/artifact. The novelty claim rests on this adaptation and demonstrated effect, **not** on the use of standard techniques.\n+- **Traceability/governance evidence.** The retained tests, evidence packages, and (when assembled by E) `docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md` link requirement → component → test/evidence → monitor. Presence of files or green CI does not by itself prove a gate is enforced or a rubric passed.\n+\n+**Honesty boundary.** Standard techniques (immutability, hashing, atomic publication, ledgers, fail-closed checks) and compliance with course instructions alone do **not** establish originality. No experiment, approval, or ADD cycle is invented here; the demonstration thread reuses existing tests and retained artifacts. The honest limits (prompt grounding ≠ deterministic ownership enforcement; Q1–Q4 ≠ truth; scorer ≠ human acceptance) are stated above and must stay visible.\n+\n+---\n+\n ## 9. The course additionally requires a **layered agent context** design, context assembly and compaction constraints, which this ADR records.\n \n Constraints from the current selection (treated as fixed working decisions): CLI-only UI; `PORTFOLIO_DIR=<root>/portfolios`; `--without-portfolio`; `--portfolio-as-of`; consent behaviour; full normalized-content SHA-256 fingerprint; no silent fallback; no invented zero holdings/cash; model cannot assign checks.\n \n ## Course-required layered context (design)\n \n | Layer | Content (bounded application context) | Source |\n |---|---|---|\n | Identity | Instrument/ticker + resolved identity context | `agents/context.py:build_instrument_context` |\n | Standing constraints | Advisory-only role; no execution; rating vocabulary; disclaimer requirement; \"no account ownership assumed\" | prompts + frozen strings |\n | Knowledge | Analyst reports, research/trader plans, risk debate | graph state |\n | History | Memory-log lessons from prior decisions | `tradingagents/memory/` |\n | State | Input mode, selected basename, as-of/basis, fingerprint (safe projection) | `RunContext` |\n | Current task | The run's instruction to produce a rating + decision | node prompt |\n \n ### Context assembly pipeline (application-bound)\n `deduplicate → prioritize (identity/constraints first) → budget (per-agent token cap) → compact (summarize low-priority narrative; never drop mode/snapshot identity/output authority/critical constraints) → assemble (final prompt)`.\n \n #### Operational budget and compaction design (B3-07, F6; proposed, unmeasured)\n All numbers are **proposed design values (ESTIMATE)**, not measured. C/D later verify/measure.\n \n - **Estimator:** token counts approximated by `ceil(len(prompt_chars)/4)` (cheap, provider-agnostic; **explicitly estimated**, no guarantee against provider tokenizer; no tokenizer dependency added).\n - **Per-agent context cap** `C_cap = 24,000` estimated tokens (proposed): bounds the **assembled prompt context** for one agent, not an aggregate run budget.\n - **Critical reserve** `R_reserve = 4,000` estimated tokens (proposed) planned for identity + standing constraints + state/authority + frozen notice/disclaimer; never compacted.\n - **Compaction threshold** `T_compact = floor(0.8 · C_cap) = floor(19,200) = 19,200`; compact when estimated context exceeds `T_compact`; hard stop at `C_cap`. (Arithmetic corrected: 0.8 × 24,000 = **19,200**, not 20,000.)\n - **Protected-context overflow (actual estimate, not the constant):** let `P` be the **measured estimate of the protected layers** (identity + constraints + state/authority + notice/disclaimer) at assembly time. If `P + (minimum irreducible task/history context) > C_cap`, or more simply if `P > C_cap − C_min_task` (where `C_min_task` is the minimum needed for the current task), **fail closed** (typed `INTERNAL_ERROR`, redacted). The guard compares the **actual protected estimate `P`**, never merely `R_reserve` (which by construction is ≤ `C_cap` and could never overflow).\n - **Compaction termination:** compaction reduces only low-priority narrative (debate prose, redundant analyst text) until total ≤ `T_compact` or until the only remaining reducible content is protected; if compacting all reducible narrative still leaves total > `C_cap`, **fail closed**. Available narrative budget = `C_cap − P`; stop when narrative reaches that bound.\n - **Compaction method:** summarize/trim **low-priority narrative layers only**; deterministic truncation with an explicit \"(compacted)\" marker is the baseline. If a summarizing **model call** is used it is an **explicitly disclosed extra provider call** logged as `event=context.compact` — not silent network behaviour. Default design = deterministic truncation (no extra model; consistent with the note that these corrections imply **no new summarizing provider call**).\n - **Re-injection:** after compaction re-inject identity, mode, snapshot identity (fingerprint/basename/as-of), output authority and frozen disclaimer/notice.\n - **Where:** node-prompt assembly in the agent context layer (`tradingagents/agents/context.py` + prompt builders); **not** OpenCode's internal context.\n - **Temporal guards:** memory/context retrieval keeps upstream as-of/time guards; compaction must not reintroduce out-of-window history.\n - **Illustrative over-cap (document example; arithmetic verified):** assembled estimate = 26,000 tokens; protected `P ≈ 3,200` (identity/constraints/state/notice). Reducible narrative ≈ 22,800. Compaction truncates older bull/bear debate prose (~6,500 → ~500, saving ~6,000) giving 26,000 − 6,000 = **20,000**, still > `T_compact`=19,200, so further low-priority narrative is trimmed (e.g., another ~800) to reach ≈ **19,200** ≤ `T_compact`; protected `P` and current task survive. If instead `P` were 23,000, then `C_cap − P = 1,000` narrative budget, and it fails closed when the minimum task context cannot fit.\n - **Distinction:** bounded **application-context** design; not OpenCode internal management; **not** an aggregate run-token/time/call budget (deferred).\n \n ## Decision\n \n Adopt **C2: an input-service + deeply immutable `RunContext` boundary with a small explicit CLI lifecycle coordinator and a shared execution service.**\n \n - `PortfolioInputService` (`tradingagents/runapi/input_service.py`): the sole discoverer/validator/freezer; produces a `RunContext`.\n - `RunContext`/`FrozenSnapshot` (`runapi/context.py`): deeply immutable value tuples + mode + full-64 canonical SHA-256 + as-of/basis + consent_state; read-only provenance source.\n - **Shared execution service** (`runapi/execution.py: run_analysis_api`): the **common application entry** for CLI and supported project API; rejects non-`CONFIRMED` contexts; owns execution, exception mapping, checks, finalize, staging/publish and terminal event; prompt-free.\n - `RunLifecycleCoordinator` (CLI layer): interactive selection/consent transitions; no LLM; no broad orchestration rewrite; no backtest/resume.\n - `OutputChecker` and `OutcomeFinalizer` are the sole assigners of `output_check`/`run_outcome`.\n - Upstream engine signature preserved; the raw primitive is a declared reduced-coverage path whose product reliance requires A's approval (R-API).\n \n ## Alternatives considered (actual, preserved)\n \n - **C1 — Minimal baseline extension.** Inline discovery/validation (sole shared module, thin inline adapter); header lines appended in reporting; small checker; inline manifest. Pros: smallest footprint. Cons: lifecycle sequencing inline; higher risk of provenance drift if reporting re-derives from `final_state` (latent FR-006/007 risk); weakest typed failure behaviour. Score 3.30.\n - **C2 — Input-service + `RunContext` + small coordinator + shared execution service (selected).** Pros: explicit input/snapshot boundary; clean test seams; shared provenance; typed outcomes; full-coverage API path. Cons: more modules than C1. Score 4.65.\n - **C3 — Phased single-run orchestrator façade.** Same service/context, plus a façade over the whole single-run lifecycle. Pros: strong phase testing. Cons: broader `cli/run.py` change; highest coupling/surface; scope-creep risk. Score 3.75.\n \n ## Human selection rationale (recorded verbatim in substance)\n \n Brian selected **C2** because of its **explicit input/snapshot boundary, test seams and shared provenance, without C3's broader orchestration change.** This is a **human design choice based on estimated tradeoffs**, explicitly **not** a claim of verified superiority.\n \n ## Consequences\n \n Positive: single provenance source; deterministic check authority; consent is an explicit transition; shared execution service gives full-coverage API path; preserved engine signature.\n Negative/risks: the raw low-level engine primitive can bypass the boundary and its product use requires A's approval (R-API); full-64 fingerprint canonicalization must be exactly implemented (`interface-contracts.md` §2.2); prompt/context wording changes are required (not optional).\n Scope note: the implemented optional-portfolio flow is retained here. The broader `REQ-TA-*` candidate's scope statement excludes portfolio files while its fixture profiles include them; that replacement-scope disagreement is **unresolved (A/C/team)** and does not change this ADR's decision.\n \n ## Repairs (2026-11-21, R1–R5)\n \n These bounded repairs keep the selected architecture; see [remediation record](../../reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md).\n \n-- **R4:** the Research Manager now receives the same protected `get_portfolio_context_from_state` block as the Trader and Portfolio Manager, so its investment plan cannot assert a nonexistent position or treat unknown input as flat. It adds a stage-appropriate instruction to correct conflicting upstream ownership premises; the five-tier research vocabulary and three-action Trader vocabulary are unchanged and no rating is forced.\n+- **R4:** the Research Manager now receives the same protected `get_portfolio_context_from_state` block as the Trader and Portfolio Manager, together with a stage-appropriate instruction to correct conflicting upstream ownership premises. The five-tier research vocabulary and three-action Trader vocabulary are unchanged and no rating is forced. **Scope of the guarantee:** this is *prompt grounding* — the trusted snapshot facts are deterministically delivered to all three decision stages (verified by prompt-capture tests), not a guarantee that the model *cannot* state a nonexistent position. Only a deterministic check could enforce that; the current Q1–Q4 checker does not inspect ownership narrative, so whether a given model response honours the grounding is a **semantic** matter pending C's GOV-004 acceptance. The R4 repair reduces the chance of an unsupported ownership claim; it does not deterministically forbid one.\n - **R5:** publication stages a private tentative terminal on the `EventSink` and only commits the caller-visible terminal after the single directory rename succeeds; a critical publication failure exposes exactly one matching `INCOMPLETE` terminal. Terminal-append failure alone still preserves the logical outcome with `terminal_event.durable=false`; report/manifest remain critical and the single-terminal rule is preserved.\n \n ## Implementation status at `a62b801` (verified 2026-11-24)\n \n The C2 boundary is present in the checkout, not merely designed:\n \n - `runapi/input_service.py` (`PortfolioInputService`, `freeze_explicit`, `freeze_no_portfolio`), `runapi/context.py` (`RunContext`, `FrozenSnapshot`, `ConsentState`), `runapi/execution.py` (`run_analysis_api`, rejects non-`CONFIRMED` at `:149`), `runapi/checks.py` (`OutputChecker`, Q1–Q4), `runapi/finalize.py` (`classify_exception`, `OutcomeFinalizer`), `runapi/persist.py` (single `os.rename` publication at `:154`), `runapi/events.py` (stage-private tentative terminal), `runapi/result.py` (`RunResult`/`CheckResult`/`Finding`), `runapi/reporting.py` (`build_envelope`, `verify_envelope_header_matches`), `runapi/redact.py`.\n - R1–R5 repairs are implemented (`agents/structured.py` applies the shared `Redactor` to its fallback warnings). Independent acceptance of these repairs remains **pending (C)**; the implementation's own remediation record is `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.\n - The C-owned tests under `tests/member_c_verification/offline/` define the seams; passing status is C's to report, not this ADR's.\n \n ## Proposed broader requirements — impact, **not** implemented\n \n The uploaded `requirements.yaml` (`status: proposed_for_adoption`) and A's later correspondence would extend the as-built system. If adopted, the following are architecture impacts, documented but **not** designed as accepted decisions here:\n \n - **`BUDGET` stop reason** and a run-wide **single-use call-reservation** controller (`REQ-TA-RUN-001`, `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002`): would add a sixth serialized `StopReason`, a shared budget component consulted before every model dispatch, and updates to every reader. The current five-value literal (`runapi/result.py:12-14`) has no `BUDGET`.\n - **R1–R8 output check** (`REQ-TA-ARCH-002`) and **corrected-only `PASSED`** (R5): R2 (evidence-ID resolution) and R4–R7 (sentiment/coverage) require new data fields and registry components the checker does not inspect; R5 would change `Finding.status`/`CheckResult` so `PASSED` can carry corrected findings — a coordinated type change across checks/report/scorer if retained.\n - **Evidence and coverage registries** (`REQ-TA-FR-001`, `REQ-TA-FR-005`, `REQ-TA-INV-002/007`), **aggregate budgets/resume** (`REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002`, `COST-001/002`, D-5): new components and a resume contract that currently conflicts with `INV-11`/`INV-12`.\n - **`REQ-TA-INV-014` / `REQ-TA-GOV-004`** are pending publication; the existing design already covers input freezing (`INV-04/05/05b`) and treats schema validation as a governance/CI boundary, so their absence does not change C2's data flow.\n \n ## Reopening conditions\n \n - Instructor mandates a single orchestration façade → revisit C3.\n - File-count/scope constraints favour C1 → revisit.\n - Real test evidence (C) shows C1's inline path is cleanly testable with no provenance drift → re-score.\n - Any change to consent semantics, provenance identity or check authority requires a new ADR.\n \n ## Related\n \n - Canonical blueprint: [../../../architecture-blueprint.md](../../../architecture-blueprint.md)\n - [../interface-contracts.md](../interface-contracts.md), [../evaluation-table.md](../evaluation-table.md), [../evaluation-logbook.md](../evaluation-logbook.md), [../risk-list.md](../risk-list.md), [../option-ledger.md](../option-ledger.md), [../invariants.md](../invariants.md), [../memory-design.md](../memory-design.md), [../runtime-policy-catalog.md](../runtime-policy-catalog.md), [../permission-model.md](../permission-model.md), [../traceability-inputs-member-b.md](../traceability-inputs-member-b.md).\n",
