      "oldString": "### 14.2 Finding and result types (target)\n```\nFinding {\n  rule: \"Q2\" | \"R1\"..\"R8\" | \"CHECK_ERROR\"   # Q2 retained; R* per table\n  status: \"BLOCKING\" | \"CORRECTED\"           # NEW: corrected class added\n  detail: str                                # redacted\n  original: str | null                       # for CORRECTED: pre-correction value (recorded)\n  corrected: str | null                      # for CORRECTED: post-correction value\n}\nCheckResult {\n  output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\"\n  findings: Finding[]\n}\n```\n**Result mapping (target), replacing the blocking-only rule:**\n- Any **BLOCKING** finding ⇒ `NEEDS_REVIEW`.\n- **Only CORRECTED** findings (no blocking) ⇒ `PASSED` (corrected changes already applied and recorded). *(This is the approved R5 target; see §16 decision.)*\n- No findings ⇒ `PASSED`.\n- Checker exception ⇒ `NEEDS_REVIEW` with single `CHECK_ERROR`.\n- `INCOMPLETE` ⇒ `NOT_RUN`, findings `[]` (checker not invoked).\n\n**Cross-field invariants (target):**\n- `PASSED` ⇔ findings contain **no BLOCKING** entries (CORRECTED allowed).\n- `NEEDS_REVIEW` ⇒ ≥1 BLOCKING (CHECK_ERROR counts as blocking).\n- `NOT_RUN` ⇒ findings `[]`.\n- `RunResult`/manifest unchanged in authority: `PASSED` still certifies only R1–R8, not truth or suitability.\n\n### 14.3 Corrected-finding handling (R5) — concrete\nWhen R5 decides confidence is too high for coverage: set `Finding{R5, CORRECTED, original=<high>, corrected=\"low\"}`, apply the corrected value to the delivered sentiment header, and keep `output_check=PASSED` (no blocking). The report shows the corrected value; the finding records both. A corrected finding never hides a blocking rule. This is a **contract extension**: `Finding.status` gains `CORRECTED`, `CheckResult(PASSED)` no longer requires empty findings, and the report/scorer render/interpret the new fields — all shipped together.",
      "newString": "### 14.2 Finding and result types, and the single-verdict pipeline (target)\n```\nFinding {\n  rule: \"Q2\" | \"R1\"..\"R8\" | \"CHECK_ERROR\"   # Q2 retained; R* per table\n  status: \"BLOCKING\" | \"CORRECTED\"           # NEW: corrected class added\n  detail: str                                # redacted\n  original: str | null                       # for CORRECTED: pre-correction value (safe field)\n  corrected: str | null                      # for CORRECTED: post-correction value (safe field)\n}\nCheckResult {\n  output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\"\n  findings: Finding[]\n  corrected_fields: SafeCorrectionFields | null  # ONLY explicitly-safe fields (e.g. sentiment confidence enum), never body text\n}\n```\n\n**Single final verdict over the exact delivered body (no freeze-before-recheck).** The verdict must describe precisely what is delivered, so evaluation happens **once, on the final body**:\n\n1. Render the body once from `final_state` + `RunContext` (§6.1), producing `body_fields`.\n2. **Normalize first:** apply authorized corrections to `body_fields` (e.g. R5 confidence) → corrected `body_fields`.\n3. **Re-render** the delivered body deterministically from the corrected `body_fields`.\n4. **Redact the final re-rendered body** (`redactor.scrub`) — redaction happens **before** evaluation and before delivery, so the checked bytes equal the delivered bytes.\n5. **Evaluate once** on that final redacted body: `Checker.evaluate(CheckInput{trusted, provenance, redacted_body, body_fields, evidence, coverage}) → CheckVerdict`. The single `CheckVerdict` (`output_check`, `findings`, `corrected_fields`) is the authoritative verdict for the delivered document. No second, competing verdict is produced.\n6. Persist only the **safe** correction fields (`corrected_fields` restricted to enumerations/flags such as sentiment confidence/band/score — never narrative or free text), plus findings.\n\n**Result mapping (target), scoped to a completed, evaluated run:**\n- Any **BLOCKING** finding ⇒ `NEEDS_REVIEW`.\n- **Only CORRECTED** findings (no blocking) ⇒ `PASSED` (corrections already reflected in the re-rendered delivered body). *(Approved R5 target; see §16.)*\n- No findings ⇒ `PASSED`.\n- Checker exception ⇒ `NEEDS_REVIEW` with single `CHECK_ERROR`.\n- `INCOMPLETE` ⇒ `NOT_RUN`, findings `[]` (checker **not invoked**).\n\n**Cross-field invariants (target), completed-and-evaluated only:**\n- For a completed run whose checker was evaluated: `PASSED ⇔ findings contain no BLOCKING (CORRECTED allowed)`; `NEEDS_REVIEW ⇒ ≥1 BLOCKING` (CHECK_ERROR counts as blocking).\n- **`INCOMPLETE ⇒ NOT_RUN` with findings `[]`.** Explicit negative: **incomplete + empty findings must remain `NOT_RUN`, never `PASSED`.** The `PASSED ⇔ no BLOCKING` equivalence therefore **does not** apply to incomplete runs.\n- `RunResult`/manifest authority unchanged: `PASSED` still certifies only R1–R8, not truth or suitability.\n\n### 14.3 Corrected-finding handling (R5) and sentiment-output cases — concrete\n\n**R5 correction (when sentiment is selected and a `SentimentReport` exists).** When coverage shows a sentiment source not `OK` and confidence `> low`: set `corrected_fields.sentiment_confidence=\"low\"` and `Finding{R5, CORRECTED, original=<high>, corrected=\"low\"}`. The re-render (§14.2 step 3) writes `low` into the delivered header; the single verdict is `PASSED` unless another rule blocks. Corrections and blocking findings may coexist; blocking dominates the verdict while the correction is still applied and recorded.\n\n**Sentiment-output cases (explicit, distinct):**\n- **Sentiment Analyst not selected** → R4–R6 **not applicable**; no finding. (Market-only fixture must not fail for an absent `SentimentReport`.)\n- **Both generation paths fail** (structured call and free-text fallback both yield nothing usable) → the run is **`INCOMPLETE` / `stop_reason=MODEL_FAILURE` / `output_check=NOT_RUN`, no final rating, no findings** (classified by the finalizer as a model failure; the checker is not invoked). This matches `REQ-TA-NFR-001`.\n- **Usable free text without structured fields** (the analyst produced usable narrative but no `SentimentReport`) → this is a **separate case**; it is **not** assigned a new adopted finding rule here. It is surfaced as an **open policy question for A/C** (whether to treat as `REVIEW`/`NEEDS_REVIEW` or to attempt extraction). The design records the case explicitly rather than inventing a rule.\n- **All three sources unavailable** (selected, report present) → R6 requires `Neutral` band (blocking if not); R5 caps confidence at `low` (corrected).     "output": "<path>/home/brian/projects/CS5351/docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n546: ## 13. Evidence and coverage model — `REQ-TA-FR-001/004/005/006` (PROPOSED, not implemented)\n547: \n548: Status: **proposed implementation-ready design** for D to build and C to test. Nothing here is implemented at `a62b801`; the existing run has **input provenance only** (`INV-04/05/05b`) and no per-run evidence or coverage record. This section is the **data contract** that the R2 (evidence-ID) and R7 (coverage-equality) check rules in §14 depend on; per the approved plan, this contract must be agreed **before** those checker integrations. Feasibility of implementing it before 25 Nov is **not promised** (see §16).\n549: \n550: ### 13.1 Proposed components and module boundaries\n551: | Component | Responsibility | Proposed path (new) | Owner(design/impl/test/enforce) |\n552: |---|---|---|---|\n553: | `EvidenceRegistry` | Assign stable evidence IDs; retain per-item records; expose lookup for citation resolution | `tradingagents/runapi/evidence.py` | B / D / C / E |\n554: | `CoverageTracker` | Accumulate one code per channel; classify core/non-core; compute `NOT_REQUESTED`; render deterministic section | `tradingagents/runapi/coverage.py` | B / D / C / E |\n555: | Router/bypass seams | Emit a record/code for every channel, including the 2 router-bypass channels (3 and 11) | `tradingagents/dataflows/router.py` (+ bypass call sites) | B / D / C / E |\n556: \n557: Dependency rule preserved: `runapi/*` must not import `cli`.\n558: \n559: ### 13.2 Field-level data contracts (authority noted per field)\n560: \n561: ```\n562: EvidenceRecord {\n563:   evidence_id: str            # stable within a run; assigned by EvidenceRegistry (AUTHORITATIVE, deterministic)\n564:   channel: ChannelCode        # see §13.3 (deterministic)\n565:   source: str                 # vendor/source label as supplied (SOURCE-PROVIDED metadata; not model text)\n566:   ticker: str                 # instrument the item concerns (SOURCE-PROVIDED)\n567:   observed_at: str | null     # ISO-8601 when observed, else null (SOURCE-PROVIDED)\n568:   published_at: str | null    # ISO-8601 publication/filing date, else null (SOURCE-PROVIDED)\n569:   as_of_window: str           # the FR-004 window this item was admitted under (deterministic)\n570:   value_ref: str | null       # opaque pointer to the retained payload; NOT the payload text (deterministic)\n571: }\n572: ```\n573: \n574: - **Invariant:** at least one of `observed_at` / `published_at` is non-null for every admitted item (R2 resolution depends on it). Enforced by `EvidenceRegistry` on admission.\n575: - **IDs are run-scoped** and never derived from model output. A citation in the rendered report references `evidence_id`; R2 (§14) resolves it against the registry.\n576: - **Retention vs outage:** records are written to the run's own artifact area. \"Retain evidence after an ordinary engine failure\" is **not** a promise that storage succeeds during a critical persistence outage; on critical report/manifest failure the run is `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` and no published paths are promised (§7.3). Evidence retention is best-effort relative to that critical boundary.\n577: \n578: ```\n579: CoverageRecord {\n580:   channel: ChannelCode        # 12 channels (§13.3)\n581:   code: \"OK\" | \"UNAVAILABLE\" | \"NO_DATA\" | \"STALE\" | \"WITHHELD\" | \"NOT_REQUESTED\"   # (deterministic)\n582:   detail: str | null          # redacted, source-metadata-derived; never model prose\n583: }\n584: CoverageSet {\n585:   entries: CoverageRecord[12]         # exactly one row per channel (deterministic)\n586:   core_channels: ChannelCode[]        # e.g. price family; configurable, default per requirement\n587:   run_core_ok: bool                   # all core channels == OK\n588: }\n589: ```\n590: \n591: - **Coverage is built from tool results, never written by the model.** The rendered \"Data coverage\" section is produced deterministically from `CoverageSet`; R7 (§14) asserts the rendered section equals the record.\n592: - `NOT_REQUESTED` = no selected analyst asked for this channel and no vendor call was made; valid for both COMPLETED and INCOMPLETE.\n593: - **Core rule:** any core channel ≠ `OK` ⇒ run ends `INCOMPLETE/DATA_FAILURE`. Non-core gaps do not stop the run.\n594: \n595: ### 13.3 Channel enumeration (12) and bypass handling\n596: Channels map to the router method map. **Channels 3 and 11 bypass the router** in the baseline and require explicit emission at their call sites (D must confirm the exact channel↔method mapping against `router.py` and the two bypass paths before implementation). The enum is a design proposal; the exact membership and the two bypass indices are **to be confirmed by D/C** against the real code (see §16 decision D5).\n597: \n598: ### 13.4 Freshness (§`REQ-TA-FR-006`) — proposed parameters\n599: - Price freshness: latest bar ≤ `STALE_PRICE_DAYS` (10, fixed) before *D*; exceeded ⇒ core gap ⇒ `INCOMPLETE/DATA_FAILURE`.\n600: - Statement freshness: filed ≤ `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` (provisional, **open**) before *D*; exceeded ⇒ coded `STALE`, shown with filing date, run continues.\n601: - News/social: item inside the *D*-clamped window; excluded items are `NO_DATA`/`UNAVAILABLE`, not `STALE`.\n602: - `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` is a **configuration decision, not a measured value** (open; A owns).\n603: \n604: ### 13.5 Normal sequence\n605: `admit(item) → assign evidence_id + record in EvidenceRegistry → set/refine CoverageRecord[channel]` for each retrieved item; at finalize, `coverage = CoverageSet.compute()` and `coverage.render()` produces the report section. Sequence integrates at the data boundary (`router`/bypass), before the checker runs.\n606: \n607: ### 13.6 Failure / concurrency / privacy / persistence policy\n608: - **Failure:** a malformed item that cannot be admitted is a data error for that channel (coded), not a crash; core-gap ⇒ `DATA_FAILURE`.\n609: - **Concurrency:** analysts fan out; `EvidenceRegistry` and `CoverageTracker` mutations must be thread-safe (single lock per registry/tracker, or per-thread accumulation merged at join). Feasibility of implementing it before 25 Nov is **not promised** (see §16).\n\n### 13.1 Proposed components and module boundaries\n| Component | Responsibility | Proposed path (new) | Owner(design/impl/test/enforce) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `EvidenceRegistry` | Assign stable evidence IDs; retain per-item records; expose lookup for citation resolution | `tradingagents/runapi/evidence.py` | B / D / C / E |\n| `CoverageTracker` | Accumulate one code per channel; classify core/non-core; compute `NOT_REQUESTED`; render deterministic section | `tradingagents/runapi/coverage.py` | B / D / C / E |\n| Router/bypass seams | Emit a record/code for every channel, including the 2 router-bypass channels (3 and 11) | `tradingagents/dataflows/router.py` (+ bypass call sites) | B / D / C / E |\n\nDependency rule preserved: `runapi/*` must not import `cli`.\n\n### 13.2 Field-level data contracts (authority noted per field)\n\n```\nEvidenceRecord {\n  evidence_id: str            # stable within a run; assigned by EvidenceRegistry (AUTHORITATIVE, deterministic)\n  channel: ChannelCode        # see §13.3 (deterministic)\n  source: str                 # vendor/source label as supplied (SOURCE-PROVIDED metadata; not model text)\n  ticker: str                 # instrument the item concerns (SOURCE-PROVIDED)\n  observed_at: str | null     # ISO-8601 when observed, else null (SOURCE-PROVIDED)\n  published_at: str | null    # ISO-8601 publication/filing date, else null (SOURCE-PROVIDED)\n  as_of_window: str           # the FR-004 window this item was admitted under (deterministic)\n  value_ref: str | null       # opaque pointer to the retained payload; NOT the payload text (deterministic)\n}\n```\n\n- **Invariant:** at least one of `observed_at` / `published_at` is non-null for every admitted item (R2 resolution depends on it). Enforced by `EvidenceRegistry` on admission.\n- **IDs are run-scoped** and never derived from model output. A citation in the rendered report references `evidence_id`; R2 (§14) resolves it against the registry.\n- **Retention vs outage:** records are written to the run's own artifact area. \"Retain evidence after an ordinary engine failure\" is **not** a promise that storage succeeds during a critical persistence outage; on critical report/manifest failure the run is `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` and no published paths are promised (§7.3). Evidence retention is best-effort relative to that critical boundary.\n\n```\nCoverageRecord {\n  channel: ChannelCode        # 12 channels (§13.3)\n  code: \"OK\" | \"UNAVAILABLE\" | \"NO_DATA\" | \"STALE\" | \"WITHHELD\" | \"NOT_REQUESTED\"   # (deterministic)\n  detail: str | null          # redacted, source-metadata-derived; never model prose\n}\nCoverageSet {\n  entries: CoverageRecord[12]         # exactly one row per channel (deterministic)\n  core_channels: ChannelCode[]        # e.g. price family; configurable, default per requirement\n  run_core_ok: bool                   # all core channels == OK\n}\n```\n\n- **Coverage is built from tool results, never written by the model.** The rendered \"Data coverage\" section is produced deterministically from `CoverageSet`; R7 (§14) asserts the rendered section equals the record.\n- `NOT_REQUESTED` = no selected analyst asked for this channel and no vendor call was made; valid for both COMPLETED and INCOMPLETE.\n- **Core rule:** any core channel ≠ `OK` ⇒ run ends `INCOMPLETE/DATA_FAILURE`. Non-core gaps do not stop the run.\n\n### 13.3 Channel enumeration (12) and bypass handling\nChannels map to the router method map. **Channels 3 and 11 bypass the router** in the baseline and require explicit emission at their call sites (D must confirm the exact channel↔method mapping against `router.py` and the two bypass paths before implementation). The enum is a design proposal; the exact membership and the two bypass indices are **to be confirmed by D/C** against the real code (see §16 decision D5).\n\n### 13.4 Freshness (§`REQ-TA-FR-006`) — proposed parameters\n- Price freshness: latest bar ≤ `STALE_PRICE_DAYS` (10, fixed) before *D*; exceeded ⇒ core gap ⇒ `INCOMPLETE/DATA_FAILURE`.\n- Statement freshness: filed ≤ `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` (provisional, **open**) before *D*; exceeded ⇒ coded `STALE`, shown with filing date, run continues.\n- News/social: item inside the *D*-clamped window; excluded items are `NO_DATA`/`UNAVAILABLE`, not `STALE`.\n- `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` is a **configuration decision, not a measured value** (open; A owns).\n\n### 13.5 Normal sequence\n`admit(item) → assign evidence_id + record in EvidenceRegistry → set/refine CoverageRecord[channel]` for each retrieved item; at finalize, `coverage = CoverageSet.compute()` and `coverage.render()` produces the report section. Sequence integrates at the data boundary (`router`/bypass), before the checker runs.\n\n### 13.6 Failure / concurrency / privacy / persistence policy\n- **Failure:** a malformed item that cannot be admitted is a data error for that channel (coded), not a crash; core-gap ⇒ `DATA_FAILURE`.\n- **Concurrency:** analysts fan out; `EvidenceRegistry` and `CoverageTracker` mutations must be thread-safe (single lock per registry/tracker, or per-thread accumulation merged at join). IDs must remain unique under concurrency.\n- **Privacy:** records carry source metadata and an opaque `value_ref`, not raw payloads; redaction applies at any sink that emits records; holdings/other-position content never enters an evidence record.\n- **Persistence:** evidence/coverage are written into the run's artifact area; a critical publication failure does not promise their durability beyond §7.3; on ordinary engine failure, retained records stay available if storage worked.\n\n### 13.7 Compatibility/migration\nAdditive fields only. Existing manifests gain `coverage` and (optionally) an evidence index reference; `schema_version` bumps. Old readers must tolerate the new fields (forward-compatible) or a version gate applies. #### Raw part 3 — tool
````json
{
  "type": "tool",

  "state": {
    "status": "completed",
    "input": {
      "filePath": "/home/brian/projects/CS5351/docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md",
      "newString": "### 13.6 Failure / concurrency / privacy / persistence policy\n- **Availability after fallback (per call → per unit):** each vendor call resolves to one of `OK`, `UNAVAILABLE` (all vendors in the chain failed/absent), `NO_DATA` (call succeeded but returned a genuinely empty result), `STALE`, `WITHHELD` (live-only data on a historical run). A unit's code is the **worst** outcome across its required calls (`OK` only if all `OK`; else the highest-severity non-OK: `UNAVAILABLE` > `STALE` > `NO_DATA`/`WITHHELD`; `NO_DATA` on a non-core unit does not stop the run).\n- **Unfinished/unavailable requests ≠ genuine empty results:** a request that was started but did not complete (exception, timeout, fallback exhausted) ⇒ `UNAVAILABLE`; a call that completed and returned zero items ⇒ `NO_DATA`; a call never made (analyst not selected) ⇒ `NOT_REQUESTED`. These three must not be conflated: `NO_DATA` means “asked and got nothing”, `UNAVAILABLE` means “asked but could not obtain”, `NOT_REQUESTED` means “never asked”.\n- **Failure:** a malformed item that cannot be admitted is coded for its unit, not a crash; a requested core unit ≠ `OK` ⇒ `DATA_FAILURE` (subject to the open core-exemption decision in §13.3).\n- **Concurrency:** analysts fan out; `EvidenceRegistry` and `CoverageTracker` mutations must be thread-safe (single lock per registry/tracker, or per-thread accumulation merged at join). A filled chat block is **not** the workflow receipt the checker verifies.\n\n```\n2a — AUTHORIZED PREPARATION (before product implementation)\nProduce, on a branch/commit (execution still requires your authorization; do not\nrun during a documentation task):\n- One front-matter plan at  docs/verification/plans/<feature-id>.md  with the\n  REQUIRED fields read by scripts/ci/check_test_approval.py:\n    feature_id, requirements[], implementation_paths[], test_files[], cases[],\n    pass_condition\n  Cases must include at least one each of kind: normal | boundary | error | security,\n  each with an explicit expected result.\n- The NAMED test files listed in test_files[] (proposed tests), committed in the\n  SAME commit as the plan. Their file fingerprints are what the receipt binds.\n- implementation_paths[] = the exact approved write set (no vague categories).\nReviewer reads the plan + proposed tests and records adequacy, incl. negatives.\n\n2b — APPROVAL THROUGH THE TRUSTED WORKFLOW (not chat)\n- The explicitly authorized reviewer posts, on the exact plan/test commit, the\n  EXACT comment command:   /approve-tests <FULL 40-CHARACTER COMMIT SHA>\n  (the command must match exactly; a short SHA, extra text or edited comment is\n  rejected by the trusted workflow.)\n- The trusted workflow (test-approval.yml -> test-approval-complete.yml) produces\n  a RECEIPT bound to the comment text, the approved commit and the test-file\n  fingerprints. Archive the accepted record under docs/verification/approvals/.\n- Product implementation starts ONLY after a successful receipt for that commit.\n- If tests change after approval, the policy's RENEWED / SPLIT-SCOPE procedure\n  applies: re-approve the new test commit; do not silently rewrite frozen tests\n  (later changed fingerprints are rejected).\n- Revocation uses /revoke-tests (a revocation receipt stays in force).\n- Self-approval is permitted but is labelled `self_review`; it is NOT independent\n  human acceptance. Retain actual reviewer attribution.\n\nReviewer confirmations (recorded, not backdated):\n1. Scope bounded; no edits to canonical requirements, other members' tests/CI/\n   evidence, or files outside implementation_paths[].\n2. Test criteria adequate BEFORE implementation; a failing/violating test defined\n   before product code.\n3. Result-contract/compat + version-gate plan acceptable.\n4. Provider/model access constraint acknowledged; no credentials in any file.\n5. One-slice approval does not approve other slices.\n\nReceipt reference to record:  approval_id: ______  approved_commit (40): ______\nNOTE: This gate approves PLAN + TESTS via the pinned receipt. It does not adopt\nrequirements or certify verification. Any commit/PR/approval/archive action needs\nexplicit authorization when executed and is not performed in a documentation task.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Template 3 — Build prompt (only after a successful Template 2 receipt)",

A denied `reserve()` dispatches nothing.\n\n### 15.3 State machine and concurrency\n- States per slot: `AVAILABLE → RESERVED → CONSUMED`; a reservation that is never dispatched (defensive) returns to `AVAILABLE` only via explicit, audited release; a dispatched attempt moves to `CONSUMED` regardless of success.\n- **Concurrency:** `reserve()` is atomic under a single lock/condition per controller; with 1 slot remaining and N concurrent callers, exactly 1 grants and N-1 raise. No branch overshoot allowance is needed (each concurrent branch holds its own reservation). Default START branches = 4 analysts + Memory Log (derived from constructed plan, not a hard-coded constant; branch count irrelevant to the strict bound).\n- **SDK retries:** `max_retries=0` for the guaranteed-budget mode; every application retry takes a **fresh** reservation. If a client cannot disable hidden retries, that client is **rejected** in guaranteed-budget mode (not silently uncovered). Gateway-internal retries are outside the client-side guarantee (stated, not hidden).\n\n### 15.4 Exhaustion propagation (must survive broad handlers)\n- `RunBudgetExhausted` must **not** be swallowed by `agents/structured.py` free-text fallback, `memory/settlement.py` (`except Exception`), or the graph memory step. D must either re-raise it or consult an authoritative exhausted-state check, so a refused **required** attempt reaches finalization as `BUDGET`.\n- **Trigger:** exhaustion stops a run only when a **required further** attempt is refused. Reaching the cap after the last needed request does **not** force failure; a workflow within cap completes normally.\n- **In-flight:** already-issued requests are accounted for (consumed); their termination is awaited before publishing immutable final counts. ````text
§15.2/15.3 still use recycling (`AVAILABLE → RESERVED → CONSUMED`, "returns to AVAILABLE via release"), which contradicts AR24 01's monotonic admission. I must apply the AR24 01 correction now (it was approved earlier but not yet written). Rewrite §15.2 and §15.3.
````

      "newString": "### 15.2 Interface (proposed signatures)\n```\nclass RunBudgetExhausted(Exception): ...       # distinguishable; must survive broad handlers\nclass BudgetProtocolError(Exception): ...      # reuse / wrong-run / invalid transition\n\nReservation {                                   # single-use; owned by one run/controller\n  id: str\n  controller_run_id: str\n  state: \"GRANTED\" | \"CONSUMED\" | \"INVALIDATED\"\n}\nBudgetAudit {\n  call_cap: int\n  granted: int          # cumulative successful admissions (MONOTONIC; never refunded)\n  dispatched: int       # CONSUMED count (attempts actually issued)\n  invalidated: int      # granted-but-unused; capacity NOT refunded\n  denied: int\n}\n\nclass RunBudgetController:\n    def __init__(self, call_cap: int, run_id: str): ...\n    def reserve(self) -> Reservation:      # atomic; increments granted; raises RunBudgetExhausted if granted >= call_cap\n    def dispatch(self, res: Reservation):  # GRANTED -> CONSUMED; must be called BEFORE the request issue\n    def invalidate(self, res: Reservation):# GRANTED -> INVALIDATED; keeps cumulative count; NEVER frees capacity\n    def audit(self) -> BudgetAudit: ...    # safe counts for manifest/event metadata\n```\n`Reservation` authorizes **exactly one** dispatch attempt and cannot be reused. A denied `reserve()` dispatches nothing. `dispatch()`/`invalidate()` raise `BudgetProtocolError` if `res.state != \"GRANTED\"` (reuse) or `res.controller_run_id != run_id` (wrong run / cross-run reuse). Between grant and request issue: if the dispatch never issues (exception before send), `invalidate()` is called and audited; `granted` stays consumed.\n\n### 15.3 State machine and cumulative bound\n- States per reservation: `GRANTED → CONSUMED` (dispatched) or `GRANTED → INVALIDATED` (granted but unused). **There is no return to available capacity.** The `granted` counter is **monotonic**, so `dispatched <= granted <= CALL_CAP` holds even if an unused grant is invalidated: invalidating never lets a second grant happen at a cap of 1.\n- **Alternative (NOT the target):** a recycling policy that returns an unused slot to capacity would require a **different counting contract** and is an **explicit requirements decision**; it is recorded as an unapproved alternative (ADR 002 D3), not implemented.\n- **Concurrency:** `reserve()` is atomic under a single lock/condition per controller; with 1 slot remaining and N concurrent callers, exactly 1 grants and N-1 raise. No branch overshoot allowance is needed (each concurrent branch holds its own reservation). Default START branches = 4 analysts + Memory Log (derived from constructed plan, not a hard-coded constant; branch count irrelevant to the strict bound).\n- **SDK retries:** `max_retries=0` for the guaranteed-budget mode; every application retry takes a **fresh** reservation. If a client cannot disable hidden retries, that client is **rejected** in guaranteed-budget mode (not silently uncovered). This is the approved published target.\n---D3---\n### D3 — Run budget: shared single-use reservation controller\n- **Chosen:** one run-scoped controller; atomic `reserve()` issuing single-use reservations; `dispatch_attempts <= successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP`; SDK `max_retries=0` (reject clients that can't); exhaustion survives broad handlers; persistence failure stays primary.\n- **Alternatives considered:** (a) reusable semaphore — rejects (bounds concurrency, not cumulative calls); (b) counter at high-level invocations with SDK retries on — rejects (cannot guarantee the bound); (c) branch-overshoot allowance — rejects (unnecessary under single-use reservations).\n- **Tradeoff:** strict cap can starve a parallel branch that loses the last slot (stops rather than degrades) — the price of a checkable guarantee.\n\n### D4 — Evidence/coverage as separate registries feeding R2/R7\n",

Documentation-only corrections applied. No application/test/requirements/CI/evidence changes; HEAD unchanged at `a62b801`; no commit/push.

## Corrections applied (per your six conditions)

**1 — Sentiment outcome & free-text (AR24 03, `interface-contracts.md` §14.3, §14.6, K14/K15).** Both generation paths failing ⇒ **`INCOMPLETE` / `MODEL_FAILURE` / `NOT_RUN`, no rating, no findings** (single explicit outcome). Usable free text without structured fields is a **separate case** recorded as an **open policy question for A/C** — no adopted finding rule invented (K15).

**2 — Approval protocol (AR24 05, prompt pack Template 2/3 + usage notes).** Rewrote the gate to the real chain: front-matter plan at `docs/verification/plans/<feature-id>.md` with required fields + named `test_files[]` committed together; reviewer posts the exact **`/approve-tests <FULL 40-CHARACTER SHA>`** command; trusted workflow issues a fingerprint-bound receipt archived under `docs/verification/approvals/`; product code only after the receipt; test changes require renewed/split-scope; `/revoke-tests` acknowledged; self-approval labelled `self_review` ≠ independent acceptance. Template 3 now proceeds only with a matching receipt for that commit.

**3 — Core data & availability (AR24 04, §13.2–13.3, §13.6, E9–E12).** Published core rule preserved; any **unrequested-core exemption is surfaced as a requirements decision** for A/C/team, not applied. Availability defined after fallback per call→unit (worst-wins); **`NOT_REQUESTED` ≠ `NO_DATA` ≠ `UNAVAILABLE`** explicitly distinguished.

**4 — Version axes (AR24 06, §16.6).** Separate **`schema_version`** (manifest/result) and **`check_rules_version`**; **explicit legacy path** for schema-1 artifacts lacking `check_rules_version`; unknown/invalid new combos **rejected (fail closed)**; three required examples (budget-only, full-v2 corrected, rejected unknown-version). ADR-002 "approved published target" clarified as draft approval, not adoption/tested ADD.

**5 — Redaction & safe persistence (§14.2, K16).** Final re-rendered body is **redacted before evaluation/delivery** (checked bytes == delivered bytes); only **safe `corrected_fields`** (enums/flags) persisted — never narrative.

**6 — Metering exactness (§15.4a, P1–P4; ADR-002 D3).** Controller attached to run tier chat-models (`trading_graph.py:79-80`); plain `invoke`, `bind_tools(...).invoke`, `with_structured_output(...).invoke` each consume **exactly one** reservation (no missed/double charge); bypass/double-wrap probes defined; **no runtime guarantee claimed until probes pass**.

## AR24 01/02 also completed (consistency with approved plan)
- **§15.2–15.3 (AR24 01):** monotonic admission — `Reservation`/`BudgetAudit` types; `dispatch()`/`invalidate()`; invalidation never refunds capacity; `BudgetProtocolError` for reuse/wrong-run; scenarios B8–B11. Recycling recorded only as an unapproved alternative (ADR-002 D3).
- **§15.4a + Template 3 (AR24 02):** exact repo-relative permitted paths including the mandatory hooks (`trading_graph.py`, `agents/structured.py`, `memory/settlement.py`, `llm_clients/factory.py`); template consumes the approved `implementation_paths[]`, not categories.

Also updated `invariants.md` (INV-18/19), `adr/002` (D1/D3), `traceability §5` (channel grouping visibly proposed; version axes; corrections), `runtime-policy` cross-refs unchanged where already correct.

## Checks performed
Markdown-link scan across 11 B docs: **0 broken**; fence parity OK; no stale patterns (`returns to AVAILABLE`, `e.g. v2`, `12/12 channels`, bare "channels 3 and 11 bypass"); key corrections present (INCOMPLETE/MODEL_FAILURE, `/approve-tests <FULL 40`, `check_rules_version`, `monotonic`); `git` shows changes confined to `docs/architecture/` + root blueprint; `tradingagents/`, `tests/`, `cli/`, `requirements.yaml`, `.github/`, `docs/reviews/evidence/`, `docs/req/` clean. C2 history and approval chronology preserved; pending-publication IDs and proposed channel grouping kept visibly provisional.

No implementation, tests, commits or pushes were performed.
