    "output": "## 15A. Atomic call + token admission — `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001` (PROPOSED; Alt-B settlement)\n\nStatus: **proposed implementation-ready design** for cumulative **token** admission, sitting **beside** the existing call-cap (§15), not replacing it. **Not implemented.** Alt-B chosen (known-usage settlement with UNKNOWN retention); see [ADR-004](adr/004-cumulative-token-admission.md). Mutable state is per-run and **outside** the frozen `RunContext`.\n\n### 15A.1 One atomic coordinator for both limits\nOne per-run `AdmissionCoordinator` consults the call controller (§15) and the token controller **under one critical section**, withholding a grant from **both** if **either** limit refuses (no partial grant). It lives at the §15 controlled application client boundary (`tradingagents/llm_clients` dispatch seam; proposed `tradingagents/runapi/token_admission.py`). Integration with §15 is **targeted**: §15's counting rules are preserved; only the entry point is wrapped (§15.1 gains a cross-reference; see §15A.6).\n\n```\nTicket { id; coordinator_run_id; call_grant; token_reservation; state: GRANTED|DISPATCHED|SETTLED_KNOWN|SETTLED_UNKNOWN|INVALIDATED }\n\nAdmissionCoordinator.admit(input_bound, output_allowance) -> Ticket\n  # atomic: (call grant ok) AND (K+R+U + input_bound + output_allowance <= TOKEN_BUDGET)\n  # if either refuses -> grant NEITHER; raise the refusing limit's typed error\ncoordinate.dispatch(ticket)                     # GRANTED -> DISPATCHED, immediately BEFORE the provider request issues\ncoordinate.settle_known(ticket, in_use, out_use)# DISPATCHED -> SETTLED_KNOWN\ncoordinate.settle_unknown(ticket)               # DISPATCHED -> SETTLED_UNKNOWN\ncoordinate.invalidate(ticket)                   # GRANTED -> INVALIDATED (unsent only; requires non-dispatch established)\n```\n\n### 15A.2 Defensible bounds vs estimates (required, not parameter choices)\nReservation requires a **defensible upper bound**, not an estimate. Per enabled profile, the **provider/profile capability contract** must assert:\n- **Input upper bound** — an exact model tokenizer, **or** a tokenizer-family + safety multiplier that is **justified for the complete supported request domain**. Empirical samples alone do **not** prove an upper bound.\n- **Tool/schema overhead** — tool schemas, `bind_tools`, `with_structured_output` schema serialization and system-message overhead included in the input bound.\n- **Finite enforced output allowance** — a per-attempt maximum the client/provider **enforces** (e.g. forwarded `max_tokens`). `max_tokens=None` and advisory 450/220-word targets are **not** finite bounds.\n- **Request binding** — the reservation is bound to the **final prepared request + effective configuration**; the payload/config must not change after measurement (immutably referenced; a post-measurement mutation invalidates the ticket).\n\nA profile lacking any of these is **UNSUPPORTED**: token admission refuses to run for it and surfaces the decision; it is not silently estimated. Character/4 is **not** an admissible input bound. Numeric values (`TOKEN_BUDGET`, multiplier, output allowance) remain parameters; the **method + UNSUPPORTED behaviour do not**. Offline accounting tests verify the *accounting logic against a scripted provider*, **not** the deployed provider's true bounds.\n\n### 15A.3 One precise token ledger (mutually exclusive buckets)\n- **K** — known actual usage of **settled-known** attempts.\n- **R** — outstanding reservations for **granted/dispatched (in-flight)** attempts.\n- **U** — retained allowances for **UNKNOWN** attempts (held capacity; never reported as measured actual).\n\n**Admission:** `admit` iff `K + R + U + (input_bound + output_allowance) <= TOKEN_BUDGET`. **This invariant is conditional on the asserted request bounds holding**; a detected violation (§15A.4) is recorded and made visible, not hidden.\n\n**Held capacity** `H = K + R + U` is **not monotonic** (known settlement may reduce it). Keep **monotonic cumulative counters** separately: `cumulative_admitted`, `cumulative_consumed_known`.\n\n### 15A.4 Transitions (no double charge; violations recorded, never clamped)\n| Op | Precondition | Effect | Call counters (§15) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `admit` | call grant ok AND token fits | token reservation → **R** (full allowance); `cumulative_admitted += allowance` | `granted += 1` |\n| `dispatch` | ticket GRANTED | ticket → DISPATCHED (request issues next) | `dispatched += 1` |\n| `settle_known` | ticket DISPATCHED; **valid** input+output usage | remove allowance from **R**, add actual to **K**; `cumulative_consumed_known += actual`. H may decrease if actual < allowance | — |\n| `settle_known` with **actual > allowance** | ticket DISPATCHED | **Bound/protocol violation:** K += actual (full, **not clamped**), R -= allowance, record audit anomaly, **stop new admissions**, propagate typed `TokenBoundViolation` | — |\n| `settle_unknown` | ticket DISPATCHED; usage missing/partial | move allowance **R → U** (retained; **not** in K, not reported as actual) | — |\n| `invalidate` | ticket GRANTED; non-dispatch established | **release the complete token allowance** from **R** (returned to capacity); record invalidation | `invalidated += 1`; **`granted` stays `+1` permanently — the call grant is NOT refunded** |\n\n- **Settlement requires a DISPATCHED ticket.** Reuse, duplicate callbacks (settle twice), a non-dispatched settle, or **wrong-run** tickets raise `TokenProtocolError`, rejected **atomically**, with no bucket move.\n- **Dispatch/invalidation race:** exactly one of `DISPATCHED` or `INVALIDATED` per ticket; a second transition raises. If dispatch was issued, `invalidate` is refused (must settle).\n- **UNKNOWN resolution:** in this version **U stays until finalization; no late U→K**. (A future resolved-late path is out of scope here.)\n- **Token vs call invalidation are intentionally different:** token capacity **is** released on proven non-dispatch (no tokens spent); the **call** grant is **never** refunded (§15 monotonic admission). The coordinator does **not** refund call grants.\n- **Violation ≠ exhaustion:** `actual > allowance` is a bound/protocol violation that **may occur while total usage < TOKEN_BUDGET**; it is not budget exhaustion. It halts new admissions and is mapped per §15A.5.\n\n### 15A.5 Result mapping (no new serialized stop reason)\n- **Bound/protocol violation** → `INCOMPLETE` / `stop_reason=INTERNAL_ERROR` with a safe diagnostic naming the overage (budget kind, allowance, actual, ticket id; no prompts/secrets). Not `BUDGET` — total may be under budget.\n- **Ordinary refusal** of a *required* request that cannot fit → `INCOMPLETE` / `stop_reason=BUDGET`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`.\n- **`PERSISTENCE_ERROR` precedence** over both (critical report/manifest failure). **In-flight** attempts are accounted (R→K/U or recorded overage) before **immutable** finalization; a refused-required drop preserves partial content through normal publication. Single terminal, truthful durability; **no** new enum value.\n\n### 15A.6 Usage seam (capture before parsing discards the response)\nUsage is captured at the **model-request boundary**, immediately after the response returns and **before** structured parsing can discard it — including calls whose parsing then fails. Concretely (`tradingagents/llm_clients/openai_client.py`, `agents/structured.py`): `NormalizedChatOpenAI.invoke`/`normalize_content` are **post-response** processing; `with_structured_output` **constructs a runnable** and issues no request; the request is `…invoke(...)`. The coordinator `dispatch`es before that `.invoke`, and reads `usage_metadata.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` from the returned response **before** `invoke_structured` may raise/fallback and drop it. **Known settlement requires valid input and output usage**; missing/partial ⇒ `settle_unknown`. Do **not** copy `cli/stats_handler.py`'s `.get(..., 0)` zero-default.\n\n### 15A.7 Compatibility / migration\n`schema_version` (result/manifest), `check_rules_version`, and the requirements JSON-Schema version are **separate axes** (§16.7). Add safe `run_budget`/token fields to `EffectiveConfig`+manifest (no prompts/secrets). Old readers **fail closed** on unknown version/fields. No new `StopReason` value. No application-format change merely because D1's schema changed.\n\n### 15A.8 Proposed verification scenarios (C inputs; not accepted)\n| # | Scenario | Expected |\n|---|---|---|\n| T1 | reserve 60, settle known 20 (BUDGET 100) | R 60→0, K 20, H 20, remaining 80; calls granted 1, dispatched 1 |\n| T2 | reserve 60, settle UNKNOWN | R→U=60, K=0, H 60, remaining 40; UNKNOWN not reported as actual |\n| T3 | grant then invalidate unsent (CALL_CAP=1) | token fully released (H 0, remaining 100); calls granted 1, dispatched 0, invalidated 1; **next admit DENIED on call cap** |\n| T4 | four concurrent, remaining fits one | exactly 1 admit, 3 refused; K+R+U ≤ BUDGET; calls granted +1 |\n| T5 | duplicate settle / wrong-run / non-dispatched settle | `TokenProtocolError`, no bucket move |\n| T6 | actual (75) > allowance (60), total < budget | INTERNAL_ERROR (not BUDGET), K=75, overage visible, admissions halted, no clamp |\n| T7 | required request can't fit, total at budget | INCOMPLETE/BUDGET/NOT_RUN, no rating, findings [] |\n| T8 | violation + critical persistence failure | PERSISTENCE_ERROR primary |\n| T9 | usage missing/partial | settle UNKNOWN, capacity retained |\n| T10 | old reader meets new field/version | fail closed |\n\n---\n\n## 16. Integration, implementation order and handoff — proposed\n",

Not `BUDGET` — total may be under budget.\n- **Ordinary refusal** of a *required* request that cannot fit → `INCOMPLETE` / `stop_reason=BUDGET`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`.\n- **`PERSISTENCE_ERROR` precedence** over both (critical report/manifest failure). **In-flight** attempts are accounted (R→K/U or recorded overage) before **immutable** finalization; a refused-required drop preserves partial content through normal publication. Single terminal, truthful durability; **no** new enum value.\n\n### 15A.6 Usage seam (capture before parsing discards the response)\nUsage is captured at the **model-request boundary**, immediately after the response returns and **before** structured parsing can discard it — including calls whose parsing then fails. Concretely (`tradingagents/llm_clients/openai_client.py`, `agents/structured.py`): `NormalizedChatOpenAI.invoke`/`normalize_content` are **post-response** processing; `with_structured_output` **constructs a runnable** and issues no request; the request is `…invoke(...)`. The coordinator `dispatch`es before that `.invoke`, and reads `usage_metadata.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` from the returned response **before** `invoke_structured` may raise/fallback and drop it. **Known settlement requires valid input and output usage**; missing/partial ⇒ `settle_unknown`. Do **not** copy `cli/stats_handler.py`'s `.get(..., 0)` zero-default.\n\n### 15A.7 Compatibility / migration\n`schema_version` (result/manifest), `check_rules_version`, and the requirements JSON-Schema version are **separate axes** (§16.7). Add safe `run_budget`/token fields to `EffectiveConfig`+manifest (no prompts/secrets). Old readers **fail closed** on unknown version/fields. No new `StopReason` value. No application-format change merely because D1's schema changed.\n\n### 15A.8 Proposed verification scenarios (C inputs; not accepted)\n| # | Scenario | Expected |\n|---|---|---|\n| T1 | reserve 60, settle known 20 (BUDGET 100) | R 60→0, K 20, H 20, remaining 80; calls granted 1, dispatched 1 |\n| T2 | reserve 60, settle UNKNOWN | R→U=60, K=0, H 60, remaining 40; UNKNOWN not reported as actual |\n| T3 | grant then invalidate unsent (CALL_CAP=1) | token fully released (H 0, remaining 100); calls granted 1, dispatched 0, invalidated 1; **next admit DENIED on call cap** |\n| T4 | four concurrent, remaining fits one | exactly 1 admit, 3 refused; K+R+U ≤ BUDGET; calls granted +1 |\n| T5 | duplicate settle / wrong-run / non-dispatched settle | `TokenProtocolError`, no bucket move |\n| T6 | actual (75) > allowance (60), total < budget | INTERNAL_ERROR (not BUDGET), K=75, overage visible, admissions halted, no clamp |\n| T7 | required request can't fit, total at budget | INCOMPLETE/BUDGET/NOT_RUN, no rating, findings [] |\n| T8 | violation + critical persistence failure | PERSISTENCE_ERROR primary |\n| T9 | usage missing/partial | settle UNKNOWN, capacity retained |\n| T10 | old reader meets new field/version | fail closed |\n\n---\n\n## 16. Integration, implementation order and handoff — proposed\n",

      "newString": "### 15A.6 Usage seam — concrete interception below the structured parser\nReading the outer structured runnable's return value is **insufficient**: `with_structured_output(...)` returns a runnable that **parses** the model reply into a schema object (or raises), discarding the raw `AIMessage` that carried `usage_metadata`. Interception must therefore sit on the **chat-model message-generating seam that every routing funnels through**, *below* the parser.\n\n**Interception point (implementable):** override `ChatOpenAI._create_chat_result(self, response, …)` on the metered chat class (the pattern `DeepSeekChatOpenAI` already uses at `tradingagents/llm_clients/openai_client.py:118`). Every request — plain `invoke`, `bind_tools(...).invoke`, and `with_structured_output(...).invoke` — reaches the provider through `_generate/_agenerate → _create_chat_result`, so this seam sees the **raw provider `response`** (including `response.usage`: input/output tokens) **and** the produced `ChatResult` (AIMessage with `usage_metadata`) for **all three routings** and **before** any schema parse can discard it.\n\n**Routing and capture:**\n- **Plain:** `NormalizedChatOpenAI.invoke` → `super().invoke` → `_generate` → `_create_chat_result`. Capture raw usage there; `normalize_content` then rewrites `.content` (post-response, irrelevant to usage).\n- **Tool-bound:** `bind_tools(tools).invoke` is a bound runnable over the **same** metered model; same `_generate → _create_chat_result` path → one captured usage per underlying request.\n- **Structured:** `with_structured_output(...)` returns a parser-bearing runnable whose `.invoke` calls the same model `_generate → _create_chat_result`; usage is captured **here**, **before** the runnable's parser converts/rejects the payload. A parse failure (`invoke_structured` raising, then free-text fallback) still has its usage captured — the metered model already recorded it when the first reply returned.\n\n**Admission/dispatch binding (must include provider-added payload fields):** `admit` binds the reservation to the **final prepared request**, i.e. the serialized chat payload **after** `_get_request_payload` adds provider-specific fields (e.g. DeepSeek `reasoning_content`, tool schemas, `tool_choice`, `max_tokens`). The input bound and the ticket's immutable request fingerprint are computed over that prepared payload (or a stable hash of it), so a later mutation of caller inputs cannot silently change what was measured. `dispatch(ticket)` wraps the send; `_create_chat_result` is the settle point: capture raw `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` and `settle_known(ticket, in, out)` **exactly once** (guarded by ticket state `DISPATCHED`; a duplicate `_create_chat_result` for the same ticket is rejected). If usage fields are **absent or non-integer** for either direction ⇒ `settle_unknown(ticket)`.\n\n**Exactly-once:** one ticket per underlying provider request (bound runnables/proxies reuse the same metered model object, so no per-call-site re-wrap); settlement occurs only transition `DISPATCHED → SETTLED_*`, so retries/fallback create **new** dispatches (each with its own ticket/reservation), never a second settle of the same ticket. SDK automatic retries must be `max_retries=0` in this mode (or independently gated) so a hidden retry cannot issue an unmetered request.\n\n**Valid usage:** known settlement requires **both** input and output token counts to be present non-negative integers from the provider; anything else (missing, partial, non-integer, negative) ⇒ `settle_unknown`. Do **not** copy `cli/stats_handler.py`'s `.get(..., 0)` zero-default (which would read a missing field as zero)."

Keep **monotonic cumulative counters** separately: `cumulative_admitted`, `cumulative_consumed_known`.\n \n ### 15A.4 Transitions (no double charge; violations recorded, never clamped)\n",

````text
All checks pass. Final confirmation.

## Changed-section mappings

**Item 1 — §15A.6 implementable usage seam (`interface-contracts.md`).** Rewrote to name the concrete interception point **`ChatOpenAI._create_chat_result`** (pattern already in `DeepSeekChatOpenAI`, `openai_client.py:118`) — *below* the structured parser, hit by all routings. Documents plain/`bind_tools`/`with_structured_output` routing, raw provider `response.usage` + AIMessage `usage_metadata` capture, parse-failure→fallback (usage captured at first reply), exactly-once settlement (ticket-state guarded; retries get new tickets; `max_retries=0`), and reservation bound to the **final prepared request** via `payload_fingerprint` over post-`_get_request_payload` payload. ADR-004 §Decision item 5 updated to match.

**Item 2 — token contracts (`interface-contracts.md` §15A.1/.2/.3/.5/.7/.8).** Added `TokenReservation`/`RequestBinding` types; typed errors `TokenBudgetExhausted`/`TokenBoundViolation`/`TokenProtocolError`/`UnsupportedProfileError`; valid-usage rule (both directions valid; else UNKNOWN; no zero-default); safe persisted audit fields; `EffectiveConfig` additions; **unsupported-profile validation timing = once at controller init, pre-dispatch → INTERNAL_ERROR**; **overage applied atomically before propagation**; separated **Admission predicate** from **Ledger invariant**; compatibility matrix with token-capable record combos + legacy path + fail-closed; new scenarios **T11 usage-despite-parse-failure, T12 (covered in T11 text), T13 mutation, T14 unsupported, T15 no-partial-grant**.

**Item 3 — current-status alignment.** Removed stale current claims that INV-014/GOV-004 are unpublished/absent and that optional portfolio input is excluded — in `architecture-blueprint.md` (§header, §1.4 items, §1.5), `interface-contracts.md` (§11, §12.4 heading+body), `invariants.md` (INV-014 row), `traceability-inputs-member-b.md` (§2 note, §3 pending items, §5 row), `risk-list.md` (R-REQ-SCOPE, R-REQ-IDS), `adr/001` (scope note, INV-014 line, integration status). `docs/req/README.md`: correct count (34→36, schema 1.2.0) and **validator instructions to its actual interface** (positional + `--registry`/`--schema`, defaults, exit codes); corrected the "`--registry` unsupported" limitation. Preserved dated historical entries (logbook 24-Nov `a62b801` record) unchanged.

## Actual verification results
- HEAD `5672a79` (unchanged); registry **36 entries**, `proposed_for_adoption`, `schema 1.2.0`, INV-014+GOV-004 present.
- Confirmed source seams: `_create_chat_result` override exists; `with_structured_output` constructs a runnable; `normalize_content` post-response; `stats_handler` `.get(...,0)`; `validate.py` supports positional/`--registry`/`--schema`.
- Local link scan across 13 docs: **0 broken**; all markdown fences balanced; tables column-consistent (T-rows 4 pipes, transitions 5, matrix 6).
- Scope: changes confined to `docs/architecture/` + root blueprint + `docs/req/README.md`; `tradingagents/`, `tests/`, `cli/`, `docs/req/requirements.yaml`/`req-schema.json`/`validate.py`/other req files, `.github/`, `docs/reviews/`, `AI-log/` **clean**; `git diff --check` clean; pre-existing `numeric-validation-extension-plan` draft preserved. No live calls/commits/pushes.
- No residual current-status stale terms ("pending publication"/"excludes portfolio"/"34-entry"); "implementation-ready" removed from §15A (now "proposed design … provider-bound evidence and parameter values remain open").

## Remaining implementation prerequisites
- **E:** per-profile **provider-bound evidence** (tokenizer or justified family+multiplier over the full supported request domain; finite enforced output allowance) and raw optimization artifacts — without it the profile is **UNSUPPORTED**, not estimated.
- **A/team:** adopt `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001`; set parameters `TOKEN_BUDGET`, `CALL_CAP`, input multiplier, output allowance (120000 candidate not adopted).
- **D:** implement `runapi/token_admission.py` + coordinator at the `_create_chat_result` seam with `payload_fingerprint` binding, `max_retries=0`, atomic overage→INTERNAL_ERROR; distinct from §15 call cap.
- **C:** accept and run proposed scenarios T1–T15 offline; independent semantic acceptance of concise optimization (dangling-reference boundary) still pending.
- **Open, unchanged:** OQ-16 consent entry; OQ-17 population; semantic acceptance; schema-gate enforcement; adoption of the registry.

Stopping for review.

It introduces **no new forced truncation** and is **distinct from** both (i) the existing per-prompt character/4 guard (`bound_agent_prompt`) and (ii) the proposed run-wide `CALL_CAP`/`BUDGET` controller (ADR-002 D3, unimplemented). **Observed token savings do not satisfy `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002` and do not implement Slice C**; no aggregate budget guarantee is introduced. A **separate proposed** cumulative-*token* admission design (`REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001`, interface-contracts §15A, ADR-004 Alt-B, catalog R23/R24) sits beside the call cap and is likewise **not implemented**.\n \n Implementing any row above is a design + D implementation change requiring C's approved tests and E's gates; it is **not** satisfied by the working `SEL-TA-*` tests or this documentation revision.\n \n ---\n \n ## 2. System and deployment boundaries\n \n - **Runtime:** a single local Python process. The user interacts through the terminal (the existing CLI). No network is required for input selection/validation; network/provider calls occur only inside the graph after confirmation.\n - **Requested interface:** current CLI (`cli/main.py`), extended with input-mode flags. This is the only new user-facing surface; no new web application.\n - **Baseline preserved:** `tradingagents/`, `cli/`, `pyproject.toml` and existing tests are preserved. The extension is discovery, explicit consent, frozen provenance and coherent reporting (Prompt.md \"Session objective and input precedence\" / \"Access and output boundaries\").\n - **Trust boundary for data:** user-supplied portfolio files are *context*, never verified account facts. The trusted state used to build provenance is the frozen snapshot produced by the input service, not model text and not re-read file bytes.\n \n ### 2.1 Data-flow (C2)\n ```\n terminal user\n    │  (interactive, or flags)\n    ▼\n CLI adapter (cli/main.py)  ──►  PortfolioInputService (discover → validate/precheck → freeze)\n    │                                         │\n    │                                         ▼\n    │                              RunContext (deeply immutable)\n    │             frozen snapshot + mode + full-64 fingerprint + as-of + disclosure flags\n    │                                         │\n    │   [notice shown; consent gate]\n    │                                         │\n    ▼                                         ▼\n runapi/execution.run_analysis_api  ── consent confirmed ──►  engine.stream_run\n    │  (CLI single-run orchestration, no LLM)         (portfolio=None | frozen snapshot)\n    │                                         │\n    │                                         ▼\n    │                     runapi/checks.py OutputChecker (non-LLM, authoritative)\n    │                                         │\n    │                                         ▼\n    │                  runapi/finalize.py OutcomeFinalizer (COMPLETED|INCOMPLETE)\n    │                                         │\n    ▼                                         ▼\n Artifact boundary (redaction + run-ID isolation)  →  report(MD/HTML), manifest, JSONL events, logs, state JSON\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## 3. Components\n \n Concrete module paths are in `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` §1 (B3-10). The `tradingagents/runapi/` modules and `cli/input_ui.py` **exist in the current checkout** (verified); the \"Status\" column records that. Reusable noninteractive services live under `tradingagents/runapi/` and must not import `cli`.\n \n | Component | Responsibility | Where (verified path) | Status vs baseline |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | **Shared execution service** | **Common application entry** `run_analysis_api(RunContext, …)`: consent check → run → render → check → finalize → stage/publish → terminal event. Prompt-free; used by CLI and supported API. | `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py` | present (additive) |\n | `PortfolioInputService` | Noninteractive discovery/precheck/freeze; **sole** discoverer/validator; prompt-free. | `tradingagents/runapi/input_service.py` | present (additive) |\n | `RunContext` / `FrozenSnapshot` (deeply immutable) | Frozen value tuples + mode + full-64 fingerprint + as-of/basis + consent_state; read-only provenance source. | `tradingagents/runapi/context.py` | present (additive) |\n | `OutputChecker` | Deterministic **Q1–Q4** on the checked **body**; assigns `output_check` + findings. Authoritative, non-LLM. | `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py` | present (additive) |\n | `OutcomeFinalizer` | Maps graph return/exceptions/attempted critical-persistence failure to `run_outcome` + `stop_reason`. | `tradingagents/runapi/finalize.py` | present (additive) |\n | `Redactor` | Central masking (keys/tokens/bearer, unsafe diagnostics) at every sink, including `agents/structured.py` warnings (R1 repair). | `tradingagents/runapi/redact.py` | present (additive) |\n | `EventSink` (JSONL) | Fixed-field structured events; stage-private tentative terminal. | `tradingagents/runapi/events.py` | present (additive) |\n | Persistence/Manifest | Staging (report+manifest **critical**; terminal event **best-effort**) → single atomic directory commit; manifest via `SafeRunMetadata`; `terminal_event.durable` decided pre-commit without blocking publication. | `tradingagents/runapi/persist.py` | present (additive) |\n | Result schemas | `RunResult`, `CheckResult`, `Finding`, `InputError`, `RunRecord`, `summarize_records`. | `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` | present (additive) |\n | CLI input UI | Interactive discovery/consent **only** here. | `cli/input_ui.py` | present (additive) |\n | CLI adapter | Thin wiring; adds `--without-portfolio`, `--portfolio-as-of`; suppresses prompts under flags. | `cli/main.py` | adapted |\n | Prompt/context semantics | Mode-aware rating-scale legend; no-portfolio Hold meaning; user-supplied/unverified wording. | `tradingagents/agents/context.py`, manager/trader prompts | adapted |\n | Concise intermediate context *(integrated at `adb4dfc`)* | Advisory evidence-first brevity guidance (`concise_analysis_instruction`); exact-substring opponent reference (`opponent_argument_or_opening(...,history)`); compaction safeguard restoring explicit copies before `bound_agent_prompt` (`bound_debate_prompt`); `concise_intermediate_reports` switch. No new forced truncation, summarizer, tool-payload limiter, role/round change. | `tradingagents/agents/context.py`, `agents/analysts/turn.py`, `agents/researchers/*_researcher.py`, `agents/risk_mgmt/*_debator.py`; config in `default_config.py`, `graph/trading_graph.py`, `runapi/execution.py` — integrated via PR #18 (merge `adb4dfc`, ancestor of current HEAD) | present on main (integrated); dangling-reference boundary/quality/approval open |\n | Reporting boundary | Renders checked **body** + trusted **envelope header** from `SafeRunMetadata`; stage labels `build_envelope`/`verify_envelope_header_matches`. | `tradingagents/runapi/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/report_html.py` | adapted |\n | Existing loader/model | `PortfolioContext`/`Position` validation and rendering; alias matching. | `tradingagents/portfolio.py` (preserved) | unchanged semantics |\n | Raw engine primitive | `TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run/create_run_state` signature preserved; **does not** traverse the boundary (reduced scope, A approval for product use). | `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` | signature preserved |\n \n ---\n \n ## 4. Advisory versus authoritative data\n \n | Data | Nature | Authority |\n |---|---|---|\n | Model narrative, ratings text, recommendations | **Advisory** | Cannot set `output_check`/`run_outcome`/provenance |\n | Final rating (Buy/Overweight/Hold/Underweight/Sell/REVIEW) | Derived deterministically from the PM output | Reported, but check Q1 only *reads* readability |\n | Frozen snapshot metadata (mode, basename, fingerprint, as-of) | **Authoritative** (trusted state) | Built by input service; used by header/result/check |\n | `output_check` (PASSED/NEEDS_REVIEW/NOT_RUN) + findings | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutputChecker` only |\n | `run_outcome` (COMPLETED/INCOMPLETE) + `stop_reason` | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutcomeFinalizer` only |\n \n The disclaimer and no-portfolio notice are **frozen strings** (selected-requirements §1) and are treated as trusted content, excluded from Q4 phrase scanning.\n \n ---\n \n ## 5. Workflow (selected C2)\n \n 1. **Discover** eligible `.json` files (non-recursive, sorted, symlinks excluded) from `PORTFOLIO_DIR` — or accept explicit `--portfolio PATH` (outside dir allowed; parent not scanned).\n 2. **Select** one file, or choose no-portfolio, or cancel.\n 3. **Validate/precheck** the frozen bytes; reuse upstream model validation after explicit shape/type/as-of prechecks. Empty positions is valid (flat); no silent fallback.\n 4. **Freeze** → `RunContext` (deeply immutable value tuples; full-64 canonical fingerprint; as-of/basis recorded). Consent state `FROZEN`.\n 5. **Notice** (portfolio mode; §6) then **confirm** → `CONFIRMED` (default No). Non-interactive: valid flags are the consent expression.\n 6. **Run / analysis execution** via the **shared execution service** (`runapi/execution.py`): rejects any `RunContext` not `CONFIRMED`; holdings reach the provider **only after** confirmation. Within this analysis-execution stage (not rendering/publication):\n    - **Intermediate context generation.** When `concise_intermediate_reports` is enabled, analysts and Bull/Bear/risk debaters receive **advisory** evidence-first brevity guidance (`concise_analysis_instruction`; ~450 words analysts, ~220 debates). **Placement:** in `analysts/turn.py` the guidance is appended to the **assembled system message** (tool-bound and wrap-up paths, preserving tool schemas/call IDs/messages); in the Bull/Bear researchers and three risk debaters it is appended to their **assembled prompt strings**. The guidance is **advisory** (subordinate to evidence/disclosures), not a hard output cap. This feature introduces **no new forced output/tool-payload truncation**; the existing per-prompt guard (`bound_agent_prompt`, character/4 estimate) can still trim narrative when a large assembled prompt exceeds its limit.\n    - **Reference substitution (deterministic).** When an opponent's exact stripped latest argument already occurs in debate history, a reference replaces the duplicate copy (`opponent_argument_or_opening(...,history)`); an empty opponent keeps an explicit opening notice. This is **exact Python string-substring matching**, not semantic deduplication.\n    - **Compaction safeguard (deterministic branch).** `bound_debate_prompt` reconstructs the explicit copies and, if the reconstructed-original length would exceed `min(context_cap_tokens, compaction_threshold_tokens) * 4`, passes the restored form to the existing `bound_agent_prompt` guard (else the reference form). This reduces but does **not** eliminate dangling-reference risk: a short argument can be replaced by a longer reference notice, so a reference form longer than the restored original can still be compacted (probe `docs/reviews/evidence/token-context-reference-probe-2026-11-24.json`). Restoring copies before the guard is **not** a guarantee that every evidence item survives compaction.\n    - **Trusted portfolio facts** and all final provenance/check/publication authority below are unchanged; prompt instructions are not deterministic semantic enforcement.\n    - **Separate from budgets:** this is neither the existing per-prompt character/4 guard nor the proposed run-wide `CALL_CAP`/`BUDGET` controller (ADR-002 D3, unimplemented).\n    - **Status:** **integrated at `adb4dfc` (PR #18, ancestor of current HEAD `5672a79`)**; the dangling-reference boundary, quality acceptance and prior approval remain **open**. Switch `concise_intermediate_reports` (default True; `TRADINGAGENTS_CONCISE_INTERMEDIATE_REPORTS=false` or programmatic False restores legacy).\n 7. **Render body → scrub → single check (Q1–Q4; Q2 inspects the pre-check provenance fragment against explicit trusted metadata) → finalize → build trusted envelope → stage report+manifest (critical) → one atomic directory commit; terminal JSONL append is best-effort.** Incomplete runs bypass the checker and get `NOT_RUN`. The checked body is delivered unchanged; the envelope adds only trusted metadata. Terminal-event durability is decided before the manifest is staged but does not block publication; a terminal-append failure preserves the logical outcome and records `durable=false`. (§ interface-contracts §6–§7).\n 8. Pre-run cancellation/rejection starts **no graph, zero LLM calls, no completed run**; a critical persistence failure yields a typed INCOMPLETE result that never contradicts a returned success.\n \n Detailed state machine, schemas, canonicalization, ordering and failure simulations: `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md`.\n \n ### 5.1 Synthetic input-mode walkthrough (document example, not a passing test)\n - **Interactive, portfolio:** user sees `a.json`, `b.json`; selects `b.json`; precheck passes; freezes `b` (fingerprint Fb); notice shows basename `b.json`, date D, as-of basis, provider-transmission statement; user answers Yes → `CONFIRMED`; run transmits frozen `b` after consent; report header carries Fb and mode `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED`.\n - **Interactive, no portfolio:** empty directory → no-portfolio confirmation with frozen notice; Yes → `CONFIRMED` with `portfolio=None`; header shows `NO_PORTFOLIO`, null file/fingerprint/as-of.\n - **Noninteractive:** `--portfolio b.json --portfolio-as-of D` → freezes b, consent via flags, no prompt. `--without-portfolio` → `NO_PORTFOLIO`. Neither/both → `InputError`, zero calls.\n - **Cancelled:** user answers No at consent → zero graph/LLM, no completed run, counted as a pre-run attempt (NFR-006).\n \n ---\n \n ## 6. Permissions and consent\n \n - Interactive discovery/selection/consent lives **only** in the CLI (`cli/`). Agents and the engine never prompt.\n - **Consent gate** is an explicit coordinator transition between freeze and run. A frozen snapshot is a *candidate input*, **not** a confirmed selection; immutability alone does **not** prevent bypass. Only a coordinator transition to `CONFIRMED` permits run entry (see interface-contracts §4, ADR §Consent).\n - Mandatory execution, exception mapping, checks and artifact finalization sit behind a **shared application boundary** (`tradingagents/runapi/execution.py: run_analysis_api`) usable without terminal prompts. The upstream Python API signature is **preserved**; the supported project API routes through `run_analysis_api` (full requirement coverage). A raw low-level engine primitive (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run`) remains available but **does not** traverse the boundary and **does not** satisfy FR-006/FR-007/NFR-002/003/004; its scope is declared and product reliance requires **A's approval** (residual risk R-API, pending A). See `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` §5.\n - Coding-agent file permissions (separate concern) are in `docs/architecture/permission-model.md`; E implements enforcement.\n \n ---\n \n ## 7. Observability\n \n - New lifecycle event sink: UTF-8 JSONL; fixed fields `run_id, ticker, node, ts(UTC), elapsed_ms, event, event_outcome`. Console stays human-readable. Raw provider payload logging disabled by default. Progress vocabulary is separate from terminal `run_outcome`.\n - Existing sinks are adapted, not silently trusted: see memory-design §Sinks and runtime-policy-catalog.\n \n ---\n \n ## 8. Verification strategy and current evidence (design-level only)\n \n - **Testability seams** (for C): `PortfolioInputService` (discover/validate/freeze), `RunContext` identity, `OutputChecker` (Q1–Q4 with injected model claims), `OutcomeFinalizer` (typed exceptions), redaction at each sink, manifest atomicity, same-date isolation.\n - **Real test definitions now exist** under `tests/member_c_verification/offline/` (C-owned), mapping to the working selection: `test_fr001_discovery.py`, `test_fr002_consent.py`, `test_fr003_validation_freeze.py`, `test_fr004_propagation.py`, `test_fr005_ratings.py`, `test_fr006_provenance.py`, `test_fr007_output_check.py`, `test_nfr001_failures.py`, `test_nfr002_events.py`, `test_nfr003_privacy.py`, `test_nfr004_persistence.py`, `test_nfr005_layering.py`, `test_nfr006_population.py`. B **links** these; B does not own, run or certify them.\n - **Developer/remediation tests** under `tests/member_b_remediation/` (R1–R5 probes) and `tests/member_d_verification/` are diagnostic regression material; they are not independent acceptance.\n - **Retained evidence** is cited by path and **not re-run here** (see `docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md`): `docs/reviews/evidence/live-verification-2026-11-21/` (fresh five-case/two-trial live cohort; all 15 deduplicated attempts `COMPLETED`), `docs/reviews/evidence/live-diagnostic-2026-11-18.json`, and the 24 November integration review. Historical formal **PASS remains unverified**; independent current semantic acceptance remains **pending (C)**.\n - **Distinction preserved:** a test *definition* existing ≠ passing; a developer diagnostic ≠ acceptance; a fresh live run ≠ formal acceptance under open `N_EVAL`/threshold parameters.\n - **Document consistency checks** (this revision) are **not** application verification.\n \n Verification links per requirement are in `docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md`; C owns the verdict.\n \n ---\n \n ## 8A. Engineering contributions (project-specific design)\n \n This section states the team's concrete engineering contributions honestly. The individual mechanisms are **standard software-engineering techniques** (immutability, content hashing, atomic directory replacement, append-before-dispatch ledgers, fail-closed checks). We do **not** claim to have invented them, and a standard technique's use does not by itself establish originality. The contribution is the **problem-specific design, its adaptation across the existing TradingAgents pipeline, and the demonstrated effect** in this application; the professor assesses originality. Each item separates what is **deterministically enforced** from what depends on **model compliance** (pending semantic acceptance).\n \n ### 8A.1 Protected portfolio facts across Research Manager, Trader and Portfolio Manager\n \n - **Concrete problem.** In the baseline the portfolio block reached some decision stages unevenly. A real observed failure (2026-11-18, F9) showed an explicit-empty `PortfolioContext(positions=[])` run completing with deterministic check `PASSED` while the Trader/Portfolio-Manager narrative still spoke of \"reducing/retaining existing exposure\" — an unsupported account claim. Downstream stages could also inherit an ownership premise asserted upstream (the Research Manager's investment plan) without access to the same supplied facts.\n - **Design decision.** Route the same protected portfolio block through a single helper, `get_portfolio_context_from_state` (`tradingagents/agents/context.py:214`), into **all three** decision stages — Research Manager, Trader, Portfolio Manager — and wrap it in `<protected_context>…</protected_context>` (`protect_context`, `context.py:271`) so context compaction cannot drop it. Absent input yields an explicit \"no account ownership is assumed / unknown, not flat\" notice; explicit-empty carries a no-nonzero-target instruction; a held book carries the supplied quantity. The stage instruction tells the model to correct conflicting upstream ownership premises (R4). The five research ratings and three Trader actions are unchanged; no rating is forced.\n - **Baseline/team change.** Bounded R4 repair (2026-11-21): equalized the block across all three stages and added the corrective instruction. It is a prompt-grounding change, **not** a new authoritative check.\n - **Tradeoff.** Prompt text grows slightly and each stage must be kept consistent; grounding reduces but cannot eliminate unsupported narrative. A deterministic ownership check would be a larger change the current Q1–Q4 checker deliberately does not make.\n - **Implementation status.** **Implemented** (R4). **Deterministically enforced:** the trusted facts are delivered to all three stages and survive compaction (prompt-capture tests). **Not enforced deterministically:** that the model's prose never asserts an unsupported position — that is assessed semantically (pending C, GOV-004).\n - **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r4_research_manager_context.py` (RM/Trader/PM prompt distinction, shared facts, user-supplied/unverified label surviving compaction, absent≠flat); C seams `tests/member_c_verification/offline/test_fr004_propagation.py`, `test_fr005_ratings.py`. Source: `tradingagents/agents/managers/research_manager.py:27-52`, `portfolio_manager.py:30-51`, `trader/trader.py:34,82-93`, `context.py:214-273`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/evidence/live-diagnostic-2026-11-18.json`; `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.\n - **Residual limitation.** Prompts cannot guarantee every future narrative; Q1–Q4 does not inspect ownership wording. The concrete demonstration is the **explicit-empty → upstream RM trim error the downstream stages corrected → protected-context repair → fresh RM/Trader/PM prompt evidence** thread recorded in the remediation review (retained diagnostics, not a new experiment run here).\n \n ### 8A.2 Separation of model advice from authoritative provenance/check results (truthful publication and failure handling)\n \n - **Concrete problem.** Model narrative, ratings text and any self-claimed \"OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED\" are advisory but can be mistaken for authoritative state; and a run can claim success while its artifacts failed to publish, or leave a caller-visible COMPLETED terminal for an unpublished run.\n - **Design decision.** Advisory model output is separated from authoritative, deterministic state:\n   - **Provenance** is built only from the frozen `RunContext` and a full 64-char SHA-256 over canonical JSON bytes (`runapi/context.py`), never re-read from the file or `final_state`.\n   - **Check authority** lives in one non-LLM `OutputChecker` (Q1–Q4); model text cannot set or override `output_check` (`runapi/checks.py`, `test_fr007_output_check.py::test_tc_fr007_c_model_claim_cannot_override`).\n   - **Outcome** is decided by `OutcomeFinalizer` from typed exceptions (`runapi/finalize.py`).\n   - **Truthful publication:** report+manifest are **critical** and published by a **single atomic directory rename**; the JSONL terminal event is **best-effort** and its real durability is recorded as `terminal_event.durable` before the immutable manifest is staged (`runapi/persist.py:130-157`). A critical staging/commit failure returns `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` with no artifact promise. A tentative terminal is staged privately and revealed only after the commit; a post-commit callback failure cannot revise a published COMPLETED result (R5).\n - **Baseline/team change.** Bounded R5 repair plus the C2 boundary (`runapi/` modules). These separate advisory from authoritative status and make publication truthfully conditional.\n - **Tradeoff.** More modules and a staging directory; best-effort events mean a run can publish with `durable=false` (stated, not hidden). Not a power-loss durability guarantee.\n - **Implementation status.** **Implemented** (Q1–Q4 + R5). **Deterministically enforced:** check authority, provenance identity, conditional result fields, single-commit publication, truthful `durable`. **Residual:** the checker only covers Q1–Q4, not factual accuracy; terminal append remains best-effort.\n - **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r5_terminal_visibility.py` (rename-failure exposes INCOMPLETE only, manifest-write consistency, terminal-append keeps logical outcome, tentative not exposed pre-commit, single terminal); C seams `tests/member_c_verification/offline/test_fr006_provenance.py`, `test_fr007_output_check.py`, `test_nfr004_persistence.py`, `test_nfr002_events.py`. Source: `runapi/checks.py`, `runapi/finalize.py`, `runapi/persist.py`, `runapi/events.py`, `runapi/reporting.py`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.\n - **Residual limitation.** Q1–Q4 certifies only its named rules, not truth or account suitability; publication durability is cooperative, not power-loss-proof. Demonstration: the **publication-failure / counterfeit-terminal negatives** in `test_r5_terminal_visibility.py` (offline regression material, not a new live run).\n \n ### 8A.3 Evaluation-evidence integrity (case/config/artifact correspondence, counterfeit rejection, unsuccessful-attempt accounting)\n - **Concrete problem.** A semantic score is only meaningful if each result is bound to the case, configuration and artifact it claims to have come from; a forged or mismatched artifact could otherwise pass, and silently dropping failed or incomplete attempts could inflate completion/quality.\n - **Design decision.** The live scorer/harness (`tests/member_c_verification/live/`) enforces the points below. **Provenance, by verified commit (roles only):** the evaluator originated as Member C's supplied tooling (`f66fc14`, `57b164c`, `b8c4a25`); it was subsequently hardened (`bb777d5`); the R2/R3 correspondence/counterfeit-replay repairs and the `tests/member_b_remediation/` regression tests were made in the supervised OpenCode repair session under a Brian-approved plan (`56bbe29`). `replay_store.py` was introduced in `56bbe29`, **not** with the original evaluator. A commit records submitted changes; it does **not** by itself prove who manually authored the code. C's **independent acceptance remains pending**. The points it enforces:\n   - **Correspondence:** per case, the trusted `(input_mode, basename, fingerprint, as-of, kind)` is derived from the authoritative case definitions (`score_gov004.py::expected_case_identity`) and compared to the manifest; tier-provider settings must match the fixed configuration (`_tier_providers_match_fixed`); case/config/provenance/result and hash checks bind each report to its record.\n   - **Counterfeit rejection:** conflicting mirror copies and bare authoritative metadata lines outside the header block are rejected (`_reject_counterfeit_metadata_outside_header`; canonical-record equality for durability mirrors).\n   - **Unsuccessful-attempt accounting:** `replay_store.claim_start` records an exclusive, durable STARTED before dispatch under a cross-process lock; an unresolved start stays a non-completed denominator entry and blocks ID reuse; the scorer reports all started/completed attempts and separates retries.\n - **Baseline/team change.** Verification-tooling changes (R2/R3) in the supervised OpenCode repair session on C's evaluator (origin/hardening/repair by commit per above). The application product code is not the evaluator; the ledger and scorer are verification governance.\n - **Tradeoff.** Binding and duplicate-detection add complexity and refuse convenience shortcuts (e.g., reusing a run ID, or substituting a held-target artifact for an empty case); a stricter scorer can fail an otherwise \"good-looking\" package.\n - **Implementation status.** **Implemented** as verification tooling: original evaluator (C), hardening (`bb777d5`), R2/R3 repairs/regressions (`56bbe29`). **Deterministically enforced:** case/config/artifact binding, counterfeit rejection, exclusive durable starts, all-start accounting. **Residual:** the scorer cannot authenticate a human reviewer or decide general financial truth; the human score sheet is intentionally unfilled and **C's independent acceptance is pending**.\n - **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r2_scorer_correspondence.py`, `test_r2_r3_differential_pins.py`, `test_r3_replay_durability.py` (durable-before-dispatch, later-failure retention, unresolved start stays non-completed, exclusive same-ID claim); C harness `tests/member_c_verification/live/test_score_gov004_exitcodes.py` (PASS/FAIL/PENDING exit codes), `test_harness_selfcheck.py`. Source: `tests/member_c_verification/live/score_gov004.py`, `replay_store.py`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/evidence/live-verification-2026-11-21/` (`gov004_starts.json`, `cohort.json`, `ai-review-proposed-scores.json`, `rescore-results.json`, `integrity.json`).\n - **Residual limitation.** The retained cohort used a narrow rubric that does **not** test general financial arithmetic; the AI-proposed 28/28 is a proposal, not C acceptance. Demonstration: the **retained live package** is re-scored from the repository; the scorer reports `PENDING` until a real reviewer supplies the score sheet, while a counterfeit/substituted artifact fails (`test_r2_02_held_target_substituted_for_empty_case_fails`, `test_r2_03_*`, `test_r3_04_unresolved_start_stays_noncompleted_and_blocks_reuse`).\n \n ### 8A.3a Concise intermediate context: a reversible cost/evidence tradeoff *(integrated at `adb4dfc`)*\n \n - **Concrete problem.** Verbose intermediate analyst reports are re-read by downstream agents, and debate prompts carried both the full history and a separate copy of the opponent's latest argument — the same evidence sent twice. The existing character/4 prompt guard bounded very large prompts but did not address this sub-threshold repetition.\n - **Design decision (feature `9102759`).** Advisory evidence-first brevity guidance (~450-word analysts, ~220-word Bull/Bear/risk): in `analysts/turn.py` appended to the **assembled system message**, in Bull/Bear/risk appended to their **assembled prompt strings**. Deterministic replacement of a duplicated opponent argument by a reference **only when the exact stripped text occurs in history** (**exact Python string-substring matching**); and a compaction safeguard that reconstructs the explicit copies and, if the reconstructed-original length exceeds `min(context_cap_tokens, compaction_threshold_tokens)*4`, passes the restored form to the existing guard. **No unconditional no-dangling guarantee:** a short argument can be replaced by a longer reference notice, so the reference form can exceed the guard target even when the restored original fits, and checking only the restored-original length can miss compaction of the reference form (probe `docs/reviews/evidence/token-context-reference-probe-2026-11-24.json`). Reversible via `concise_intermediate_reports` (default True; env/programmatic False restores legacy).\n - **Deterministic vs advisory.** Flag/metadata plumbing, the exact-string reference, and the reconstruct-then-guard branch are deterministic; the word targets and evidence-preservation wording are **advisory** prompt guidance. **No new forced output/tool-payload truncation** is introduced (the existing guard may still trim narrative); it is not a guarantee that every evidence item survives compaction.\n - **Kept separate.** Not the existing per-prompt guard; not the proposed Slice C `CALL_CAP`/`BUDGET` controller (ADR-002 D3, unimplemented). Observed savings do not satisfy `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002`.\n - **Tradeoff.** Shorter intermediate context can omit nuance the model would otherwise restate; the reference depends on exact text presence (no semantic dedup). Reversible configuration bounds the risk.\n - **Implementation status.** **Integrated at `adb4dfc` (PR #18 merge; ancestor of current HEAD `5672a79`).** The dangling-reference boundary (probe `docs/reviews/evidence/token-context-reference-probe-2026-11-24.json`), independent quality acceptance and prior approval remain **open**. Source changes touch files included in `prompt_hash`, so new-run `prompt_hash` differs; mode is recorded separately in `EffectiveConfig`.\n - **Measurements (E-reported; not rerun here).** Optimized 99,532 / 103,120 / 110,725 tokens (mean 104,459) vs historical mean 138,896.5 (24.7936%) and a same-day one-sample control 160,826 (35.0484%); single NVDA/2026-01-09 case, four analysts, English, 1+1 rounds, school `openai_compatible` + DeepSeek V4 Flash, empty memory, no portfolio, caching; exclusions and a failed attempt disclosed; **no ablation**, **no universal/runtime/quality claim**.         "patch": "Index: docs/architecture/adr/003-concise-intermediate-context.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/architecture/adr/003-concise-intermediate-context.md\t\n+++ docs/architecture/adr/003-concise-intermediate-context.md\t\n@@ -1,39 +1,39 @@\n # ADR 003 — Concise intermediate context and reversible repeated-argument references\n \n - Status: **Proposed (architecture record 2026-11-24)** — decision status unchanged. Documents the design of E's concise intermediate-context feature as **inspected from source** (`aa3b02d` / `9102759`, PR #18). **Integration (recorded separately, not a status change):** merged to main at `adb4dfc` (ancestor of current HEAD); the dangling-reference boundary, quality acceptance and prior approval remain **open**. This is a *current rationale and retrospective source analysis*, **not** a historical ADD experiment, candidate comparison, human approval or ablation.\n - Deciders: Member B (author); A/C/D/E coordination pending. Does not adopt requirements or approve implementation.\n - Scope: intermediate context generation/assembly in the analysis-execution stage. It does **not** change checker/evidence/publication contracts or ADR-002's proposed slices.\n - Relationship: does not supersede ADR 001 (C2) or ADR 002. Preserves C1/C2/C3 history and the C2 choice.\n \n ## Context\n \n Analysts produce verbose intermediate reports that downstream research/risk agents re-read, and debate prompts carried both the full history and a separate copy of the opponent's latest argument (duplicate evidence below the existing character/4 prompt guard's threshold). The existing `bound_agent_prompt` guard (`agents/context.py`) bounds very large assembled prompts by estimation `ceil(len/4)` against `context_cap_tokens`/`compaction_threshold_tokens`, trimming low-priority narrative; it did not prevent this sub-threshold repetition.\n \n ## Decision\n \n This proposed record describes three mechanisms already implemented on the feature branch; retention/integration remains subject to team review and C acceptance:\n \n 1. **Advisory brevity guidance.** `concise_analysis_instruction(stage)` appends evidence-first brevity text (~450 words analysts, ~220 debates). **Placement differs by path:** in the analyst tool loop (`analysts/turn.py`) it is appended to the **assembled system message** (preserving tool schemas, call IDs and original input messages); in the Bull/Bear researchers and the three risk debaters it is appended to their **assembled prompt strings**. Advisory only — evidence, disclosures and required fields take priority; no hard output cap and no new forced truncation.\n 2. **Exact-string opponent reference.** `opponent_argument_or_opening(text, opponent, history)` returns a reference when the exact stripped argument occurs in history; empty opponents keep an explicit opening notice. This is exact Python string-substring matching, not semantic deduplication.\n 3. **Restore-before-guard safeguard.** `bound_debate_prompt` reconstructs explicit copies and, if the reconstructed original exceeds `min(context_cap_tokens, compaction_threshold_tokens) * 4`, passes the restored form to the existing guard; else the reference form. **No unconditional no-dangling guarantee:** a demonstrated boundary shows a short argument can be replaced by a *longer* reference notice, so the reference form can exceed the guard target even when the restored-original length fits; checking only the restored-original length can therefore miss compaction of the reference form (and thus of the history it cites). The safeguard reduces but does not eliminate dangling-reference risk. See `docs/reviews/evidence/token-context-reference-probe-2026-11-24.json`; follow-up for E/C below.\n \n **Configuration/rollback:** `concise_intermediate_reports` (default `True`); `TRADINGAGENTS_CONCISE_INTERMEDIATE_REPORTS=false` or programmatic `False` restores legacy. Recorded in `run_settings()`/`EffectiveConfig`; the flag is not hashed, but the touched prompt sources are in `_prompt_hash` (interface-contracts §3.8), so new-run `prompt_hash` differs. Legacy artifacts lacking the field are `unknown/legacy`, not today's default.\n \n ## Alternatives considered (bounded)\n - **No change (verbose baseline):** rejected as the measured driver of repeated input cost.\n - **New summarizer/summary-model call:** rejected — adds provider cost/calls and a new failure mode; out of the bounded goal.\n - **Hard output-token cap / tool-payload truncation:** rejected — risks dropping required evidence/disclosures; the feature adds no new forced truncation (the existing guard may still trim narrative).\n - **Semantic deduplication:** rejected — not deterministically enforceable cheaply; the exact-substring reference is deterministic and reversible, subject to the documented reference-boundary risk.\n \n ## Consequences\n - **Positive:** shorter intermediate context and removed duplicate argument text, with a concrete reversible switch; trusted portfolio facts, provenance/check/publication authority unchanged; existing guard preserved.\n - **Cost/tradeoff:** advisory brevity can omit nuance; reference depends on exact text presence; one measured case with no ablation (E-reported optimized mean 104,459 vs historical 138,896.5 ≈ 24.79%, same-day control 160,826 ≈ 35.05%) — **not** a universal, runtime, or quality guarantee, and **not** COST-002/Slice C.\n-- **Limits:** feature unmerged; benchmark uses raw `run_transient` (not product acceptance); compaction preservation not proven end-to-end; semantic acceptance pending C; PR #18 approval checks failed and prior approval is not established.\n+- **Limits:** concise optimization **integrated at `adb4dfc`** (PR #18); the dangling-reference boundary, quality acceptance and prior approval remain **open**. Benchmark uses raw `run_transient` (not product acceptance); compaction preservation not proven end-to-end; semantic acceptance pending C; PR #18 approval checks failed and prior approval is not established.\n - **Known boundary and follow-up (E/C, not implemented here):** the reference notice can be longer than the argument it replaces, so the restore-before-guard length check (on the restored-original form) can pass while the reference form still exceeds the guard and has its cited history trimmed. Follow-up for **E**: use a reference notice no longer than the replaced argument, or evaluate compaction against the reference form; for **C**: add a regression fixture reproducing the synthetic boundary and asserting the delivered prompt never cites trimmed history. Recorded in `risk-list.md` R-CONCISE.\n - **Separateness preserved:** distinct from the existing per-prompt guard and from ADR-002's proposed run-wide `CALL_CAP`/`BUDGET` controller.\n \n ## Related\n - Canonical blueprint: [../../../architecture-blueprint.md](../../../architecture-blueprint.md) §5 step 6, §8A.3a\n - [001-portfolio-aware-cli.md](001-portfolio-aware-cli.md) (C2; unchanged) · [002-extended-result-evidence-budget.md](002-extended-result-evidence-budget.md) (proposed slices; unchanged)\n - [../interface-contracts.md](../interface-contracts.md) §3.7/§3.8/§3.11 · [../memory-design.md](../memory-design.md) §9 · [../runtime-policy-catalog.md](../runtime-policy-catalog.md) R22 · [../traceability-inputs-member-b.md](../traceability-inputs-member-b.md) §4/§5.1\n - Review: `docs/reviews/token-context-architecture-review-2026-11-24.md`\n",

        "patch": "Index: docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md\t\n+++ docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md\t\n@@ -1,1172 +1,1228 @@\n # Interface Contracts (Member B)\n \n Status: architecture draft (revised 2026-11-12 per the Stage-3 architecture review; implementation-aligned 2026-11-24). Typed shapes were **proposed design contracts** for C (test seams) and D (implementation). As of `a62b801` they are **implemented** in `tradingagents/runapi/` (verified against source; see §12). Where the implementation is narrower than this spec, §12 records the difference; the contract text below is the design of record. Independent acceptance (C) and enforcement (E) remain their owners'. Synthetic examples are **document examples**, not passing application tests.\n \n This revision designs the required contracts rather than deferring them to D. External-owner items (final D1 approval, the pending `REQ-TA-INV-014`/`REQ-TA-GOV-004` publication, C's tests/rubric, E's enforcement, instructor layout) remain explicitly pending.\n \n ---\n \n ## 1. Module map and ownership (addresses B3-10)\n \n Paths below **exist in the `a62b801` checkout** (verified 2026-11-24) except where marked *(existing)*. Ownership is by team role.\n \n | Planned path (new unless marked) | Responsibility | Owner (design / implement / test / enforce) |\n |---|---|---|\n | `tradingagents/runapi/__init__.py` | Package for the shared application boundary; **no `cli` import** | B / D / C / E |\n | `tradingagents/runapi/context.py` | `RunContext`, `FrozenSnapshot`, canonicalization, deep immutability | B / D / C / E |\n | `tradingagents/runapi/input_service.py` | `PortfolioInputService` (discover/precheck/freeze) — **noninteractive**, prompt-free | B / D / C / E |\n | `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py` | `OutputChecker` (Q1–Q4, deterministic) | B / D / C / E |\n | `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` | `RunResult`, `CheckResult`, findings, `InputError` schemas | B / D / C / E |\n | `tradingagents/runapi/finalize.py` | `OutcomeFinalizer`, exception mapping | B / D / C / E |\n | `tradingagents/runapi/persist.py` | Staging, commit, manifest, publication ordering | B / D / C / E |\n | `tradingagents/runapi/events.py` | JSONL `EventSink` | B / D / C / E |\n | `tradingagents/runapi/redact.py` | Central `Redactor` (sink boundary) | B / D / C / E |\n | `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py` | **Shared application entry service** `run_analysis_api(...)` (see §5) | B / D / C / E |\n | `cli/input_ui.py` | Interactive discovery/consent UI (prompts **only** here) | B / D / C / E |\n | `cli/main.py`, `cli/run.py` (existing) | Thin adapters: call `execution.run_analysis_api` with confirmed input | adapted |\n | `tradingagents/portfolio.py` (existing) | `PortfolioContext` model + `render`; upstream loader unchanged | preserved |\n | `tradingagents/agents/context.py`, manager/trader prompts (existing) | Mode-aware wording; no-portfolio Hold meaning | adapted |\n | `tradingagents/reporting.py`, `report_html.py` (existing) | Body rendering + final envelope header; projection-driven | adapted |\n \n **Dependency rule:** `cli/*` → `tradingagents/runapi/*` → (engine, agents, portfolio, reporting). `tradingagents/runapi/*` must **not** import `cli`. This keeps the shared boundary usable without a terminal (B3-01, B3-10).\n \n ---\n \n ## 2. Design types and canonicalization (addresses B3-02, B3-03)\n \n ### 2.1 `InputMode`\n ```\n InputMode = NO_PORTFOLIO | PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED\n ```\n - `NO_PORTFOLIO`: holdings/cash unknown; nothing assumed.\n - `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED`: an explicitly selected, validated, frozen snapshot. An explicitly supplied empty `positions` list is a **flat** snapshot, not missing input.\n \n ### 2.2 Canonical fingerprint bytes (B3-03, F2)\n The new provenance fingerprint is **SHA-256 (64 lowercase hex chars)** over a **canonical JSON byte string** of the normalized snapshot. Exact rules:\n \n 1. **Normalized object** contains exactly: `{\"cash\":…,\"currency\":…,\"positions\":[{\"ticker\":…,\"quantity\":…,\"average_price\":…}, …]}`. No other keys participate.\n 2. **Key order:** lexicographic ascending at every object level (`sort_keys=True`).\n 3. **Encoding:** UTF-8, **no BOM**, **no trailing newline**; bytes are `json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(\",\", \":\"), ensure_ascii=False).encode(\"utf-8\")`.\n 4. **Separators:** `,` and `:` with **no whitespace** (`separators=(\",\", \":\")`).\n 5. **String escaping:** JSON string escaping only (`ensure_ascii=False`, so non-ASCII tickers are emitted as UTF-8, not `\\uXXXX`); no additional escaping. Tickers are trimmed and uppercased before serialization.\n 6. **Null/default handling:** an absent optional field and an explicit JSON `null` are the **same** and are serialized as the JSON token `null` (`average_price`, `cash`, `currency`).\n 7. **Number-token serialization (exact):** every numeric field is first converted by `to_canonical_number(x)`:\n    - reject non-finite (`NaN`/`±Inf`) at validation (never reach canonicalization);\n    - normalize `-0.0` to `0.0`;\n    - if the value is integral and `|x| < 2**53`, emit the **integer token** (e.g., `10`, `1`, `0`), so `1` and `1.0` → token `1`;\n    - otherwise emit Python `float.__repr__` (shortest round-trippable decimal, e.g., `150.5`, `0.1`).\n    This defines the exact byte token; it is not \"whatever JSON does\".\n 8. **Positions sort — total order (no `None`/float comparison):** sort the canonical **row objects** by the composite key `(ticker_upper, to_canonical_number(quantity), price_key)` where `price_key = (0, 0.0)` when `average_price is None` and `(1, to_canonical_number(average_price))` otherwise (a tagged tuple: null sorts **before** any number; numeric compares numerically). Because `ticker_upper` is a string and is part of the key, **two different broker spellings that normalize to the same symbol but differ in spelling sort by their hashed spelling**, and a full-row tie is impossible unless all three hashed fields are equal (identical rows are interchangeable, so input order cannot change the digest). This is a **total order over every field that participates in the digest**, so reordering input never changes the digest and no valid portfolio is rejected by sorting.\n 9. **Symbol spelling:** `ticker` is hashed using the **original spelling** as supplied (trimmed, uppercased). Holdings keep their spelling (`portfolio.py:40-68`); alias matching is a runtime concern, not identity. Two files differing only by broker alias spelling are **different** provenance and therefore **different** digests (both are accepted; ordering above remains total).\n 10. **Excluded fields:** `basename`, filesystem path, mtime, `portfolio_as_of`, `as_of_basis`, `mode` are recorded separately in metadata, **not** in the content digest.\n \n > Invariant: INV-05. Upstream truncated 12-char checkpoint fingerprint (`portfolio.py:70-72`, `trading_graph.py:158`) is **preserved unchanged** and unrelated to this digest.\n \n #### 2.2.1 Exact canonical-byte examples (verified against the rules above)\n Row order after sorting is shown; bytes are exactly the string inside quotes.\n \n - **Reason A — null vs numeric price (reversed input):**\n   - Input `[(\"AAPL\",10,None),(\"AAPL\",10,2.0)]` and reversed `[(\"AAPL\",10,2.0),(\"AAPL\",10,None)]` both serialize to\n     `{\"cash\":null,\"currency\":null,\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":null,\"quantity\":10,\"ticker\":\"AAPL\"},{\"average_price\":2,\"quantity\":10,\"ticker\":\"AAPL\"}]}` → **equal digest** (null sorts before numeric; `10`/`2` are integer tokens).\n - **Reason B — broker-alias tie (reversed input):**\n   - Input `[(\"BRK.B\",5,100.0),(\"BRK-B\",5,100.0)]` and reversed both serialize to\n     `{\"cash\":null,\"currency\":null,\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":100,\"quantity\":5,\"ticker\":\"BRK-B\"},{\"average_price\":100,\"quantity\":5,\"ticker\":\"BRK.B\"}]}` → **equal digest** (`\"BRK-B\"` < `\"BRK.B\"`; spelling is part of the sort key). Reindexing the **spelling** (e.g., `BRK.B`→`BRK-B` on the other row) is a **different** portfolio by rule 9 and yields a different digest.\n - **Reason C — numeric `1` vs `1.0`:**\n   - `[(\"MSFT\",1,50)]` cash `1` and `[(\"MSFT\",1.0,50.0)]` cash `1.0` both serialize to\n     `{\"cash\":1,\"currency\":null,\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":50,\"quantity\":1,\"ticker\":\"MSFT\"}]}` → **equal digest**.\n - **Reason D — missing vs explicit null:** a position with absent `average_price` and one with explicit `null` serialize identically (`\"average_price\":null`) → **equal digest**.\n - **Reason E — full example with cash:** `[(\"AAPL\",10,150.5),(\"MSFT\",5,None)]`, cash `2500.0`, currency `\"USD\"` →\n   `{\"cash\":2500,\"currency\":\"USD\",\"positions\":[{\"average_price\":150.5,\"quantity\":10,\"ticker\":\"AAPL\"},{\"average_price\":null,\"quantity\":5,\"ticker\":\"MSFT\"}]}`\n   → SHA-256 `45f07d9eb3359b059525da0cee26f8a9810269dad11ffb4c42e1dcc7072cef72`.\n - **Expected difference:** changing `quantity` from `10` to `10.5`, adding a position, or altering cash/currency changes the digest.\n \n These are **document examples** checked against the written rules, not passing application tests.\n \n ### 2.3 Deep immutability (B3-03)\n Upstream `PortfolioContext` holds a mutable `list[Position]` of mutable model instances. `RunContext` immutability alone is insufficient. Design:\n \n - The frozen snapshot is stored as **immutable value tuples**:\n   ```\n   FrozenPositions = tuple[tuple[str, float, float | None], ...]   # (ticker, quantity, average_price)\n   FrozenSnapshot = (basename, cash: float|None, currency: str|None,\n                     positions: FrozenPositions, fingerprint_sha256, portfolio_as_of)\n   ```\n - `RunContext` is a frozen dataclass holding these tuples; it exposes **no mutable accessor**.\n - When agents need a `PortfolioContext`, the boundary **constructs a fresh `PortfolioContext`** from the frozen tuples (defensive copy) on each use; it never hands out a shared mutable object. Mutation of that constructed object cannot affect the stored identity.\n - The canonical bytes are computed from the frozen tuples, so they are stable regardless of later copies.\n \n ### 2.4 `RunContext`\n ```\n RunContext (frozen dataclass) {\n   run_id: str\n   ticker: str\n   analysis_date: str\n   mode: InputMode\n   snapshot: FrozenSnapshot | None      # None ⇔ NO_PORTFOLIO\n   unverified_holdings: bool\n   provider_transmission_disclosed: bool\n   consent_state: FROZEN | CONFIRMED    # see §4\n }\n ```\n `snapshot is None` **iff** `mode == NO_PORTFOLIO`. `consent_state=FROZEN` ⇒ run not authorized; a snapshot existing does **not** authorize (B3-01, §4).\n \n ---\n \n ## 3. Complete schemas and conditional fields (addresses B3-02)\n \n All projections below are **separately defined** and **never** serialize the portfolio payload or full `RunContext`. Field names use the selected spelling.\n \n ### 3.1 `InputError`\n ```\n InputError {\n   kind: \"MALFORMED_JSON\" | \"MISSING_POSITIONS\" | \"MISSING_QUANTITY\" | \"NONFINITE_NUMBER\"\n         | \"WRONG_SCALAR_TYPE\" | \"UNREADABLE_PATH\" | \"AS_OF_MISMATCH\" | \"FLAG_CONFLICT\"\n   basename: str | null          # null when path unreadable before basename known\n   field: str | null             # e.g. \"positions[2].quantity\"\n   detail: str                   # redacted, no file contents/credentials\n }\n ```\n \n ### 3.2 `Finding`\n ```\n Finding {\n   rule: \"Q1\" | \"Q2\" | \"Q3\" | \"Q4\" | \"CHECK_ERROR\"\n   status: \"BLOCKING\"\n   detail: str                   # redacted\n }\n ```\n \n ### 3.3 `CheckResult` (F3 — case table)\n ```\n CheckResult {\n   output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\"\n   findings: Finding[]\n }\n ```\n Authoritative case table (**checker is invoked only on the completed path**, §6):\n \n | Case | `output_check` | `findings` | When |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | All rules hold | `PASSED` | `[]` (exactly empty) | Completed run; Q1–Q4 all hold |\n | Any rule broken OR checker exception | `NEEDS_REVIEW` | **≥ 1** blocking finding (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4, or a single `CHECK_ERROR` on exception) | Completed run |\n | Run incomplete | `NOT_RUN` | `[]` (exactly empty) | Checker **not invoked**; assigned by finalizer branch (§6) |\n \n Invariants (H2 — empty-findings equivalence qualified to **completed** runs): **Completed** ⇒ `PASSED ⇔ findings==[]` and `NEEDS_REVIEW ⇒ findings≠[]`; **Incomplete** ⇒ `NOT_RUN` with `findings==[]` (checker not invoked). There is no global `PASSED ⇔ findings==[]` — `NOT_RUN` also has empty findings.\n \n ### 3.4 `RunResult` (returned to caller)\n ```\n RunResult {\n   run_id: str\n   ticker: str\n   analysis_date: str\n   input_mode: InputMode\n   run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\"\n   stop_reason: null | \"MODEL_FAILURE\" | \"DATA_FAILURE\" | \"INTERNAL_ERROR\"\n                | \"PERSISTENCE_ERROR\" | \"INTERRUPTED\"\n   final_rating: null | \"Buy\" | \"Overweight\" | \"Hold\" | \"Underweight\" | \"Sell\" | \"REVIEW\"\n   output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\"\n   findings: Finding[]\n   manifest_path: str | null     # non-null iff the run directory was published (§7)\n   report_path: str | null       # non-null iff the report was published (§7)\n }\n ```\n **Conditional fields (enforced by finalizer):**\n - `COMPLETED` ⇒ `final_rating != null` and `stop_reason == null`.\n - `INCOMPLETE` ⇒ `final_rating == null`, `output_check == \"NOT_RUN\"`, `findings == []`, `stop_reason != null`.\n \n ### 3.5 Safe input metadata projection (for sinks; never the payload)\n ```\n SafeInputMetadata {\n   run_id, ticker, analysis_date,\n   input_mode: InputMode,\n   basename: str | null,                 # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n   fingerprint_sha256: str | null,       # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO (64 hex)\n   portfolio_as_of: str | null,          # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n   as_of_basis: \"USER_CONFIRMED\" | null  # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO\n }\n ```\n The `null` conditions are **portfolio-only** (mode-dependent); distinct from **outcome-conditional** `RunResult` fields.\n \n ### 3.6 `SafeRunMetadata` (durable run record; never the payload) — F3\n ```\n SafeRunMetadata {\n   schema_version: \"1\",\n   run_id, ticker, analysis_date, input_mode,\n   basename: str|null, fingerprint_sha256: str|null, portfolio_as_of: str|null, as_of_basis: \"USER_CONFIRMED\"|null,\n   run_outcome: \"COMPLETED\" | \"INCOMPLETE\",\n   stop_reason: ... | null,               # §3.4 conditional\n   final_rating: ... | null,              # §3.4 conditional — NOW CARRIED IN THE DURABLE RECORD\n   output_check: \"PASSED\" | \"NEEDS_REVIEW\" | \"NOT_RUN\",\n   findings: Finding[],\n   code_version: str,                     # tradingagents.__version__\n   source_revision: str | null,           # separate source identifier, e.g. git describe or \"unknown\" (§3.7)\n   prompt_hash: str,                      # §3.8\n   effective_config: EffectiveConfig,     # §3.7\n   start_ts_utc: str, end_ts_utc: str     # ISO-8601 UTC; set once at finalize\n }\n ```\n The **same** `final_rating` spelling/conditional rules as `RunResult` apply. Timestamps are captured once at finalize and are never mutated later.\n \n ### 3.7 `EffectiveConfig` (safe, behaviour-relevant; secrets/endpoints omitted) — F3\n ```\n EffectiveConfig {\n   llm_provider, deep_think_provider, deep_think_llm, quick_think_provider, quick_think_llm,\n   analysts: str[], max_debate_rounds: int, max_risk_discuss_rounds: int,\n   output_language: str,\n   temperature: float | null, max_tokens: int | null,          # behaviour-affecting (baseline keys if set)\n   context_cap_tokens: int, compaction_threshold_tokens: int,  # the designed context budget (ADR §Context)\n   concise_intermediate_reports: bool,                         # concise-mode flag (feature 9102759); see §3.11/§3.8\n   data_vendors: map, tool_vendors: map\n }\n ```\n Derived from `run_settings()` (`trading_graph.py:255-275`) **plus** the behaviour-affecting keys this design introduces (`temperature`, `max_tokens`, context cap/threshold, and the concise-mode flag). `backend_url`, keys, OAuth tokens, local paths are **never** included. `source_revision` is recorded **separately** from `code_version` (upstream `version` stays `0.7.1`; the revision id identifies the actual source state and is `\"unknown\"` when unavailable).\n \n - **Concise-mode recording (integrated at `adb4dfc`):** the flag is recorded in `run_settings()` and `_effective_config()` with default `True`. An **old artifact that lacks the field** must NOT be read as having run with today's `True` default; absence is `unknown/legacy`, not `False` and not `True`. Do not infer historical mode from a missing field.\n - **Mode is recorded separately from `prompt_hash`** (§3.8): the flag itself does not enter the hash material, but the feature's prompt-source edits do.\n \n ### 3.8 `prompt_hash` (deterministic input spec) — reconciled to the actual implementation\n \n The implemented `_prompt_hash` (`tradingagents/runapi/execution.py`) hashes **selected source-file contents plus frozen strings**, not an extracted active runtime template/legend variant:\n \n - **Inventory:** a fixed, selected set of prompt/source files — `agents/structured.py`, `agents/analysts/turn.py`, `portfolio.py`, `agents/context.py`, `agents/managers/research_manager.py`, `agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py`, `agents/trader/trader.py`, `agents/researchers/bull_researcher.py`, `agents/researchers/bear_researcher.py`, `agents/risk_mgmt/aggressive_debator.py`, `agents/risk_mgmt/conservative_debator.py`, `agents/risk_mgmt/neutral_debator.py`, plus the registered source file for each **selected** analyst (`market → agents/analysts/market_analyst.py`, `social → agents/analysts/sentiment_analyst.py`, `news → agents/analysts/news_analyst.py`, `fundamentals → agents/analysts/fundamentals_analyst.py`), plus the two frozen strings `frozen.disclaimer` (`DISCLAIMER`) and `frozen.no_portfolio_notice` (`NO_PORTFOLIO_NOTICE`). Identifiers such as `agents/context.py` are **relative to the `tradingagents` package directory** (the implementation resolves them as `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / relative`); **their exact strings are preserved** in the hash material.\n - **Source reading:** contents are read with `Path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")`, which opens in text mode and therefore applies **universal-newline translation** (`CRLF` and lone `CR` are translated to `LF` in the returned `str`). The returned text is hashed as-is; the implementation performs **no additional stripping or newline cleanup** beyond that text-mode translation. Characters already in the returned text remain included (no separate BOM removal or newline insertion outside the literal construction below).
