        "file": "docs/architecture/proposals/implementation-prompt-pack-2026-11-24.md",
        "patch": "Index: docs/architecture/proposals/implementation-prompt-pack-2026-11-24.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/architecture/proposals/implementation-prompt-pack-2026-11-24.md\t\n+++ docs/architecture/proposals/implementation-prompt-pack-2026-11-24.md\t\n@@ -1,280 +1,281 @@\n # Staged implementation prompt pack (Member B) — UNEXECUTED TEMPLATES\n \n Status: **unexecuted templates, 2026-11-24; approval-protocol status reconciled 2026-11-25.** These are drafting artifacts for a *future* implementation handoff. **Architecture approval does not authorize code implementation.** Each slice's execution plan and test criteria still require prior human approval before any build, and the model-provider access constraint is stated below. No template here has been run; no code, tests, approvals or results are claimed.\n \n > **Approval-protocol status (reconciled with root `AGENTS.md`).** Root `AGENTS.md` states that **test-plan pre-approval is paused as a required merge check** by the user's instruction. The `/approve-tests <SHA>` receipt protocol described in Template 2 below is therefore **inactive/historical for current use** — it can still run and show a result, but it must **not** be imposed as a mandatory prerequisite for the current development workflow, and it must **not** be reactivated until explicitly instructed. What remains required today: **human supervision, explicit authorization for any commit/PR/build, and defined proposed test criteria** (Templates 1/4/5). The receipt workflow is preserved as a documented, executable mechanism for a possible later re-enable; **no prior approval may be fabricated** and the paused-policy gap must be recorded separately, not erased. This reconciliation changes no requirement, course obligation, or runtime contract.\n \n Scope of these templates: the prioritised slices in [interface-contracts.md](../interface-contracts.md) §13–§16 and [ADR 002](../adr/002-extended-result-evidence-budget.md):\n - **Slice C — run budget controller + `BUDGET`** (first handoff; §15).\n - **Slice A — evidence & coverage** (§13).\n - **Slice B — output-check v2 R1–R8** (§14).\n \n **Model access constraint (access, not a mandate).** As of drafting, DeepSeek V4 Flash is the only model available to Member B's OpenCode work via the school API key. This is an access constraint for this implementation route; it is **not** a course requirement, an evaluated model choice, or a restriction on TradingAgents' inherited provider capabilities. No model comparison or model-saving claim is made. **No credentials belong in any prompt or document**; provide keys only through the environment, never pasted into a prompt.\n \n **Baseline to cite in every prompt (verify before use):** repository `Le-kk/CS5351`; recorded local revision for this planning pack `a62b801a51e6310f3b46860f6d2790583a95e0e0` (or the then-current integration HEAD named by E). Read `docs/req/requirements.yaml` (`schema_version 1.2.0`, `proposed_for_adoption`), `docs/req/selected-requirements.md`, the named architecture contracts, and `docs/reviews/project-integration-review-2026-11-24.md`.\n \n ---\n \n ## Template 1 — Read-only planning prompt\n \n Copy the block for the chosen slice. This stage **must not modify files**.\n \n ```\n You are planning (NOT implementing) a bounded change in the CS5351 TradingAgents\n repository. READ-ONLY: do not edit, create, delete, commit, push, pull, switch\n branches, reset or stash. Do not read .env, credentials, provider auth stores, or\n private raw transcripts. Do not run paid/live model tests.\n \n Slice: <C_budget | A_evidence_coverage | B_checker_v2>\n Baseline revision to inspect: <integration HEAD; planning pack used a62b801...>\n \n Read first:\n - docs/req/requirements.yaml (schema_version 1.2.0, status proposed_for_adoption) — note\n   <REQ-TA-... IDs for this slice>; treat status/priority as A owns meaning.\n - docs/req/selected-requirements.md (implemented baseline scope).\n - docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md §<13|14|15> and §16.\n - docs/architecture/adr/002-extended-result-evidence-budget.md.\n - docs/architecture/invariants.md, runtime-policy-catalog.md (namespaces!).\n - The REAL source seams for this slice:\n     C_budget: tradingagents/runapi/{result.py,finalize.py,execution.py},\n       agents/structured.py, memory/settlement.py, graph memory step,\n       llm_clients/factory.py, runapi/reporting.py, report/manifest validators.\n     A_evidence_coverage: tradingagents/dataflows/router.py (+ the two router\n       bypass call sites), runapi/{persist.py,execution.py}.\n     B_checker_v2: tradingagents/runapi/{checks.py,result.py,reporting.py},\n       agents/schemas.py (SentimentReport); tests/member_c_verification/... for seam style.\n \n Produce a PLAN ONLY:\n 1. Component/module boundary and exact proposed file paths (new vs edited).\n 2. Interface signatures + field-level contracts (nullability + authority).\n 3. Normal sequence and state transitions.\n 4. Failure, concurrency, retry, privacy, persistence policies.\n 5. Compatibility/migration (schemas, readers, version gates).\n 6. Proposed verification scenarios: inputs, expected outputs/counters, and >=1\n    violating negative per behaviour. Label them PROPOSED C inputs; do not claim\n    accepted test IDs or results.\n 7. Dependency order and the first handoff.\n 8. Open decisions and feasibility limits (label ESTIMATE).\n \n Do not propose changes outside this slice. Do not adopt requirements, declare\n gates enforced, or claim test results. End by listing every file you would touch.\n You may inspect code/tests read-only; do not run the suite or live tests.\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## Template 2 — Human checkpoint via the installed approval protocol\n \n This is a **human gate**. Sub-stage **(2a) prepare plan + proposed tests + human review** remains required. Sub-stage **(2b) the `/approve-tests` receipt protocol** is **inactive/historical for current use** (pre-approval is paused per `AGENTS.md`); it is documented as a possible later re-enable and must not be imposed as a mandatory prerequisite today. A filled chat block is **not** a workflow receipt, and no approval may be fabricated.\n \n ```\n 2a — AUTHORIZED PREPARATION (before product implementation)\n Produce, on a branch/commit (execution still requires your authorization; do not\n run during a documentation task):\n - One front-matter plan at  docs/verification/plans/<feature-id>.md  with the\n   REQUIRED fields read by scripts/ci/check_test_approval.py:\n     feature_id, requirements[], implementation_paths[], test_files[], cases[],\n     pass_condition\n   Cases must include at least one each of kind: normal | boundary | error | security,\n   each with an explicit expected result.\n - The NAMED test files listed in test_files[] (proposed tests), committed in the\n   SAME commit as the plan. Their file fingerprints are what the receipt binds.\n - implementation_paths[] = the exact approved write set (no vague categories).\n Reviewer reads the plan + proposed tests and records adequacy, incl. negatives.\n \n 2b — APPROVAL THROUGH THE TRUSTED WORKFLOW (not chat) — INACTIVE/HISTORICAL unless explicitly re-enabled\n - The authorized reviewer posts the EXACT comment command **on the OPEN FEATURE PR**\n   (its `issue_comment`; the workflow requires `github.event.issue.pull_request`):\n       /approve-tests <FULL 40-CHARACTER COMMIT SHA>\n   The comment must match exactly (a short SHA, extra text or an edited comment is\n   rejected). The SHA names the plan+test commit on that PR.\n - The trusted workflow (test-approval.yml -> test-approval-complete.yml) produces\n   a RECEIPT bound to the comment, the approved commit and the test-file\n   fingerprints. Archive the accepted record under docs/verification/approvals/.\n - **Unless re-enabled by explicit instruction, pre-approval is paused:** product implementation is gated on **explicit human authorization for this change**, not on the (inactive) receipt. If re-enabled, implementation starts only after a successful receipt for that commit.\n - **Approved test files are FROZEN during product implementation.** Do not edit\n   them to make implementation pass; changed test fingerprints are rejected. If a\n   test must change, use the policy's RENEWED / SPLIT-SCOPE procedure (re-approve\n   the new test commit) — never silently rewrite frozen tests.\n - Revocation uses /revoke-tests (a revocation receipt stays in force).\n - Self-approval is permitted but is labelled `self_review`; it is NOT independent\n   human acceptance. Retain actual reviewer attribution.\n \n Reviewer confirmations (recorded, not backdated):\n 1. Scope bounded; no edits to canonical requirements, other members' tests/CI/\n    evidence, or files outside implementation_paths[].\n 2. Test criteria adequate BEFORE implementation; a failing/violating test defined\n    before product code.\n 3. Result-contract/compat + version-gate plan acceptable.\n 4. Provider/model access constraint acknowledged; no credentials in any file.\n 5. One-slice approval does not approve other slices.\n \n Receipt reference to record:  approval_id: ______  approved_commit (40): ______\n NOTE: This gate approves PLAN + TESTS via the pinned receipt. It does not adopt\n requirements or certify verification. Any commit/PR/approval/archive action needs\n explicit authorization when executed and is not performed in a documentation task.\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## Template 3 — Build prompt (only after explicit human authorization; receipt gated only if re-enabled)\n \n ```\n You are implementing an APPROVED, bounded slice in CS5351 TradingAgents.\n Pre-approval is PAUSED (per AGENTS.md): proceed ONLY with EXPLICIT human\n authorization for this change. If the `/approve-tests` receipt protocol is\n re-enabled by instruction, also require a successful receipt for this exact\n commit (trusted workflow; `/approve-tests <FULL 40-CHAR SHA>` on the OPEN FEATURE\n PR; archived under docs/verification/approvals/) and reject absent/mismatched\n receipts or differing test-file fingerprints.\n APPROVED TEST FILES ARE FROZEN during implementation (when a plan/test set was\n approved): a needed test change uses the renewed/split-scope procedure, never a\n silent rewrite.\n Do not expand scope. Do not edit files outside the APPROVED implementation_paths[]\n from the plan. Do not touch canonical requirements, other members' tests/CI/\n evidence, or secrets. Work offline with the scripted/offline profile; no paid/live.\n \n Slice: <C_budget | A_evidence_coverage | B_checker_v2>\n-Approval receipt: approval_id ______  approved_commit (40) ______\n+Authorization: [REDACTED] human authorization ______ (required today)\n+Approval receipt: OPTIONAL/INACTIVE while paused — approval_id ______  approved_commit (40) ______ (fill only if `/approve-tests` is explicitly re-enabled)\n \n PERMITTED FILES = the EXACT implementation_paths[] from the approved plan plus the\n approved test_files[]. Do not use category names. The approved set must explicitly\n include every mandatory hook for the slice; if it does not, STOP and escalate\n (Template 5) rather than editing an unapproved file. Authoritative examples the\n plan must have covered (exact repo-relative paths):\n   C_budget (metering + budget): new tradingagents/runapi/budget.py;\n     tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py (attach controller to deep/quick llm at\n     :79-80; budget-aware _memory_step); tradingagents/agents/structured.py\n     (re-raise budget); tradingagents/memory/settlement.py (re-raise budget);\n     tradingagents/llm_clients/factory.py (force max_retries=0 in budget mode,\n     reject unsupported clients); tradingagents/runapi/result.py, finalize.py,\n     execution.py, reporting.py, persist.py (manifest), events.py (log fields).\n   A_evidence_coverage: new tradingagents/runapi/evidence.py, coverage.py;\n     tradingagents/dataflows/router.py; the direct-source call sites\n     tradingagents/agents/analysts/sentiment_analyst.py,\n     tradingagents/agents/context.py, tradingagents/agents/tools.py;\n     tradingagents/runapi/persist.py, execution.py.\n   B_checker_v2: tradingagents/runapi/checks.py, result.py, reporting.py;\n     tradingagents/agents/schemas.py (only if a field is required); manifest field\n     additions (separate schema_version vs check_rules_version).\n TESTS: named in the approved plan test_files[]; do not modify existing C-owned\n     tests unless the plan explicitly lists them (otherwise renewed/split-scope).\n \n MET/POINTS (budget): reserve() single-use atomic; dispatch() pairs GRANTED->CONSUMED;\n   invalidation never refunds cumulative admission (monotonic granted<=CALL_CAP);\n   wrap the run's deep/quick chat models so plain invoke, bind_tools(...).invoke and\n   with_structured_output(...).invoke each consume EXACTLY ONE reservation (no missed\n   or double charge); RunBudgetExhausted survives structured/settlement/memory broad\n   handlers; budget recognized BEFORE generic classification; PERSISTENCE_ERROR stays\n   primary over BUDGET. Do NOT claim a runtime metering guarantee before the\n   verification probes (B-variants) pass.\n \n ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (must hold; mirror the approved test list):\n   <paste the approved proposed scenarios for the slice (e.g. B1-B7 / E1-E12 / K1-K16)>\n   Each criterion needs a passing positive and at least one violating negative.\n   For the budget slice these MUST include the metering probes:\n     - plain llm.invoke -> exactly one reservation consumed\n     - llm.bind_tools(...).invoke -> exactly one reservation consumed\n     - llm.with_structured_output(...).invoke -> exactly one reservation consumed\n     - a path that would double-wrap/double-count is rejected by the probe\n     - structured/settlement/memory broad handlers do not swallow RunBudgetExhausted\n     - invalidate/reserve/re-reserve at cap is denied (monotonic admission)\n     - wrong-run / reuse of a reservation is rejected (BudgetProtocolError)\n \n SCOPE LIMITS:\n - No change to public engine signatures beyond what the slice requires; preserve\n   upstream tests where unaffected.\n - No new provider/model, no credentials, no live tests, no network.\n - Do not mark requirements satisfied, do not claim verification, do not adopt scope.\n - If a genuine ambiguity affects correctness, STOP and ask (see Template 5).\n \n DELIVERABLES: code + regression tests + a short note of exact commands run\n (offline) and their outcomes captured in the interaction. Do not commit/push.\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## Template 4 — Verification prompt (checks, outcomes, negatives, evidence)\n \n ```\n You are verifying an implemented, approved slice in CS5351. You are NOT the\n implementer. Verify against the approved plan and acceptance criteria. Do not\n modify application code or the implementation's tests to make them pass.\n \n Slice: <C_budget | A_evidence_coverage | B_checker_v2>\n-Approved plan/acceptance revision/hash: <from Template 2/3>\n+Approved plan/acceptance revision/hash: <from Template 2/3> (receipt only if `/approve-tests` re-enabled)\n \n CHECKS TO RUN (offline; scripted model; record exact commands + results):\n - Targeted slice tests, then the prior offline suite, Ruff, dependency and\n   whitespace checks. Use the project virtual environment; no paid/live calls.\n - Positive cases: each approved scenario passes.\n - NEGATIVE cases (must fail as designed):\n     C_budget: >CALL_CAP attempts admitted; exhaustion swallowed by fallback;\n       shared counter across runs; budget relabelled INTERNAL_ERROR; BUDGET stop\n       overriding a co-occurring persistence failure.\n     A_evidence_coverage: dangling cited ID passes; unrequested channel mislabelled\n       as gap; core-gap completes; coverage section differs under prose change.\n     B_checker_v2: CORRECTED treated as NEEDS_REVIEW; BLOCKING treated as PASSED;\n       Q2 and R2 conflated; R3 phrase downgraded to corrected; model \"PASSED\" text\n       overriding a blocking rule.\n - Compatibility: a reader that enumerates old StopReason / old finding status\n   fails closed on the new value (not silent coercion); schema_version behavior.\n \n EXPECTED OUTCOMES: state precisely per case (counters, fields, status, stop_reason,\n output_check, paths null/not-null). Compare to the approved criteria; do not relax.\n \n EVIDENCE TO RETAIN: the exact commands, stdout/exit codes, the new/changed test\n files (paths), and any captured manifests/events for the positive and negative\n runs. Do not overwrite existing retained evidence; write to a new path if live is\n ever used (it is not in this template). Distinguish test DEFINITION, developer\n diagnostic and independent acceptance.\n \n VERDICT: report PASS/FAIL/PENDING per criterion with the evidence path. This is a\n verification recommendation; independent acceptance remains C's recorded decision.\n Do not claim team adoption or requirement satisfaction.\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## Template 5 — Review and escalation conditions\n \n ```\n STOP AND ESCALATE (to the human approver / B / C) if any of the following occurs;\n do not silently work around it:\n \n 1. A required change falls OUTSIDE the permitted file set (Template 3).\n 2. A genuine ambiguity or conflicting contract affects correctness (e.g. channel\n    map or bypass indices unknown; whether BUDGET is retained; R5/R3 scope unresolved;\n    resume identity). Surface it; do not decide A/C/team scope.\n 3. A negative test cannot be made to fail as designed (criterion unmet).\n 4. The result-contract/compat change would break an existing reader without a\n    version gate; propose the gate, do not weaken validation.\n 5. A failure would tempt relabelling a stop reason, hiding an attempt, skipping a\n    gate, or editing retained evidence to go green.\n 6. Any request to edit canonical requirements, other members' files/tests/CI/\n    evidence, or to run paid/live tests.\n 7. Provider/model access: if the only available model for this route cannot satisfy\n    the offline/scripted requirement or would require credentials in a file, stop.\n \n REVIEW EXPECTATIONS:\n - Implementer and verifier are different people where practical.\n - The verifier reproduces original negatives with black-box/synthetic probes, not\n   only the implementer's new tests.\n - All chronology (plan approval -> tests -> implementation -> verification) is\n   recorded in the authentic interaction; nothing is backdated.\n - Historical F8 stays unverified; current acceptance is a separate result.\n \n On escalation: state the concrete choice, the options, the impact and the exact\n minimum approval needed. Do not proceed past the approved scope without it.\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## Template usage notes (human, not agent)\n \n - Run per slice; do not bundle all three into one unapproved mega-change.\n - **First handoff = Slice C (budget + BUDGET)** (interface-contracts §16.1): most isolated, offline-testable, unblocks a Must plus `BUDGET`.\n - **Evidence/coverage data contracts (Slice A §13) must be agreed before** Slice B's R2/R7 checker integration (approved dependency order).\n - These are **unexecuted templates**: no build, test, approval or result has occurred. Each single in a new interaction with **explicit human authorization**; the (currently **paused**) `/approve-tests <full 40-char SHA>` receipt protocol (Template 2b) is preserved as inactive/historical and applies only if explicitly re-enabled.\n - **Do not claim a runtime metering guarantee** (or any \"exactly once\" property) before the verification probes pass; before that, ≤1-attempt intent and the tests are the only evidence.\n - Preserve authentic interactions for D5; do not backdate approvals; a handoff summary is not a raw transcript.\n",

        "deletions": 2,
        "status": "modified"

        "file": "docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md",
        "patch": "Index: docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md\t\n+++ docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md\t\n@@ -1,144 +1,144 @@\n # Traceability Inputs — Member B (for E)\n \n Status: **revised 2026-11-24** (implementation-aligned). This is B's contribution of component/invariant/runtime-monitor rows for E's shared `trace-matrix.md`. B does **not** publish a competing final matrix (E owns assembly). Where relevant, show that a planted violation is detected and the valid control passes; keep planted defects in isolated synthetic workspaces, never merge them.\n36: \n37: Run suitable existing regression coverage as well. Do not weaken assertions, hide failures with skips or alter frozen evidence to make a change appear green. Intended requirement changes need explicit authorization and updated expectations; do not silently turn an observed defect into the new contract. Follow C's [verification constraints](../docs/code-governance/verification-constraints.md), reading its superseding notices before historical PASS claims.\n38: \n39: If permissions prevent the test command, hand the exact command to an authorized human/session. Mark it not run until its actual result is available. Report passes, failures, skips, incomplete audits and environmental errors separately. Independent acceptance remains a separate claim from developer regression results.\n40: \n41: ## 4. Safety-critical changes and approval\n42: \n43: Safety-critical scope includes consent and input immutability, portfolio mode/provenance, check/result authority, privacy/redaction, publication/durability, credential/network/model-dispatch boundaries, budget admission, authentication/permissions, dependency exceptions and CI/protection changes. A change to this covenant or the operating rules is a governance change and must not become a way to self-authorize weaker protections.\n44: \n45: Before applying a safety-critical change, establish a concrete authorized scope. Existing explicit user authorization can supply this; do not ask again merely because the file is governed. An agent cannot manufacture human authorization or treat green CI as approval. A materially new privilege, external side effect or scope extension outside that authorization requires an authorized human decision before that step.\n46: \n47: Before presenting a safety-critical change as accepted or ready for merge/deployment, retain a reviewable record containing:\n48: \n49: 1. The affected requirement/contract, changed paths and exact source revision (including dirty-state limits where applicable).\n50: 2. The risk and before/after behavior, with the affected B boundary/ADR; add/update an ADR when a genuine architecture or safety decision changes.\n51: 3. Relevant valid/negative tests, regression results, limitations and independent acceptance status.\n52: 4. The authorized human's decision/reference and actual reviewer identity, accurately labelled self-review or peer review. A decision made before the final change only covers its recorded scope; material later changes need renewed review.\n53: 5. Rollback or safe fallback, and unresolved risks/owners. Identify the prior usable configuration/revision; do not reset unrelated work during rollback.\n54: \n55: Use the existing PR/review evidence mechanisms or a linked retained decision record; this covenant introduces no compulsory new receipt format or fictitious sign-off. A's adoption, B's design interpretation, C's independent acceptance and E's governance integration remain distinct responsibilities; only affected roles need to contribute their actual decision/evidence.\n56: \n57: **Current enforcement:** required CI checks still apply. Test-plan pre-approval is paused as a required merge check; this covenant does not reinstate `/approve-tests`, add mandatory GitHub peer Reviews or change self-review/merge permissions. Safety review and independent-negative-test obligations here are recorded process requirements; this file does not automatically enforce reviewer identity, prior approval or review completeness in GitHub. Record any unmet obligation as pending rather than claim full course compliance. See the [self-review workflow](../docs/code-governance/self-review-workflow.md) and actual repository settings for what is enforced.\n58: \n59: ## 5. Rule freshness and conflicts\n60: \n61: E reviews the covenant and its linked rules when requirements/adoption, architecture/interfaces, data/model flows, role permissions, dependency policy, tool version, verification criteria or merge checks change, and again before final delivery. This is change-triggered review; a date alone does not prove freshness.\n62: \n63: For each relevant change, check the actual source layout and active configuration, follow links, compare the current CI/branch-protection evidence and update the affected rule/document together. Preserve dated baselines and original evidence. Do not copy old test counts, tool versions, requirement status or historical approvals into a new release as current facts without rechecking them.\n64: \n65: Maintain the revision/date/reference above and a concise change record below. A contradiction must be resolved against higher-priority instructions, current source and the relevant owner's decision; record the discrepancy and do not silently select the weaker rule. Historical documents can remain authentic with a dated superseding correction rather than rewritten history. Requirements IDs from different namespaces are mapped by meaning, not suffix.\n66: \n67: The permission configuration must allow A–E to read this covenant and only E to write it by default. Its availability is not automatic prompt injection or a new security sandbox: the root startup instructions require reading it, while native tool permissions control access. Rule freshness and human review are not currently certified by a dedicated CI gate. If a new enforcer is later added, verify actual loading, allowed/denied examples and live protection separately.\n68: \n69: ## 6. Evidence and handoff\n70: \n71: Important changes require the applicable AI-use log update. Retain selected original user requests/public assistant replies, changed-file summaries, actual commands/results, relevant source/configuration hashes and review references. Omit secrets, internal reasoning and full write payloads; label omissions. Do not forge transcripts, fabricate citations or overwrite a failure with a pass. A Q1–Q4 pass does not imply factual, semantic or independent acceptance.\n72: \n73: Handoff must state changed files/purpose, observed verification, unexecuted checks, acceptance/approval gaps and the next owner/action. Use the root architecture-blueprint.md, B's interface contracts/invariants and docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md. Distinguish current source, proposed design and historical evidence.\n- Preserve the shared application boundary: CLI interaction stays in cli/; runapi must not import cli. Shared engine/agent services must not introduce terminal prompts. Root main.py/raw graph primitives are not substitutes for the full audited entry.\n- Keep vendor access behind dataflow services; do not introduce direct vendor-library imports into agents. Keep trusted input, deterministic checks, finalization, reporting and publication responsibilities in their owning components.\n\n## Inputs, output and privacy\n\n- Never browse or disclose credentials, environment files, private holdings or unrelated home-directory material. Do not follow symlinks to escape scope. Use only sanitized fixtures in examples and evidence.\n- Preserve explicit consent and the single frozen input snapshot; do not silently select another portfolio, reread it after freeze or infer trusted provenance from model prose.\n- NO_PORTFOLIO means unknown holdings/cash; an explicitly empty supplied portfolio is a known flat book. Do not invent positions, cash, verified prices or evidence.\n- Preserve deterministic result/check authority and coherent terminal/publication outcomes. A Q1–Q4 PASSED result does not certify factual or semantic correctness. External failure is not proof of absent market activity.\n- Keep secrets and raw portfolio details out of reports, logs, events, diagnostics and committed artifacts. Route new sinks through the applicable sanitization/publication boundary.\n\n## Changes and verification\n\n- Make the smallest complete task-scoped change. Do not weaken, delete or skip tests/checks to hide failures. Intentional public API or contract changes need coordinated fixtures, documentation and recorded review.\n- Follow the current permissions.jsonc and capability manifest. Shell, broad search, delegation and external tools are denied in strict role sessions; do not use file tools to recreate a prohibited interpreter, command runner or network channel.\n- Use the existing verification commands and coverage limits in AGENTS.md. When a required command cannot run in this profile, give the human the command and mark it not run until actual output is available.\n- Report exact passes, failures, skips, incomplete audits and environment limitations separately. Never fabricate commands, outputs, commits, approvals, citations or model measurements. Developer probes are not independent acceptance.\n- Do not run paid/live diagnostics without task authorization. Token comparisons must retain the six fixed settings; measured savings are not proof of an enforced run-wide budget.\n- Preserve existing required CI checks and branch protection. Test-plan pre-approval remains paused as a required merge check; do not reactivate it or impose approval commands without explicit user instruction. Ordinary tests do not constitute live semantic acceptance.\n\n## Evidence and handoff\n\n- Important changes require an AI-log update under the assigned member's log area. Preserve selected original user questions and public assistant replies; omit internal reasoning and full write payloads, label omissions and summarize changed files/amounts.\n- Preserve authentic evidence and approval history; add dated corrections rather than rewrite past results. Do not claim another member has adopted, reviewed or accepted a change without evidence.\n- Finish with changed files/purpose, actual verification, remaining gaps and next required action. Do not claim a file is committed, pushed, merged or a gate enabled from local creation alone.",

Do not fabricate approvals, change a failed historical result into a pass, weaken tests to hide failures, or commit credentials/private account data. E coordinates governance integration; this does not automatically grant administrative rights to an agent or other roles.\n\nUse normal Git/hosting interfaces; preserve unrelated work. No destructive reset, force-push, protection changes, administrative bypass or publication is authorized merely by this inventory. Do not expose credential-bearing remote URLs. Respect required checks and do not impersonate another member's approval.\n\n### DEV-LIVE — External data and model diagnostics\n\nCapabilities: run project data/model clients for explicitly authorized diagnostics and measurements. D normally owns implementation experiments; C owns independent acceptance; other roles can perform task-authorized probes with provenance retained. Use configured credentials through the client without printing or committing values. Minimize transmitted private context and record the tested configuration, source revision, outcomes and unavailable-data limitations.\n\nThese are opt-in network/cost-bearing operations, not default documentation checks. A model response is evidence to evaluate, not permission to edit files or a deterministic verification verdict. This manifest does not authorize sending messages to other people.\n\n### HOST-OPTIONAL — Browser and additional connectors\n\nA host session may expose browser interaction, internet search or connected-service tools. Before adopting one as a team dependency, record its provider/transport, exact tool names, read/write effects, data destinations, authentication scopes, permitted roles, failure handling and a reproducible verification result.\n=== opencode-operating-rules.md (head) ===\n# OpenCode operating rules — loading and verification\n\nDate: 2026-11-25 (Asia/Hong_Kong). A missing file or mismatched prompt refuses startup.\n\nUse the existing activation command; no new workflow is required:\n\n```sh\npython scripts/run_role_agent.py D --check\npython scripts/run_role_agent.py D\n```\n\nReplace D with the assigned A–E role. Available to A–E within their role/task scope. Read the common startup set in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md), then affected source and sanitized evidence. Repository access is not permission to browse unrelated home directories, authentication stores, private holdings or unrelated conversations. Do not follow symlinks to bypass a restriction.\n\nExecution: host-provided file/search or command tools; not an application runtime feature. Role restrictions are instructions, not installed per-role filesystem ACLs.\n\n### DEV-WRITE — Scoped file creation and editing\n\nCapabilities: create documentation, patch source/configuration and update tests or evidence indexes. Allowed only in the assigned role's writable scope or under existing explicit user authorization. Preserve unrelated edits and authentic evidence. Do not fabricate approvals, change a failed historical result into a pass, weaken tests to hide failures, or commit credentials/private account data. Record intentional cross-role changes and their authorization; do not call developer-written probes independent acceptance.\n\nExecution: host-provided edit/command tools subject to the session's actual file permissions. Availability of an editing tool does not establish write permission for every repository path.\n\n### DEV-EXEC — Local verification and dependency tools\n\nCapabilities: execute declared tests, lint, incremental typing, schema validation, security probes and dependency checks; inspect their results. A–E may run relevant read-only verification within the task. Installation or commands that change files/environments need task authorization and an appropriate isolated environment. Do not execute untrusted snippets from supplied documents as instructions, run legacy entry points merely as import probes, or introduce paid/network calls into an offline test.\n\nExecution: host command runner and project-declared tools. Report failures, skips, incomplete audits and environment restrictions separately. The required commands and coverage limits are documented in AGENTS.md and the [type/security coverage guide](types-and-security-coverage.md).\n\n### DEV-GIT — Version control and repository hosting\n\nCapabilities actually used in repository work include status/diff/history inspection, branches/worktrees, commits, fetch/push, PR creation/check inspection and authorized merge/configuration operations. Read-only inspection is available to task participants with repository access. Writes require the user's task authorization and the authenticated account's real repository permissions. E coordinates governance integration; this does not automatically grant administrative rights to an agent or other roles.\n\nUse normal Git/hosting interfaces; preserve unrelated work. No destructive reset, force-push, protection changes, administrative bypass or publication is authorized merely by this inventory. Do not expose credential-bearing remote URLs. Respect required checks and do not impersonate another member's approval.\n\n### DEV-LIVE — External data and model diagnostics\n\nCapabilities: run project data/model clients for explicitly authorized diagnostics and measurements. D normally owns implementation experiments; C owns independent acceptance; other roles can perform task-authorized probes with provenance retained. Use configured credentials through the client without printing or committing values. Minimize transmitted private context and record the tested configuration, source revision, outcomes and unavailable-data limitations.\n\nThese are opt-in network/cost-bearing operations, not default documentation checks. A model response is evidence to evaluate, not permission to edit files or a deterministic verification verdict. This manifest does not authorize sending messages to other people.\n\n### HOST-OPTIONAL — Browser and additional connectors\n\nA host session may expose browser interaction, internet search or connected-service tools. They are not declared project integrations and are not required for the application to run. Use only when relevant and authorized; respect the connected account's actual scopes. No specific server, connector, persistent credential, role assignment or successful use is certified here. System and deployment boundaries\n \n - **Runtime:** a single local Python process. The user interacts through the terminal (the existing CLI). No network is required for input selection/validation; network/provider calls occur only inside the graph after confirmation.\n - **Requested interface:** current CLI (`cli/main.py`), extended with input-mode flags. This is the only new user-facing surface; no new web application.\n - **Baseline preserved:** `tradingagents/`, `cli/`, `pyproject.toml` and existing tests are preserved. The extension is discovery, explicit consent, frozen provenance and coherent reporting (Prompt.md \"Session objective and input precedence\" / \"Access and output boundaries\").\n - **Trust boundary for data:** user-supplied portfolio files are *context*, never verified account facts. The trusted state used to build provenance is the frozen snapshot produced by the input service, not model text and not re-read file bytes.\n \n ### 2.1 Data-flow (C2)\n ```\n terminal user\n    │  (interactive, or flags)\n    ▼\n CLI adapter (cli/main.py)  ──►  PortfolioInputService (discover → validate/precheck → freeze)\n    │                                         │\n    │                                         ▼\n    │                              RunContext (deeply immutable)\n    │             frozen snapshot + mode + full-64 fingerprint + as-of + disclosure flags\n    │                                         │\n    │   [notice shown; consent gate]\n    │                                         │\n    ▼                                         ▼\n runapi/execution.run_analysis_api  ── consent confirmed ──►  engine.stream_run\n    │  (CLI single-run orchestration, no LLM)         (portfolio=None | frozen snapshot)\n    │                                         │\n    │                                         ▼\n    │                     runapi/checks.py OutputChecker (non-LLM, authoritative)\n    │                                         │\n    │                                         ▼\n    │                  runapi/finalize.py OutcomeFinalizer (COMPLETED|INCOMPLETE)\n    │                                         │\n    ▼                                         ▼\n Artifact boundary (redaction + run-ID isolation)  →  report(MD/HTML), manifest, JSONL events, logs, state JSON\n ```\n \n ---\n \n ## 3. Components\n \n Concrete module paths are in `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` §1 (B3-10). The `tradingagents/runapi/` modules and `cli/input_ui.py` **exist in the current checkout** (verified); the \"Status\" column records that. Reusable noninteractive services live under `tradingagents/runapi/` and must not import `cli`.\n \n | Component | Responsibility | Where (verified path) | Status vs baseline |\n |---|---|---|---|\n | **Shared execution service** | **Common application entry** `run_analysis_api(RunContext, …)`: consent check → run → render → check → finalize → stage/publish → terminal event. Prompt-free; used by CLI and supported API. | `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py` | present (additive) |\n | `PortfolioInputService` | Noninteractive discovery/precheck/freeze; **sole** discoverer/validator; prompt-free. | `tradingagents/runapi/input_service.py` | present (additive) |\n | `RunContext` / `FrozenSnapshot` (deeply immutable) | Frozen value tuples + mode + full-64 fingerprint + as-of/basis + consent_state; read-only provenance source. | `tradingagents/runapi/context.py` | present (additive) |\n | `OutputChecker` | Deterministic **Q1–Q4** on the checked **body**; assigns `output_check` + findings. Authoritative, non-LLM. | `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py` | present (additive) |\n | `OutcomeFinalizer` | Maps graph return/exceptions/attempted critical-persistence failure to `run_outcome` + `stop_reason`. | `tradingagents/runapi/finalize.py` | present (additive) |\n | `Redactor` | Central masking (keys/tokens/bearer, unsafe diagnostics) at every sink, including `agents/structured.py` warnings (R1 repair). | `tradingagents/runapi/redact.py` | present (additive) |\n | `EventSink` (JSONL) | Fixed-field structured events; stage-private tentative terminal. | `tradingagents/runapi/events.py` | present (additive) |\n | Persistence/Manifest | Staging (report+manifest **critical**; terminal event **best-effort**) → single atomic directory commit; manifest via `SafeRunMetadata`; `terminal_event.durable` decided pre-commit without blocking publication. | `tradingagents/runapi/persist.py` | present (additive) |\n | Result schemas | `RunResult`, `CheckResult`, `Finding`, `InputError`, `RunRecord`, `summarize_records`. | `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` | present (additive) |\n | CLI input UI | Interactive discovery/consent **only** here. | `cli/input_ui.py` | present (additive) |\n | CLI adapter | Thin wiring; adds `--without-portfolio`, `--portfolio-as-of`; suppresses prompts under flags. | `cli/main.py` | adapted |\n | Prompt/context semantics | Mode-aware rating-scale legend; no-portfolio Hold meaning; user-supplied/unverified wording. | `tradingagents/agents/context.py`, manager/trader prompts | adapted |\n | Concise intermediate context *(integrated at `adb4dfc`)* | Advisory evidence-first brevity guidance (`concise_analysis_instruction`); exact-substring opponent reference (`opponent_argument_or_opening(...,history)`); compaction safeguard restoring explicit copies before `bound_agent_prompt` (`bound_debate_prompt`); `concise_intermediate_reports` switch. Advisory versus authoritative data\n \n | Data | Nature | Authority |\n |---|---|---|\n | Model narrative, ratings text, recommendations | **Advisory** | Cannot set `output_check`/`run_outcome`/provenance |\n | Final rating (Buy/Overweight/Hold/Underweight/Sell/REVIEW) | Derived deterministically from the PM output | Reported, but check Q1 only *reads* readability |\n | Frozen snapshot metadata (mode, basename, fingerprint, as-of) | **Authoritative** (trusted state) | Built by input service; used by header/result/check |\n | `output_check` (PASSED/NEEDS_REVIEW/NOT_RUN) + findings | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutputChecker` only |\n | `run_outcome` (COMPLETED/INCOMPLETE) + `stop_reason` | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutcomeFinalizer` only |\n \n The disclaimer and no-portfolio notice are **frozen strings** (selected-requirements §1) and are treated as trusted content, excluded from Q4 phrase scanning.\n \n ---\n \n ## 5. Workflow (selected C2)\n \n 1. **Discover** eligible `.json` files (non-recursive, sorted, symlinks excluded) from `PORTFOLIO_DIR` — or accept explicit `--portfolio PATH` (outside dir allowed; parent not scanned).\n 2. **Select** one file, or choose no-portfolio, or cancel.\n 3. **Validate/precheck** the frozen bytes; reuse upstream model validation after explicit shape/type/as-of prechecks. Empty positions is valid (flat); no silent fallback.\n 4. **Freeze** → `RunContext` (deeply immutable value tuples; full-64 canonical fingerprint; as-of/basis recorded). Consent state `FROZEN`.\n 5. **Notice** (portfolio mode; §6) then **confirm** → `CONFIRMED` (default No). Non-interactive: valid flags are the consent expression.\n 6. **Run / analysis execution** via the **shared execution service** (`runapi/execution.py`): rejects any `RunContext` not `CONFIRMED`; holdings reach the provider **only after** confirmation. Within this analysis-execution stage (not rendering/publication):\n    - **Intermediate context generation.** When `concise_intermediate_reports` is enabled, analysts and Bull/Bear/risk debaters receive **advisory** evidence-first brevity guidance (`concise_analysis_instruction`; ~450 words analysts, ~220 debates). **Placement:** in `analysts/turn.py` the guidance is appended to the **assembled system message** (tool-bound and wrap-up paths, preserving tool schemas/call IDs/messages); in the Bull/Bear researchers and three risk debaters it is appended to their **assembled prompt strings**. The guidance is **advisory** (subordinate to evidence/disclosures), not a hard output cap. This feature introduces **no new forced output/tool-payload truncation**; the existing per-prompt guard (`bound_agent_prompt`, character/4 estimate) can still trim narrative when a large assembled prompt exceeds its limit.\n    - **Reference substitution (deterministic).** When an opponent's exact stripped latest argument already occurs in debate history, a reference replaces the duplicate copy (`opponent_argument_or_opening(...,history)`); an empty opponent keeps an explicit opening notice. This is **exact Python string-substring matching**, not semantic deduplication.\n    - **Compaction safeguard (deterministic branch).** `bound_debate_prompt` reconstructs the explicit copies and, if the reconstructed-original length would exceed `min(context_cap_tokens, compaction_threshold_tokens) * 4`, passes the restored form to the existing `bound_agent_prompt` guard (else the reference form). This reduces but does **not** eliminate dangling-reference risk: a short argument can be replaced by a longer reference notice, so a reference form longer than the restored original can still be compacted (probe `docs/reviews/evidence/token-context-reference-probe-2026-11-24.json`). Restoring copies before the guard is **not** a guarantee that every evidence item survives compaction.\n    - **Trusted portfolio facts** and all final provenance/check/publication authority below are unchanged; prompt instructions are not deterministic semantic enforcement.\n    - **Separate from budgets:** this is neither the existing per-prompt character/4 guard nor the proposed run-wide `CALL_CAP`/`BUDGET` controller (ADR-002 D3, unimplemented).\n    - **Status:** **integrated at `adb4dfc` (PR #18, ancestor of current HEAD `5672a79`)**; the dangling-reference boundary, quality acceptance and prior approval remain **open**. Switch `concise_intermediate_reports` (default True; `TRADINGAGENTS_CONCISE_INTERMEDIATE_REPORTS=false` or programmatic False restores legacy).\n 7. **Render body → scrub → single check (Q1–Q4; Q2 inspects the pre-check provenance fragment against explicit trusted metadata) → finalize → build trusted envelope → stage report+manifest (critical) → one atomic directory commit; terminal JSONL append is best-effort.** Incomplete runs bypass the checker and get `NOT_RUN`. The checked body is delivered unchanged; the envelope adds only trusted metadata. Terminal-event durability is decided before the manifest is staged but does not block publication; a terminal-append failure preserves the logical outcome and records `durable=false`. (§ interface-contracts §6–§7).\n 8. Pre-run cancellation/rejection starts **no graph, zero LLM calls, no completed run**; a critical persistence failure yields a typed INCOMPLETE result that never contradicts a returned success.\n \n Detailed state machine, schemas, canonicalization, ordering and failure simulations: `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md`.\n \n ### 5.1 Synthetic input-mode walkthrough (document example, not a passing test)\n - **Interactive, portfolio:** user sees `a.json`, `b.json`; selects `b.json`; precheck passes; freezes `b` (fingerprint Fb); notice shows basename `b.json`, date D, as-of basis, provider-transmission statement; user answers Yes → `CONFIRMED`; run transmits frozen `b` after consent; report header carries Fb and mode `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED`.\n - **Interactive, no portfolio:** empty directory → no-portfolio confirmation with frozen notice; Yes → `CONFIRMED` with `portfolio=None`; header shows `NO_PORTFOLIO`, null file/fingerprint/as-of.\n - **Noninteractive:** `--portfolio b.json --portfolio-as-of D` → freezes b, consent via flags, no prompt. `--without-portfolio` → `NO_PORTFOLIO`. Neither/both → `InputError`, zero calls.\n - **Cancelled:** user answers No at consent → zero graph/LLM, no completed run, counted as a pre-run attempt (NFR-006).\n \n ---\n \n ## 6. Permissions and consent\n \n - Interactive discovery/selection/consent lives **only** in the CLI (`cli/`). Agents and the engine never prompt.\n - **Consent gate** is an explicit coordinator transition between freeze and run. A frozen snapshot is a *candidate input*, **not** a confirmed selection; immutability alone does **not** prevent bypass. Only a coordinator transition to `CONFIRMED` permits run entry (see interface-contracts §4, ADR §Consent).\n - Mandatory execution, exception mapping, checks and artifact finalization sit behind a **shared application boundary** (`tradingagents/runapi/execution.py: run_analysis_api`) usable without terminal prompts. The upstream Python API signature is **preserved**; the supported project API routes through `run_analysis_api` (full requirement coverage). A raw low-level engine primitive (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run`) remains available but **does not** traverse the boundary and **does not** satisfy FR-006/FR-007/NFR-002/003/004; its scope is declared and product reliance requires **A's approval** (residual risk R-API, pending A). See `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` §5.\n - Coding-agent file permissions (separate concern) are in `docs/architecture/permission-model.md`; E implements enforcement.\n \n ---\n \n ## 7. Observability\n \n - New lifecycle event sink: UTF-8 JSONL; fixed fields `run_id, ticker, node, ts(UTC), elapsed_ms, event, event_outcome`. Console stays human-readable. Raw provider payload logging disabled by default. Progress vocabulary is separate from terminal `run_outcome`.\n - Existing sinks are adapted, not silently trusted: see memory-design §Sinks and runtime-policy-catalog.\n \n ---\n \n ## 8. Engineering contributions (project-specific design)\n \n This section states the team's concrete engineering contributions honestly. The individual mechanisms are **standard software-engineering techniques** (immutability, content hashing, atomic directory replacement, append-before-dispatch ledgers, fail-closed checks). We do **not** claim to have invented them, and a standard technique's use does not by itself establish originality. The contribution is the **problem-specific design, its adaptation across the existing TradingAgents pipeline, and the demonstrated effect** in this application; the professor assesses originality. Each item separates what is **deterministically enforced** from what depends on **model compliance** (pending semantic acceptance).\n \n ### 8A.1 Protected portfolio facts across Research Manager, Trader and Portfolio Manager\n \n - **Concrete problem.** In the baseline the portfolio block reached some decision stages unevenly. A real observed failure (2026-11-18, F9) showed an explicit-empty `PortfolioContext(positions=[])` run completing with deterministic check `PASSED` while the Trader/Portfolio-Manager narrative still spoke of \"reducing/retaining existing exposure\" — an unsupported account claim. Downstream stages could also inherit an ownership premise asserted upstream (the Research Manager's investment plan) without access to the same supplied facts.\n - **Design decision.** Route the same protected portfolio block through a single helper, `get_portfolio_context_from_state` (`tradingagents/agents/context.py:214`), into **all three** decision stages — Research Manager, Trader, Portfolio Manager — and wrap it in `<protected_context>…</protected_context>` (`protect_context`, `context.py:271`) so context compaction cannot drop it. Absent input yields an explicit \"no account ownership is assumed / unknown, not flat\" notice; explicit-empty carries a no-nonzero-target instruction; a held book carries the supplied quantity. The stage instruction tells the model to correct conflicting upstream ownership premises (R4). The five research ratings and three Trader actions are unchanged; no rating is forced.\n - **Baseline/team change.** Bounded R4 repair (2026-11-21): equalized the block across all three stages and added the corrective instruction. It is a prompt-grounding change, **not** a new authoritative check.\n - **Tradeoff.** Prompt text grows slightly and each stage must be kept consistent; grounding reduces but cannot eliminate unsupported narrative. A deterministic ownership check would be a larger change the current Q1–Q4 checker deliberately does not make.\n - **Implementation status.** **Implemented** (R4). **Deterministically enforced:** the trusted facts are delivered to all three stages and survive compaction (prompt-capture tests). **Not enforced deterministically:** that the model's prose never asserts an unsupported position — that is assessed semantically (pending C, GOV-004).\n - **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r4_research_manager_context.py` (RM/Trader/PM prompt distinction, shared facts, user-supplied/unverified label surviving compaction, absent≠flat); C seams `tests/member_c_verification/offline/test_fr004_propagation.py`, `test_fr005_ratings.py`. Source: `tradingagents/agents/managers/research_manager.py:27-52`, `portfolio_manager.py:30-51`, `trader/trader.py:34,82-93`, `context.py:214-273`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/evidence/live-diagnostic-2026-11-18.json`; `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.\n - **Residual limitation.** Prompts cannot guarantee every future narrative; Q1–Q4 does not inspect ownership wording. A critical staging/commit failure returns `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` with no artifact promise. A tentative terminal is staged privately and revealed only after the commit; a post-commit callback failure cannot revise a published COMPLETED result (R5).\n - **Baseline/team change.** Bounded R5 repair plus the C2 boundary (`runapi/` modules). These separate advisory from authoritative status and make publication truthfully conditional.\n - **Tradeoff.** More modules and a staging directory; best-effort events mean a run can publish with `durable=false` (stated, not hidden). The existing character/4 prompt guard bounded very large prompts but did not address this sub-threshold repetition.\n - **Design decision (feature `9102759`).** Advisory evidence-first brevity guidance (~450-word analysts, ~220-word Bull/Bear/risk): in `analysts/turn.py` appended to the **assembled system message**, in Bull/Bear/risk appended to their **assembled prompt strings**. Deterministic replacement of a duplicated opponent argument by a reference **only when the exact stripped text occurs in history** (**exact Python string-substring matching**); and a compaction safeguard that reconstructs the explicit copies and, if the reconstructed-original length exceeds `min(context_cap_tokens, compaction_threshold_tokens)*4`, passes the restored form to the existing guard. **No unconditional no-dangling guarantee:** a short argument can be replaced by a longer reference notice, so the reference form can exceed the guard target even when the restored original fits, and checking only the restored-original length can miss compaction of the reference form (probe `docs/reviews/evidence/token-context-reference-probe-2026-11-24.json`). Reversible via `concise_intermediate_reports` (default True; env/programmatic False restores legacy).\n - **Deterministic vs advisory.** Flag/metadata plumbing, the exact-string reference, and the reconstruct-then-guard branch are deterministic; the word targets and evidence-preservation wording are **advisory** prompt guidance. **No new forced output/tool-payload truncation** is introduced (the existing guard may still trim narrative); it is not a guarantee that every evidence item survives compaction.\n - **Kept separate.** Not the existing per-prompt guard; not the proposed Slice C `CALL_CAP`/`BUDGET` controller (ADR-002 D3, unimplemented).
